01Chapter 1 · From Generalist to Specialist

From Generalist to Specialist

Honeymoon khatam ho gaya hai. Pehle jab aapne ek bade generalist model ko prompt diya aur usne ekdum perfect, coherent jawab diya, to laga ki future infinite hai — prompting hi nayi programming language hai. Lekin jab aapko ek real product ship karna ho, to wahi generalist kai baar galat tool sabit hota hai. Ye chapter usi gap ke baare me hai — aur iska jawab hai specialist banana.

API wall kya hai?

Ek cool hackathon demo aur ek profitable business ke beech ek invisible barrier hai — API wall. Iske peeche teen hard realities hain: scale par kuchalne wala kharch, unpredictable latency, aur data privacy ka darr. Jab aap customer ka data kisi third party ko bhejte hain, to security team ka sawaal bilkul valid hota hai — data kahan ja raha hai, kaun dekh raha hai, aur wapas delete hoga ya nahi?

Generalist model ko internet bhar ke data par train kiya gaya hai — woh haiku bhi likh sakta hai aur code bhi optimize kar sakta hai. Lekin aapka kaam alag hai: aapko chahiye ki woh aapke legacy database ko query karte waqt aisi tables invent na kare jo exist hi nahi karti. Generalist thoda-thoda sab kuch jaanta hai, lekin aapke specialised domain ke baare me lagbhag kuch nahi jaanta — aur har call par aap uske liye per-token paise dete hain.

Renting se owning tak

Is book ka core idea simple hai: intelligence rent karne se owning ki taraf badho. Ek chhota open model lo, apne domain aur apne data se use sikhao, aur use privately chalao — ek specialist jo aapka apna hai. Prompt engineering ka paradigm tod kar, knowledge ko model ke weights ke andar bake kar do, taaki har request par use dobara samjhana na pade.

  • Generalist: sab kuch thoda-thoda jaanta hai, hosted API se milta hai, har token par kharch hota hai.
  • Specialist: ek domain me deep expert hai, aapke paas chalta hai, aur aapke business ko kisi bade model se behtar jaanta hai.
  • Book ka scope: ye book sirf fine-tuning cover karti hai — prompt engineering ya RAG nahi — aur running example ek medical Q&A expert hai jo Gemma 4 par bana hai.

Is chapter me aap wo brutal unit economics dekhenge jisne kai AI startups ko maar diya, aur samjhenge ki ek chhota open-source model ek single GPU par duniya ke sabse smart AI ko aapke specific domain me kaise hara sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Generalist impressive hai, lekin product ke liye aapko specialist chahiye — chhota model, aapka data, aapka control.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — From Generalist to Specialist

01.1Chapter 1 · From Generalist to Specialist

The Token Tax and the Hidden Costs

Har project masoomiyat se shuru hota hai — API key lo, system prompt banao, beta par deploy karo, sab kaam karta hai. Phir bill aata hai aur aankhen chaudi ho jaati hain. Is section me wahi hisaab hai: token tax aur uske peeche chhupe hue kharch.

Token tax — per-token pricing ka hisaab

Prototype phase me inference cost negligible lagti hai — ek request par ek cent ka fraction, matlab lagbhag free. Lekin jab aap chatting se automation ki taraf badhte hain, to math aapke against ho jaata hai. Zyada tar providers token ke hisab se charge karte hain, aur ek token lagbhag 0.75 words ke barabar hota hai. Table 1-1 me spread saaf dikhta hai — ek high-end model par $30 input aur $180 output per million tokens, jabki ek sasta model par sirf $0.14 input aur $0.28 output per million tokens.

Worked example — legal contract analyzer

Ek legal contract analyzer app ko socho: user contract upload karta hai, app usme se risk aur issues ka summary nikaalta hai. Ek typical contract lagbhag 15,000 tokens ka hota hai, system prompt ke instructions aur JSON output format ke tokens alag se. Kul milakar maan lo 17,000 input tokens aur 1,000 output tokens — lagbhag 20 cents per document.

  • 1,000 users, har user din me 5 documents — to roz ka kharch model par depend karke $21 se $7,950 per day tak ho sakta hai.
  • Ye sirf model chalane ka kharch hai — infrastructure alag se. Aur end me aapke paas intelligence ki ownership bhi nahi hai, aap sirf rent de rahe hain.
  • Agar aap users se $20 per month charge karte hain, to woh jaldi hi net loss ban sakte hain — margins bahut risky ho jaate hain.

Agentic multiplier

Agents ne token use ko aur badha diya hai. Ek 5-step agentic workflow — intent samjho, plan banao, tools se execute karo, results par reflect karo, solution present karo — simple prompt-result se 5 se 10 guna zyada tokens kha sakta hai. Ek industry estimate ke mutabik 2024 me 1% se kam enterprise software me agentic AI thi, lekin 2026 ke end tak 40% se zyada me hone ka anumaan hai. Matlab token tax ka problem aane wale samay me aur bada hone wala hai.

Instruction tax aur lost in the middle

Generalist ko aapka task samjhane ke liye aapko har request par rules, formatting guides aur edge cases system prompt me chipkane padte hain — aur un tokens ke paise bhi aap dete hain. Isi ko instruction tax kehte hain. Upar se research batati hai ki jaise-jaise context window instructions se bharte hain, model ki performance girne lagti hai — beech me dabi hui information kho jaati hai, jise lost in the middle kehte hain.

Latency, data firewall, metadata leak aur drift

  • Latency killer: time-to-first-token 500 ms se kai seconds tak ho sakta hai, aur uske baad per-token generation time alag se. Real-time use cases — jaise coding autocomplete ya voice apps — me ye lag conversation ko tod deta hai. Shared hosted machine par aapki query ko lakhon dusre users ke saath line me lagna padta hai.
  • Data firewall: ek hospital wali kahani me patient data legally building se bahar hi nahi ja sakta tha, aur security team ne cloud calls ko outright block kar diya. Demo kamaal ka tha, lekin deal usi table par mar gayi.
  • Metadata leak: prompt ka content na bhi dekha jaye, provider ko pata chalta hai ki aap kaun hain, kitna bada request bhej rahe hain, aur kis par research kar rahe hain. M&A jaise high-stakes business me ye leak insider trading jaisa risk ban sakta hai.
  • Compliance: GDPR jaise frameworks me agar user apna data delete karne ko kahe, to aap apne infrastructure se to delete kar sakte hain, lekin third-party server se delete hone ki guarantee kaise denge?
  • Model drift: provider model ko chupchaap update kar deta hai, to kal ka achha jawab aaj badal sakta hai — aur aapki mehnat se banayi prompt engineering raat bhar me evaporate ho sakti hai.
Yaad rakho: Fine-tuning instructions ko context window (jiske paise aap har baar dete hain) se nikaal kar model ke weights me permanent kar deta hai — token tax aur instruction tax dono ek saath khatam.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — From Generalist to Specialist

01.2Chapter 1 · From Generalist to Specialist

The Specialist Revolution

Lambe samay tak scaling laws hi future ki direction thi — bigger, zyada data, zyada layers, zyada parameters, hamesha behtar. Lekin ab ek bifurcation aa raha hai: models itne chhote aur itne capable ho gaye hain ki unhe khud host kiya ja sakta hai, aur unhe apne task par fine-tune kiya ja sakta hai. Yahi specialist revolution hai.

Turning point — chhote open models

2023 ke shuru me ek open model ki release ne ye ball rolling kar di — usne prove kiya ki achhe se engineered chhote models bhi apne weight se bahut upar punch kar sakte hain. Uske baad research me optimization par innovation ki baadh aa gayi — sirf scale phenkne ke bajaye quality par kaam hone laga. Generalist abhi bhi zinda hai aur kamaal ka kaam kar sakta hai, lekin developers ke liye bright future specialists banane me hai.

Hardware ab blocker nahi hai

Kuch saal pehle ek medical researcher ki sabse badi bottleneck data nahi, compute thi — dus researchers, ek GPU, aur uska slot sirf Tuesday afternoon. Aaj ek standard MacBook Pro bhi us samay ke model se orders of magnitude zyada powerful model ko fine-tune kar sakta hai. Apple Silicon ki unified memory ki wajah se 70B-parameter model bhi system RAM me load ho sakta hai. AI R&D lab ab backpack me fit ho jaata hai — datacentre ki zaroorat nahi.

Spectrum of customization

Model ko customize karne ke teen broad tareeke ek hi spectrum par hain — saste se lekar sabse deeply baked-in tak:

  1. Prompts: prompt me examples dekar model ko sikhao — sabse sasta, lekin model badalta nahi, sirf prompt smart hota hai.
  2. RAG: retrieval-augmented generation — related content ko prompt me add karke model ko extra context do. Ye bhi model ko change nahi karta.
  3. Fine-tuning: naye patterns ko model ke dimaag me burn kar do, taaki woh bina extra prompting ke wahi kaam kare. Sabse mushkil, lekin long run me sabse valuable.

Ye book pehle do tareekon ko cover nahi karti — woh extensively cover ho chuke hain, aur woh model ko change nahi karte. Ye book hard part ke liye hai — fine-tuning — jisme aap VRAM calculate karenge, messy data scrape aur clean karenge, aur converge na hone wale training loops ko debug karenge.

Fine-tuning kyun jeetta hai?

Fine-tuning domain knowledge ko weights ke andar bake kar deta hai. Isse aap har call par token tax aur instruction tax dena band kar dete hain, latency kam ho jaati hai kyunki model chhota aur local hai, data aapke building se bahar nahi jaata, aur model ek static artifact ban jaata hai jo aapke permission ke bina nahi badalta. API wall bahut unchi hai, lekin ab pehle se zyada ek alternative maujood hai — aur kal ka high-value skill wahi developers ke paas hoga jo is wall ko tod kar aisi AI bana sakte hain jo poori tarah unki apni ho.

Yaad rakho: Prompt aur RAG model ko nahi badalte — woh sirf smarter prompting hain. Fine-tuning hi model ko sach me badalta hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — From Generalist to Specialist

02Chapter 2 · Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

Fine-tuning karne se pehle aapko samajhna hoga ki aap customize kya kar rahe hain. Ek mechanic jo engine ko nahi samajhta, woh oil to change kar sakta hai, lekin transmission rebuild nahi kar sakta. Waisa hi fine-tuning practitioner ke saath hai — transformer ki anatomy samjhe bina aap sirf surface-level adjustments kar payenge, deep strategic decisions nahi.

Transformer se information ka flow

Text model me discrete symbols ki sequence ke roop me enter karta hai. Pehle text tokens me tutta hai — tokens words ya subwords ke numerical representations hain, inme apne aap koi meaning nahi hota. Phir har token ek embedding banta hai — ek high-dimensional space me ek vector, jiski direction uska meaning batati hai. Similar meaning wale words, jaise "King" aur "Prince", lagbhag ek hi direction me point karte hain.

  • Tokenization: text ko tokens me todna — isme byte pair encoding (BPE) common hai.
  • Embeddings: har token ek dense vector banta hai — Gemma 4 me 4,096 dimensions ka.
  • Positional encoding: word ki position bhi vector me add hoti hai, kyunki "The man bit the dog" aur "The dog bit the man" me tokens wahi hain, lekin meaning position se poori tarah badal jaata hai.
  • Transformer blocks: inke andar attention aur feed-forward layers tokens ko transform karke predictions banate hain.

Embeddings me meaning geometry me rehta hai

Do dimensions me socho to samajh aasan ho jaata hai: ek classic novel ke characters ko gender aur nobility ke axes par plot karo, aur vector ki length se wealth dikhao — to related characters ek saath cluster karte dikhenge. Real model me ye 4,096 dimensions me hota hai, lekin idea wahi hai: meaning vectors ke beech ke relationships me rehta hai, kisi dictionary definition me nahi. Isi liye model training examples se naye phrasing par generalise kar pata hai.

Positional encoding — RoPE

Transformer saare tokens ko parallel process karta hai, to use order ka koi inherent sense nahi hota. Modern models rotary position embeddings (RoPE) use karte hain: har step aage badhne par embedding vector ko ek angle theta se rotate kiya jaata hai — pehla embedding theta se, dusra 2-theta se, teesra 3-theta se. Isse paas wale words ki rotations similar rehti hain, aur relative distance absolute position se zyada matter karti hai. RoPE ki khaasiyat ye hai ki model training se lambi sequences par bhi bina zyada quality giraye generalise kar leta hai.

Ye chapter practically kyun matter karta hai

Baad ke har decision ki jad yahi chapter hai — LoRA kis par attach hota hai, chat template kyun matter karta hai, KV cache kya hai, aur kaunsa base model chunna hai. Ye chapter high-level hai — transformers par to poori kitabein likhi ja sakti hain — lekin end tak aapke paas apne fine-tuning project ke liye informed choice karne ki foundation hogi.

Yaad rakho: Token ka koi inherent meaning nahi hota — meaning embedding vectors ki geometry me rehta hai, aur position RoPE se aati hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

02.1Chapter 2 · Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

Attention: How the Model Decides What Matters

Attention transformer ka dil hai. Socho aap ek document padh rahe hain aur haath me highlighter hai — har paragraph padhte hue aap kuch words highlight karte hain kyunki woh current sentence ko samajhne me madad karenge. Attention mechanism artificially wahi kaam karta hai: har position ke liye calculate karta hai ki sequence ki har dusri position par kitna dhyaan dena hai.

Attention ka formula — Q, K, V

Har token se teen alag projections bante hain — query (Q): "Main kya dhoondh raha hoon?", key (K): "Mere paas kya hai?", value (V): "Main kya information deta hoon?" — jo embedding vector ko learned weight matrices se multiply karke bante hain. Poora process ek formula me bandha hai: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V. Pehle Q ko har word ke K se multiply karke scores nikaalo, softmax se unhe probabilities banao, phir un weights se V ko multiply karke output banao.

Example — "it" ka matlab kaise milta hai

Sentence lo: "The cat sat on the mat because it was tired." Jab model "it" ko process karta hai, to use infer karna hai ki "it" kisse refer karta hai — cat ya mat? Training data ke basis par attention "it" aur "cat" ke beech zyada strong connection banata hai, "it" aur "mat" ke beech nahi. Multi-layer, multihead model me deeper layers me isse bhi gehri meanings seekhi jaati hain.

Training kaise hoti hai

Training me model baar-baar passage ka next token predict karne ki koshish karta hai, aur cross-entropy loss measure karta hai ki woh kitna galat tha. Backpropagation us error ko network me peeche trace karke batata hai ki har weight — Q, K, V matrices samet — ne galti me kitna contribute kiya; phir gradient descent har weight ko us direction me nudge karta hai jo error kam kare. Practical me Adam ya AdamW jaise optimizer ye nudging handle karte hain, har weight ke liye step size alag se adapt karke.

Multihead attention

Ek attention operation ek hi type ka relationship capture karta hai, lekin language me ek saath kai relationship types hote hain. Isliye multihead attention kai attention operations ko parallel chalata hai, har ek ke apne learned Q, K, V matrices ke saath. Gemma 4 ke E4B variant me 42 layers me 8 attention heads per layer hain, aur kai heads KV share karte hain. Hidden dimension 4,096 ko 32 heads me baanta jaata hai to har head 128 dimensions par kaam karta hai (4,096 / 32 = 128) — phir 32 outputs ko concatenate karke ek output projection se guzara jaata hai, jo heads ke beech information mix karta hai.

Ek common galatfahmi ye hai ki har head neatly ek kaam karta hai — ek grammar, ek semantics. Reality messy hai: specialization layers ke across zyada hoti hai — early layers local syntactic patterns pakadti hain, deeper layers abstract semantic relationships banati hain. Kisi ek layer ke andar heads alag patterns seekhte hain, lekin woh human-interpretable categories me neatly map nahi hote.

Self-attention vs cross-attention

  • Self-attention: sequence khud par attend karti hai — Q, K, V sab ek hi sentence se aate hain. Yehi fine-tune karne wale models me dominant mechanism hai.
  • Cross-attention: ek sequence dusri sequence par attend karti hai — Q ek sequence se, K aur V dusri se. Ye encoder-decoder architectures aur multimodal models me dikhta hai, jahan model ko image ya voice features par bhi attend karna hota hai.
Yaad rakho: Attention seekha hua hota hai — Q, K, V matrices training se bante hain. Multihead ka fayda redundancy aur diversity me hai, neatly divided labour me nahi.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

02.2Chapter 2 · Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

The Transformer Stack and Its Efficiency Tricks

Attention ke baad har token ek feed-forward network se guzarta hai, aur poora stack normalization aur residual connections se stable rehta hai. Is section me transformer stack ke andar ki machinery aur woh efficiency tricks hain jinhone chhote models ko bada banaya — GQA, sliding window, mixture of experts, aur Gemma 4 ki design.

Feed-forward network — model ki knowledge store

Attention context gather karta hai, FFN us contextualized representation ko process karta hai. Structure expand-then-contract hai: pehli layer dimensionality ko 4,096 se 14,336 tak expand karti hai, phir SiLU / SwiGLU jaisi nonlinear activation lagti hai, phir dusri layer wapas 4,096 par project kar deti hai. Nonlinearity zaroori hai — bina iske stacked linear layers ek hi matrix me collapse ho jaayenge aur depth se kuch nahi milega. Nonlinear activation se neurons selective ho jaate hain: ek neuron sirf tab strongly activate hota hai jab input uske seekhe hue pattern se match kare.

Researchers FFN layers ko key-value memory jaisa describe karte hain — pehli layer ke weights keys hain jo input patterns se match karte hain, dusri layer ke weights values hain jo match hone par retrieve hote hain. Fine-tuning ke liye ye bahut matter karta hai, kyunki FFN layers me model ki deep knowledge ka bada hissa rehta hai — aur LoRA jaisi techniques yahi knowledge inject karti hain. Short me: attention decide karta hai kya dekhna hai, FFN decide karta hai uske saath kya karna hai.

LayerNorm / RMSNorm aur residual connections

  • Residual (skip) connections: har sublayer ka input uske output me add kar diya jaata hai, jisse gradients aasani se flow karte hain aur model har layer par incremental refinement seekh sakta hai. Ye gradients ko explode ya vanish hone se bhi rokte hain.
  • Layer normalization: activations ko feature dimension par normalize karke values ki distribution stable rakhta hai. Modern models jaise Llama RMSNorm use karte hain, jo computationally simpler hai.

Decoder-only vs encoder-decoder

Original transformer machine translation ke liye encoder-decoder tha — encoder poora input padhta tha, decoder cross-attention se translation generate karta tha. Lekin generation ke liye aage wale words exist hi nahi karte, to har token sirf peeche dekh sakta hai — ise causal attention kehte hain, jo mask se lookahead rokti hai. Isliye encoder ki zaroorat nahi rahi aur decoder-only architecture popular ho gaya: ek architecture, ek training objective (next-token prediction), aur input-output ki koi artificial boundary nahi. Scale karne par in models me in-context learning, chain-of-thought reasoning aur instruction following jaise capabilities ubhar aayi — bina explicitly train kiye. Fine-tuning me aap zyada tar isi decoder-only architecture par kaam karenge.

Grouped Query Attention (GQA)

Standard multihead attention me inference ke dauran saare previous tokens ke key aur value tensors cache karne padte hain — KV cache — jo lambi sequences par memory bottleneck ban jaata hai. GQA query heads ko group karke har group ko ek K-V projection share karwata hai. Ek family ke 8B model me 32 query heads 8 groups me bante hain, sirf 8 KV heads rehte hain, aur KV cache 75% shrink ho jaata hai. Context is dauran 2,048 se 4,096, phir 8,192 aur eventually 128k tokens tak badha, aur vocabulary 32k se 128k ho gayi. Trade-off ye hai ki alag heads alag cheezein dekhna chahte hain, lekin unhe context ka wahi "view" milta hai — nuance thodi kam ho sakti hai. Phir bhi fine-tuning ke liye GQA wale models behtar inference performance dete hain bina zyada quality khoye.

Sliding window attention aur Mixture of Experts

  • Sliding window (Mistral, September 2023): har token sirf pichhle 4,096 tokens par attend karta hai, to quadratic cost khatam ho jaata hai. Multi-layer model me pyramid effect se receptive field depth ke saath linearly badhta hai — layer 3 tak token position 10 ko position 4 tak ka context mil jaata hai. 7B ka chhota model bhi bahut bade models ke barabar perform karne laga.
  • Mixture of Experts (Mixtral 8x7B): FFN layer ki jagah multiple expert FFNs hote hain, aur ek router har token ke liye top-2 experts choose karta hai. Model me kul 46.7B parameters hain, lekin per token sirf lagbhag 12.9B active hote hain — bade model ki capacity, chhote model ki compute cost. Fine-tuning me MoE tricky hota hai — saare parameters memory me rakhne padte hain aur routing dynamics complex hoti hain, isliye kai projects ke liye non-MoE aasan rehta hai.

Gemma 4 — book ki model family

Gemma 4 sizes me 2B se 31B tak aati hai, -it (instruction-tuned) aur -pt (pretrained) variants ke saath. Isme hybrid attention hai — layers sliding window aur global attention ke beech alternate karti hain, final layers hamesha global hoti hain. Edge models (E2B aur E4B) me lagbhag aadhi layers apne K-V projections compute hi nahi karti — E2B me 35 me se 20 layers, E4B me 42 me se 18 layers pichhli layer ke tensors reuse karte hain (cross-layer KV sharing). Bade models me global layers keys ko values ke roop me reuse karti hain. Result: chhote models 128k tokens tak, bade models 256k tokens tak context support karte hain, bina memory explode kiye.

Yaad rakho: FFN knowledge store karta hai, attention context gather karta hai. GQA, sliding window aur MoE — teeno tricks ka maksad ek hi hai: kam memory aur kam compute me zyada capability.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Model Architectures: The DNA of AI
← Previous02.1 · Attention: How the Model Decides What Matters→ Next02.3 · Tokenization, Embeddings, and Choosing a Model
02.3Chapter 2 · Model Architectures: The DNA of AI

Tokenization, Embeddings, and Choosing a Model

Architecture ke baad ab text ke model tak pahunchne ke pehle kadam par aate hain — tokenization aur embeddings — aur phir us practical checklist par jo batati hai ki fine-tune karne ke liye kaunsa model chunna hai.

Tokenization ke trade-offs

Tokenization sirf words par split karna nahi hai. Rare words ke liye alag token rakhna vocabulary ko bada kar dega, non-English languages me spacing alag hoti hai, typos aur naye slang words handle karne mushkil hote hain, aur word ke variants (run, running, runs) bilkul alag tokens ban kar apni semantic similarity kho dete hain. Isliye modern LLMs subword tokenization use karte hain: common words jaise "the" single token hote hain, rare words tukdon me tut jaate hain. Badi vocabulary ka matlab hai kam tokens per word, lekin badi embedding matrix — ek trade-off.

Ek hi text alag tokenizer par alag token count de sakta hai. Chinese phrase "Hello World" ek English-trained tokenizer par 4 tokens banti hai, jabki ek multilingual tokenizer use sirf 2 tokens me todta hai — matlab token count, cost aur context usage, teeno tokenizer par depend karte hain. Aur ek baat pakki hai: aap model ka tokenizer change nahi kar sakte bina scratch se retrain kiye. Agar aap kisi specific programming language ya non-English language ke liye fine-tune kar rahe hain, to pehle verify karo ki tokenizer excessively lambi sequences to nahi bana raha.

BPE — byte pair encoding

Sabse common tokenization algorithm BPE hai, jo originally data compression ke liye bana tha. Process simple hai: characters se shuru karo, corpus me sabse frequent adjacent pair ko merge karke naya token banao, aur desired vocabulary size tak repeat karo. Example: "low", "lower", "lowest" wale corpus me pehle "l"+"o" merge hokar "lo" banta hai, phir "lo"+"w" merge hokar "low" — isiliye teeno words "low" subword share karte hain, aur model word forms ke across generalise kar pata hai.

Embeddings kya dete hain

Tokenize hone ke baad har token ID ek embedding vector me map hota hai. Similar meanings vector space me paas rehte hain — isiliye model training examples se naye phrasing par generalise kar sakta hai. Ek classic novel ke characters ka 2-D plot iska achha illustration hai: related characters ek saath cluster karte hain, aur vector ki direction aur length se unke beech ke relationships padhe ja sakte hain. Ye concrete definition nahi hai — relative meaning hai, jo axes aur vectors ke beech ke relations se banta hai.

Instruction following aur reasoning depth

  • Instruction following: model instructions follow karta hai kyunki use post-training me question-answer pairs par instruction-tune kiya gaya tha. "-it" ya "Instruct" wale models isme behtar hote hain, aur precise instruction following chahiye to instruction-tuned base se shuru karna usually behtar hota hai.
  • Reasoning depth: reasoning aksar model ka khud se "baat karna" hota hai — bade models generally behtar multi-step reasoning dikhate hain, lekin architecture bhi matter karti hai. Deep reasoning (jaise mathematical proofs) ke liye bada model chahiye ho sakta hai, ya chain-of-thought prompting se multiple inference calls karne pad sakte hain. Ise fine-tune karna mushkil ho sakta hai, to expectations manage karke chalo.
  • Lost in the middle, dobara: bada context window hone ka matlab ye nahi ki model use effectively use karta hai — beech ki information sabse aasani se kho jaati hai. Fine-tune karne se pehle base model ki recall ability ko document ki alag-alag positions se test karo.

Model chunne ki checklist

Model chunna kai factors par depend karta hai — koi single right answer nahi hai. Ye sawaal poochho: tokenizer mera data accurately encode karta hai? Context window asal me kitni badi hai, aur kya woh mere users ki demands meet karti hai? Model kitna bada hai — kya woh mere available memory me fit hoga, kya use quantize kiya ja sakta hai? Training ke memory constraints kya hain? GQA wale models generally high inference efficiency dete hain. Dense models fine-tune karne me aasan hote hain, MoE models zyada capacity dete hain lekin mushkil hote hain. Base model aapko final behavior par zyada control deta hai, lekin chat jaise instruction-based scenario me instruction-tuned variant behtar ho sakta hai. Aur yaad rakho — training inference se significantly zyada resources leti hai. Book ke baaki hisse me Gemma 4 family use hoti hai, kyunki usne in sawaalon ke author ke liye sabse achhe jawab diye.

Yaad rakho: Tokenizer ko fine-tuning ke time par change nahi kar sakte — model chunne se pehle tokenizer efficiency check karo, baad me nahi.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Model Architectures: The DNA of AI
← Previous02.2 · The Transformer Stack and Its Efficiency Tricks→ Next03 · The Fine-Tuner's Workshop
03Chapter 3 · The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

Galat tools se furniture assemble karne ki koshish ki hai? Best case me wobbly desk milti hai, woh bhi equipment se ladne ke baad. Fine-tuning bhi waisa hi hai — sahi hardware aur software setup critical hai, aur ye investment un frustrating raaton ko bachata hai jo cryptic error messages se bhari hoti hain. Ye chapter aapka workbench hai.

Setup kyun matter karta hai

Inference lightweight kaam hai — weights memory me baithe hain, data flow hota hai, output tokens aate hain. Ek decent laptop 7B model par inference handle kar leta hai. Lekin fine-tuning fundamentally alag hai: aap sirf data model se pass nahi kar rahe, aap parameters ko update kar rahe hain. Har training step me weights ke saath-saath gradients (har weight kis direction me move kare) aur optimizer states (har parameter ki momentum aur variance history) bhi store karne padte hain. Adam jaise common optimizer ko weights se double storage chahiye ho sakta hai.

Ek rough hisaab: 7B-parameter model 16-bit precision me sirf parameters ke liye lagbhag 14 GB leta hai. Gradients, optimizer states aur activations add karo to 70–80 GB ho jaata hai — jo kisi bhi reasonable price wale consumer GPU se bahar hai. Isiliye "CUDA out of memory" woh error hai jo inference par kabhi nahi aaya, lekin fine-tuning par achanak aa jaata hai. Model ka size naapna sirf pehla kadam hai — training memory usse bahut zyada hoti hai.

Vibe-coding wali warning

Software environment bhi utna hi tricky hai. CUDA aur PyTorch ka version mismatch aksar silent failure deta hai — code chalta hai, lekin GPU ka fayda nahi milta, aur training time bahut badh jaata hai. Vibe-coding yahan khaas taur par dangerous hai: LLM jo code deta hai woh reference implementations par based hota hai jo bas kaam karte hain, lekin agar aapka environment sahi se set nahi hai, to code factually sahi hote hue bhi fail karega — aur LLM code ko fix karne ki koshish karega, jabki code toota hi nahi tha! Isse silent decay bhi ho sakta hai — model train hota dikhta hai, lekin environment ki inconsistencies ki wajah se perform achha nahi karta. Bottom line: environment ko samjho aur real checks se verify karo, training run se pehle.

Is chapter ka kaam

Chapter ka job hai: ek working GPU, sahi software stack, aur ek verified training run — koi real data aane se pehle. Hardware options near-infinite hain, isliye book opinionated hai: jo setup book me use hota hai, wohi aapko shuru karne ke liye suggest kiya gaya hai. Aapko use follow karna mandatory nahi hai, lekin saare examples usi par chalte hain. Is chapter ke end tak aapke paas ek verified, reproducible workshop hoga, jisse baad ke har chapter ka training run ek known-good base se shuru hoga.

Yaad rakho: Inference aur training ki memory bilkul alag hai — weights + gradients + optimizer states + activations ka total dekho, sirf model size nahi.
Book Ch 3 (The Fine-Tuner's Workshop) — encourage double-checking that it's working as recommended with code, like this: [book.txt lines 2361–2369] 
import torch
print(f"PyTorch version: {torch.__version__}")
print(f"CUDA available: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
    print(f"VRAM: {torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_mem
/ 1e9:.1f} GB")
Book Ch 3 (The Fine-Tuner's Workshop) — enough for individual practitioners. All of these can be installed with a single pip command: [book.txt lines 2468–2472] 
pip install transformers peft bitsandbytes trl accelerate
datasets wandb
            sentencepiece protobuf
Book Ch 3 (The Fine-Tuner's Workshop) — your results. Setting it up is straightforward: [book.txt lines 2563–2567] 
# Create a free account at wandb.ai, then
wandb login
# Paste your API key when prompted
Book Ch 3 (The Fine-Tuner's Workshop) — automatically log into wandb. You can also configure it explicitly in your training arguments: [book.txt lines 2572–2581] 
from transformers import TrainingArguments

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="./outputs/checkpoints",
    report_to="wandb",
    run_name="...",
    # ... other arguments
)
Book Ch 3 (The Fine-Tuner's Workshop) — source alternative that runs entirely locally, and can easily be used in environments like Colab. Install it as follows: [book.txt lines 2591–2599] 
pip install tensorboard

# In your TrainingArguments:
# report_to="tensorboard"

# After training, launch the viewer:
tensorboard --logdir ./logs

03.1Chapter 3 · The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

VRAM Math and Choosing a GPU

GPU fine-tuning ke liye optional nahi hai — transformer basically bade matrix multiplications ka khel hai, aur GPU ke hazaaron chhote cores ek hi operation ko kai pieces of data par simultaneously kar sakte hain. Lekin GPU chunne se pehle ek number samajhna zaroori hai: VRAM. Ye hard constraint hai jo tay karta hai ki aap kya fine-tune kar sakte hain aur kya nahi.

VRAM math — per parameter kitne bytes?

Precision ke hisab se har parameter ka cost: FP32 = 4 bytes, FP16 / BF16 = 2 bytes, INT8 = 1 byte, INT4 = 0.5 bytes. To 7B model FP32 me 28 GB, FP16/BF16 me 14 GB, INT8 me 7 GB aur INT4 me sirf 3.5 GB leta hai. FP16 aur BF16 size me same hain, lekin range alag hai — modern NVIDIA stack BF16 prefer karta hai. Aur haan, next-token predict karne ke liye 32-bit precision ki zaroorat nahi — 99.00002% accurate hona 99.0000234023523% jitna hi kaafi hai.

Tables 3-1 se 3-5 — full fine-tuning vs LoRA vs QLoRA

7B model ki full fine-tuning FP16 me: weights 14 GB + gradients 14 GB + optimizer states (FP32) 56 GB + activations 2 GB = lagbhag 86 GB. Ye kisi bhi single consumer GPU me nahi aata — 80 GB wala A100 bhi aggressive optimization ke bina struggle karega, aur uski keemat lagbhag $14,000 hai.

  • LoRA: sirf chhota adapter train hota hai — weights 14 GB + adapter 0.14 GB + gradients 0.14 GB + optimizer 0.56 GB + activations 2 GB = lagbhag 17 GB. Ye RTX 4090 (24 GB, lagbhag $1,400) par aaram se chalta hai.
  • QLoRA: base model 4-bit me — weights 3.5 GB + baaki wahi — kul lagbhag 7 GB. Ye sirf 8 GB VRAM me fit ho jaata hai, aur aise GPUs $100–$200 me mil jaate hain, ya Colab ke free tier par T4 (16 GB) par milta hai.
  • Dusre sizes: 3B full fine-tune lagbhag 36 GB, LoRA lagbhag 8 GB, QLoRA lagbhag 4 GB; 13B full fine-tune lagbhag 160 GB (multi-GPU), LoRA lagbhag 32 GB, QLoRA lagbhag 12 GB; 70B full fine-tune lagbhag 800 GB (multinode), LoRA lagbhag 160 GB, QLoRA lagbhag 40 GB (A100).

Activations batch size ke saath linearly badhte hain — 7B model, batch size 1, 2,048 tokens par activations 2–4 GB le sakte hain. Isiliye VRAM aapke batch size ko bhi limit karta hai. Takeaway saaf hai: shuruaat LoRA ya QLoRA se karo — sweet spot hai, highly effective hai, aur consumer hardware par accessible hai.

GPU anatomy aur consumer GPUs

CPU sequential logic ke liye bana hai — kuch powerful cores, ek kaam bahut tez. GPU me hazaaron chhote cores hote hain — A100 me lagbhag 7,000, H100 me 15,000 se zyada. Consumer side par flagship RTX 4090 hai (24 GB VRAM, MSRP lagbhag $1,400), aur pichhli generation ka RTX 3090 (24 GB) bhi discount par perfectly serviceable hai. VRAM ki matra hi behtar indicator hai — kam VRAM wala tez card bhi aapko limit kar dega. AMD ka RX 7900 XTX (24 GB, ROCm) bhi competitive hai aur sasta milta hai, lekin fine-tuning ecosystem NVIDIA-first bana hai — Flash Attention aur bitsandbytes jaise tools AMD par peeche hain.

Apple Silicon alag duniya hai: unified memory ki wajah se GPU aur CPU wahi RAM share karte hain — M4 Max 128 GB unified memory ke saath technically A100 se zyada "VRAM" report karta hai. Lekin throughput kam hai — A100 par ek ghante ka run M4 Max par chaar se chhe ghante le sakta hai. Aur bitsandbytes jaise libraries macOS par support nahi karti, to QLoRA nahi chalta.

Data-centre GPUs aur Colab

A100 industry standard hai — 40 GB aur 80 GB variants, 80 GB wala 2 TB/s memory bandwidth ke saath. Ye 70B par LoRA aur 7B tak full fine-tuning handle kar leta hai. H100 har dimension me tez hai — zyada bandwidth, behtar tensor cores, FP8 support — lekin cloud par premium charge hota hai; book ke zyada tar workloads ke liye A100 kaafi hai. L4 (24 GB) aur L40S (48 GB) cost-effective mid-tier options hain.

Google Colab book ka recommended starting point hai: free T4 High-RAM par lagbhag 15 GB VRAM milti hai, lagbhag 13 cents per hour (1.27 compute units per hour, 100 units $10). Ye LoRA ya QLoRA ke liye kaafi hai. Dhyaan rakho — free tier limited hai, busy time par paid users ko priority milti hai, aur A100 ke 40 GB vs 80 GB variants ke liye High-RAM toggle check karna padta hai.

Distributed training

Jab ek GPU kaafi na ho, to do strategies hain: data parallelism — poora model har GPU par copy karo, batch ko baanto, gradients average karo (model har GPU par fit hona chahiye, training tez hoti hai); aur model parallelism — model ko hi GPUs ke beech baanto (bade models ke liye ekmatra raasta, lekin communication overhead zyada). ZeRO jaise techniques redundancy kam karte hain. Hugging Face Accelerate ise approachable banata hai — accelerate config se interactive setup, phir accelerate launch train.py se multi-GPU run. Lekin book ke models aur techniques ke liye single low-VRAM GPU LoRA/QLoRA ke saath kaafi hai.

Yaad rakho: VRAM hard constraint hai — agar model VRAM me fit nahi hota, to pareshan mat ho, chhota model ya QLoRA chuno. Full fine-tune 86 GB, LoRA 17 GB, QLoRA 7 GB — 7B model ke liye.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

03.2Chapter 3 · The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

Operating System, Python, PyTorch, and the Core Libraries

Hardware ke baad software stack aata hai — operating system, Python environment, PyTorch aur CUDA ka match, aur woh core libraries jo poori book me use hongi. Yahan ek galat version silent failure de sakta hai, isliye har step ko verify karna part of the job hai.

Operating system

  • Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS): sabse smooth path — ecosystem compatibility aur first-class CUDA support. Lagbhag har tutorial, Docker image aur cloud template Linux assume karta hai.
  • Windows: WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2) surprisingly achha hai — real Linux kernel aur native CUDA passthrough, jisme Windows NVIDIA drivers seedha WSL2 ke saath share hote hain. Seedha Linux use karna phir bhi kam complexity deta hai.
  • macOS (Apple Silicon): PyTorch ka MPS backend basic training ke liye kaam karta hai, MLX zyada native experience deta hai, lekin bitsandbytes support nahi hai — to QLoRA nahi. Mac ko cloud GPU ka thin client bana kar SSH se training chalana ek valid raasta hai.

Python environments — Conda vs venv

Fine-tuning ke liye Python hi language hai — libraries aur ecosystem support sabse behtareen hai. Lekin version drift bahut hai, isliye virtual environments prerequisite hain. Conda comprehensive hai — Python packages ke saath CUDA toolkit versions bhi manage karta hai, to ek environment me CUDA 11.8 aur dusre me 12.1 rakh sakte hain. Venv (pip ke saath) lightweight hai, tez set hota hai, aur tab achha hai jab CUDA system-wide pehle se installed ho.

PyTorch install — CUDA match sabse bada trap

PyTorch install karte waqt Compute Platform row par dhyaan do — default Linux select karne par CPU version load hota hai, aur GPU install karne ke baad bhi PyTorch use ignore kar dega. Book likhte waqt PyTorch CUDA 12.6, 13.0 aur 13.2 support karta tha, jabki latest CUDA 13.3 tha — "latest use karo" wali advice yahan apply nahi hoti, strictly supported version use karo. Install ke baad verify karo:

import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()) — agar False aaye to kuch galat hai: ya CPU-only PyTorch install hua hai, ya CUDA version mismatch hai. nvidia-smi se bhi check karo ki driver version PyTorch ke supported version se match karta hai ya nahi.

Core libraries — har ek ka role

  • PyTorch: deep learning framework — tensor operations, autograd, GPU acceleration; baaki sab isi par bana hai.
  • Transformers: Hugging Face ki library jo thousands of pretrained models ko ek consistent API se deti hai — AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(...) se architecture aur weights Hub se download hokar ready PyTorch model ban jaate hain.
  • PEFT: parameter-efficient fine-tuning — LoRA, QLoRA jaise adapter methods; base weights freeze karke chhoti trainable matrices inject karta hai (detail Chapter 7 me).
  • bitsandbytes: quantization library jo QLoRA enable karti hai — 4-bit aur 8-bit quantization se 14 GB model 3.5 GB VRAM me load hota hai, load_in_4bit=True se. Ye NVIDIA par highly optimized hai.
  • TRL: high-level training APIs — SFTTrainer supervised fine-tuning ka training loop, data collation, gradient accumulation, logging aur checkpointing handle karta hai; DPOTrainer Chapter 10 me aayega.
  • Accelerate: mixed precision, device placement aur distributed training ke details sambhalta hai — aksar TRL ke peeche chup kar kaam karta hai.
  • Datasets: Apache Arrow aur memory-mapped files par based efficient data loading — RAM se bade datasets bhi handle ho jaate hain; load_dataset(...) ek line me public dataset load karta hai.
  • Weights & Biases (wandb): experiment tracking — loss curves, learning rate, gradient norms ko dashboard par visualize karta hai.

Install ek hi command me: pip install transformers peft bitsandbytes trl accelerate datasets wandb sentencepiece protobuf — sentencepiece aur protobuf tokenizer dependencies hain, jo kuch models ko chahiye hoti hain, isliye preemptively include karna wise hai.

Environment check — Chapter3.ipynb

Book ke notebook ko Colab par A100 40 GB par chalane par ye output milti hai — proof ki stack kaam karta hai: GPU NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, VRAM 42.4 GB; TinyLlama 1.1B-Chat 4-bit me load, footprint 0.75 GB; inference "The capital of France is Paris" sahi; LoRA me 1,126,400 trainable parameters (0.1023%); single training step loss 3.4863, gradient successfully compute. Agar ye na mile to common errors check karo: "CUDA available: False" matlab CPU-only PyTorch; "CUDA out of memory" matlab koi dusra model memory kha raha hai — process kill karo ya reboot karo; bitsandbytes compilation errors matlab CUDA toolkit mismatch; model download failures matlab Hugging Face cache (~/.cache/huggingface/) me space kam hai.

Yaad rakho: PyTorch install karne ke baad torch.cuda.is_available() se verify karo — False aaye to aage badhne se pehle fix karo, warna silent decay me ghante barbaad honge.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — The Fine-Tuner's Workshop
← Previous03.1 · VRAM Math and Choosing a GPU→ Next03.3 · Tracking Experiments and Renting Compute
03.3Chapter 3 · The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

Tracking Experiments and Renting Compute

Setup ka aakhri hissa hai experiment tracking aur compute rent karna — kyunki 30 experiments ke baad aapko yaad nahi rahega ki sabse achha run kaunsa tha, aur apna GPU khareedna har kisi ke liye sahi nahi hota. Ye section dono ka framework deta hai.

Experiment tracking — har run record karo

Har training run metrics generate karta hai — step 1,000 par loss kya tha, learning rate kaise decay hua, model ne kis step par overfit karna shuru kiya? Log files se in sawaalon ke jawab nikaalna lagbhag namumkin hai, lekin ek proper tracker se trivial hai.

  • Weights & Biases (wandb): ML community ka standard — free individual use, wandb login ke baad TrainingArguments me report_to="wandb" aur run_name="..." set karo. Har run ek dashboard ban jaata hai — loss curves, learning rate schedules, gradient norms, GPU memory usage — real time me, taaki kharab run ko manually early stop kar sako.
  • TensorBoard: open-source alternative jo poori tarah locally chalta hai, Colab me aasani se use hota hai — report_to="tensorboard", phir tensorboard --logdir ./logs.
  • Manual log bhi chalega: agar koi tool use na karo, to ek spreadsheet ya notepad me date, model name, dataset version, key hyperparameters (LoRA rank, learning rate, epochs), final training loss aur evaluation score record karo. Checkpoints ko bhi isi sheet ke entries ke hisab se naam do, taaki woh aasani se mil jayein.

Cloud options — Colab ke aage

  • Kaggle Notebooks: Colab jaisa experience, free GPU (T4 aur P100 dikhe hain) 30 hours per week quota ke saath. Bonus: datasets Kaggle par hi hosted hote hain, to integration aasan hai.
  • Lambda Labs: notebook ke bajaye SSH se poora Linux machine — A100 aur H100 instances, apna software aur files manage karne ki poori freedom.
  • RunPod: GPU marketplace — Community Cloud sasta lekin kam reliable, Secure Cloud mehenga lekin reliable; spot instances saste hain lekin preempt ho sakte hain, jo lambi training runs ke liye ideal nahi.
  • Vast.ai: GPU rental ka marketplace jahan individual GPU owners apna hardware rent par dete hain — reliability aur security vary karti hai.
  • DigitalOcean: ROCm-powered AMD chips ke saath cloud service.

Local vs cloud — decision framework

Koi universally right choice nahi hai — ye chaar sawaal poochho: (1) Kya aapke paas 16 GB ya zyada VRAM wala GPU hai? Haan, to local machine 7B tak QLoRA handle kar legi; nahi, to cloud primary option hai. (2) Ye one-time experiment hai ya ongoing kaam? Regular fine-tuning karni hai to local GPU kuch mahino me apni keemat vasool kar leta hai; one-off exploration ke liye cloud bina commitment ke access deta hai. (3) Kya data sovereignty requirements hain? Healthcare, finance ya government me data premises se bahar nahi ja sakta — to local training mandatory hai. (4) Kya 13B se bade models train karne hain? 70B par QLoRA ko bhi lagbhag 40 GB VRAM chahiye — consumer GPU se bahar, A100 (cloud) ya multi-GPU setup chahiye.

Three tiers aur hybrid workflow

Zyada tar practitioners hybrid workflow par settle hote hain: locally ya free Colab par chhote model aur data subset se develop aur debug karo, phir full training cloud GPU par chalao jab sab kaam kar raha ho. Local iteration speed ke liye hai — seconds me restart, hyperparameter tweak, dobara try. Cloud final training run ke liye hai — bada GPU ya lamba runtime.

  • Tier 1 — Colab Free (T4, 16 GB): 7B tak QLoRA. Minimum requirement — sirf isse bhi har example follow kar sakte hain.
  • Tier 2 — Local RTX 4090 ya Colab Pro A100 (24–40 GB): 13B tak QLoRA, ya 7B par LoRA bina quantization ke.
  • Tier 3 — Cloud A100 80 GB: 70B par LoRA, 7B par full fine-tuning, ya koi bhi experiment jahan VRAM bottleneck ho.

Techniques har tier par wahi rehti hain — sirf model size aur training speed badalti hai. Apne resources se match karta tier chuno aur baaki ki chinta mat karo.

Yaad rakho: Har run ko track karo — bina record ke tuning guesswork hai. Aur hybrid workflow apnao: develop local, train final cloud par.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — The Fine-Tuner's Workshop
← Previous03.2 · Operating System, Python, PyTorch, and the Core Libraries→ Next04 · Excavating Data
04Chapter 4 · Excavating Data

Excavating Data

Model architectures open hain — reference implementations, papers, tutorials sab available hain. Training techniques aur hyperparameters bhi aasani se mil jaate hain. Lekin data — khaas taur par woh data jo aapne ya aapke customers ne saalon ki practice se kamaya hai — proprietary hai, domain-specific hai, aur hard won hai. Wahi cheez aapko sabse alag karti hai. Ye chapter data ko khodne, saaf karne aur audit karne ke baare me hai.

Data is the moat

Model commodity hai — koi bhi team wahi base model download kar sakti hai. Lekin ek achha domain dataset copy karna mushkil hai, aur wahi aapke expert ko banata hai. Iske alawa structured datasets ke andar bhi "data within data" hota hai — massive unstructured data me chhupa value, jise modern models ki understanding se nikaala ja sakta hai. Ye double opportunity hai: apne business ka reach badhao, aur data se zyada value nikalo.

Teen pillars — relevance, correctness, diversity

  • Relevance: kya data aapke target domain se match karta hai?
  • Correctness: kya answers sahi hain?
  • Diversity: kya data production me dikhne wale inputs ki range cover karta hai?

Teeno ko equal priority do. Aur quantity ko lekar ek rule of thumb yaad rakho: LoRA ke saath kuch sau (hundreds) well-chosen examples hi needle move kar dete hain — quantity goal nahi hai, quality hai.

Chapter ka arc

Is chapter me aap sourcing, scraping, cleaning, privacy protection aur quality audit se guzrenge — public datasets aur Kaggle se lekar web scraping, structured systems aur PDFs tak, phir normalization, filtering, deduplication, PII redaction aur quality audit tak. Synthetic data — apna dataset khud banana — agle chapter me aayega. Ye sab seekhne ke baad aapka role value chain me upar badhega: domain-specific fine-tuning aur data se value nikaalna, wahi jagah hai jahan ek engineer sabse zyada valuable banta hai.

Ek aur baat yaad rakhne layak hai: aapke paas jo data pehle se hai, woh aksar do hisso me hota hai — structured data jo systems ke liye banaya gaya tha, aur unstructured data jo saalon se pile up hota raha hai (wikis, tickets, manuals, documents). AI ki understanding se dusre hisse me bhi value milti hai, isliye excavation ka matlab sirf naye sources dhoondhna nahi hai — apne existing data ke andar chhupa value nikaalna bhi hai. Aur jab aapko lage ki automated tools sab kuch kar denge, to yaad rakho ki vibe-coding ke zamane me bhi data ka kaam human judgment mangta hai — kya relevant hai, kya sahi hai, kya diverse hai, ye decisions aapko hi leni hain.

Yaad rakho: Architecture aur techniques commoditized hain — aapka curated, domain-relevant dataset hi aapki competitive advantage hai.

Book Ch 4 (Excavating Data) — A simple normalization pipeline to use some of the tools I mention in this section would look like this: [book.txt lines 3222–3241] 
import unicodedata
import re
import ftfy

def normalize_text(text):
    # Fix encoding issues
    text = ftfy.fix_text(text)
    # Unicode normalization
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text)
    # Strip residual HTML tags
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text)
    # Decode HTML entities
    text = text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">",
">")
    # Normalize whitespace
    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text)
    return text.strip()
Book Ch 4 (Excavating Data) — example (using MD5, SHA-256, or even Python's built-in hash) and remove exact matches. This is fast and easy: [book.txt lines 3351–3363] 
import hashlib

def exact_dedup(examples):
    seen = set()
    unique = []
    for ex in examples:
        h = hashlib.md5(ex.encode()).hexdigest()
        if h not in seen:
            seen.add(h)
            unique.append(ex)
    return unique
Book Ch 4 (Excavating Data) — documents with similar fingerprints. The datasketch library makes this accessible in Python: [book.txt lines 3375–3397] 
from datasketch import MinHash, MinHashLSH

def build_minhash(text, num_perm=128):
    m = MinHash(num_perm=num_perm)
    for word in text.lower().split():
        m.update(word.encode("utf-8"))
    return m

# Create LSH index with Jaccard similarity threshold
lsh = MinHashLSH(threshold=0.8, num_perm=128)

for idx, text in enumerate(examples):
    mh = build_minhash(text)
    lsh.insert(str(idx), mh)

# Query for near-duplicates
for idx, text in enumerate(examples):
    mh = build_minhash(text)
    results = lsh.query(mh)
    if len(results) > 1:
        print(f"Example {idx} has near-duplicates: {results}")
Book Ch 4 (Excavating Data) — containing a phone number, detects it, and then removes it for anonymization: [book.txt lines 3499–3524]

from presidio_anonymizer import AnonymizerEngine

default)

# Call analyzer to get results
results = analyzer.analyze(text=text,
                           entities=["PHONE_NUMBER"],
                           language='en')
print(results)
# Analyzer results are passed to the AnonymizerEngine for
anonymization

anonymized_text =
anonymizer.anonymize(text=text,analyzer_results=results)

print(anonymized_text)

04.1Chapter 4 · Excavating Data

Sourcing Datasets and Scraping Domain Data

Fine-tuning me kaam largely data selection ka function hai, volume ka nahi. Sabse aasan shuruaat woh data hai jo pehle se exist karta hai — lekin aapka business vertical shayad hi kisi prepackaged dataset me milega. Is section me public sources, Kaggle, scraping aur internal systems — chaaro tareeke hain.

Hugging Face datasets

Hugging Face Hub thousands of datasets ka primary repository hai, task aur license type se categorized. Book chaar standard datasets par focus karta hai:

  • Alpaca-cleaned: 52,000 instruction-response pairs — general-purpose instruction tuning ke liye, chhota footprint.
  • OpenOrca: lagbhag 1M examples, chain-of-thought reasoning par focus — step-by-step logical steps sikhata hai.
  • UltraChat 200k: 200,000 dialogues — multiturn conversational tuning ka standard.
  • Dolly-15k: 15,011 human-curated examples, CC BY-SA 3.0 license ke saath — purely commercial, clean-room applications ke liye viable options me se ek.

Load karna do lines ka kaam hai: from datasets import load_dataset; ds = load_dataset("databricks/databricks-dolly-15k", split="train") — phir print(ds) aur print(ds[0]) se features aur ek example inspect karo. Dolly me features hain instruction, context, response aur category — aur pehla record ek airline ke baare me closed_qa example hai. Load karne se pehle inspect karna time well spent hai.

Licensing warning — legal gray area

Licensing research se production jaane ka primary blocker ban sakta hai. Apache 2.0 aur MIT permissive hain, lekin kai popular datasets proprietary models se distilled hain, jinki apni licensing terms hoti hain. Kuch bade providers ki terms of service explicitly prohibit karti hain ki unke model output se competing models train kiye jayein — isse OpenOrca ya Alpaca jaise datasets commercial sale ke liye legal gray area me aa jaate hain. Hamesha Hugging Face metadata card par "License" aur "Data Source" tags verify karo. Apne khud ke data par fine-tune karna hai to licensing kam issue hoti hai — lekin agar woh data kahin aur se partially sourced hai, to wahan bhi check karo.

Kaggle — 710,000+ datasets

Kaggle ka fayda domain-specific, raw, real-world data hai — uncurated datasets aapki cleaning skills ko improve karte hain. 710,000 se zyada public datasets hain, aur community uploads me SEC filings, clinical radiology reports aur legal corpora jaise underrepresented verticals bhi hain. Quality variable hoti hai, isliye validate karna mandatory hai. Prioritize karo: usability rating 8.8 ya zyada (10 me se score — metadata completeness aur documentation par based), license constraints (kai datasets CC-BY-NC ya competition-restricted hote hain), aur provenance (data legally aur ethically obtain kiya gaya ya nahi).

Kaggle API workflow chaar steps ka hai: (1) domain keywords se search karo, votes aur usability score se sort karo; (2) description aur community discussions padho; (3) sample download karke inspect karo — file format, schema, distribution, quality; (4) license check karo. Tabhi conversion aur cleaning code likhne me time invest karo. Ek medical VQA example me question tha "Are regions of the brain infarcted?" aur answer "Yes" — lekin Hugging Face se farak ye hai ki Kaggle data raw hota hai (CSV, JSON, nested directories), to aapko khud conversion step likhna padta hai.

Data interview — sabse high-value technique

Internal data ke liye sabse pehle data interview karo: domain experts ke saath baitho — woh log jo asal me woh kaam karte hain jisme model madad karega — aur poochho ki achha output kaisa dikhta hai. Ek great customer support response me kya hota hai? Regulatory filing summary useful kab hoti hai, useless kab? Junior analysts kaunsi common galtiyan karte hain? Ye conversations aapki data collection priorities shape karti hain aur quality ko define karti hain — aisa kaam jo automated metrics nahi kar sakte.

Web scraping, structured systems aur PDFs

  • Web scraping: simple pages ke liye Requests + BeautifulSoup, bade crawls (thousands of pages, pagination, rate limits, retries) ke liye Scrapy. Public site bhi ho to pehle robots.txt aur terms of service check karo — publicly visible hona crawl aur repurpose karne ka right nahi deta.
  • Structured systems: Zendesk, Jira aur Salesforce jaise platforms me APIs ya MCP servers hote hain — REST ya GraphQL se clean JSON pull karo. Confluence, Notion aur SharePoint jaise document stores se content extract karne ke tools bhi hain.
  • PDFs: text-based PDFs ke liye PyMuPDF aur pdfplumber; scanned PDFs ke liye OCR — Tesseract, docTR, PaddleOCR, DeepSeek-OCR, ya cloud OCR APIs. Tables, multicolumn layouts aur headers/footers complexity badhate hain — extraction pipeline ko apne document format ke liye tune karne me time lagega.

Scraping pipeline ko perfect karne aur document karne me time invest karo — fine-tuning glamorous dikhta hai, lekin data funnel ka wide end hi long-term savings deta hai.

Yaad rakho: Public datasets se proof-of-concept banao, lekin data interview se shuru karo — domain experts hi batayenge ki achha data kaisa dikhta hai.

04.2Chapter 4 · Excavating Data

Cleaning: Normalization, Filtering, and Deduplication

"Garbage in, garbage out" fine-tuning me khaas urgency le leta hai. Pretrained model ke paas pehle se broad knowledge hai — fine-tuning use scratch se nahi badhata, woh aapke data ke patterns se uska ek hissa overwrite karta hai. Agar woh patterns garbage hain — noisy, inconsistent ya errors se bhare — to model high confidence ke saath galat hona seekh lega. Ek pretrained model ka kabhi-kabhi medical question galat karna annoying hai; ek fine-tuned model ka consistently galat medical answers dena dangerous hai.

Normalization — encoding aur HTML saaf karo

Unicode me wahi visible character kai tareekon se encode ho sakta hai — jaise "é" ek single code point ho sakta hai ya "e" + combining accent. Dono render same hote hain, lekin tokenizer ke liye alag byte sequences hain, to "café" do alag words ki tarah seekha ja sakta hai. NFC conservative option hai — sirf truly same character wali encodings merge karta hai. NFKC aage jaata hai — lookalike compatibility characters bhi fold kar deta hai, jaise ligature ya full-width characters ko regular bana deta hai — lekin ye lossy hai, NFKC ke baad "10²" aur "102" indistinguishable ho jaate hain. Jo form base model ka tokenizer use karta hai, fine-tuning time par wahi match karna matter karta hai.

Iske alawa: Windows line endings (\r\n) vs Unix (\n) tokenizer ko confuse karte hain; Latin-1 me encoded document ko UTF-8 se padhne par mojibake banta hai — jaise "don't" ka apostrophe bigad jaata hai — iske liye ftfy library purpose-built hai; aur scraped HTML me bache hue tags aur entities (jaise &) strip karne padte hain. Ek simple pipeline: ftfy se encoding fix, unicodedata.normalize("NFC"), regex se HTML tags strip, entities decode, whitespace normalize.

Filtering — jo belong nahi karta, use nikaalo

  • Length filtering: bahut chhote examples usually incomplete hote hain, bahut lambe context window se exceed karke truncate ho jaate hain — to model broken examples se seekhta hai. Apne domain aur model ke hisab se minimum aur maximum length thresholds set karo.
  • Language detection: scraped data me kai languages mix hoti hain — fasttext ya langdetect se har example ki language classify karke sirf target language rakho.
  • Quality scoring: perplexity se measure karo ki model sample ko kitna predict kar sakta hai — fluent English ki perplexity tens me hoti hai, random character soup ki thousands me. CCNet-style classifiers aur heuristic signals (stop-word ratio, character distribution) bhi use hote hain.
  • Topic filtering: keyword matching se domain-relevant examples rakho — lekin false positives aur negatives se savdhaan raho. Sophisticated tareeka: sentence embeddings encode karke reference domain documents se cosine similarity nikaalo aur threshold se neeche wale discard karo.

Deduplication — do baar kyun matter karta hai

Duplicate examples model ko overfit karwate hain — woh generalizable patterns seekhne ke bajaye exact phrasings memorize karne lagta hai, aur output repetitive ho jaata hai. Pehli line of defense exact dedup hai: har example ko MD5 ya SHA-256 se hash karke exact matches hatao — fast aur easy.

Lekin zyada tar duplicates exact nahi hote — minor formatting differences, spelling ya punctuation ke saath near-copies hote hain. Inke liye MinHash + LSH use hota hai (datasketch library, threshold 0.8): har document ka n-grams par based compact fingerprint banao, phir LSH se similar fingerprints efficiently dhoondho. Substring dedup alag case hai — jab ek example poori tarah dusre lambe example ke andar ho; iske liye n-gram overlap heuristics ya suffix arrays (dedup-dataset tool) kaam aate hain.

Dedup do baar matter karta hai: duplicates training compute waste karte hain, aur usse bura — test examples training me leak hokar evaluation ko inflate kar dete hain. Ambiguous flagged pairs ko manually review karna mat bhoolo.

Yaad rakho: Ek ganda example problem nahi hai — systematic gandagi problem hai. Cleaning optional nahi hai, kyunki model wahi seekhega jo aap use khilayenge.

04.3Chapter 4 · Excavating Data

Privacy, Redaction, and the Quality Audit

Data saaf karne ke baad do cheezein bachti hain jo training se pehle mandatory hain: personal data ko bahar nikaalna, aur ye verify karna ki bacha hua data asal me achha hai. Dono ko skip karna mehenga padta hai — ek legal risk deta hai, dusra bekaar model.

Memorization risk — PII leak kaise hota hai

PII me names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses aur aisi har information aati hai jo kisi individual ko identify kar sake. Model training data ko memorize karke inference ke time par wapas produce kar sakta hai — ye theoretical nahi hai. Ek research paper me dikhaya gaya ki model se ek shabd baar-baar repeat karwane par woh eventually diverge karke training set ke words emit karne lagta hai — matlab memorized content nikaala ja sakta hai. Agar PII data me hi nahi hai, to kam se kam woh risk mitigate ho jaata hai.

Regulatory implications severe hain: GDPR (Europe), CCPA (California) aur HIPAA (healthcare) personal data ke handling par bahut strict requirements lagate hain. Bina proper consent ya safeguards ke PII wale data par train karna significant legal liability deta hai — chahe model sirf internal hi kyun na ho, memorized PII audit aur compliance risks banata hai.

Detection — regex + NER + Presidio

  • Regex: structured PII — email, phone number, credit card number, IP address — ke liye fast aur precise. Lekin unstructured PII (person names, street addresses) miss kar deta hai.
  • Named-entity recognition (NER): spaCy jaise models running text me person names, organizations, locations aur dates detect karte hain — zyada flexible, lekin kam precise.
  • Microsoft Presidio: production-grade open-source framework jo regex recognizers aur NER models ko combine karta hai. Worked example me "My phone number is 212-555-5555" par analyzer ne PHONE_NUMBER flag kiya, 0.75 confidence score ke saath, aur anonymizer ne use placeholder se replace kar diya. Threshold set karna important hai — bahut low rakha to valuable non-PII bhi strip ho jaayega, bahut high rakha to PII leak ho sakta hai.

Redaction strategies — teen options

  1. Placeholders se replacement: sabse simple aur safe — values ko [PERSON], [EMAIL], [PHONE] jaise placeholders se badlo. Lekin agar data ka bada hissa placeholders se bhar jaaye, to model placeholder tokens wala text produce karna seekh lega.
  2. Synthetic equivalents: naturalness preserve karta hai — asli values ko plausible synthetic values se badlo. Faker library iske liye purpose-built hai — names, addresses, phone numbers, emails generate karta hai. Consistency maintain karni padti hai — ek example me ek hi value har jagah same synthetic value se replace honi chahiye.
  3. Generalization: specifics strip karke context bachao — exact address ko general area me badlo. Ye middle-ground hai, jab geographic ya demographic context matter karta hai lekin specific identity nahi.

Kai practitioners hybrid use karte hain: names aur organizations ke liye synthetic replacement (jahan naturalness sabse zyada matter karti hai), aur highly sensitive items ke liye placeholders ya generalization.

Quality audit — statistics, visualization, spot check, contamination

  • Statistical profiling: example lengths ki distribution (characters aur tokens dono me), mean, median, standard deviation, min, max — aur khaas taur par class imbalance par dhyaan do. Agar 80% examples ek subtopic ke hain aur 5% dusre ke, to model majority par strong aur minority par weak hoga. Upsampling, downsampling, ya underrepresented topics ke liye aur data collect karna — ye strategies hain.
  • Visualization: sentence transformer se examples embed karke UMAP ya t-SNE se clusters plot karo — off-topic clusters, outlier groups ya coverage gaps dikh jaate hain. Word clouds per category bhi vocabulary differences highlight karte hain.
  • Random 50 rule: har training run se pehle randomly 50 examples ko carefully padho — skim nahi, read karo. Agar do-teen se zyada par aapko wince aaye — jawab galat hai, formatting tooti hai, instruction aur response match nahi karte — to badi problem hai. Gut feeling ko follow karo: agar feel galat hai, to aur mistakes bhi hongi.
  • Contamination checks: training set aur evaluation set ka overlap evaluation scores ko meaningless bana deta hai — model generalize nahi, memorize kar raha hota hai. Exact matches search karo, eval examples ke long n-grams training me dhoondho, ya embeddings se similarity search karo. Overlap mile to training set se woh examples hatao — thoda chhota training set meaningless evaluation se behtar hai.

Pipeline discipline aur dataset cards

Sab stages ko ek config-driven YAML pipeline me compose karo — normalization, filtering, deduplication, PII redaction, quality audit, phir processed output. Har stage independent aur rerunnable honi chahiye: length threshold badla to filtering stage se onward rerun karo, raw data ko kabhi modify mat karo. Output format ke liye JSONL (ek line par ek JSON object) chhote data ke liye best hai; 1 GB se bade datasets ke liye Hugging Face Datasets format (Arrow / Parquet) behtar performance deta hai — memory-mapped access aur columnar compression ke saath. Aur har dataset ke liye ek dataset card banao — README jisme sources, collection date, processing steps, size, limitations aur license documented ho. SQuAD ka dataset card gold standard mana jaata hai.

Yaad rakho: PII data me hi na ho to leak ka risk hi khatam. Aur training se pehle random 50 examples padhna sabse sasta quality test hai.

05Chapter 5 · Synthetic Data

Synthetic Data

Chapter 4 me aapne real-world data collect aur clean karna seekha. Lekin kya ho jab woh strategies exhaust ho jayein aur phir bhi coverage kaafi na ho? Domain itna specialized ho ki public datasets exist hi na karte hon, ya data privacy regulations ke peeche locked ho — jaise real patient questions ya financial transactions — aur aapke paas hote hue bhi aap use training ke liye use na kar sakte hon. Tab synthetic data aata hai.

Teacher-student paradigm

Core idea simple hai: ek bada capable model (teacher) training examples generate karta hai, aur ek chhota sasta model (student) un par fine-tune hota hai. Teacher ko kuch naya seekhna nahi hai — woh jo pehle se jaanta hai, use structured format me demonstrate karta hai, scale par. Ye knowledge distillation ka ek form hai, lekin traditional distillation se alag — yahan student teacher ki internal representations ya output probabilities ko match nahi karta, woh sirf teacher se bana dataset dekhta hai. Student teacher se kabhi directly interact nahi karta, aur teacher ke learned weights ko reverse engineer ya copy karne ki koshish bhi nahi hoti.

Running example: 1,000 medical Q&A pairs Gemma 4 fine-tune ke liye. Medical domain isliye chuna gaya kyunki real data haasil karna mushkil hai, accuracy enormously matter karti hai (galat medical information harm kar sakti hai), aur quality control non-negotiable hai. Agar aap is demanding domain ke liye robust synthetic pipeline bana sakte hain, to wahi techniques kisi bhi similarly demanding domain me transfer ho jaati hain.

Teacher-model inconsistency — honestly note karo

Is chapter me ek discrepancy hai jise book khud note karta hai aur aapko bhi honestly rakhna chahiye: chapter ka code locally GPT-OSS-20B teacher use karta hai, jabki Hugging Face par hosted datasets GPT-OSS-120B se bane the. Ye do alag teachers hain — inhe ek claim me merge mat karo. Code samples 20B isliye use karte hain taaki aap unhe simple hardware par khud chala saken; hosted datasets bade 120B teacher se bane the.

Terms-of-service warning

Kai hosted models ki terms aapko unke outputs se competing model train karne se mana karti hain — ye distillation se bachne ke liye hota hai. Is ambiguity se bachne ka sabse saaf raasta open-weights teachers hain — GPT-OSS, Llama 3 ya Mistral jaise models ko apne infrastructure par chalao, to outputs aapke hain kyunki model aap khud chala rahe hain. Teacher model hamesha use karne se pehle uski current terms check karo — policies samay ke saath evolve hoti hain.

Synthetic data kab sahi hai — aur kab nahi

Synthetic data sahi call hai jab real data scarce ho, private ho, ya expensive ho. Lekin ye real data ka replacement nahi hai — jahan real data mil sakta hai, wahi jeet-ta hai. Bina filter ke naive synthetic dataset koi data na hone se bura ho sakta hai, kyunki aap model ko teacher ki galtiyan aur stylistic approach high confidence ke saath reproduce karna sikha denge. Isliye quality control afterthought nahi hai — asli system me wahi majority of the work hoga. Data generate karna fast aur sasta hai, kuch ghanton ka kaam; use verify, filter aur curate karke quality dataset banana wahi jagah hai jahan engineering aur real value rehti hai.

Yaad rakho: Teacher bada model, student chhota model — teacher dataset banata hai, student us dataset se seekhta hai. Aur code wala teacher (GPT-OSS-20B) aur hosted datasets wala teacher (GPT-OSS-120B) alag hain — dono ko honestly alag rakho.

    {"category": "Orthopedics", "conditions": [
        "osteoarthritis", "rotator cuff injury", "plantar fasciitis",
        "herniated disc", "carpal tunnel syndrome"]},
    {"category": "Psychiatry", "conditions": [
        "generalized anxiety", "major depression", "insomnia",
        "ADHD in adults", "panic disorder"]},
]

QUESTION_TYPES = [
    "symptoms and presentation",
    "treatment options",
    "lifestyle modifications",
    "when to seek emergency care",
    "diagnostic workup",
    "medication side effects",
    "prognosis and long-term management",
    "prevention strategies",
]


def generate_seeds(n: int) -> list[dict]:
    """Create n seed combinations of (category, condition, question_type)."""
    seeds = []
    for _ in range(n):
        topic = random.choice(MEDICAL_TOPICS)
        condition = random.choice(topic["conditions"])
        q_type = random.choice(QUESTION_TYPES)
        seeds.append({
            "category": topic["category"],
            "condition": condition,
            "question_type": q_type,
        })
    return seeds


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Teacher Prompting — Single & Batch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a board-certified physician creating educational medical
content. Generate a realistic patient question and a detailed, accurate medical answer.

Rules:
- The question should sound like a real patient asking their doctor — natural language,
  not clinical jargon.
- The answer should be medically accurate, cite specific guidance where appropriate,
  and be 150-300 words.
- Include practical advice the patient can act on.
- Always recommend consulting a healthcare provider for personalized advice.
- Never fabricate drug names, dosages, or clinical trial results."""

COT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a board-certified physician working through a
clinical reasoning exercise. When answering the patient's question:

1. First, identify the key clinical considerations (2-3 sentences).
2. Then, work through the relevant differential or decision points step by step.
3. Finally, provide your recommendation with clear rationale.

Format your answer with these labeled sections:
CLINICAL CONSIDERATIONS: ...
REASONING: ...
RECOMMENDATION: ...

Be medically accurate. Never fabricate drug names or dosages."""


def _strip_markdown_fences(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove ```json ... ``` wrappers that Gemini often adds around JSON."""
    text = text.strip()
    if text.startswith("```"):
        # Remove opening fence (```json or just ```)
        first_newline = text.index("\n")
        text = text[first_newline + 1:]
    if text.endswith("```"):
        text = text[:-3]
    return text.strip()


def _call_gemini(system_prompt: str, user_prompt: str,
                 temperature: float = 0.9, max_tokens: int = 2000) -> str:
    """Send a request to Gemini and return the text response.

    NOTE: We fold the system prompt into the user message rather than using
    system_instruction, because gemini-3-pro-preview appears to count
    system_instruction tokens against max_output_tokens, causing truncation.
    We also do NOT use response_mime_type="application/json" because it
    burns the token budget on internal schema processing.
    """
    # Combine system + user prompts into a single message
    if system_prompt:
        combined_prompt = f"{system_prompt}\n\n---\n\n{user_prompt}"
    else:
        combined_prompt = user_prompt

    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=temperature,
        max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
    )

    response = client.models.generate_content(
        model=TEACHER_MODEL,
        contents=combined_prompt,
        config=config,
    )

    # Check for safety blocks or empty responses
    if not response.candidates:
        block_reason = getattr(response, "prompt_feedback", None)
        raise RuntimeError(f"Gemini returned no candidates. Prompt feedback: {block_reason}")

    candidate = response.candidates[0]
    finish = candidate.finish_reason

    if finish and str(finish) not in ("FinishReason.STOP", "STOP", "0"):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Gemini finish_reason={finish}. "
            f"Safety ratings: {candidate.safety_ratings}"
        )

    text = response.text
    if not text:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Gemini returned empty text. finish_reason={finish}, "
            f"safety_ratings={candidate.safety_ratings}"
        )

    return _strip_markdown_fences(text)


def generate_pair(seed: dict, use_cot: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Generate a single Q&A pair from a seed (Section 5.3.3)."""
    sys_prompt = COT_SYSTEM_PROMPT if use_cot else SYSTEM_PROMPT
    user_prompt = (
        f"Generate a medical Q&A pair about {seed['condition']} "
        f"({seed['category']}), focusing on {seed['question_type']}.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY valid JSON with exactly two keys: \"instruction\" and \"output\". "
        f"No other text before or after the JSON."
    )

    content = _call_gemini(
        sys_prompt, user_prompt,
        temperature=0.9,
        max_tokens=8192 if use_cot else 8192,
    )
    pair = json.loads(content)
    pair["metadata"] = seed
    pair["is_cot"] = use_cot
    return pair


def generate_batch(seed_batch: list[dict], use_cot: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Generate multiple Q&A pairs in a single API call (Section 5.3.4)."""
    sys_prompt = COT_SYSTEM_PROMPT if use_cot else SYSTEM_PROMPT
    batch_size = len(seed_batch)
    seed_descriptions = "\n".join([
        f"{i+1}. {s['condition']} ({s['category']}): {s['question_type']}"
        for i, s in enumerate(seed_batch)
    ])

    user_prompt = (
        f"Generate {batch_size} distinct medical Q&A pairs for these topics:\n\n"
        f"{seed_descriptions}\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a JSON array of objects, each with \"instruction\" and \"output\" keys. "
        f"No other text before or after the JSON."
    )

    content = _call_gemini(
        sys_prompt, user_prompt,
        temperature=0.9,
        max_tokens=8192,
    )
    pairs = json.loads(content)
    # Attach metadata to each pair
    for pair, seed in zip(pairs, seed_batch):
        pair["metadata"] = seed
        pair["is_cot"] = use_cot
    return pairs


def run_generation(seeds: list[dict], cot_fraction: float = COT_FRACTION) -> list[dict]:
    """Generate all Q&A pairs from seeds, one at a time for reliability."""
    results = []
    errors = 0
    cot_cutoff = int(len(seeds) * (1 - cot_fraction))

    for i, seed in enumerate(seeds):
        use_cot = i >= cot_cutoff
        retries = 2

        for attempt in range(retries + 1):
            try:
                pair = generate_pair(seed, use_cot=use_cot)
                results.append(pair)
                break
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, Exception) as e:
                if attempt < retries:
                    time.sleep(2)
                else:
                    errors += 1
                    if errors <= 10:  # Only print first 10 errors
                        print(f"  Skipping seed {i} ({seed['condition']}): {e}")
                    elif errors == 11:
                        print(f"  ... suppressing further error messages")

        # Progress update every 10 examples
        if (i + 1) % 10 == 0:
            print(f"  Progress: {i + 1}/{len(seeds)} seeds processed, "
                  f"{len(results)} pairs generated, {errors} errors")

    print(f"Generation complete: {len(results)} pairs ({errors} errors)")
    return results


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Evol-Instruct Complexity Evolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

EVOLUTION_PROMPTS = {
    "add_constraints": """Take a medical question and make it more complex by
adding 1-2 patient-specific constraints (e.g., age, comorbidities, allergies,
pregnancy, current medications). Return the evolved question only.

Example:
Original: What are the treatment options for GERD?
Evolved: What are the treatment options for GERD in a 72-year-old who is
already taking clopidogrel after a stent placement?

Example:
Original: How is asthma diagnosed?
Evolved: How is asthma diagnosed in a patient who smokes and whose symptoms
only appear during exercise?

Now evolve this question:
Original: {question}""",

    "deepen_reasoning": """Take a medical question and evolve it to require
deeper clinical reasoning — the answer should need to explain underlying
mechanisms, weigh trade-offs, or consider multiple factors. Return the
evolved question only.

Example:
Original: Should I take a statin for high cholesterol?
Evolved: How do statins reduce cardiovascular risk beyond lowering my LDL
number, and how should I weigh that benefit against the risk of muscle
side effects?

Example:
Original: What is the treatment for insomnia?
Evolved: Why do doctors recommend cognitive behavioral therapy before sleep
medication for chronic insomnia, and what are the trade-offs if I start
with medication instead?

Now evolve this question:
Original: {question}""",

    "increase_specificity": """Take a medical question and make it more specific
— add lab values, specific staging, or particular clinical scenarios that
narrow the question. Return the evolved question only.

Example:
Original: What do my thyroid test results mean?
Evolved: My TSH came back at 6.8 with a normal free T4 — does subclinical
hypothyroidism like this need treatment, or should we just monitor it?

Example:
Original: How serious is my kidney disease?
Evolved: My eGFR has dropped from 55 to 48 over the past year and my urine
albumin is 40 mg/g — what does stage 3a kidney disease with moderate
albuminuria mean for my long-term outlook?

Now evolve this question:
Original: {question}""",
}


def evolve_question(instruction: str, evolution_type: str) -> str:
    """Evolve a question to be more complex (Section 5.4)."""
    prompt = EVOLUTION_PROMPTS[evolution_type].format(question=instruction)
    content = _call_gemini("", prompt, temperature=0.8, max_tokens=400)
    return content.strip()


def generate_answer_for_evolved(instruction: str) -> str:
    """Generate a new answer for an evolved question."""
    content = _call_gemini(
        SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        f"Answer this medical question in 150-300 words. Be accurate "
        f"and practical.\n\nQuestion: {instruction}",
        temperature=0.7,
        max_tokens=1000,
    )
    return content.strip()
