08Chapter 8 · The Training Loop

The Training Loop

Ab tak ke chapters me tumne data banaya, format kiya, aur LoRA samjha. Is chapter me saare pieces ek saath aate hain: actual training run. Notebook Chapter08_FineTuneGemma.ipynb Gemma 4 E4B-IT ko medical Q&A par QLoRA ke saath NF4 me fine-tune karta hai.

Training stack

Hugging Face ka stack hai: Trainer plus TRL ka SFTTrainer, jahan SFTConfig TrainingArguments ko extend karta hai. Formatted text ek text column me hota hai, jise config me dataset_text_field point karta hai. Data collator ke baare me ek welcome simplification: default collator kaam karta hai, aur Gemma 4 ko koi special collator nahi chahiye.

Chapter ka safar

  • Hyperparameters: learning rate, batch size, epochs, optimizer — aur pehle 50–100 steps se unhe diagnose karna.
  • Memory: gradient checkpointing, mixed precision, aur poora memory budget — 12–14 GB total, to lagbhag 16 GB VRAM kaafi hai.
  • Data pipeline aur run: examples format karna, loss samajhna, poora training script, aur 20 epochs ka actual run — lagbhag 45 minutes, 50 cents se kam.
  • Debugging aur tracking: loss curves padhna, tuning workflow, aur reproducibility — TensorBoard vs Weights & Biases, run names, seeds aur pinned versions.

Is chapter ka mindset hai: training ek experiment hai, ek one-shot event nahi. Defaults se shuru karo, pehle steps ko dhyaan se dekho, loss curves ko padho, aur phir ek ek karke adjust karo. Jo run book me dikhaya gaya hai, woh A100 par Colab me bf16 me chala — lekin settings aise chune gaye hain ki chhote GPU par bhi adapt kiye ja sakein.

Yaad rakho: training loop koi black box nahi hai — hyperparameters, memory aur data pipeline, teeno ko ek saath samajhna hota hai. Pehle 50–100 steps hi bata dete hain ki run sahi direction me hai ya nahi.
Chapter08_FineTuneGemma.ipynb — Notebook — code cells only (outputs skipped) — 14 code cells  ·  GitHub ↗ 
!nvidia-smi
!pip install trl bitsandbytes peft
import math


import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    AutoTokenizer,
    BitsAndBytesConfig,
)
from peft import LoraConfig, TaskType
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig

# -----------------------------------------------
# 1. Model and Tokenizer
# -----------------------------------------------

model_name = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"

# 4-bit quantization configuration (QLoRA)
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
tokenizer.padding_side = "right"
tokenizer.model_max_length = 1024 # Reduced model_max_length to conserve memory

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name,
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

# Note: prepare_model_for_kbit_training() is no longer called here.
# SFTTrainer handles quantized-model preparation internally when
# peft_config is provided (PEFT >= 0.12).

# -----------------------------------------------
# 2. LoRA Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------

lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=4, # Reduced LoRA rank
    lora_alpha=4, # Adjusted with r for more conservative updates
    target_modules="all-linear",
    # E4B is multimodal: keep the adapters out of the vision/audio towers
    exclude_modules=r".*(vision|audio).*",
    lora_dropout=0.2,
    bias="none",
    task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 3. Dataset
# -----------------------------------------------

# Load the synthetic GPT-120B medical QA dataset.
# Schema: {"instruction": str, "input": str, "output": str, "metadata": {...}}
raw_dataset = load_dataset(
    "json",
    data_files="medical_qa_synthetic_hf.jsonl",
    split="train",
)

def format_example(example):
    """
    Convert instruction/output pairs into Gemma 4 chat-template format.
    If the optional 'input' field has content it is appended to the instruction
    as additional context.  The result is stored in a 'text' column that
    SFTTrainer will use directly for training.
    """
    user_content = example["instruction"]
    if example.get("input", "").strip():
        user_content = f"{example['instruction']}\n\n{example['input']}"

    messages = [
        {"role": "user",      "content": user_content},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": example["output"]},
    ]
    return {
        "text": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize=False,
            add_generation_prompt=False,
        )
    }

# Apply the chat template and drop the original columns
dataset = raw_dataset.map(
    format_example,
    remove_columns=raw_dataset.column_names,
)

# Create a 90/10 train/validation split (seed fixed for reproducibility)
split = dataset.train_test_split(test_size=0.1, seed=42)
train_dataset = split["train"]
eval_dataset  = split["test"]
eval_dataset.to_json("eval_dataset.jsonl", orient="records", lines=True)
print(f"Wrote Eval Dataset")
print(f"Training examples:   {len(train_dataset)}")
print(f"Validation examples: {len(eval_dataset)}")
print(f"Sample formatted text (first 300 chars):\n{train_dataset[0]['text'][:300]}")

# -----------------------------------------------
# 4. Training Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------

# Compute warmup_steps from dataset size (replaces deprecated warmup_ratio).
# effective_batch = per_device_batch * gradient_accumulation_steps
# total_optimizer_steps = ceil(train_size / effective_batch) * epochs
effective_batch = 8 * 8  # per_device_train_batch_size * gradient_accumulation_steps (Changed to 8)
total_steps = math.ceil(len(train_dataset) / effective_batch) * 5 # Reduced num_train_epochs for calculation
warmup_steps = max(1, int(0.1 * total_steps))
print(f"Total optimizer steps: {total_steps}  |  Warmup steps: {warmup_steps}")

# SFTConfig = TrainingArguments + SFT-specific args (e.g. dataset_text_field).
# In TRL >= 0.9 these args moved from SFTTrainer.__init__() to SFTConfig.
training_args = SFTConfig(
    output_dir="./results/medical-qa-v1",

    # SFT-specific
    dataset_text_field="text",

    # Training duration
    num_train_epochs=20, # Reduced number of epochs further

    # Batch size — A100/H100 has ample VRAM; larger batches improve throughput.
    # Effective train batch = 8 * 8 = 64.
    per_device_train_batch_size=8,
    per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=8,

    # Learning rate
    learning_rate=1e-4, # Changed to 1e-4
    lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
    warmup_steps=warmup_steps,

    # Regularization
    weight_decay=0.05, # Increased weight decay
    max_grad_norm=0.3,

    # Precision — A100/H100 has native BF16 tensor cores
    bf16=True,

    # Logging
    logging_steps=5,
    logging_first_step=True,
    report_to="tensorboard",

    # Evaluation
    eval_strategy="steps",
    eval_steps=5,

    # Checkpointing
    save_strategy="steps",
    save_steps=50,
    save_total_limit=3,
    load_best_model_at_end=True,
    metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",

    # Memory optimization
    gradient_checkpointing=True,
    gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False},
    optim="paged_adamw_8bit",
)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 5. Data Collator
# -----------------------------------------------

# None needed! TRL's default collator pads input_ids and labels
# correctly. (Gemma 3 required a custom collator here to inject
# token_type_ids into every batch -- Gemma 4 does not, so if you are
# adapting this notebook back to Gemma 3, that is the piece to restore.)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 7. Trainer
# -----------------------------------------------

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    args=training_args,
    train_dataset=train_dataset,
    eval_dataset=eval_dataset,
    processing_class=tokenizer,
    peft_config=lora_config
)

# Verify the configuration
trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()
                       if p.requires_grad)
total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
print(f"\nTrainable parameters: {trainable_params:,}")
print(f"Total parameters:     {total_params:,}")
print(f"Trainable %:          {100 * trainable_params / total_params:.4f}%")

# -----------------------------------------------
# 8. Train
# -----------------------------------------------

print("\nStarting training...")
trainer.train()

# -----------------------------------------------
# 9. Save the adapter
# -----------------------------------------------

trainer.save_model("./adapters/medical-qa-v1")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("./adapters/medical-qa-v1")

print("\nTraining complete. Adapter saved to ./adapters/medical-qa-v1")
%load_ext tensorboard
%tensorboard --logdir ./results/medical-qa-v1

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

# Extract log history from the trainer
logs = trainer.state.log_history

# Filter for training and evaluation steps
train_metrics = [log for log in logs if 'loss' in log and 'learning_rate' in log]
eval_metrics = [log for log in logs if 'eval_loss' in log]

# Create DataFrames for easier plotting
train_df = pd.DataFrame(train_metrics)
eval_df = pd.DataFrame(eval_metrics)

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(train_df['step'], train_df['loss'], label='Training Loss', marker='o', linestyle='-')
plt.plot(eval_df['step'], eval_df['eval_loss'], label='Validation Loss', marker='x', linestyle='--')

plt.title('Training and Validation Loss Over Steps')
plt.xlabel('Steps')
plt.ylabel('Loss')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()
%pip install -U torchao
# (stale torchao versions in shared environments break model loading;
# restart the runtime if this upgrades anything)
# Free the training run's GPU memory first (see Chapter 3!) --
# without this, the second copy of the model spills off the GPU and
# generate() fails with "Tensor on device meta" errors.
import gc
import torch

for name in ("trainer", "model"):
    if name in dir():
        del globals()[name]
gc.collect()
torch.cuda.empty_cache()

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
from peft import PeftModel

model_name = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"

# Load the base in 4-bit for inference: ~6GB instead of ~16GB, so
# everything stays on the GPU
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name,
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    device_map="auto",
)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)

# Attach the LoRA adapter. Note: no merge_and_unload() here -- merging
# isn't supported into 4-bit weights, and the adapter runs alongside
# the quantized base with negligible overhead.
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, "./adapters/medical-qa-v1")
model.eval()
# Format a test prompt using the chat template
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What are the common symptoms of hypothyroidism?"},
]

input_text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
)

inputs = tokenizer(input_text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model.generate(
        **inputs,
        max_new_tokens=512,
        temperature=0.7,
        top_p=0.9,
        do_sample=True,
    )

response = tokenizer.decode(
    outputs[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:],
    skip_special_tokens=True,
)
print(response)
# Compare base vs fine-tuned WITHOUT loading a second copy of the model.
# PeftModel can disable its adapter on the fly, so one 4-bit base serves
# as both models -- half the memory, no meta-device spills.
import torch

medical_qa_prompts = [
    "What are the common symptoms of influenza?",
    "Explain the role of insulin in the human body.",
    "What is hypertension and how is it managed?",
    "Describe the benefits of regular exercise for cardiovascular health.",
    "What are the signs of a severe allergic reaction and what should be done?"
]

def generate_response(prompt_text):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt_text}]
    input_text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True,
    )
    inputs = tokenizer(input_text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model.generate(
            **inputs,
            max_new_tokens=256,
            temperature=0.7,
            top_p=0.9,
            do_sample=True,
        )
    return tokenizer.decode(
        outputs[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True,
    )

print("\n--- Comparing Base Model vs. Fine-tuned Model ---\n")

for i, prompt in enumerate(medical_qa_prompts):
    print(f"\n--- Prompt {i+1} ---")
    print(f"Question: {prompt}")

    # Base model: temporarily switch the adapter off
    with model.disable_adapter():
        base_response = generate_response(prompt)
    print("\nBase Model Response:")
    print(base_response)

    # Fine-tuned: adapter active (the default)
    finetuned_response = generate_response(prompt)
    print("\nFine-tuned Model Response:")
    print(finetuned_response)
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
!pip install unsloth
"""
FineTuneGemma_unsloth.py
========================

Unsloth version of the Chapter 8 medical Q&A fine-tuning script.

This file is a drop-in alternative to FineTuneGemma.ipynb that uses the
Unsloth library (https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth) to train a
LoRA / QLoRA adapter on top of google/gemma-4-E4B-it.

Compared to the standard Hugging Face stack used in the notebook, Unsloth:

  * Loads the model through FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained, which
    applies custom Triton kernels for attention and the LoRA forward /
    backward passes.
  * Attaches LoRA adapters via FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model
    (no separate LoraConfig + peft_config= argument to SFTTrainer).
  * Produces roughly 2x faster training and ~60% less peak VRAM on a
    single consumer GPU.

Everything else (data pipeline, chat template, the SFTConfig
hyperparameters, and the trainer call) is intentionally
identical to the notebook so you can compare the two runs directly.

Prerequisites
-------------
    pip install "unsloth[colab-new] @ git+https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth.git"
    pip install --no-deps trl peft accelerate bitsandbytes
    # medical_qa_synthetic_hf.jsonl must be in the working directory.

Run with
--------
    python FineTuneGemma_unsloth.py
"""

# -----------------------------------------------
# IMPORTANT: import unsloth BEFORE transformers / trl
# -----------------------------------------------
# Unsloth patches several classes inside transformers at import time.
# If you import transformers first, the patches are not applied and you
# lose the speed-up (and will get a warning).
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

import math
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig


# -----------------------------------------------
# 1. Model and Tokenizer (Unsloth)
# -----------------------------------------------
# FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained replaces:
#   - AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained
#   - BitsAndBytesConfig
#   - AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained
#
# load_in_4bit=True turns on NF4 quantisation internally with the same
# bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4" / double-quant settings used in the notebook.
# Unsloth also auto-selects bf16 or fp16 compute dtype based on the GPU.
MAX_SEQ_LENGTH = 1024   # matches tokenizer.model_max_length in the notebook

model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it",   # pre-optimised Unsloth mirror
    max_seq_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH,
    dtype=None,                           # None = auto (bf16 on Ampere+, fp16 on T4)
    load_in_4bit=True,
)

# Same padding conventions as the notebook
tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
tokenizer.padding_side = "right"


# -----------------------------------------------
# 2. LoRA Configuration (Unsloth)
# -----------------------------------------------
# FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model replaces the separate LoraConfig +
# peft_config= argument. The hyperparameters mirror the notebook:
#     r=4, lora_alpha=4, target_modules="all-linear", dropout=0.2
#
# Unsloth enables its own gradient-checkpointing variant
# ("unsloth") which is ~30% more memory-efficient than the standard
# HF implementation and is a drop-in replacement.
model = FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(
    model,
    r=4,
    lora_alpha=4,
    target_modules="all-linear",
    lora_dropout=0.2,
    bias="none",
    use_gradient_checkpointing="unsloth",
    random_state=42,
    use_rslora=False,
    loftq_config=None,
)


# -----------------------------------------------
# 3. Dataset (identical to the notebook)
# -----------------------------------------------
raw_dataset = load_dataset(
    "json",
    data_files="medical_qa_synthetic_hf.jsonl",
    split="train",
)


def format_example(example):
    """
    Convert instruction/output pairs into Gemma 4 chat-template format.
    If the optional 'input' field has content, it is appended to the
    instruction as additional context. The result is stored in a 'text'
    column that SFTTrainer will use directly for training.
    """
    user_content = example["instruction"]
    if example.get("input", "").strip():
        user_content = f"{example['instruction']}\n\n{example['input']}"

    messages = [
        {"role": "user",      "content": user_content},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": example["output"]},
    ]
    return {
        "text": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize=False,
            add_generation_prompt=False,
        )
    }


dataset = raw_dataset.map(
    format_example,
    remove_columns=raw_dataset.column_names,
)

# 90/10 train/validation split (fixed seed for reproducibility)
split = dataset.train_test_split(test_size=0.1, seed=42)
train_dataset = split["train"]
eval_dataset = split["test"]

print(f"Training examples:   {len(train_dataset)}")
print(f"Validation examples: {len(eval_dataset)}")
print(f"Sample formatted text (first 300 chars):\n{train_dataset[0]['text'][:300]}")


# -----------------------------------------------
# 4. Training Configuration (identical to the notebook)
# -----------------------------------------------
# effective_batch = per_device_batch * gradient_accumulation_steps
# total_optimizer_steps = ceil(train_size / effective_batch) * epochs
NUM_EPOCHS = 20
PER_DEVICE_BATCH = 8
GRAD_ACCUM = 8

effective_batch = PER_DEVICE_BATCH * GRAD_ACCUM
total_steps = math.ceil(len(train_dataset) / effective_batch) * NUM_EPOCHS
warmup_steps = max(1, int(0.1 * total_steps))
print(f"Total optimizer steps: {total_steps}  |  Warmup steps: {warmup_steps}")

# Detect bf16 support at runtime. Ampere (CC 8.0) and newer GPUs have
# native bf16 tensor cores; Turing (T4, CC 7.5) does not and must use fp16.
bf16_supported = torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported()

training_args = SFTConfig(
    output_dir="./results/medical-qa-v1-unsloth",

    # SFT-specific
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_seq_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH,
    packing=False,

    # Training duration
    num_train_epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,

    # Batch size
    per_device_train_batch_size=PER_DEVICE_BATCH,
    per_device_eval_batch_size=4,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=GRAD_ACCUM,

    # Learning rate
    learning_rate=1e-4,
    lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
    warmup_steps=warmup_steps,

    # Regularization
    weight_decay=0.05,
    max_grad_norm=0.3,

    # Mixed precision — auto-selected based on GPU capability
    bf16=bf16_supported,
    fp16=not bf16_supported,

    # Logging
    logging_steps=5,
    logging_first_step=True,
    report_to="tensorboard",

    # Evaluation
    eval_strategy="steps",
    eval_steps=5,

    # Checkpointing
    save_strategy="steps",
    save_steps=50,
    save_total_limit=3,
    load_best_model_at_end=True,
    metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",

    # Memory / optimizer
    optim="paged_adamw_8bit",
    seed=42,
)


# -----------------------------------------------
# 5. Data Collator
# -----------------------------------------------
# None needed! TRL's default collator pads input_ids and labels
# correctly, and unlike Gemma 3, Gemma 4 does not require a
# token_type_ids injection for text-only training.


# -----------------------------------------------
# 6. Trainer
# -----------------------------------------------
# NOTE: we do NOT pass peft_config=... here. The model is already a
# PEFT model (wrapped by FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model above), so
# SFTTrainer should treat it as a pre-prepared model and train the
# existing adapters.
trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    args=training_args,
    train_dataset=train_dataset,
    eval_dataset=eval_dataset,
    processing_class=tokenizer,
)

# Verify the configuration
trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
print(f"\nTrainable parameters: {trainable_params:,}")
print(f"Total parameters:     {total_params:,}")
print(f"Trainable %:          {100 * trainable_params / total_params:.4f}%")


# -----------------------------------------------
# 7. Train
# -----------------------------------------------
print("\nStarting training with Unsloth...")
trainer.train()


# -----------------------------------------------
# 8. Save the adapter
# -----------------------------------------------
# trainer.save_model saves the LoRA adapter in the standard PEFT format,
# which means you can later load it without Unsloth installed, using:
#
#     from peft import PeftModel
#     base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-E4B-it", ...)
#     model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, "./adapters/medical-qa-v1-unsloth")
#
# This is the compatibility check recommended at the end of Section 8.11.
OUTPUT_DIR = "./adapters/medical-qa-v1-unsloth"
trainer.save_model(OUTPUT_DIR)
tokenizer.save_pretrained(OUTPUT_DIR)

print(f"\nTraining complete. Adapter saved to {OUTPUT_DIR}")
eval_dataset.to_json("eval_dataset.jsonl", orient="records", lines=True)

08.1Chapter 8 · The Training Loop

Learning Rate, Batch Size, Epochs, and the Optimizer

Hyperparameters training ki steering wheel hain. Inhe sahi set karna aur galat hone par pehchan paana — yehi skill ek successful fine-tune aur ek barbaad run ke beech ka farak hai.

Learning rate — sabse important dial

LoRA fine-tuning ke liye common starting range hai 1e-4 se 2e-4 — full fine-tuning ke 1e-5 se 5e-5 se zyada. Book ke run me 1e-4 use hua. Ise poora run khatam hone ke baad nahi, pehle 50–100 steps se diagnose karo. Learning rate bahut zyada ho to loss diverge karega (achanak infinity ki taraf spike); bahut kam ho to loss barely move karega. Warmup lagbhag 10% rakho — learning rate dheere-dheere badhta hai — aur cosine schedule linear schedule se behtar perform karta hai, kyunki woh training ke end me learning rate ko smoothly kam karta hai.

Batch size — gradient accumulation se bada batch

Effective batch size badi rakhna stability deta hai, lekin GPU memory chhota batch force karti hai. Solution hai gradient accumulation: chhote batches par gradients compute karo aur kai steps tak accumulate karke ek saath weights update karo. Book me per-device batch 8 aur accumulation 8 steps ka combination effective batch 64 deta hai — bade batch ka fayda, chhote hardware ki memory cost par. Yaad rakho: accumulation se memory nahi badhti, sirf update frequency kam hoti hai.

Epochs — dataset size ke hisaab se

  • 1–2 epochs: bade datasets ke liye.
  • 3–5 epochs: medium datasets ke liye.
  • 10–20 epochs: chhote datasets (lagbhag 600 se kam examples) ke liye — hamara medical dataset sirf 549 training examples ka hai, isliye book ka run 20 epochs ka hai.

Chhote dataset par zyada epochs ka matlab hai memorization ka risk, isliye regularization (zyada dropout, weight decay) saath me zaroori hai.

Supporting cast

  • Weight decay 0.05: book ke example me badhaya gaya value — stronger regularization, jo chhote dataset par overfitting se ladta hai. Ye gradients se decoupled hota hai, isliye learning rate se alag tareeke se kaam karta hai.
  • Max gradient norm 0.3: gradient clipping — agar gradients ka combined norm 0.3 se zyada ho, to sabhi gradients ko scale karke norm 0.3 par le aaya jaata hai. Update ki direction preserve rehti hai, sirf magnitude cap hoti hai. Ye exploding gradients se bachata hai. Agar grad norm baar-baar 0.3 se takra raha hai, to ye signal hai ki kuch aur galat hai — shayad learning rate zyada hai.
  • Optimizer — paged_adamw_8bit: AdamW ka 8-bit version, jisme optimizer states 8-bit me store hote hain. Book ke example me optimizer memory 80 MB se 20 MB tak shrink ho jaati hai. Paged hone se memory spikes CPU par offload ho jaate hain, jo out-of-memory errors se bachata hai.

Learning curves bhi ek guide hain: healthy, overfitting, underfitting, diverging aur oscillating shapes alag-alag problems batate hain — inhe detail me agle sections me dekhenge.

Yaad rakho: LoRA ke liye learning rate 1e-4 se 2e-4 se shuru karo, warmup 10% aur cosine schedule ke saath. Learning rate ko pehle 50–100 steps me diagnose karo — poora run barbaad karne ke baad nahi.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — The Training Loop
← Previous08 · The Training Loop→ Next08.2 · Gradient Checkpointing, Mixed Precision, and the Memory Budget
08.2Chapter 8 · The Training Loop

Gradient Checkpointing, Mixed Precision, and the Memory Budget

Training me memory hi asli bottleneck hai — model ke weights to sirf shuruaat hain. Optimizer states, gradients aur activations mil kar memory ko kai guna badha dete hain. Is section me do techniques hain jo memory ko control me laati hain, aur phir poora budget hisaab ke saath.

Gradient checkpointing — speed ke badle memory

Normal training me forward pass ke dauraan har layer ki activations save ki jaati hain, taaki backward pass me gradients compute ho sakein. Gradient checkpointing sirf kuch checkpoints save karta hai aur baaki activations ko backward pass ke dauraan dobara compute karta hai. Ye lagbhag 30% speed ke badle activation memory me 60–70% ki katauti karta hai — ek bahut achha trade, jab memory hi limit ho. Config me gradient_checkpointing=True ke saath gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False} use karo — reentrant checkpointing purane PyTorch versions me common failure mode tha, aur non-reentrant reliably kaam karta hai.

Mixed precision — bf16 vs fp16

bf16=True se bfloat16 mixed-precision training enable hoti hai: forward aur backward passes bf16 me hote hain, jabki master weights zyada precision me rehte hain. Ampere aur uske baad ke GPUs (jaise A100) par bf16 behtar choice hai, kyunki uski range fp16 se badi hoti hai aur gradient scaler ki zaroorat nahi padti. Purane hardware par fp16 plus ek gradient scaler use hota hai. Ek caution: torch.compile ko free win mat samjho — book use caution ke saath flag karta hai, kyunki woh har setup me fayda nahi deta aur debug karna mushkil kar sakta hai.

Poora memory budget — 12–14 GB

Book ke run ka hisaab aisa hai:

  • Quantized linear layers: 2.8 GB
  • Embeddings (quantize nahi hote): 7 GB
  • LoRA adapter: 19 MB
  • Optimizer states: 19 MB
  • Gradients: 19 MB
  • Activations: 1–3 GB (gradient checkpointing ke saath)
  • Overhead: 1 GB

Total: 12–14 GB, to lagbhag 16 GB VRAM kaafi hai. Dhyaan do: embeddings 7 GB lete hain kyunki woh quantize nahi hote — yehi wajah hai ki QLoRA ki saving clean 4× nahi hoti. Aur LoRA, optimizer aur gradients — teeno sirf 19 MB ke aas-paas hain, kyunki trainable parameters bahut kam hain. Yehi PEFT ki taakat hai: memory ka bada hissa base model ka hai, training ka hissa chhota sa.

Yaad rakho: gradient checkpointing ~30% speed ke badle 60–70% activation memory bachata hai, aur bf16 Ampere+ GPUs par sahi choice hai. Poora run 12–14 GB me fit hota hai — 16 GB VRAM kaafi hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — The Training Loop
← Previous08.1 · Learning Rate, Batch Size, Epochs, and the Optimizer→ Next08.3 · The Data Pipeline, the Run, and Debugging It
08.3Chapter 8 · The Training Loop

The Data Pipeline, the Run, and Debugging It

Ab actual run ki baari hai: data pipeline se lekar poora training script, 20 epochs ka run, loss curves padhna, aur jab kuch galat ho to use debug karna.

Data pipeline

format_example har example ko Gemma ke <|turn> markers ke saath text column me banata hai. Median example 435 tokens ka hai, to 1,024-token sequence me lagbhag do examples fit ho sakte hain. Isse packing kehte hain — multiple examples ko ek sequence me pack karna, jisse throughput lagbhag double ho jaati hai, kyunki aadhi batch padding hoti hai. Book ne is run me packing off rakha, kyunki sirf 549 examples aur aadhe ghante ki training me fayda kam tha aur ek kam setting matlab ek kam cheez debug karni. Lekin dataset bada ho ya budget tight ho, to packing ek one-line change hai jiska real payoff hai — bas enable karne ke baad loss curve dobara check karo.

Loss — aur masking na karne ka faisla

Loss hai cross-entropy, next-token prediction par, Gemma 4 ki 262,144-token vocabulary ke upar. Har position par model poori vocabulary par ek probability distribution predict karta hai, aur sahi next token se compare hota hai. Label masking (-100) available hai — lekin book ke run me author ne masking na karne ka faisla kiya, aur loss saare tokens par compute hone diya. Wajah: conversations aam taur par long-running hoti hain — ek jawab ke baad ek aur sawaal aata hai — to sawaal ke patterns predict karna seekhna bhi useful ho sakta hai. Lekin dusre tasks me, jahan user input assistant ke response se bahut lamba ho (jaise document summarization), masking bahut important hai — nahi to chhote response ka loss signal lambe input ke loss me doob jaata hai.

Poora training script

  • Split: 90 / 10 — 549 training aur 62 validation examples. Validation har 5 steps par evaluate hoti hai, taaki loss curves achhi frequency se plot ho sakein.
  • Padding: tokenizer.pad_token ko end-of-sequence token par set karna standard fix hai — kuch models me pad token defined hi nahi hota aur batching shuru hote hi fail ho jaati hai. padding_side="right" rakho, kyunki model left-to-right generate karta hai aur left padding token positions ko shift kar dega.
  • Max length: 1,024 tokens — medical Q&A data aam taur par isse bahut neeche hai, to kuch khota nahi aur VRAM bachta hai.
  • LoRA settings: rank 4, alpha 4, dropout 0.2 — bahut conservative. Chhote dataset par chhota adapter plus strong regularization overfitting se bachata hai. Sirf lagbhag 0.17% parameters train hote hain.
  • Checkpoints: save_total_limit=3 — sirf 3 recent checkpoints save hote hain, purane auto-delete. Aur load_best_model_at_end=True — training khatam hone par lowest validation loss wala model load hota hai, kyunki final checkpoint overfit kar chuka ho sakta hai. Ye simple early stopping hai.

Run — 20 epochs, 45 minutes, 50 cents se kam

Colab par A100 me bf16 ke saath 20 epochs lagbhag 45 minutes me chale — lagbhag 4 compute units, 50 cents se kam ki cost. Training loss pehle 50 steps me tezi se gira, phir dheere decline hua; validation loss bhi usi trajectory par chali aur lagbhag 0.88 par level ho gayi. Step 75 ke aas-paas training aur validation loss ke beech gap khulne laga — model training data ko memorize karne laga tha, generalizable patterns seekhne ke bajaye. Chhote dataset par ye expected hai, aur hyperparameters ne use manageable rakha.

Loss curves padhna aur tuning workflow

  • Healthy: dono losses girti hain aur plateau karti hain, ek dusre ko closely track karti hain. Ideal outcome.
  • Overfitting: training loss girti rehti hai, validation loss badhne lagti hai, gap widen hota hai. Remedies: epochs kam karo, dropout badhao, LoRA rank kam karo, data badhao.
  • Underfitting: dono losses bahut high aur barely gir rahi hain. Learning rate bahut kam, rank bahut kam, ya data me formatting/template ki problem ho sakti hai.
  • Diverging: loss achanak infinity ki taraf spike — learning rate bahut zyada hai, kam karo.
  • Oscillating: loss upar-neeche ho rahi hai — learning rate ya batch size adjust karo.

Tuning workflow: sensible defaults se shuru karo, phir learning rate ko half ya double karo, phir epochs adjust karo, phir rank. Aur "good enough" principle yaad rakho — kab rukna hai, ye jaanna bhi ek skill hai. Tracking ke liye TensorBoard vs Weights & Biases dono dikhaye gaye hain; descriptive run names, ek custom MemoryCallback, seed 42 aur data seed, aur pinned library versions reproducibility ke liye zaroori hain. Lekin honest note ye hai: hardware variance ki wajah se exact reproduction guarantee nahi hoti.

Yaad rakho: loss curves tumse baat karti hain — healthy, overfitting, underfitting, diverging, oscillating. Pehle learning rate ko half/double karo, phir epochs, phir rank. Aur best model wahi hai jiska validation loss sabse kam ho, final checkpoint nahi.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — The Training Loop

09Chapter 9 · Using the Adapter

Using the Adapter

Training khatam ho gayi, checkpoints save ho gaye — lekin ab tumhare paas asal me kya hai? Colab me ek folder, jisme kuch strange-looking files hain. Is chapter me tum seekhoge ki adapter asal me kya hota hai, use kaise load karein, aur use honestly evaluate kaise karein — taaki ek achha adapter kharab na lage.

Adapter ki anatomy — sirf 71 MB

Poora adapter lagbhag 71 MB ka hota hai — base model ke 16 GB ke muqable me kuch bhi nahi. Uske andar:

  • adapter_model.safetensors (~39 MB): adapter ke weights — lagbhag 9.7M parameters, base ke sirf 0.17%. Safetensors format isliye chuna gaya kyunki ye load karne me safe hai — pickle-based .bin files ke ulta, jo arbitrary code execute kar sakti hain.
  • adapter_config.json: adapter ki pehchan — rank 4, alpha 4, dropout 0.2, PEFT version, inference mode. Ye file batati hai adapter kis base model ke liye bana tha.
  • Tokenizer files (~32 MB): tokenizer aur vocab — adapter ka aadha size asal me tokenizer hai, weights nahi.
  • chat_template.jinja: model ka chat template, taaki inference time par wahi formatting use ho.
  • training_args.bin: run ka logbook — training ke arguments aur settings, jo baad me reproduce karne me madad karte hain.

Chapter ka safar

  • Loading aur sharing: Colab ephemeral hai — adapter ko ZIP karke download karo, Drive par mount karo, ya Hugging Face Hub par push karo taaki woh session ke baad bhi survive kare.
  • Merging vs hot-swapping: merge karne se zero inference overhead milta hai, lekin swap karne ki flexibility kho jaati hai.
  • Honest evaluation: side-by-side comparison, perplexity, LLM-as-a-judge aur domain benchmarks — sabse sasta method pehle.
  • Pitfalls: galat base model, dtype mismatch, missing chat template, aur merged ya multiple adapters ki uljhane.

Is chapter ke end tak tum "mere paas kuch weights hain" se "mere paas ek deployable, evaluated, trustworthy fine-tuned model ki shuruaat hai" tak pahunch jaoge.

Yaad rakho: adapter sirf 71 MB ka hai — 39 MB weights, 32 MB tokenizer. Chhota size hi LoRA ki taakat hai: share karna, load karna aur swap karna, sab aasan.

import math
import gc
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from peft import PeftModel

model_name = "google/gemma-4-E4b-it"
adapter_path = "./adapters/medical-qa-v1"
# Or the Hub version:
# adapter_path = "[Name]/medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(adapter_path)
test_dataset = load_dataset(
    "json", data_files="test_set.jsonl", split="train"
)


def compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, dataset, max_length=1024):
    model.eval()
    total_loss = 0.0
    total_tokens = 0

    for example in dataset:
        messages = [
            {"role": "user", "content": example["question"]},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": example["answer"]},
        ]
        text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False,
        )
        inputs = tokenizer(
            text, return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True, max_length=max_length,
        ).to(model.device)
        labels = inputs["input_ids"].clone()

        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = model(**inputs, labels=labels)

        total_loss += outputs.loss.item() * inputs["input_ids"].numel()
        total_tokens += inputs["input_ids"].numel()

    return math.exp(total_loss / total_tokens)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto",
)
base_ppl = compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, test_dataset)
print(f"Base model perplexity: {base_ppl:.3f}")
del model
gc.collect()
torch.cuda.empty_cache()
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto",
)
adapter_path = "./adapters/medical-qa-v1"
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, adapter_path)
ft_ppl = compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, test_dataset)
print(f"Fine-tuned model perplexity: {ft_ppl:.3f}")
improvement = (base_ppl - ft_ppl) / base_ppl * 100
print(f"\nBase model perplexity:       {base_ppl:.3f}")
print(f"Fine-tuned model perplexity: {ft_ppl:.3f}")
print(f"Relative improvement:        {improvement:.1f}%")

"""
build_test_set.py
-----------------
Build a trustworthy held-out test set for the medical Q&A fine-tune.

Pipeline:
  1. Pull 100 random examples from MedQA (USMLE-style, human-written).
  2. Reshape them into the {"question": ..., "answer": ...} schema the
     fine-tune was trained on.
  3. Run an overlap check against the training set - both exact and fuzzy.
  4. Drop any leaked examples.
  5. Save to disk with a SHA-256 fingerprint so future loads are verifiable.

Usage:
  pip install datasets transformers --break-system-packages
  python build_test_set.py

Outputs:
  ./test_set_medqa_v1_<date>.jsonl                (one JSON object per line)
  ./test_set_medqa_v1_<date>.jsonl.manifest.json  (provenance + sha256)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import random
import re
from datetime import date
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path

from datasets import Dataset, load_dataset, load_from_disk  # noqa: F401

# --- Configuration -----------------------------------------------------------

RANDOM_SEED = 42
N_SAMPLES = 100
SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.80  # anything above this is treated as a near-duplicate

# Where your training set lives. Adjust to match your setup.
# Accepts:
#   - a local .jsonl / .json file   (e.g. "./medical_qa_synthetic_hf.jsonl")
#   - a local path saved via save_to_disk()
#   - a Hugging Face Hub dataset id (e.g. "[Name]/medical-qa-v1")
TRAIN_SOURCE = "./medical_qa_synthetic_hf.jsonl"
TRAIN_SPLIT = "train"                            # only used for Hub datasets

# Where we'll write the final test set (single JSONL file).
OUT_FILE = Path(f"./test_set_medqa_v1_{date.today().isoformat()}.jsonl")

# --- Step 1: Pull MedQA ------------------------------------------------------

def load_medqa_sample(n: int, seed: int) -> Dataset:
    """Grab `n` random USMLE-style questions from MedQA.

    We use GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options, a parquet-native mirror of the
    original MedQA USMLE set. Same questions, no loading script.
    """
    print("Loading MedQA (GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options, test split)...")
    ds = load_dataset("GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options", split="test")
    print(f"  full test split: {len(ds)} examples")
    ds = ds.shuffle(seed=seed).select(range(n))
    print(f"  sampled: {len(ds)} examples")
    return ds


def medqa_to_qa(example: dict) -> dict:
    """
    GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options example shape:
        {
          "question":   "<stem>",
          "answer":     "<correct option text>",
          "options":    {"A": "...", "B": "...", "C": "...", "D": "..."},
          "answer_idx": "A",
          "meta_info":  "step1" | "step2&3",
        }

    Some revisions of the dataset pack options as a list of {key, value}
    dicts instead of a plain dict - we handle both.

    We flatten to the {"question", "answer"} schema the model was trained
    on. We keep the option list inside the question so the task is
    well-specified, and the answer is the correct letter plus its
    expanded text.
    """
    opts = example["options"]
    if isinstance(opts, dict):
        items = sorted(opts.items())
    else:  # list of {"key": "...", "value": "..."}
        items = [(o["key"], o["value"]) for o in opts]

    options_block = "\n".join(f"{k}. {v}" for k, v in items)
    question = f"{example['question'].strip()}\n\nOptions:\n{options_block}"
    answer = f"{example['answer_idx']}. {example['answer'].strip()}"
    return {"question": question, "answer": answer}


# --- Step 2: Load training set for overlap check -----------------------------

def load_training_questions(source: str, split: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return a normalized list of training-set question strings.

    Supports:
      - local .jsonl / .json files (one example per line or a JSON array)
      - local HF datasets saved via save_to_disk()
      - Hugging Face Hub dataset ids
    """
    print(f"Loading training set from {source!r}...")
    src_path = Path(source)

    try:
        if src_path.is_file() and src_path.suffix.lower() in {".jsonl", ".json"}:
            ds = load_dataset("json", data_files=str(src_path), split="train")
        elif src_path.exists():
            ds = load_from_disk(source)
            if hasattr(ds, "keys") and split in ds:
                ds = ds[split]
        else:
            ds = load_dataset(source, split=split)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  WARNING: could not load training set ({e}).")
        print("  Overlap check will be skipped. You should fix this.")
        return []

    # Find the question field - tolerate a few common names.
    candidate_fields = ["question", "prompt", "input", "instruction", "query"]
    field = next((f for f in candidate_fields if f in ds.column_names), None)

    # Some synthetic datasets store everything in a "messages" list or a
    # single "text" field. Handle those too.
    if field is None and "messages" in ds.column_names:
        qs = []
        for msgs in ds["messages"]:
            user_turns = [m["content"] for m in msgs if m.get("role") == "user"]
            if user_turns:
                qs.append(user_turns[0].strip().lower())
        print(f"  training questions (from messages): {len(qs)}")
        return qs

    if field is None:
        print(f"  WARNING: no question-like column in {ds.column_names}.")
        return []

    qs = [str(q).strip().lower() for q in ds[field]]
    print(f"  training questions: {len(qs)}")
    return qs


# --- Step 3: Overlap detection -----------------------------------------------

_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[a-z]{4,}\b")

def _shingles(text: str, k: int = 4) -> set[tuple]:
    """k-word shingles for cheap near-duplicate prefilter."""
    words = _TOKEN_RE.findall(text.lower())
    return {tuple(words[i:i + k]) for i in range(len(words) - k + 1)}


def find_overlaps(
    test_qs: list[str],
    train_qs: list[str],
    threshold: float,
) -> tuple[set[int], set[int]]:
    """
    Return (exact_idx, near_idx) - indices into test_qs that should be dropped.

    We use a shingle-based prefilter so we don't run SequenceMatcher
    over N*M pairs. Any test question sharing >=1 4-word shingle with
    any training question gets a full ratio check.
    """
    if not train_qs:
        return set(), set()

    train_set = set(train_qs)
    train_shingles_by_idx = [_shingles(q) for q in train_qs]
    # invert: shingle -> list of train indices that contain it
    shingle_index: dict[tuple, list[int]] = {}
    for i, sh in enumerate(train_shingles_by_idx):
        for s in sh:
            shingle_index.setdefault(s, []).append(i)

    exact: set[int] = set()
    near: set[int] = set()

    for ti, tq in enumerate(test_qs):
        if tq in train_set:
            exact.add(ti)
            continue

        # Candidates = any train question sharing a 4-gram
        candidate_idxs: set[int] = set()
        for s in _shingles(tq):
            candidate_idxs.update(shingle_index.get(s, []))

        for ci in candidate_idxs:
            ratio = SequenceMatcher(None, tq, train_qs[ci]).ratio()
            if ratio >= threshold:
                near.add(ti)
                break

    return exact, near


# --- Step 4 & 5: Save with fingerprint ---------------------------------------

def save_test_set(ds: Dataset, out_file: Path, manifest: dict) -> None:
    """Write the test set as a JSONL file plus a sidecar manifest."""
    out_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    rows = [{"question": ex["question"], "answer": ex["answer"]} for ex in ds]

    # One JSON object per line.
    with out_file.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    # Fingerprint the exact text we'll evaluate on.
    payload = json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

    manifest["fingerprint_sha256"] = fingerprint
    manifest_path = out_file.with_suffix(out_file.suffix + ".manifest.json")
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))

    print(f"\nSaved test set to: {out_file}")
    print(f"  manifest:    {manifest_path}")
    print(f"  fingerprint: {fingerprint[:16]}...")
    print(f"  examples:    {len(rows)}")


# --- Main --------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)

    # 1. Pull MedQA
    raw = load_medqa_sample(N_SAMPLES, RANDOM_SEED)

    # 2. Reshape to our Q&A schema
    test = raw.map(medqa_to_qa, remove_columns=raw.column_names)

    # 3. Overlap check against training set
    train_qs = load_training_questions(TRAIN_SOURCE, TRAIN_SPLIT)
    test_qs_norm = [ex["question"].strip().lower() for ex in test]

    print(f"\nChecking for leakage against {len(train_qs)} training questions...")
    exact, near = find_overlaps(test_qs_norm, train_qs, SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD)
    print(f"  exact duplicates:      {len(exact)}")
    print(f"  near-duplicates (>{int(SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD * 100)}%): {len(near)}")

    # 4. Drop any leaked examples
    to_drop = exact | near
    if to_drop:
        keep_idx = [i for i in range(len(test)) if i not in to_drop]
        print(f"  dropping {len(to_drop)} leaked example(s); {len(keep_idx)} remain")
        test = test.select(keep_idx)
    else:
        print("  no leakage detected")

    # 5. Save with fingerprint + manifest
    manifest = {
        "created": date.today().isoformat(),
        "source": "bigbio/med_qa (en_source, test split)",
        "n_sampled": N_SAMPLES,
        "n_after_leakage_filter": len(test),
        "exact_overlap_dropped": len(exact),
        "near_overlap_dropped": len(near),
        "similarity_threshold": SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD,
        "train_source": TRAIN_SOURCE,
        "seed": RANDOM_SEED,
    }
    save_test_set(test, OUT_FILE, manifest)

    # Peek at one example so you can see what you're evaluating on.
    print("\nSample example:")
    print("-" * 60)
    print("Q:", test[0]["question"][:300], "...")
    print("A:", test[0]["answer"])
    print("-" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

← Previous08.3 · The Data Pipeline, the Run, and Debugging It→ Next09.1 · Loading, Sharing, and Running the Adapter
09.1Chapter 9 · Using the Adapter

Loading, Sharing, and Running the Adapter

Adapter train ho gaya — ab use bachana, load karna aur chalana hai. Colab ka session khatam hote hi sab kuch gayab ho jaata hai, isliye pehla kaam hai adapter ko safe jagah pahunchana.

Adapter ko bachana — Colab ephemeral hai

Teen tareeke hain: adapter ko ZIP karke download karo, Google Drive mount karke wahan save karo, ya Hugging Face Hub par push karo — private ya public. Hub par push karna sabse durable hai: adapter ek repo ban jaata hai jise kahin se bhi load kiya ja sakta hai. Book ka Hub repo hai author/medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora.

Three-step load

Adapter load karna teen steps ka hai: pehle base model load karo, phir tokenizer, phir PeftModel.from_pretrained se adapter ko base par attach karo. Hub se load karte waqt HF_TOKEN secret ke roop me use karo — token ko code me kabhi hardcode mat karo. PeftModel adapter ko pull karke base model me jod deta hai, aur phir model adapter ke saath inference ke liye taiyaar hai.

Merging vs hot-swapping

  • merge_and_unload: adapter ko base weights me fold kar deta hai — zero inference overhead, kyunki ab koi extra branch nahi hai. Lekin iske baad wapas nahi ja sakte: merged adapter ko unmerge nahi kiya ja sakta.
  • Adapter ko alag rakhna: flexibility milti hai — ek hi base model par alag-alag adapters ko inference time par swap kar sakte ho, request ke hisaab se. Multi-task serving ka yehi pattern hai.

Inference test — farak dikhta hai

Ek hypothyroidism wale sawaal par farak saaf dikhta hai: base model ek verbose markdown jawab deta hai, jabki fine-tuned model ek curt list deta hai — wahi style jo training data ne sikhayi thi. Side-by-side comparison karna — wahi prompt base aur adapted dono models se chalana — farak dekhne ka sabse seedha tareeka hai.

Colab gotcha aur sampling

Ek aam Colab gotcha hai adapter ka silently fail hona — adapter load to ho jaata hai, lekin apply nahi hota, aur model base jaisa hi behave karta hai. Fix hai: model ko delete karo, garbage collection chalao, aur dobara reload karo. Aur do_sample sampling flag par dhyaan do — deterministic comparison ke liye temperature 0 use karo, taaki har run me wahi output aaye aur farak saaf dikhe.

Yaad rakho: load karte waqt teen steps — base, tokenizer, phir PeftModel.from_pretrained. Merge karna permanent hai; swap karna hai to adapter ko alag rakho. Aur token ko kabhi code me hardcode mat karo.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Using the Adapter
← Previous09 · Using the Adapter→ Next09.2 · Evaluating Honestly, and the Pitfalls
09.2Chapter 9 · Using the Adapter

Evaluating Honestly, and the Pitfalls

Model train ho gaya aur jawab bhi de raha hai — lekin kya woh asal me behtar hai? Evaluation ka kaam hai is sawaal ka honest jawab dena, na ki woh jawab jo tum sunna chahte ho. Book chaar methods deta hai, sabse saste se shuru karke.

Method 1 — Side-by-side comparison

Sabse sasta aur sabse direct: 100+ prompts par base aur fine-tuned model ko side by side chalao, deterministic temperature 0 par, poore answers check karo, aur safety refusals par nazar rakho. Ye tumhe batata hai ki style aur content me farak dikhta bhi hai ya nahi.

Method 2 — Perplexity

Perplexity batata hai model held-out data ko kitni confidence se predict karta hai: perplexity = exp(eval_loss). Book ke numbers: 100 MedQA records par base model ki perplexity 27.412 se gir kar adapted model par 8.446 ho gayi — lagbhag 69% behtar. Validation set ki perplexity 2.76 thi (eval loss 1.016 ka exp), to 8.446 usse lagbhag 3× hai — MedQA data training data se alag hai, isliye ye expected hai. Rule of thumb: perplexity 1–2 ka matlab leakage (test data training me aa gaya), 2–4 healthy, aur 6 se upar overfitting ka signal ho sakta hai. Lekin perplexity ki limits bhi samjho: ye batata hai model kitna confident hai, ye nahi ki jawab behtar hai — do models ki perplexity ek jaisi ho sakti hai aur outputs bilkul alag. Ye tokenization ke prati bhi sensitive hai. Sample generation ke liye book ek notebook deta hai jo MedQA se test_set.jsonl banata hai.

Method 3 — LLM-as-a-judge

Ek frontier model ko judge banao: held-out questions ko base aur fine-tuned dono se chalao, phir dono answers ko ek golden reference answer ke saath judge ko do aur poochho kaunsa behtar hai. Golden answer human experts se, established datasets se, ya human review ke saath stronger model se banta hai — is order me quality hoti hai. Book ke experiment me fine-tuned model ki win rate lagbhag 73% thi, judge model ke roop me ek chhota frontier model use karke. Best practices: A/B position ko randomize karo (positional bias se bachne ke liye), judge ko base se stronger rakho (4B base ko 4B judge se judge karne se kuch seekhne ko nahi milega), reference answers wala dataset use karo, test ko multiple baar chalao taaki spikes smooth ho jaayein, aur ideally aisa held-out data use karo jo internet par kabhi nahi aaya — taaki judge ne use training me na dekha ho. Dhyaan do: judge models bhi biased hote hain — woh verbosity aur kuch reasoning styles ko systematically prefer karte hain.

Method 4 — Domain benchmarks

Real world me domain-specific benchmarks chahiye hote hain: recall lists (expert dwara banayi gayi known symptom lists se string match karke recall nikalo), open-ended judged answers, safety prompts (jahan sabse achha jawab kabhi-kabhi jawab na dena hota hai — jaise "main doctor nahi hoon, please real doctor se consult karo"), aur general-knowledge checks jo catastrophic forgetting pakadte hain — fine-tuning ne model ki general abilities to kharab nahi kar di.

Common pitfalls

  • Ghalat base model: adapter ko -it variant par train kiya aur -pt variant par load kar diya — PEFT shayad complain bhi na kare, kyunki shapes match karte hain, lekin adapter nonsense produce karega. Hamesha check karo ki adapter_config.json ka base model load kiye hue base se match karta hai.
  • Dtype mismatch: fp16 aur bf16 ke beech farak kuch GPUs par outputs ka matlab hi badal sakta hai. Poori pipeline me ek hi numeric system use karo.
  • Chat template apply kiye bina generate karna: template ke bina outputs dramatically alag hote hain. Hamesha template ke saath format karo aur raw output print karke turn markers confirm karo.
  • Merged ya multiple adapters: merged adapter ko unmerge nahi kar sakte. Multiple adapters ko hot-swap karna powerful hai, lekin galti aasan hai — jab tak confident na ho, ek baar me ek adapter use karo.

QLoRA at inference — deployment configuration me evaluate karo

Training QLoRA se hui thi: 4-bit NF4 base plus full-precision adapter. Inference par bhi wahi combination kaam karta hai — Gemma 4 E4B lagbhag 16 GB se 6–8 GB par aa jaata hai. Lekin do baatein yaad rakho: pehli, merge_and_unload off the table hai — full-precision deltas ko 4-bit weights me fold nahi kar sakte, adapter alag module ke roop me attached rehta hai. Dusri aur zyada important: us configuration me evaluate karo jisme deploy kar rahe ho. Agar tumne perplexity aur judge tests bf16 base par measure kiye aur 4-bit base par ship kar rahe ho, to tumne ek aisa model validate kiya hai jo tum serve hi nahi kar rahe. Farak aam taur par minor hota hai, lekin medical application me "usually" kaafi nahi hai — deployment configuration me canary prompts aur kam se kam perplexity check dobara chalao.

Yaad rakho: perplexity confidence batata hai, quality nahi — isliye side-by-side, perplexity, LLM-as-a-judge aur domain benchmarks, chaaron ko mila kar dekho. Aur evaluation hamesha deployment configuration me karo, kisi aur me nahi.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Using the Adapter

10Chapter 10 · Alignment and Preference Optimization

Alignment and Preference Optimization

SFT ne model ko sikhaya kya kehna hai. Lekin kaise kehna hai — woh abhi baaki hai. Ek parent ka example lo: uska chhota bachha do din se 103°F bukhaar me hai, aur woh poochhta hai kya karein. SFT model use ek differential diagnosis de deta hai — medically sahi, lekin parent ko us waqt ye chahiye: saaf guidance ki kab emergency care chahiye. Information sahi hai, delivery galat hai. Is gap ko bharne ka naam hai alignment.

RLHF — teen stages, bahut complexity

Classic alignment recipe hai RLHF, teen stages me: pehle SFT, phir ek reward model train karo jo achhe jawab ko score de, phir PPO optimisation se model ko reward maximize karne ke liye train karo. Yehi recipe thi jisne ek base model ko conversational assistant me badla. Lekin iski keemat hai: teen models aur do datasets chahiye, PPO finicky hai (tune karna mushkil), aur isme reward hacking ka risk hai — model reward ko maximize karne ke shortcuts dhoondh leta hai, jaise excessively verbose ya sycophantic (khush karne wale) jawab dena, bina asal me behtar hue.

Chapter ka jawab — DPO

Is chapter ka jawab hai DPO (Direct Preference Optimization): alignment ka fayda, reward model ke bina. DPO reward model ko poori tarah skip karke chosen vs rejected answer pairs par seedhe optimise karta hai. Agle sections me dekhenge: preference dataset kaise banayein, DPO loss kaise kaam karta hai, training kaise chalate hain, aur DPO kab use karna hai — aur kab bilkul nahi.

Yaad rakho: SFT sikhata hai kya kehna hai, alignment sikhata hai kaise kehna hai. Sahi information galat tareeke se di jaaye, to woh bhi kaam ki nahi.

"""
Chapter 10: DPO Training & Evaluation
======================================
Runs Direct Preference Optimization on the SFT-tuned Gemma 3 4B model
using the preference pairs generated by chapter10_preference_dataset.py.

Covers these sections 1 of the book:
  - Load and split the preference dataset
  - Load the SFT model, merge adapter, configure a fresh DPO LoRA
  - Configure and launch DPOTrainer
  - Training metrics to watch (logged to TensorBoard)
  - Evaluate: side-by-side comparison of base / SFT / SFT+DPO

Requirements:
    pip install torch transformers peft trl datasets accelerate bitsandbytes \
                tensorboard

Usage:
    # Default settings (trains 3 epochs, β=0.1):
    python chapter10_dpo_training.py

    # Override key hyperparameters:
    python chapter10_dpo_training.py --beta 0.05 --epochs 5 --lr 3e-5

    # Skip training and just run evaluation on an existing adapter:
    python chapter10_dpo_training.py --eval-only

    # Launch TensorBoard to inspect training curves:
    tensorboard --logdir ./results/medical-qa-dpo-v1
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, TaskType
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from trl import DPOConfig, DPOTrainer


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths — adjust these to match your local layout
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

MODEL_NAME = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"
# Local path (if you saved the adapter locally):
SFT_ADAPTER = "./adapters/adapters/medical-qa-v1"
# Hub version:
# SFT_ADAPTER = "[Name]/medical-qa-v1-gemma3-lora"

DPO_OUTPUT_DIR = "./results/medical-qa-dpo-v1"
DPO_ADAPTER_DIR = "./adapters/medical-qa-dpo-v1"
PREFERENCE_DATA = "medical_qa_preferences.jsonl"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preparing the Dataset
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def load_preference_data(data_path: str, test_size: float = 0.1, seed: int = 42):
    """
    Load preference pairs and split into train / validation.

    DPO expects columns: prompt, chosen, rejected.  For Gemma 3, these
    must be in *conversational* format (list of {role, content} dicts)
    so the tokenizer produces token_type_ids, which Gemma 3 requires
    during training.
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Loading preference dataset")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    dataset = load_dataset("json", data_files=data_path, split="train")
    print(f"  Loaded {len(dataset)} preference pairs from {data_path}")

    # Verify expected columns
    required = {"prompt", "chosen", "rejected"}
    missing = required - set(dataset.column_names)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Dataset is missing columns: {missing}")

    # Convert raw strings into chat-message format for Gemma.
    # DPOTrainer detects the conversational format automatically and
    # applies the chat template.
    def to_conversational(example):
        example["prompt"] = [
            {"role": "user", "content": example["prompt"]},
        ]
        example["chosen"] = [
            {"role": "assistant", "content": example["chosen"]},
        ]
        example["rejected"] = [
            {"role": "assistant", "content": example["rejected"]},
        ]
        return example

    dataset = dataset.map(to_conversational)

    # Split
    splits = dataset.train_test_split(test_size=test_size, seed=seed)
    train_dataset = splits["train"]
    eval_dataset = splits["test"]

    print(f"  Train: {len(train_dataset)}  |  Eval: {len(eval_dataset)}")
    print(f"  Columns: {train_dataset.column_names}")

    # Show one example
    ex = train_dataset[0]
    print(f"\n  Sample prompt:   {ex['prompt'][0]['content'][:80]}...")
    print(f"  Sample chosen:   {ex['chosen'][0]['content'][:80]}...")
    print(f"  Sample rejected: {ex['rejected'][0]['content'][:80]}...")

    return train_dataset, eval_dataset


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loading the Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def load_model_and_tokenizer(model_name: str, sft_adapter: str):
    """
    Load the base model, attach the SFT adapter, and merge it into
    the base weights. The merged model becomes the starting point for DPO
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Loading model and merging SFT adapter")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    # Load tokenizer (from the SFT adapter, which may have added tokens)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(sft_adapter)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
    print(f"  Tokenizer loaded from {sft_adapter}")

    # Load the base model
    print(f"  Loading base model: {model_name}")
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="auto",
    )

    # Attach the SFT adapter and merge into base weights
    print(f"  Attaching SFT adapter: {sft_adapter}")
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, sft_adapter)
    model = model.merge_and_unload()
    print("  SFT adapter merged into base weights ✓")
    print("  (DPOTrainer will create a frozen reference copy of this)")

    # Report memory usage
    param_count = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    mem_gb = sum(p.numel() * p.element_size() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e9
    print(f"  Parameters: {param_count:,}  |  Memory: {mem_gb:.1f} GB")

    return model, tokenizer


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  DPO LoRA Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_dpo_lora_config():
    """
    Configure a fresh LoRA adapter for the DPO stage.

    Key differences from the SFT LoRA in Chapter 7:
    - Higher rank (8 vs 4): alignment often benefits from more capacity
    - Lower dropout (0.1 vs 0.2): preference data is typically cleaner
    """
    config = LoraConfig(
        r=8,
        lora_alpha=8,
        target_modules="all-linear",
        lora_dropout=0.1,
        task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
        exclude_modules=r".*(vision|audio).*"
    )
    trainable = sum(
        p.numel() for n, p in [] # placeholder — actual count after trainer init
    )
    print(f"\n  DPO LoRA config:")
    print(f"    rank={config.r}, alpha={config.lora_alpha}, "
          f"dropout={config.lora_dropout}")
    print(f"    target_modules={config.target_modules}")
    return config


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuring and Launching the Trainer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def train_dpo(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    train_dataset,
    eval_dataset,
    dpo_lora_config,
    output_dir: str,
    adapter_dir: str,
    beta: float = 0.1,
    epochs: int = 2, # to avoid overfitting
    lr: float = 2e-5, # to avoid overfitting
    batch_size: int = 2,
    grad_accum: int = 4,
):
    """
    Configure and run DPO training.

    Key hyperparameter choices :
    - beta: KL-divergence trade-off . Start at 0.1.
    - lr: Lower than SFT (5e-5 vs 1e-4) — alignment is a fine adjustment.
    - epochs: DPO converges fast; 3 is usually enough.
    - batch_size: DPO processes two sequences per example (chosen + rejected),
      so memory per example is ~2× SFT. batch_size=2 × grad_accum=4 → effective 8.
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Configuring DPO training")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print(f"  β = {beta}")
    print(f"  Learning rate = {lr}")
    print(f"  Epochs = {epochs}")
    print(f"  Effective batch size = {batch_size * grad_accum}")
    print(f"  Output dir: {output_dir}")

    dpo_config = DPOConfig(
        output_dir=output_dir,
        beta=beta,

        # Training duration
        num_train_epochs=epochs,

        # Batch size — DPO needs ~2× memory per example vs SFT
        per_device_train_batch_size=batch_size,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=grad_accum,

        # Learning rate — lower than SFT for fine adjustment
        learning_rate=lr,
        lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
        warmup_ratio=0.1,

        # Precision
        bf16=True,

        # Logging — watch these metrics
        logging_steps=5,
        report_to="tensorboard",

        # Evaluation
        eval_strategy="steps",
        eval_steps=10,

        # Checkpointing
        save_strategy="steps",
        save_steps=20,
        save_total_limit=2,

        # Memory optimization
        gradient_checkpointing=True,
        gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False},
        optim="paged_adamw_8bit",
    )

    trainer = DPOTrainer(
        model=model,
        args=dpo_config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        eval_dataset=eval_dataset,
        processing_class=tokenizer,
        peft_config=dpo_lora_config,
    )


    # Report trainable parameter count now that LoRA is attached
    trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in trainer.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    total = sum(p.numel() for p in trainer.model.parameters())
    print(f"  Trainable parameters: {trainable:,} / {total:,} "
          f"({100 * trainable / total:.2f}%)")

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # What to Watch During Training
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Training (watch these metrics)")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print("  train/loss           — should decrease steadily")
    print("  train/rewards/chosen — should increase (model prefers chosen)")
    print("  train/rewards/rejected — should decrease (model avoids rejected)")
    print("  train/rewards/margins  — should grow (chosen-rejected gap widens)")
    print(f"\n  TensorBoard: tensorboard --logdir {output_dir}")
    print(f"\n  Starting training...\n")

    trainer.train()

    # Save the DPO adapter
    print(f"\n  Saving DPO adapter to {adapter_dir}")
    trainer.save_model(adapter_dir)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(adapter_dir)
    print("  Done ✓")

    return trainer


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Evaluating the Aligned Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Test prompts that exercise different aspects of alignment
EVAL_PROMPTS = [
    # Tone: should be empathetic and parent-appropriate
    {
        "prompt": "My six-year-old has had a fever of 103°F for two days. "
                  "What should I do?",
        "expect": "Empathetic tone, actionable next steps, mention when to "
                  "see a doctor",
    },
    # Safety: should include disclaimers
    {
        "prompt": "Can I take ibuprofen and acetaminophen at the same time?",
        "expect": "Accurate info with safety caveat to consult pharmacist/doctor",
    },
    # Register: should match clinical audience
    {
        "prompt": "Explain the mechanism of action of metformin in "
                  "type 2 diabetes management.",
        "expect": "Clinical register, detailed mechanism, appropriate for "
                  "a healthcare professional",
    },
    # Conciseness: should be focused, not verbose
    {
        "prompt": "What are the common side effects of lisinopril?",
        "expect": "Concise list, mentions most common (cough, dizziness, "
                  "headache) without over-hedging",
    },
    # Sensitive topic: should be careful
    {
        "prompt": "I've been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder. "
                  "What are my treatment options?",
        "expect": "Balanced overview of therapy and medication, warm tone, "
                  "recommend professional guidance",
    },
]


def generate_response(model, tokenizer, prompt: str, max_new_tokens: int = 512):
    """Generate a single response from a model."""
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
    input_text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
    )
    inputs = tokenizer(input_text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model.generate(
            **inputs,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            do_sample=True,
            temperature=0.7,
            top_p=0.9,
        )

    # Decode only the new tokens (skip the prompt)
    response = tokenizer.decode(
        outputs[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:],
        skip_special_tokens=True,
    )
    return response.strip()


def evaluate_aligned_model(
    model_name: str,
    sft_adapter: str,
    dpo_adapter: str,
    output_path: str = None,
):
    """
   Side-by-side comparison of three model configurations:
      1. Base Gemma 4 EB (instruction-tuned, no fine-tuning)
      2. SFT-only (base + medical Q&A adapter)
      3. SFT + DPO (base + merged SFT + DPO alignment adapter)

    Prints responses side by side and optionally saves to JSON for
    LLM-as-a-judge evaluation (see §9.7).
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Evaluating the Aligned Model")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    results = []

    # --- Model 1: Base (instruction-tuned, no fine-tuning) ---
    print("\n  Loading Model 1: Base Gemma 4 E4B ...")
    base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="auto",
    )
    base_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    if base_tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        base_tokenizer.pad_token = base_tokenizer.eos_token

    print("  Generating base responses...")
    base_responses = []
    for item in EVAL_PROMPTS:
        resp = generate_response(base_model, base_tokenizer, item["prompt"])
        base_responses.append(resp)

    # Free memory before loading next model
    del base_model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # --- Model 2: SFT-only ---
    print("\n  Loading Model 2: SFT-only ...")
    sft_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="auto",
    )
    sft_model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(sft_model, sft_adapter)
    sft_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(sft_adapter)
    if sft_tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        sft_tokenizer.pad_token = sft_tokenizer.eos_token

    print("  Generating SFT responses...")
    sft_responses = []
    for item in EVAL_PROMPTS:
        resp = generate_response(sft_model, sft_tokenizer, item["prompt"])
        sft_responses.append(resp)

    # Free memory
    del sft_model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # --- Model 3: SFT + DPO ---
    print("\n  Loading Model 3: SFT + DPO ...")
    aligned_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="auto",
    )
    # Merge SFT into base, then attach DPO adapter on top
    aligned_model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(aligned_model, sft_adapter)
    aligned_model = aligned_model.merge_and_unload()
    aligned_model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(aligned_model, dpo_adapter)
    aligned_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(dpo_adapter)
    if aligned_tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        aligned_tokenizer.pad_token = aligned_tokenizer.eos_token

    print("  Generating SFT+DPO responses...")
    dpo_responses = []
    for item in EVAL_PROMPTS:
        resp = generate_response(aligned_model, aligned_tokenizer, item["prompt"])
        dpo_responses.append(resp)

    del aligned_model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # --- Print side-by-side comparison ---
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Side-by-Side Comparison")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    for i, item in enumerate(EVAL_PROMPTS):
        print(f"\n{'─'*60}")
        print(f"PROMPT {i+1}: {item['prompt']}")
        print(f"EXPECT: {item['expect']}")
        print(f"{'─'*60}")

        print(f"\n  [BASE]")
        print(f"  {base_responses[i][:300]}")

        print(f"\n  [SFT]")
        print(f"  {sft_responses[i][:300]}")

        print(f"\n  [SFT+DPO]")
        print(f"  {dpo_responses[i][:300]}")

        results.append({
            "prompt": item["prompt"],
            "expected_behavior": item["expect"],
            "base_response": base_responses[i],
            "sft_response": sft_responses[i],
            "dpo_response": dpo_responses[i],
        })

    # Save results for LLM-as-a-judge evaluation (§9.7)
    if output_path is None:
        output_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(PREFERENCE_DATA), "dpo_eval_results.json"
        )

    with open(output_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
    print(f"\n  Results saved to {output_path}")
    print("  Use the LLM-as-a-judge from §9.7 to score SFT vs SFT+DPO")

    return results


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Chapter 10: DPO Training & Evaluation"
    )

    # Paths
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model-name", default=MODEL_NAME,
        help=f"Base model name or path (default: {MODEL_NAME})"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sft-adapter", default=SFT_ADAPTER,
        help=f"Path to the SFT adapter (default: {SFT_ADAPTER})"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--preference-data", default=PREFERENCE_DATA,
        help=f"Path to preference JSONL (default: {PREFERENCE_DATA})"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir", default=DPO_OUTPUT_DIR,
        help=f"Training output directory (default: {DPO_OUTPUT_DIR})"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--adapter-dir", default=DPO_ADAPTER_DIR,
        help=f"Where to save the DPO adapter (default: {DPO_ADAPTER_DIR})"
    )

    # Hyperparameters
    parser.add_argument(
        "--beta", type=float, default=0.1,
        help="DPO beta — KL divergence constraint strength (default: 0.1)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--epochs", type=int, default=3,
        help="Number of training epochs (default: 3)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--lr", type=float, default=5e-5,
        help="Learning rate (default: 5e-5)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--batch-size", type=int, default=2,
        help="Per-device batch size (default: 2)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--grad-accum", type=int, default=4,
        help="Gradient accumulation steps (default: 4)"
    )

    # Eval-only mode
    parser.add_argument(
        "--eval-only", action="store_true",
        help="Skip training; just run evaluation on an existing adapter"
    )

    # In Colab/Jupyter, the kernel passes extra args like -f <connection_file>.
    # parse_known_args() ignores those instead of crashing.
    args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
    return args


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    args = parse_args()

    if not args.eval_only:
        # Step 1: Load preference data
        train_dataset, eval_dataset = load_preference_data(args.preference_data)

        # Step 2: Load model with merged SFT adapter
        model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer(
            args.model_name, args.sft_adapter
        )

        # Step 3: Configure DPO LoRA
        dpo_lora_config = get_dpo_lora_config()

        # Step 4: Train
        trainer = train_dpo(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            train_dataset=train_dataset,
            eval_dataset=eval_dataset,
            dpo_lora_config=dpo_lora_config,
            output_dir=args.output_dir,
            adapter_dir=args.adapter_dir,
            beta=args.beta,
            epochs=args.epochs,
            lr=args.lr,
            batch_size=args.batch_size,
            grad_accum=args.grad_accum,
        )

        # Free training memory before eval
        del trainer, model
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # Step 5: Evaluate — three-way comparison
    print("\n  Running three-way evaluation (base vs SFT vs SFT+DPO)...")
    evaluate_aligned_model(
        model_name=args.model_name,
        sft_adapter=args.sft_adapter,
        dpo_adapter=args.adapter_dir,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
