10.1Chapter 10 · Alignment and Preference Optimization

DPO and Building a Preference Dataset

DPO ka big idea simple hai: tumhe ye batane ke liye numeric score ki zaroorat nahi ki kaunsa jawab behtar hai — sirf preference kaafi hai. Food critic wali analogy samjho: do dishes me se kaunsi behtar hai, ye batane ke liye tumhe har dish ko 10 me se score dene ki zaroorat nahi; bas ye bata do ki tumhe kaunsi pasand aayi. DPO wahi karta hai — reward model ko skip karke chosen aur rejected answers ke pairs par seedhe optimise karta hai.

Preference dataset — gold standard aur practical raasta

Preference data ka gold standard hai human labels — insaan batayein kaunsa jawab behtar hai. Lekin human labeling slow aur mehenga hai. Book practical raasta use karta hai: ek bade teacher model se synthetic pairs generate karna, phir ek LLM judge se unhe verify karwana. Teacher yahan ek bada open-weights model hai, aur judge bhi ek model hai jo pairs ko score karta hai.

Psoriasis worked example

Book ka worked example ek skin condition se related sawaal par hai: ek chosen answer jo empathetic, safe aur actionable hai, versus ek rejected answer jo clinical aur terse hai. Dono me information lagbhag wahi hai — farak sirf delivery me hai. Generation ka process: 300 questions generate kiye gaye, jinme se 296 quality checks pass hue. Target hai 1,000–1,500 pairs — 296 pairs se DPO kaam to karta hai, lekin overfitting ke signs dikhte hain. Community experience batati hai ki DPO surprisingly data-efficient hai, lekin kuch hundred pairs se zyada chahiye hote hain achhe generalization ke liye.

Generation code — do system prompts aur ek judge

Har sawaal ke liye do answers generate kiye jaate hain, do alag system prompts se: prompt A empathetic style me, temperature 0.5 par; prompt B clinical style me, temperature 1.0 par. Phir ek judge dono ko score karta hai, is order me: pehle SAFETY, phir ACCURACY, TONE, ACTIONABILITY aur COMPLETENESS. Judge ko A/B ki position randomized karke di jaati hai, taaki positional bias na aaye — judge hamesha pehle wale ko prefer na karne lage. Judge low temperature (0.1) par chalta hai, taaki uske decisions deterministic rahein.

Yaad rakho: DPO ko score nahi, preference chahiye — chosen vs rejected. Judge pehle SAFETY dekhta hai, phir accuracy, tone, actionability aur completeness. Aur A/B ki position randomize karna mat bhoolo.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Alignment and Preference Optimization
← Previous10 · Alignment and Preference Optimization→ Next10.2 · The DPO Loss and Running DPO
10.2Chapter 10 · Alignment and Preference Optimization

The DPO Loss and Running DPO

DPO ka loss dekhne me mathematical lagta hai, lekin uske peeche ka idea seedha hai: chosen answer ki probability badhao, rejected ki ghatao — aur base model se zyada door mat jao.

DPO loss — chaar steps

  1. Log-probabilities: model chosen aur rejected dono answers ki log-probabilities compute karta hai.
  2. Reference se ratio: har answer ki log-probability ko ek frozen reference model (tumhara SFT model) ki log-probability se compare kiya jaata hai. Ye ratio batata hai ki model SFT behaviour se kitna shift hua hai.
  3. Margin: chosen aur rejected ke ratios ke beech ka farak — margin. Margin bada matlab model chosen ko rejected se zyada prefer karta hai.
  4. Loss: loss = −log σ(β · margin) — margin ko beta se scale karke sigmoid se guzaro aur negative log lo. Margin badhne par loss kam hota hai.

Reference model aur beta — drift se bachav

Reference model DPO ki critical innovation hai: woh model ko SFT behaviour se zyada door jaane se rokta hai. Ye constraint loss function me hi built-in hai, aur beta uski strength control karta hai. Beta ka default 0.1 hai, aur 0.01–0.05 bhi increasingly common hain. Beta zyada ho to model reference ke kareeb rehta hai (kam seekhta hai); beta kam ho to model zyada freely shift karta hai — aur reward hacking aur verbosity ka risk badhta hai. Agar model degenerate text generate karne lage, to beta badhao; agar kuch seekh hi nahi raha, to beta kam karo.

DPO run karna — pehle SFT adapter merge karo

DPO chalane se pehle SFT adapter ko merge karo, phir us merged model par ek fresh LoRA train karo (rank 8, alpha 8, dropout 0.1). TRL ka DPOTrainer loss aur training loop sambhalta hai. Dataset me prompt, chosen aur rejected fields hote hain. Config: beta 0.1, 3 epochs, batch 2 × 4 = 8, learning rate 2e-5 — SFT ke 1e-4 se kam, kyunki alignment fine tuning hai. Book ne pehle 5e-5 try kiya tha, jo overfit kar gaya, to 2e-5 par halving ki gayi. Cosine schedule, warmup 10%. Data: 296 pairs se 90/10 split — 266 training aur 30 evaluation examples, lagbhag 33 steps per epoch. Trainable parameters lagbhag 19M (0.25% se kam). Ek important detail: har example do sequences hoti hai (chosen aur rejected), to memory lagbhag double ho jaati hai SFT ke muqable.

Metrics padhna

  • Training loss: 0.68 se gir kar 0.14 hui, lagbhag 100 steps me — model preference seekh raha hai.
  • Chosen rewards: upar ki taraf badhte hain, 1 ki taraf — model chosen answers ko prefer karne laga.
  • Rejected rewards: neeche girte hain — model rejected answers se door ja raha hai.
  • Margins: widen hote hain — chosen aur rejected ke beech ka gap badhta hai.
  • Validation loss: lagbhag step 40 se flat ho gayi — overfitting ka signal. Chhote dataset (296 pairs) ki wajah se ye expected hai, aur yehi wajah hai ki 1,000–1,500 pairs target hai.
Yaad rakho: DPO loss hai −log σ(β · margin), jahan reference model drift ko rokta hai aur beta uski strength hai. Learning rate SFT se kam rakho (2e-5), aur yaad rakho — har example do sequences hai, to memory double hoti hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Alignment and Preference Optimization
← Previous10.1 · DPO and Building a Preference Dataset→ Next10.3 · Evaluating Alignment and Going Beyond DPO
10.3Chapter 10 · Alignment and Preference Optimization

Evaluating Alignment and Going Beyond DPO

DPO training khatam ho gayi — ab sawaal hai: kya model asal me behtar tareeke se baat kar raha hai? Aur DPO ke aage kya hai? Is section me evaluation, ek practical decision framework, aur DPO ke aage ke methods hain.

Three-way eyeball test — base vs SFT vs SFT+DPO

Wahi fever wala prompt — do din se 103°F bukhaar wala bachha — teeno models se chalao aur teen criteria par judge karo. Base model generic jawab deta hai. SFT model seedhe point par aata hai, lekin bahut impersonal hai — ek curt list, jaise textbook se copy ki ho. SFT+DPO sweet spot hit karta hai: woh pehle batata hai parent ko kya karna chahiye, medical attention ki taraf prompt karta hai, aur step-by-step easy-to-follow guide deta hai. Information nahi badli — sirf framing aur delivery badli. Ye pattern evaluation prompts me mostly repeat hua. Criteria hain:

  • Tone: kya model context ke hisaab se apni communication adjust karta hai? Medical cases me empathetic, accessible language behtar hai; dusre scenarios me framing alag ho sakti hai.
  • Safety: safety warnings sabse important hain. Model ko professional consultation ki taraf drive karna chahiye — "consult your doctor" jaisi lines chosen responses me honi chahiye, taaki model woh communication path seekhe. Ye financial, legal aur bahut se dusre scenarios me bhi lagu hota hai.
  • Conciseness: model seedhe important point par aaye, technical jargon ki deewar me safety caveats kho na jaayein.

Eyeball test ke aage, Chapter 9 wali LLM-as-a-judge approach ko adapt karo — lekin judge ko accuracy ke bajaye preferred responses (tone, helpfulness, safety, conciseness) par score karne ko kaho, kyunki is stage par saare results accuracy me lagbhag ek jaise hote hain.

Kab DPO use karein — aur kab nahi

DPO use karo jab: SFT great information de raha ho, lekin galat style me — ye sweet spot hai. Tum clearly articulate kar sakte ho ki "behtar" kaisa dikhta hai, aur woh zyadaatar users ke liye universal ho. Aur tumhare paas kaafi high-quality reference pairs hon — sweet spot 1,000–1,500 hai.

DPO skip karo jab: factual accuracy problem ho — DPO behaviour adjust karega, knowledge nahi. Agar model galat hai, to pehle SFT dobara karo jab tak woh sahi na ho; nahi to DPO sirf surface polish hoga. Jab prompt ka sirf ek hi correct answer ho (jaise math problem ya code compile hota hai ya nahi) — DPO ko pairs chahiye, single-answer tasks me SFT hi kaafi hai. Aur jab dataset bahut chhota ho — model preference pairs par overfit karke long-term quality sacrifice kar dega; sahi lekin optimal voice me na hona, galat lekin optimal voice se behtar hai.

Beyond DPO

  • IPO (Identity Preference Optimization): DPO ke ek theoretical concern ko address karta hai — jab chosen aur rejected responses ki length bahut alag ho, to loss preference data par overfit kar sakta hai. IPO loss function ko modify karke use zyada robust banata hai.
  • KTO: pairs ke bajaye binary approach — response "good" ya "bad". Chatbot par thumbs-up / thumbs-down dekhte ho, to tum likely KTO ke liye data label kar rahe ho.
  • ORPO (Odds Ratio Preference Optimization): SFT aur alignment stages ko ek hi training run me combine karta hai — ek loss function jo simultaneously achhe responses generate karna aur unhe prefer karna sikhata hai. Pipeline simplify hoti hai, lekin granularity par control kam ho jaata hai.
  • SimPO (Simple Preference Optimization): reference model ki zaroorat hi khatam kar deta hai — response ki log probability ko implicit reward ke roop me use karta hai, to training sasti ho jaati hai kyunki frozen reference copy memory me rakhne ki zaroorat nahi. Bade models ke liye khaas taur par impactful hai, aur kai benchmarks par competitive results dikhaye hain.

Ye sab dekhne layak hain, lekin starting point standard DPO hi rakho — woh well-understood hai aur TRL library me bahut achhe se supported hai. Kuch DPO runs ke baad, jab mechanics samajh aa jayein, tab variants experiment karo.

Yaad rakho: DPO style aur safety fix karta hai, facts nahi. Agar model galat hai, to pehle SFT theek karo. Aur starting point hamesha standard DPO rakho — variants baad me.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Alignment and Preference Optimization

11Chapter 11 · Vision Language Models

Vision Language Models

Ab tak ka saara kaam sirf text ka tha — prompt andar, jawab bahar. Lekin asli duniya sirf bhasha nahi hai, woh visual bhi hai: X-ray, screenshot, chart, factory floor. Ek text-only model ko X-ray dikha kar pneumonia ke baare me poochho to uske paas dekhne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi — woh sirf sawal ke text se guess karega, aur medicine me guessing ek bahut bura idea hai. Vision language models (VLM) isi gap ko bharte hain: image + sawal andar, image ko samajh kar jawab bahar.

VLM possible kyun hue?

Teen developments ne VLM ko practical banaya. Pehla, CLIP aur uske successors — vision encoders jo images ko language concepts ke terms me samajhte hain, sirf pixel patterns ke terms me nahi. Dusra, instruction tuning — model complex, multi-step instructions follow kar sakta hai. Teesra, PEFT stack (LoRA, QLoRA aur baaki) — bade multimodal models ko consumer hardware par adapt karna possible hua.

Two-tower architecture

Har modern VLM ek hi high-level design follow karta hai: ek vision encoder pixels ko vectors ki sequence me badalta hai, ek chhota projector un vectors ko language model ki embedding space me map karta hai, aur phir language model unhe text tokens ke saath process karta hai — jaise woh aur words hon. Trick yeh hai ki image vectors ko text embeddings ki "bhasha" bolni aani chahiye.

Gemma 4 ka vision encoder

  • 27-layer ViT: image ko 16×16 patches me kaat ta hai, har patch ko embedding me badal kar self-attention se process karta hai. Kul lagbhag 150M parameters.
  • 2-D RoPE: har patch ki x aur y position alag-alag encode hoti hai, isliye model ko pata chalta hai ki cheez image ke top-right corner me hai ya neeche — 1-D positional encoding se yeh samajhna mushkil tha.
  • Aspect ratio preserved: image ko fixed square me force nahi kiya jata; natural proportions rakhte hue pixel budget me fit kiya jata hai.
  • Soft tokens: pooling ke baad har image 70, 140, 280, 560 ya 1,120 soft tokens me compress hoti hai — detail chahiye to 1,120, VRAM tight hai to kam.

SigLIP — CLIP ka improved variant — lagbhag 4× kam compute me CLIP jaisi quality deta hai. Gemma 4 usse aage badh kar ek custom vision encoder use karta hai, jo CLIP/SigLIP tradition me train hua ViT hai, lekin spatial awareness ke liye redesign kiya gaya.

Projector — translator ka kaam

Vision encoder aur language model alag embedding spaces me rehte hain — alag dimensions, alag geometry. Projector (Gemma 4 me Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder) ek chhota MLP hai, lagbhag 2M parameters, jo soft tokens ko language model ki hidden dimension me map karta hai. Processor unki jagah text me ek special <|image|> token se mark karta hai. Socho translator ki tarah: vision encoder "image-ese" bolta hai, language model "text-ese" — projector dono ke beech translate karta hai, taaki "top-right corner me red button" wala vector "button", "red" aur "corner" wale text embeddings ke paas land kare.

LLaVA blueprint aur parts ka size

Yeh design LLaVA blueprint se aaya hai — ek pretrained vision encoder ko ek pretrained language model se ek simple projection se jodna aur visual instruction-following data par fine-tune karna. Aaj ke lagbhag har open VLM ki yahi skeleton hai. Gemma 4 E4B-it load karo to parts ka size yeh hai: vision tower 167.4M, projector 2.0M, language model 7,463.0M parameters.

Forward pass — paanch steps

Ek mobile screenshot (1,170×2,532) aur sawal "What buttons are visible?" ko trace karo: (1) processor image ko aspect ratio rakhte hue 336×720 par resize karta hai; (2) 16×16 patches me kaatne par 21×45 = 945 patches bante hain, 27 transformer layers se guzarte hain, phir 3×3 pooling har 9 patches ko ek soft token me badal deti hai — 105 soft tokens; (3) projector unhe 2,560 dimensions (language model ki hidden size) me map karta hai; (4) sawal ke 12 text tokens ke saath sequence 117 vectors ki banti hai; (5) language model us par attend karke jawab generate karta hai. Audio aur video inputs bhi isi pattern par aate hain, aur context 256k tokens tak jaata hai.

Yaad rakho: VLM me knowledge teen jagah rehta hai — vision encoder dekhna janta hai, language model bolna janta hai, aur projector + fine-tuning data sikhata hai ki jo dekha uske baare me kya kehna hai. Fine-tune karte waqt tum zyada tar teesra hissa sikha rahe ho.

def hex_to_rgb(h):
    h = h.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))

def get_font(size, bold=False):
    paths = [
        "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf" if bold
        else "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf",
        "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf",
    ]
    for p in paths:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            try:
                return ImageFont.truetype(p, size)
            except Exception:
                continue
    return ImageFont.load_default()


class ScreenGenerator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.w, self.h = WIDTH, HEIGHT
        self.palette = random.choice(PALETTES)
        self.app_name = random.choice(APP_NAMES)
        self.img = Image.new("RGB", (self.w, self.h),
                             hex_to_rgb(self.palette["bg"]))
        self.draw = ImageDraw.Draw(self.img)
        self.y = 0
        self.font_title = get_font(22, bold=True)
        self.font_heading = get_font(18, bold=True)
        self.font_body = get_font(14)
        self.font_small = get_font(12)
        self.font_button = get_font(15, bold=True)
        self.font_nav = get_font(10)

    def c(self, key):
        return hex_to_rgb(self.palette[key])

    def status_bar(self):
        self.draw.rectangle([0, 0, self.w, 44], fill=self.c("bg"))
        self.draw.text((20, 14), "9:41", fill=self.c("text"),
                       font=self.font_body)
        bx = self.w - 45
        self.draw.rectangle([bx, 16, bx+25, 28], outline=self.c("text"))
        self.draw.rectangle([bx+2, 18, bx+18, 26], fill=self.c("primary"))
        self.y = 44

    def nav_header(self, title, back=False, right=None):
        h = 48
        self.draw.rectangle([0, self.y, self.w, self.y+h],
                           fill=self.c("nav_bg"))
        self.draw.line([0, self.y+h-1, self.w, self.y+h-1],
                      fill=self.c("divider"))
        if back:
            self.draw.text((16, self.y+14), "<", fill=self.c("primary"),
                          font=self.font_heading)
        self.draw.text((50 if back else 20, self.y+14), title,
                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)
        if right:
            bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), right, font=self.font_body)
            self.draw.text((self.w - (bbox[2]-bbox[0]) - 20, self.y+16),
                          right, fill=self.c("primary"), font=self.font_body)
        self.y += h

    def text_field(self, placeholder, filled=False):
        m, h = 24, 48
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m, self.y, self.w-m, self.y+h],
                                   radius=10, fill=self.c("input_bg"),
                                   outline=self.c("divider"))
        txt = random.choice(["alex@email.com", "johndoe", "********"]) \
            if filled else placeholder
        self.draw.text((m+16, self.y+15), txt,
                      fill=self.c("text" if filled else "text_secondary"),
                      font=self.font_body)
        self.y += h + 12

    def button(self, label, outlined=False):
        m, h = 24, 50
        if outlined:
            self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m, self.y, self.w-m, self.y+h],
                                       radius=12, outline=self.c("primary"),
                                       width=2)
            tc = self.c("primary")
        else:
            self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m, self.y, self.w-m, self.y+h],
                                       radius=12, fill=self.c("primary"))
            tc = self.c("primary_text")
        bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), label, font=self.font_button)
        tw = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
        self.draw.text(((self.w - tw)//2, self.y+15), label, fill=tc,
                      font=self.font_button)
        self.y += h + 16

    def card(self, title, subtitle="", has_image=False):
        m = 20
        ch = 140 if has_image else 90
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m+2, self.y+2, self.w-m+2, self.y+ch+2],
                                   radius=12, fill=self.c("divider"))
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m, self.y, self.w-m, self.y+ch],
                                   radius=12, fill=self.c("card_bg"),
                                   outline=self.c("divider"))
        cy = self.y + 12
        if has_image:
            self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m+12, cy, m+80, cy+65], radius=8,
                                       fill=self.c("primary"))
            self.draw.text((m+96, cy+4), title, fill=self.c("text"),
                          font=self.font_body)
            if subtitle:
                self.draw.text((m+96, cy+24), subtitle,
                              fill=self.c("text_secondary"),
                              font=self.font_small)
        else:
            self.draw.text((m+16, cy+4), title, fill=self.c("text"),
                          font=self.font_body)
            if subtitle:
                self.draw.text((m+16, cy+26), subtitle,
                              fill=self.c("text_secondary"),
                              font=self.font_small)
        self.y += ch + 12

    def list_item(self, text, toggle=False, chevron=True):
        h = 52
        self.draw.line([24, self.y+h-1, self.w-24, self.y+h-1],
                      fill=self.c("divider"))
        self.draw.text((24, self.y+16), text, fill=self.c("text"),
                      font=self.font_body)
        if toggle:
            on = random.choice([True, False])
            tx = self.w - 70
            self.draw.rounded_rectangle(
                [tx, self.y+16, tx+44, self.y+36], radius=10,
                fill=self.c("primary") if on else self.c("divider"))
            cx = tx + 32 if on else tx + 12
            self.draw.ellipse([cx-8, self.y+18, cx+8, self.y+34],
                            fill=(255,255,255))
        elif chevron:
            self.draw.text((self.w-40, self.y+16), ">",
                          fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_body)
        self.y += h

    def bottom_nav(self):
        by = self.h - 70
        self.draw.rectangle([0, by, self.w, self.h], fill=self.c("nav_bg"))
        self.draw.line([0, by, self.w, by], fill=self.c("divider"))
        active = random.randint(0, 4)
        for i, label in enumerate(NAV_ICONS):
            cx = (self.w // 5) * i + self.w // 10
            col = "primary" if i == active else "text_secondary"
            self.draw.ellipse([cx-10, by+10, cx+10, by+30], fill=self.c(col))
            bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), label, font=self.font_nav)
            self.draw.text((cx - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])//2, by+36), label,
                          fill=self.c(col), font=self.font_nav)

    def avatar(self, x, y, size=40):
        colors = ["#E91E63", "#9C27B0", "#3F51B5", "#009688", "#FF9800"]
        self.draw.ellipse([x, y, x+size, y+size],
                         fill=hex_to_rgb(random.choice(colors)))
        ini = random.choice("ABCDEFGHIJKLM")
        bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), ini, font=self.font_body)
        self.draw.text((x + (size-(bbox[2]-bbox[0]))//2,
                       y + (size-(bbox[3]-bbox[1]))//2 - 2),
                      ini, fill=(255,255,255), font=self.font_body)

    def search_bar(self):
        m, h = 20, 44
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([m, self.y, self.w-m, self.y+h],
                                   radius=22, fill=self.c("input_bg"))
        self.draw.text((m+36, self.y+13), "Search...",
                      fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_body)
        self.y += h + 12

    def chat_bubble(self, text, mine=False):
        max_w = self.w * 2 // 3
        words, lines, cur = text.split(), [], ""
        for w in words:
            test = f"{cur} {w}".strip()
            bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), test, font=self.font_body)
            if bbox[2]-bbox[0] > max_w - 30:
                lines.append(cur); cur = w
            else:
                cur = test
        if cur: lines.append(cur)
        bh = len(lines) * 20 + 16
        if mine:
            x1 = self.w - 20 - max_w
            bg, tc = self.c("primary"), self.c("primary_text")
        else:
            x1 = 20
            bg, tc = self.c("surface"), self.c("text")
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([x1, self.y, x1+max_w, self.y+bh],
                                   radius=16, fill=bg)
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            self.draw.text((x1+14, self.y+8+i*20), line, fill=tc,
                          font=self.font_body)
        self.y += bh + 8

    # ── Screen types ──────────────────────────────────────────
    def gen_login(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.y += 60
        cx = self.w // 2
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([cx-30, self.y, cx+30, self.y+60],
                                   radius=15, fill=self.c("primary"))
        self.y += 80
        self.draw.text((cx-60, self.y), f"Welcome to {self.app_name}",
                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)
        self.y += 40
        self.text_field("Email address"); self.text_field("Password")
        self.y += 8; self.button("Sign In")
        self.button("Create Account", outlined=True)

    def gen_signup(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Create Account", back=True)
        self.y += 20
        self.draw.text((24, self.y), "Join " + self.app_name,
                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)
        self.y += 32
        for f in ["Full name", "Email address", "Password", "Confirm password"]:
            self.text_field(f)
        self.y += 8; self.button("Sign Up")

    def gen_home_feed(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header(self.app_name, right="Filter")
        self.search_bar()
        for _ in range(random.randint(3,5)):
            if self.y > self.h - 150: break
            self.card(random.choice(HEADINGS), random.choice(BODY_TEXTS),
                     has_image=random.random() > 0.3)
        self.bottom_nav()

    def gen_settings(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Settings", back=True)
        toggles = {"Dark Mode", "Notifications"}
        for item in random.sample(LIST_ITEMS, min(10, len(LIST_ITEMS))):
            if self.y > self.h - 140: break
            self.list_item(item, toggle=item in toggles,
                          chevron=item not in toggles)
        self.bottom_nav()

    def gen_profile(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Profile", right="Edit")
        self.y += 20; cx = self.w // 2
        self.avatar(cx-40, self.y, 80); self.y += 90
        name = random.choice(USERNAMES)
        bbox = self.draw.textbbox((0,0), name, font=self.font_heading)
        self.draw.text((cx-(bbox[2]-bbox[0])//2, self.y), name,
                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)
        self.y += 50
        stats = [("Posts", random.randint(10,999)),
                 ("Followers", random.randint(50,9999)),
                 ("Following", random.randint(50,500))]
        for i, (lab, val) in enumerate(stats):
            x = (self.w//3)*i + self.w//6
            self.draw.text((x-15, self.y), str(val), fill=self.c("text"),
                          font=self.font_heading)
            self.draw.text((x-15, self.y+24), lab,
                          fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_small)
        self.y += 60; self.button("Follow"); self.bottom_nav()

    def gen_product_detail(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Details", back=True, right="Share")
        ih = 220
        self.draw.rectangle([0, self.y, self.w, self.y+ih],
                           fill=self.c("surface"))
        self.y += ih + 16
        self.draw.text((24, self.y), random.choice(PRODUCT_NAMES),
                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)
        self.y += 28
        self.draw.text((24, self.y),
                      f"${random.randint(9,299)}.{random.randint(0,99):02d}",
                      fill=self.c("primary"), font=self.font_heading)
        self.y += 32
        self.draw.text((24, self.y), random.choice(BODY_TEXTS),
                      fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_body)
        self.y += 40; self.button("Add to Cart")
        self.button("Buy Now", outlined=True)

    def gen_search_results(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Search", back=True)
        self.search_bar()
        self.y += 4
        for _ in range(random.randint(3,6)):
            if self.y > self.h - 150: break
            self.card(random.choice(PRODUCT_NAMES),
                     f"${random.randint(9,299)}.{random.randint(0,99):02d}",
                     has_image=True)

    def gen_chat(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header(random.choice(USERNAMES), back=True)
        self.y += 8
        for i, msg in enumerate(random.sample(CHAT_MESSAGES, min(6, len(CHAT_MESSAGES)))):
            if self.y > self.h - 160: break
            self.chat_bubble(msg, mine=(i % 2 == 1))
        by = self.h - 60
        self.draw.rectangle([0, by, self.w, self.h], fill=self.c("nav_bg"))
        self.draw.rounded_rectangle([16, by+10, self.w-70, by+44],
                                   radius=18, fill=self.c("input_bg"))

                      fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_body)

    def gen_notifications(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.nav_header("Notifications", right="Clear")
        times = ["2m", "15m", "1h", "3h", "5h", "1d"]

                          fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_small)
            self.draw.line([72, self.y+h-1, self.w-20, self.y+h-1],
                          fill=self.c("divider"))

    def gen_onboarding(self):
        self.status_bar(); self.y += 80
        cx = self.w // 2

    def gen_checkout(self):

                      fill=self.c("text"), font=self.font_heading)

                    radius=12, fill=self.c("card_bg"),

                val = random.choice(["$1,234", "89%", "156", "2.4K"])

                self.draw.text((x+16, self.y+16), val,
                              fill=self.c("primary"), font=self.font_heading)
                self.draw.text((x+16, self.y+44), lab,

            self.y += 96
        self.bottom_nav()

        self.status_bar()

        self.y += 12
        self.draw.text((24, self.y), random.choice(BODY_TEXTS),
                      fill=self.c("text_secondary"), font=self.font_body)

        for item in random.sample(LIST_ITEMS, min(8, len(LIST_ITEMS))):
            if self.y > self.h - 120: break
            self.list_item(item)
        self.bottom_nav()

    def generate(self, screen_type=None):
        if screen_type is None:
            screen_type = random.choice(SCREEN_TYPES)
        gen_fn = {
            "login": self.gen_login, "signup": self.gen_signup,
            "home_feed": self.gen_home_feed, "settings": self.gen_settings,
            "profile": self.gen_profile,
            "product_detail": self.gen_product_detail,
            "search_results": self.gen_search_results,
            "chat": self.gen_chat, "notifications": self.gen_notifications,
            "onboarding": self.gen_onboarding, "checkout": self.gen_checkout,
            "dashboard": self.gen_dashboard,
            "list_detail": self.gen_list_detail,
        }.get(screen_type, self.gen_home_feed)
        gen_fn()
        return self.img


def generate_screenshots():
    """Generate synthetic UI screenshots."""
    out = Path(OUTPUT_DIR)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    print(f"Generating {NUM_IMAGES} synthetic UI screenshots...")

    paths = []
    for i in range(NUM_IMAGES):
        stype = SCREEN_TYPES[i % len(SCREEN_TYPES)]
        gen = ScreenGenerator()
        img = gen.generate(stype)
        fname = f"ui_{stype}_{i:03d}.png"
        fpath = out / fname
        img.save(fpath)
        paths.append(str(fpath))
        print(f"  [{i+1}/{NUM_IMAGES}] {fname}")

    print(f"Done! {NUM_IMAGES} screenshots saved to {out}/\n")
    return paths

# ── Cell 5: Load Gemma 4 31B ─────────────────────────────────
import torch
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration

print("Loading Gemma 4 31B (this takes a few minutes)...")
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
model = Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)
model.eval()
print("Model loaded!\n")


# ── Cell 6: Define the teacher analysis function ─────────────
SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a senior UX analyst examining a mobile app screenshot.
Provide a structured analysis with these sections:

1. LAYOUT OVERVIEW: Describe the overall screen layout (navigation bars,
   content areas, floating elements).
2. UI ELEMENTS: List the key interactive elements (buttons, text fields,
   toggles, cards) with their approximate positions.
3. TEXT CONTENT: Transcribe any visible text on the screen.
4. ACCESSIBILITY NOTES: Flag potential accessibility issues (small tap
   targets, low contrast text, missing labels).
5. SUMMARY: One sentence describing the screen's purpose.

Be specific and factual. Describe what you see, not what you assume."""


def analyze_image(image_path: str) -> str | None:
    """Run Gemma 4 31B locally on a single image."""
    try:
        image = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")

        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {"type": "image"},
                    {"type": "text",
                     "text": "Analyze this mobile app screenshot."},
                ],
            },
        ]

        text = processor.apply_chat_template(
            messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
        )
        inputs = processor(
            text=text, images=[image], return_tensors="pt"
        ).to(model.device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            output_ids = model.generate(
                **inputs, max_new_tokens=1000, temperature=0.3, do_sample=True
            )

        generated = output_ids[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:]
        return processor.decode(generated, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Error: {e}")
        return None


# ── Cell 7: Build the dataset ────────────────────────────────
print(f"Processing {len(image_paths)} images with Gemma 4 31B...\n")

examples = []
for i, img_path in enumerate(image_paths):
    fname = Path(img_path).name
    print(f"[{i+1}/{len(image_paths)}] {fname}...", end=" ", flush=True)

    description = analyze_image(img_path)
    if description is None:
        print("FAILED")
        continue

    print(f"OK ({len(description)} chars)")
    question = random.choice(QUESTION_TEMPLATES)
    examples.append({
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {"type": "image", "url": img_path},
                    {"type": "text", "text": question},
                ],
            },
            {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": [
                    {"type": "text", "text": description},
                ],
            },
        ]
    })

print(f"\nGenerated {len(examples)} examples from {len(image_paths)} images.")


# ── Cell 8: Save the dataset ─────────────────────────────────
random.shuffle(examples)
split_idx = int(len(examples) * TRAIN_SPLIT)
train_examples = examples[:split_idx]
val_examples = examples[split_idx:]

os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(DATASET_FILE), exist_ok=True)

with open(DATASET_FILE, "w") as f:
    for ex in examples:
        f.write(json.dumps(ex) + "\n")

train_file = DATASET_FILE.replace(".jsonl", "_train.jsonl")
with open(train_file, "w") as f:
    for ex in train_examples:
        f.write(json.dumps(ex) + "\n")

val_file = DATASET_FILE.replace(".jsonl", "_val.jsonl")
with open(val_file, "w") as f:
    for ex in val_examples:
        f.write(json.dumps(ex) + "\n")

print(f"\nDataset saved!")
print(f"  Total: {len(examples)} → {DATASET_FILE}")
print(f"  Train: {len(train_examples)} → {train_file}")
print(f"  Val:   {len(val_examples)} → {val_file}")

def extract_image_path(example):
    """Find the first image entry in the user message and return its relative path."""
    for msg in example["messages"]:
        if msg["role"] != "user":
            continue
        for part in msg["content"]:
            if part.get("type") == "image":
                # Field might be "url", "path", or "image" depending on the dataset
                return part.get("url") or part.get("path") or part.get("image")
    return None


def extract_user_prompt(example):
    for msg in example["messages"]:
        if msg["role"] == "user":
            for part in msg["content"]:
                if part.get("type") == "text":
                    return part["text"]
    return None


def load_image(relative_path):
    url = HUB_BASE + relative_path.lstrip("/")
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return Image.open(BytesIO(resp.content))


# Display the first example
example = dataset["train"][0]
rel_path = extract_image_path(example)
print(f"Image path: {rel_path}")
print(f"Prompt: {extract_user_prompt(example)}\n")

img = load_image(rel_path)
display(img)
print(f"Image size: {img.size}, mode: {img.mode}")

import os
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from PIL import Image
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoProcessor,
    Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration,
    Trainer,
    TrainingArguments,
)

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
MODEL_ID = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"
HF_DATASET = "[Name]/uiscreenshots"
OUTPUT_DIR = "./results/ui-vision-v1"
ADAPTER_DIR = "./adapters/ui-vision-v1"
MAX_LENGTH = 1024
NUM_EPOCHS = 10
LEARNING_RATE = 2e-5
LORA_RANK = 8
LORA_ALPHA = 8
LORA_DROPOUT = 0.1
BATCH_SIZE = 2
GRAD_ACCUM = 16

# ── Part 1: Model Loading ─────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading model and processor...")

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)

model = Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

print(f"\nModel class: {type(model).__name__}")
print(f"Vision tower:   {model.model.vision_tower.__class__.__name__}")
print(f"Projector:      {model.model.embed_vision.__class__.__name__}")
print(f"Language model:  {model.model.language_model.__class__.__name__}")

# ── Part 2: LoRA Configuration ────────────────────────────────
print("\nConfiguring LoRA...")

from transformers.models.gemma4.modeling_gemma4 import Gemma4ClippableLinear
from peft.tuners.lora.model import LoraModel

if not getattr(LoraModel, "_clippable_patched", False):
    _orig_create_module = LoraModel._create_new_module

    @staticmethod
    def _create_module_with_clippable(config, adapter_name, target, **kw):
        if isinstance(target, Gemma4ClippableLinear):
            target = target.linear
        return _orig_create_module(config, adapter_name, target, **kw)

    LoraModel._create_new_module = _create_module_with_clippable
    LoraModel._clippable_patched = True

projector_linears = [
    name for name, mod in model.model.embed_vision.named_modules()
    if isinstance(mod, torch.nn.Linear)
]
print(f"Projector linear layers: {projector_linears}")

lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=LORA_RANK,
    lora_alpha=LORA_ALPHA,
    lora_dropout=LORA_DROPOUT,
    bias="none",
    task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
    target_modules=[
        # Language model layers (same as Chapter 7)
        "q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj",
        "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj",
        # Strategy 2: adapt the projector's layers too
        *projector_linears,
    ],
    # Keep the vision and audio towers frozen -- their attention
    # layers share names (q_proj etc.) with the language model's
    exclude_modules=r".*(vision_tower|audio).*",
)

model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()

# Verify the adapters landed where we intended: expect entries under
# the language model AND embed_vision, and NONE under vision_tower
lora_locations = sorted({
    n.split(".lora")[0] for n, _ in model.named_modules() if ".lora" in n
})
assert any("embed_vision" in n for n in lora_locations), \
    "Projector did not get LoRA adapters!"
assert not any("vision_tower" in n for n in lora_locations), \
    "Vision tower got LoRA adapters -- it should be frozen!"
print(f"LoRA attached to {len(lora_locations)} modules; "
      f"projector included, vision tower untouched ✓")

# ── Part 3: Dataset ───────────────────────────────────────────
class VisionChatDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, hf_split, processor, max_length: int = 1024):
        self.hf_split = hf_split
        self.processor = processor
        self.max_length = max_length

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.hf_split)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        example = self.hf_split[idx]
        messages = example["messages"]

        images = []
        if "image" in example and example["image"] is not None:
            images.append(example["image"].convert("RGB"))

        clean_messages = []
        for msg in messages:
            if isinstance(msg["content"], list):
                clean_parts = []
                for part in msg["content"]:
                    if part.get("type") == "image":
                        clean_parts.append({"type": "image"})
                    else:
                        clean_parts.append(part)
                clean_messages.append({"role": msg["role"],
                                       "content": clean_parts})
            else:
                clean_messages.append(msg)

        text = self.processor.apply_chat_template(
            clean_messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False
        )

        inputs = self.processor(
            text=text,
            images=images if images else None,
            return_tensors="pt",
            padding="max_length",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.max_length,
        )

        inputs = {k: v.squeeze(0) for k, v in inputs.items()}
        inputs["labels"] = inputs["input_ids"].clone()
        inputs["labels"][inputs["attention_mask"] == 0] = -100

        return inputs


print(f"\nDownloading dataset from {HF_DATASET}...")
hf_dataset = load_dataset(HF_DATASET)

train_dataset = VisionChatDataset(hf_dataset["train"], processor,
                                  max_length=MAX_LENGTH)
val_dataset = VisionChatDataset(hf_dataset["validation"], processor,
                                max_length=MAX_LENGTH)

print(f"Train: {len(train_dataset)} examples")
print(f"Val:   {len(val_dataset)} examples")

# ── Part 4: Training ──────────────────────────────────────────
print("\nConfiguring training...")

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir=OUTPUT_DIR,
    num_train_epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
    per_device_train_batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    per_device_eval_batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=GRAD_ACCUM,
    learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE,
    lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
    warmup_steps=10,
    weight_decay=0.05,
    max_grad_norm=0.3,
    bf16=True,
    logging_steps=5,
    logging_first_step=True,
    report_to="tensorboard",
    eval_strategy="steps",
    eval_steps=20,
    save_strategy="steps",
    save_steps=40,
    save_total_limit=3,
    load_best_model_at_end=True,
    metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",
    gradient_checkpointing=False,
    optim="adamw_torch",
    remove_unused_columns=False,
)


def collate_fn(examples):
    batch = {}
    for key in examples[0].keys():
        batch[key] = torch.stack([ex[key] for ex in examples])
    return batch


trainer = Trainer(
    model=model,
    args=training_args,
    train_dataset=train_dataset,
    eval_dataset=val_dataset,
    data_collator=collate_fn,
)

print("\nStarting training...")
print(f"  Epochs: {NUM_EPOCHS}")
print(f"  Batch size: {BATCH_SIZE} x {GRAD_ACCUM} = {BATCH_SIZE * GRAD_ACCUM}")
print(f"  Learning rate: {LEARNING_RATE}")
print(f"  LoRA rank: {LORA_RANK}")
print()

trainer.train()

# Save the adapter
os.makedirs(ADAPTER_DIR, exist_ok=True)
trainer.save_model(ADAPTER_DIR)
processor.save_pretrained(ADAPTER_DIR)

print(f"\nTraining complete!")
print(f"Adapter saved to {ADAPTER_DIR}")

# Based on chapter11/code/vision_inference.py (simplified for inline use)
import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
from transformers.models.gemma4.modeling_gemma4 import Gemma4ClippableLinear
from peft.tuners.lora.model import LoraModel
from peft import PeftModel

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────

MODEL_ID = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"
ADAPTER_PATH = "./adapters/ui-vision-v1"

# Load base model (same bf16 setup as training)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ADAPTER_PATH)
base_model = Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

if not getattr(LoraModel, "_clippable_patched", False):
    _orig_create_module = LoraModel._create_new_module

    @staticmethod
    def _create_module_with_clippable(config, adapter_name, target, **kw):
        if isinstance(target, Gemma4ClippableLinear):
            target = target.linear
        return _orig_create_module(config, adapter_name, target, **kw)

    LoraModel._create_new_module = _create_module_with_clippable
    LoraModel._clippable_patched = True


# Load the fine-tuned adapter
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, ADAPTER_PATH)
model.eval()


def ask_about_image(image, question: str) -> str:
    """Send an image and question to the fine-tuned VLM.

    Args:
        image: A PIL Image, or a file path string.
        question: The question to ask about the image.
    """
    if isinstance(image, str):
        image = Image.open(image).convert("RGB")

    messages = [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image"},
                {"type": "text", "text": question},
            ],
        }
    ]

    # Apply chat template
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(
        messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
    )

    # Process text + image
    inputs = processor(
        text=text,
        images=[image],
        return_tensors="pt",
    ).to(model.device)

    # Generate
    with torch.no_grad():
        output_ids = model.generate(
            **inputs,
            max_new_tokens=1024,
            temperature=0.3,
            do_sample=True,
        )

    # Decode only the generated tokens
    generated = output_ids[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:]
    return processor.decode(generated, skip_special_tokens=True)

"""
Chapter 11: Vision Model Evaluation Script
============================================
Evaluates a fine-tuned VLM using:
1. Mismatch test — checks whether the model attends to image content
2. LLM-as-a-judge — uses a teacher VLM to grade responses

Usage:
    export API_KEY="sk-..."
    python chapter11_vision_eval.py

Requires:
    - A fine-tuned adapter at ./adapters/ui-vision-v1
    - Test images in ./images/test/
    - An OpenAI-compatible API for the judge model
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import sys
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from openai import OpenAI
from PIL import Image
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import (
    AutoProcessor,
    Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration,
)
from transformers.models.gemma4.modeling_gemma4 import Gemma4ClippableLinear
from peft.tuners.lora.model import LoraModel

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
MODEL_ID = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"
ADAPTER_PATH = os.getenv("ADAPTER_PATH", "./adapters/ui-vision-v1")
TEST_DIR = os.getenv("TEST_DIR", "./images/test")
EVAL_OUTPUT = os.getenv("EVAL_OUTPUT", "./eval_vision_results.json")

# Judge model config — In this case I hosted a Gemma-4-31B on a cloud service.
ENDPOINT_URL = os.getenv("ENDPOINT_URL",
    "<ENDPOINT URL>")
API_KEY = os.getenv("API_KEY",
    "<DEFAULT API KEY>")
JUDGE_MODEL = os.getenv("JUDGE_MODEL", "google/gemma-4-31B-it")

client = OpenAI(base_url=ENDPOINT_URL, api_key=API_KEY)


# ── Model Loading ─────────────────────────────────────────────
def load_model():
    if not getattr(LoraModel, "_clippable_patched", False):
      _orig_create_module = LoraModel._create_new_module

      @staticmethod
      def _create_module_with_clippable(config, adapter_name, target, **kw):
          if isinstance(target, Gemma4ClippableLinear):
              target = target.linear
          return _orig_create_module(config, adapter_name, target, **kw)

      LoraModel._create_new_module = _create_module_with_clippable
      LoraModel._clippable_patched = True
    """Load the fine-tuned VLM."""
    print("Loading model...")
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ADAPTER_PATH)
    base_model = Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID,
        device_map="auto",
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    )
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, ADAPTER_PATH)
    model.eval()
    print("Model loaded.\n")
    return model, processor


def ask_about_image(model, processor, image_path: str, question: str) -> str:
    """Send an image and question to the VLM."""
    image = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")

    messages = [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image"},
                {"type": "text", "text": question},
            ],
        }
    ]

    text = processor.apply_chat_template(
        messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
    )
    inputs = processor(text=text, images=[image], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

    with torch.no_grad():
        output_ids = model.generate(
            **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.3, do_sample=True
        )

    generated = output_ids[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :]
    return processor.decode(generated, skip_special_tokens=True)


# ── Evaluation 1: Mismatch Test ──────────────────────────────
def mismatch_test(
    model, processor, image_a: str, image_b: str, question: str
) -> dict:
    """Test whether the model's answer changes when the image changes.

    If the model produces very similar responses for two different images,
    it may not be attending to the visual content.
    """
    response_a = ask_about_image(model, processor, image_a, question)
    response_b = ask_about_image(model, processor, image_b, question)

    similarity = SequenceMatcher(None, response_a, response_b).ratio()

    return {
        "image_a": image_a,
        "image_b": image_b,
        "question": question,
        "response_a": response_a[:200] + "..." if len(response_a) > 200 else response_a,
        "response_b": response_b[:200] + "..." if len(response_b) > 200 else response_b,
        "similarity": round(similarity, 3),
        "likely_using_image": similarity < 0.7,
    }


def run_mismatch_tests(model, processor, test_images: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Run mismatch tests on pairs of test images."""
    question = "Describe the UI layout and elements in this screenshot."
    results = []

    for i in range(0, len(test_images) - 1, 2):
        img_a = test_images[i]
        img_b = test_images[i + 1]
        print(
            f"  Mismatch test: {Path(img_a).name} vs {Path(img_b).name}...",
            end=" ",
        )

        result = mismatch_test(model, processor, img_a, img_b, question)
        status = "PASS" if result["likely_using_image"] else "FAIL"
        print(f"similarity={result['similarity']:.3f} [{status}]")
        results.append(result)

    return results


# ── Evaluation 2: LLM-as-a-Judge ─────────────────────────────
def encode_image(image_path: str) -> str:
    """Read an image file and return its base64 encoding."""
    with open(image_path, "rb") as f:
        return base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8")


JUDGE_SYSTEM = """You are evaluating a VLM's description of a UI screenshot.
You can see the original screenshot. Grade the response on:

1. ACCURACY (1-5): Does the description match what's actually in the image?
2. COMPLETENESS (1-5): Are all major UI elements mentioned?
3. SPECIFICITY (1-5): Does it describe THIS screenshot, not a generic screen?
4. USEFULNESS (1-5): Would a developer find this analysis actionable?

Reply with ONLY a JSON object:
{"accuracy": N, "completeness": N, "specificity": N,
 "usefulness": N, "total": N, "reasoning": "one sentence"}

where total = accuracy + completeness + specificity + usefulness (max 20)."""


def judge_vision_response(image_path: str, question: str, response: str) -> dict:
    """Have a teacher VLM grade the fine-tuned model's response."""
    b64 = encode_image(image_path)
    ext = Path(image_path).suffix.lower().lstrip(".")
    mime = {"png": "image/png", "jpg": "image/jpeg", "jpeg": "image/jpeg"}.get(
        ext, "image/png"
    )

    try:
        judge_response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=JUDGE_MODEL,
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
                {
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": [
                        {
                            "type": "image_url",
                            "image_url": {"url": f"data:{mime};base64,{b64}"},
                        },
                        {
                            "type": "text",
                            "text": (
                                f"Question asked: {question}\n\n"
                                f"Model's response:\n{response}\n\n"
                                f"Grade this response."
                            ),
                        },
                    ],
                },
            ],
            temperature=0.1,
            max_tokens=300,
        )
        content = judge_response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        # Try to parse JSON from the response
        if "```" in content:
            content = content.split("```")[1]
            if content.startswith("json"):
                content = content[4:]
        return json.loads(content)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Judge error: {e}")
        return {
            "accuracy": 0,
            "completeness": 0,
            "specificity": 0,
            "usefulness": 0,
            "total": 0,
            "reasoning": f"Judge error: {e}",
        }


def run_judge_evaluation(
    model, processor, test_images: list[str]
) -> list[dict]:
    """Run LLM-as-a-judge evaluation on test images."""
    question = "Analyze this mobile app screenshot."
    results = []

    for img_path in test_images:
        print(f"  Judging response for {Path(img_path).name}...", end=" ")

        response = ask_about_image(model, processor, img_path, question)
        scores = judge_vision_response(img_path, question, response)

        print(f"total={scores.get('total', 'N/A')}/20")
        results.append(
            {
                "image": img_path,
                "response": response[:300] + "..."
                if len(response) > 300
                else response,
                "scores": scores,
            }
        )

    return results


# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def main():
    # Find test images
    test_dir = Path(TEST_DIR)
    if not test_dir.exists():
        print(f"Error: Test directory '{TEST_DIR}' does not exist.")
        print("Create the directory and add test screenshots.")
        sys.exit(1)

    test_images = sorted(
        str(p)
        for p in test_dir.iterdir()
        if p.suffix.lower() in {".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg"}
    )

    if len(test_images) < 2:
        print(f"Need at least 2 test images in {TEST_DIR}")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"Found {len(test_images)} test images in {TEST_DIR}\n")

    # Load model
    model, processor = load_model()

    # Run evaluations
    all_results = {}

    print("=" * 50)
    print("1. MISMATCH TESTS (image grounding)")
    print("=" * 50)
    mismatch_results = run_mismatch_tests(model, processor, test_images)
    all_results["mismatch_tests"] = mismatch_results

    passing = sum(1 for r in mismatch_results if r["likely_using_image"])
    total = len(mismatch_results)
    print(f"\nMismatch test summary: {passing}/{total} passed\n")

    print("=" * 50)
    print("2. LLM-AS-A-JUDGE (response quality)")
    print("=" * 50)
    judge_results = run_judge_evaluation(model, processor, test_images[:5])
    all_results["judge_results"] = judge_results

    if judge_results:
        avg_total = sum(
            r["scores"].get("total", 0) for r in judge_results
        ) / len(judge_results)
        print(f"\nAverage judge score: {avg_total:.1f}/20\n")

    # Save results
    with open(EVAL_OUTPUT, "w") as f:
        json.dump(all_results, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Full results saved to {EVAL_OUTPUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

11.1Chapter 11 · Vision Language Models

Three Fine-Tuning Strategies and the VRAM Budget

Text fine-tune me sirf ek sawal tha — language model ke kin layers par LoRA lagana hai. Vision fine-tune me choices zyada hain, kyunki ab teen components hain: vision tower, projector aur language model. Kaun sa freeze karna hai aur kaun sa train karna hai, yeh task par depend karta hai. Book teen strategies deti hai.

Teen strategies

  • Strategy 1 — language model only: vision tower aur projector frozen, sirf language model par LoRA. Sabse halka, sabse sasta. Kaam karta hai jab tumhari images wohi hain jo encoder ne pretraining me dekhi hain (natural photos, web images, screenshots) — encoder pehle se hi unhe achhe se encode karta hai, tum sirf language model ko unke baare me alag tareeke se bolna sikha rahe ho.
  • Strategy 2 — language model + projector (book ki choice): language model par LoRA ke saath projector ko bhi train karo. Sirf 2M extra parameters, VRAM me barely zyada, lekin model seekh leta hai ki visual information ko language space me kaise translate karna hai — jaise chest X-ray me subtle density differences par dhyaan dena. Zyada tar real-world tasks ke liye yahi sweet spot hai. Ek warning: projector delicate hota hai, aggressive fine-tune uski mapping ko bigaad sakta hai.
  • Strategy 3 — full vision: vision tower ko bhi unfreeze karo. Sabse bhaari — VRAM aur data dono me — aur sirf tab worth hai jab images encoder ki training distribution se bahut bahar hon (electron microscopy, satellite imagery, specialized industrial sensors). Risk bhi hai: encoder ki general visual knowledge degrade ho sakti hai.

VRAM budget — lagbhag 19–22 GB

Vision fine-tune me memory text fine-tune se zyada lagti hai, kyunki frozen vision tower ko bhi forward pass ke liye VRAM me load karna padta hai. Gemma 4 E4B ke liye budget kuch aisa hai: language model (bf16, frozen) ~15 GB, vision tower ~0.35 GB, audio tower (use na ho to bhi load hota hai) ~0.6 GB, projector ~5 MB, LoRA trainable params (17.4M, float32) ~70 MB, gradients aur optimizer states ~0.2 GB, activations + image features ~2–5 GB, framework overhead ~1 GB — total ~19–22 GB. Yeh 24 GB wale RTX 4090 me modest headroom ke saath fit hota hai, aur A100 par comfortable hai.

Ek farak dhyaan do: Chapter 8 me QLoRA se language model chhota ho gaya tha, lekin yahan full model bf16 me chahiye — kyunki model ko quantize karna vision encoder ko tod deta hai (agle section me detail). Soft token budget bhi VRAM ko affect karta hai: 1,120 soft tokens per image, 280 ke mukable, sequence aur activations dono me significantly zyada memory khata hai.

Strategy kaise chunni hai?

Pehle apni images ko dekho: kya woh encoder ki dekhi hui cheezon jaisi hain — photographs, screenshots, documents? To pretrained features kaafi hain, full retrain ki zaroorat nahi. Phir base model se apni kuch images describe karvao — "Describe this image in detail." Agar woh main elements sahi pehchan le, to Strategy 2 best bet hai. Agar woh obvious features bhi nahi pehchan pa raha (X-ray ko sirf black-and-white image keh raha hai), to vision encoder ko adaptation chahiye — Strategy 3 par vichar karo. Zyada tar real-world tasks Strategy 2 se cover ho jate hain.

Yaad rakho: pehle base model ko apni images par test karo, phir strategy chuno. Agar base model pehle se dekh sakta hai, to sasti strategy kaafi hai — mehenga full-vision train sirf tab karo jab encoder sach me andha ho.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 11 — Vision Language Models

11.2Chapter 11 · Vision Language Models

The Dataset, the Script, and the Training Run

Vision fine-tune me training example sirf text conversation nahi hota — usme ek ya zyada images bhi hoti hain. Model seekhta hai "image me jo dikha" se "uske baare me kya kehna hai" tak ka mapping. Is chapter ka example mobile app screenshots ko dekh kar unka accessibility audit karna hai — layout describe karna, UI elements pehchanna aur issues flag karna.

Dataset schema

Har example ek conversation hai jisme image bhi hai: user role me image + text ("Audit this mobile UI screenshot for WCAG compliance and usability issues. Return structured JSON."), aur assistant role me structured JSON — screen_type, app_name, elements ki list (type, position, text, has_back_button / has_toggle jaise fields). Output JSON isliye hai kyunki fine-tune ka point yahi hai: base model UI describe to kar leta hai, lekin structured, parseable output nahi deta — aur wahi output ek accessibility-audit application me kaam aata hai.

Dataset — 250 screenshots

Dataset author/uiscreenshots hai: 250 screenshots — 225 train, 25 validation — 13 screen types (login, signup, home feed, settings, profile, product detail, search results, chat, notifications, onboarding, checkout, dashboard, list detail) aur 6 colour palettes me. Har screenshot ko bade teacher VLM (Gemma 4 31B variant) ne label kiya hai. Screenshots Pillow se programmatically generate kiye gaye (generate_synthetic_screenshots.py), aur har UI element draw karte waqt uski position, text aur properties ka metadata record kiya gaya. Real project me tum apne app ke actual screenshots loge, ya browser automation, ya Rico dataset (66,000+ real Android screenshots) use karoge. Focused domain ke liye 200–500 high-quality examples kaafi hote hain — 300 diverse, detailed examples 3,000 repetitive examples se behtar hain.

Script — QLoRA vision me FAIL hota hai

Model Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration se load hota hai aur tokenizer ki jagah AutoProcessor aata hai — text tokenization + image preprocessing ek object me. Processor ko hamesha keyword arguments se call karo — processor(text=..., images=...) — positional arguments image processor ko route ho jate hain aur mushkil bugs aate hain.

Sabse important finding: vision fine-tune me QLoRA FAIL hota hai. Bitsandbytes se har linear layer quantize hoti hai, vision tower bhi — aur chhota vision encoder 4-bit par image encode karne ki ability kho deta hai. Model confidently hallucinate karta hai, training loss achha dikhta hai, output grammatically sahi lagta hai — sirf visual inspection se pata chalta hai ki jawab galat hai. Isliye book bf16 LoRA use karti hai (quantize kiye bina), rank 8, 17,467,392 trainable parameters (0.2195%), vision aur audio towers ko exclude karte hue (exclude_modules me vision_tower/audio pattern — kyunki unke attention layers ke naam language model jaisi hi hain). Projector ki linear layers ko target list me add kiya jata hai. Rank 4 ki jagah 8 isliye, kyunki vision tasks ko visual-to-language mapping ke liye zyada capacity chahiye. Adapter save karte waqt processor bhi save karo (processor.save_pretrained()) — special tokens jaise <|image|> usi me rehte hain.

Training config aur run

  • 10 epochs, batch 2 × gradient accumulation 16 = effective batch 32 (batch chhota isliye kyunki har example me image tensors bhi hain).
  • Learning rate 2e-5, cosine schedule — vision fine-tune me conservative LR behtar hai; aggressive updates projector ki visual-to-language mapping ko scramble kar sakte hain.
  • remove_unused_columns=False — critical. Trainer aam taur par model ke forward signature me na hone wale columns strip kar deta hai, aur multimodal me pixel values ke naam nonstandard hote hain. Yeh False na ho to image data silently drop ho jata hai — training normally chalti dikhegi, lekin model kuch seekhega hi nahi.
  • Gradient checkpointing off, optimizer adamw_torch, weight decay 0.05, max grad norm 0.3, eval har 20 steps, save har 40 steps.

80 steps me loss 8.77 se 4.42 tak gira, aur validation loss bilkul saath-saath chali (step 80 par train 4.42, validation 4.41) — overfitting ka koi sign nahi.

Yaad rakho: do cheezein kabhi mat bhoolna — vision me QLoRA mat lagana (quantized encoder confidently hallucinate karega), aur remove_unused_columns=False set karna (warna image data silently drop ho jayega aur training dikhawa ban jayegi).

← Previous11.1 · Three Fine-Tuning Strategies and the VRAM Budget→ Next11.3 · Inference, Evaluation, Domains, and Troubleshooting
11.3Chapter 11 · Vision Language Models

Inference, Evaluation, Domains, and Troubleshooting

Training ke baad inference wahi adapter-loading pattern follow karta hai jo text models me tha: base model + PeftModel.from_pretrained + processor. ask_about_image helper image aur sawal le kar structured JSON deta hai — temperature 0.3, aur JSON output ke liye 0.1–0.3 best hai (zyada temperature JSON syntax bigaad deta hai — ek missing bracket aur output unparseable). Base model usi prompt par free-form prose deta hai; fine-tuned model clean JSON deta hai jise linter, CI pipeline ya accessibility dashboard seedha consume kar sakta hai.

Evaluation — model dekh raha hai ya hallucinate kar raha hai?

VLM evaluate karna text model se mushkil hai, kyunki ek extra dimension hai: kya model sach me image dekh raha hai, ya sawal se plausible description bana raha hai? Isliye pehla test mismatch / hallucination test hai: do alag images par wahi sawal poochho — agar jawab lagbhag same aaye (similarity 0.7 se upar), to model image use hi nahi kar raha. Yeh canary test hai: pehle yahi chalao, iske fail hone par baaki evaluation ka koi matlab nahi. Phir LLM-as-a-judge with vision: judge ko image + sawal + jawab bhej kar 1–5 score karvao — accuracy, completeness, specificity, usefulness. Judge ko bhi image milti hai, isliye woh visual claims verify kar sakta hai (text-only judge yeh nahi kar sakta). Sabse convincing evaluation base vs fine-tuned side-by-side comparison hai — aur structured output tasks me to JSON parse hona aur expected fields hona khud hi programmatic check hai.

Domains — wahi pipeline, nayi images

  • Medical imaging: X-ray/CT aur reports ke pairs — MIMIC-CXR (370,000+ chest X-ray images), CheXpert, PadChest. Subtle findings ke liye maximum soft token budget (1,120 tokens per image) use karo. Warning: clinical use par regulatory requirements lagte hain — fine-tuned VLM decision-support tool hai, diagnostic system nahi.
  • Manufacturing / quality inspection: circuit board, weld ya molded parts ki photos + QA reports. Sirf 50–100 examples bhi kaam kar sakte hain agar annotation achha ho aur main defect types cover hon. Consistent lighting aur framing bahut matter karti hai.
  • Document understanding: invoice, form, receipt se structured JSON extract karna. 300 DPI ya zyada par scan karo, skew correct karo, contrast normalize karo — garbage in, garbage out yahan bhi lagta hai.

Practical rules: resolution vs token budget ka trade-off yaad rakho (chhota text padhna hai to zyada tokens, coarse counting hai to kam); multi-image conversations me har extra image ek aur vision-tower pass aur zyada soft tokens mangta hai, to batch size aur kam karni pad sakti hai; aur vision tower ko sirf tab fine-tune karo jab images fundamentally alag domain ki hon — pehle projector-only fine-tune se evaluate karo, agar model human expert ko obvious dikhne wali features bhi miss kare to hi tower ko chhedo.

Troubleshooting

  • Flat loss: model images se seekh hi nahi raha — remove_unused_columns True to nahi, aur AutoTokenizer ki jagah AutoProcessor use ho raha hai ya nahi, check karo.
  • Out of memory: soft token budget kam karo, batch size ghata kar gradient accumulation badhao, gradient checkpointing on karo, vision tower bf16 me load ho raha hai confirm karo.
  • Model image ignore kar raha hai: data problem hai — diverse images aur diverse annotations check karo; agar har jawab ek hi template se shuru hota hai, to model ne template seekh liya hai, image nahi.
  • Encoder kharab hai ya data? do alag images ko vision tower se guzaro aur raw outputs ki cosine similarity dekho — mismatch test batata hai ki model dekh nahi raha, encoder probe batata hai ki kaun sa component fail hua.
  • Positional arguments: processor ko hamesha keyword arguments do. Saved adapter garbage de raha hai: processor save karna bhool gaye honge. Judge ke scores low hain lekin output achha lagta hai: judge ko image base64 me pass ho rahi hai ya nahi, check karo.

Complete 9-step workflow

(1) Dataset lo ya banao (200–500 examples, teacher VLM se annotate karo). (2) Output format decide karo (structured JSON, checklist, domain report template). (3) 20–30 examples inspect karo — JSON parse hota hai, element lists image se match karti hain. (4) Train/validation split karo (90/10). (5) Train karo, loss curve par overfitting dekho. (6) Mismatch test pehle chalao. (7) LLM-as-a-judge se score karo. (8) Base vs fine-tuned compare karo, JSON parse aur schema validate karo. (9) Scores low hon to data par iterate karo — zyada data, behtar annotations, ya schema adjust karna hyperparameters tweak karne se zyada effective hota hai.

Yaad rakho: vision fine-tune ki value do jagah se aati hai — model ko woh dikhana jo woh pehle nahi dekh sakta tha, aur use woh format me bolna sikhana jo tumhe chahiye. UI screenshots me pehla hissa pehle se tha, dusra tumne sikhaya — aur wahi kaafi tha.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 11 — Vision Language Models
