12Chapter 12 · Diffusion Models

Diffusion Models

Chapter 11 me tumne transformer ko pixels dekh kar words likhna sikhaya. Ab ulta kaam: diffusion models words se images paint karte hain. Yeh autoregressive transformer nahi hain — pixels ko left-to-right predict nahi karte. Yeh pure static (noise) se shuru karte hain aur use step by step refine karte hain, jab tak text description se match karti hui coherent image na ban jaye. Fine-tuning ka playbook wahi rehta hai — LoRA, trainer, data curation — sirf math aur output alag hai.

Transformer se image kyun nahi banate?

Pixel ko token maan kar raster order me predict karna try kiya gaya tha (PixelRNN / PixelCNN). Problem: 512×512 RGB image me 262,144 pixels × 3 channels = 786,432 sequential forward passes per image — bahut slow. Aur usse bura: decisions irreversible hain — top-left corner lock ho jata hai, chahe baad me pata chale woh galat tha. Diffusion ulta approach leta hai: saare pixels ek saath, pure noise se shuru karo, aur har refinement step me har pixel ko simultaneously thoda cleaner karo. Kuch dozen steps me static se corgi ban jata hai.

Forward process — controlled destruction

Kisi image me thoda Gaussian noise add karo — image pehchani ja sakti hai, bas static dikhta hai. Aur add karo, aur add karo — ant me sirf noise bachta hai. Yeh forward diffusion process hai, timestep t = 0 (no noise) se T = 1,000 (pure noise) tak, beta schedule par: β₁ = 0.00085 se β₁₀₀₀ = 0.012 tak. Noise ε ~ N(0,1) — har pixel ke liye bell curve se ek independent random number. t = 200 par image abhi pehchani ja sakti hai, t = 500 par sirf shape bachta hai, t = 800 par mostly noise, t = 1,000 par pure noise. Beta schedule isliye badhta hai taaki har timestep alag difficulty ka training signal de — fixed noise se zyada tar steps ya to trivially easy hote ya trivially impossible.

Reverse process — denoising

Model ko millions of (image, noisy version, noise amount) triples par train karo: noisy image + timestep dekh kar woh added noise predict kare. Loss simple MSE hai — predicted noise vs actual noise, same shape ka comparison. Inference par pure noise se shuru karo, model noise predict kare, scheduler uska ek fraction subtract kare, repeat — t = 999 se t = 0 tak. Network ne real images ki structure seekh li hai, isliye woh "guided hallucination" karta hai: text prompt se condition karo to hallucinated image prompt se match karti hai. Training me (xt, t, ε) examples ko schedule bhar randomly scatter karo, taaki model har step par effective ho.

Latent-space trick — 48× chhota

Pixel space me diffusion bahut slow hota: 512×512×3 image = 786,432 values. VAE use image ko 64×64×4 latent me compress kar deta hai — sirf 16,384 values, 48× kam. Saara diffusion math latent space me hota hai, aur ant me VAE decode karke wapas pixels banata hai. Latent ek learned compression hai — paas ke points similar dikhne wali images hote hain.

Is chapter ka arc: UNet (noise predict karne wala network), latent pipeline aur scheduler, phir full generation pipeline — aur wahan LoRA kahan lagta hai. Agle chapter me yahi knowledge DreamBooth aur style LoRA ban jayegi.

Yaad rakho: transformer "agle token" ko predict karta hai, diffusion "kitna noise hai" ko predict karta hai aur use subtract karta hai. Ek chhota sa badlav — aur image generation possible ho jata hai, kyunki har pixel har dusre pixel ke saath globally consistent rehta hai.
01_inspect_pipeline.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter12/code/01_inspect_pipeline.py

Inspect a Stable Diffusion pipeline at three levels of detail:

  1) The four components of the pipeline (text encoder, VAE, UNet,
     scheduler) and their parameter counts.
  2) The UNet's down/mid/up block structure with channel counts, so
     you can verify the layer-by-layer claims in section 12.5.1.
  3) A live trace of tensor shapes flowing through the UNet, so you
     can see the U-shape (64x64 -> 32x32 -> 16x16 -> 8x8 -> 16x16
     -> 32x32 -> 64x64) actually happening.

Setup:
    # Always upgrade diffusers and transformers together. Older diffusers
    # versions reference symbols (like FLAX_WEIGHTS_NAME) that newer
    # transformers releases removed, which produces import errors.
    pip install --upgrade \\
        "diffusers>=0.30" "transformers>=4.44" "accelerate>=0.30" \\
        "safetensors>=0.4" "huggingface_hub>=0.24" torch

Run:
    python 01_inspect_pipeline.py
"""

import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=dtype).to(device)


def count_params(module):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters())


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Pipeline components
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"\nLoaded pipeline: {MODEL_ID}")
print(f"Device: {device}, dtype: {dtype}\n")
print(f"{'Component':<18}{'Class':<32}{'Params':>14}")
print("-" * 64)
print(f"{'text_encoder':<18}{type(pipe.text_encoder).__name__:<32}"
      f"{count_params(pipe.text_encoder)/1e6:>12.1f} M")
print(f"{'tokenizer':<18}{type(pipe.tokenizer).__name__:<32}"
      f"{'-':>14}")
print(f"{'vae':<18}{type(pipe.vae).__name__:<32}"
      f"{count_params(pipe.vae)/1e6:>12.1f} M")
print(f"{'unet':<18}{type(pipe.unet).__name__:<32}"
      f"{count_params(pipe.unet)/1e6:>12.1f} M")
print(f"{'scheduler':<18}{type(pipe.scheduler).__name__:<32}"
      f"{'(config only)':>14}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) UNet structure: down blocks, mid block, up blocks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
unet = pipe.unet
print("\n\n=== UNet structure ===")
print(f"latent in:  {unet.conv_in.in_channels} channels")
print(f"latent out: {unet.conv_out.out_channels} channels")
print(f"block_out_channels: {list(unet.config.block_out_channels)}")


def has_attention(block):
    return getattr(block, "attentions", None) is not None and len(block.attentions) > 0


def fmt_block(idx, block, kind):
    name = type(block).__name__
    in_ch = block.resnets[0].in_channels
    out_ch = block.resnets[-1].out_channels
    attn = "yes" if has_attention(block) else "no "
    resampler = "downsamplers" if kind == "down" else "upsamplers"
    has_resampler = getattr(block, resampler, None) is not None
    flag = "↓" if (kind == "down" and has_resampler) else (
        "↑" if (kind == "up" and has_resampler) else "·")
    return (f"  [{idx}] {flag} {name:<26} "
            f"in={in_ch:>4}  out={out_ch:>4}  attn={attn}")


print(f"\nDown blocks ({len(unet.down_blocks)}):")
for i, block in enumerate(unet.down_blocks):
    print(fmt_block(i, block, "down"))

print(f"\nMid block:")
mid = unet.mid_block
print(f"  {'·':<3} {type(mid).__name__:<26} "
      f"in={mid.resnets[0].in_channels:>4}  "
      f"out={mid.resnets[-1].out_channels:>4}")

print(f"\nUp blocks ({len(unet.up_blocks)}):")
for i, block in enumerate(unet.up_blocks):
    print(fmt_block(i, block, "up"))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Trace tensor shapes through the UNet with forward hooks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n\n=== Tensor shape trace through the UNet ===")

trace = []


def make_hook(label):
    def hook(_module, _inputs, outputs):
        # Block outputs can be a tensor or a tuple of (hidden_states, skips, ...)
        primary = outputs[0] if isinstance(outputs, tuple) else outputs
        trace.append((label, tuple(primary.shape)))
    return hook


handles = []
for i, block in enumerate(unet.down_blocks):
    handles.append(block.register_forward_hook(make_hook(f"down[{i}]")))
handles.append(unet.mid_block.register_forward_hook(make_hook("mid")))
for i, block in enumerate(unet.up_blocks):
    handles.append(block.register_forward_hook(make_hook(f"up[{i}]")))

# Fake inputs at SD 1.5's native latent size and text embedding shape.
fake_latent = torch.zeros(1, 4, 64, 64, device=device, dtype=dtype)
fake_t = torch.tensor([500], device=device, dtype=torch.long)
fake_text = torch.zeros(1, 77, 768, device=device, dtype=dtype)

with torch.no_grad():
    _ = unet(fake_latent, fake_t, fake_text)

for h in handles:
    h.remove()

print(f"{'block':<10}{'output shape':<30}")
print("-" * 40)
for name, shape in trace:
    print(f"{name:<10}{str(shape):<30}")

print("\nThe spatial dims should walk 64 -> 32 -> 16 -> 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64.")
print("Channel counts should follow the block_out_channels you printed above.")
02_forward_noise.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter12/code/02_forward_noise.py

Visualise the forward diffusion process. Given an image, sample noisy
versions of it at several timesteps and save them as a horizontal strip.
This is the q(x_t | x_0) closed-form sampling formula in action.

x_t = sqrt(alpha_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1 - alpha_bar_t) * eps

Run:
    python 02_forward_noise.py path/to/photo.jpg
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from PIL import Image
from torchvision import transforms
from diffusers import DDPMScheduler

IMG_SIZE = 256
TIMESTEPS_TO_SHOW = [0, 100, 250, 500, 750, 999]


def load_image(path: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    img = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    tfm = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.Resize(IMG_SIZE),
        transforms.CenterCrop(IMG_SIZE),
        transforms.ToTensor(),                  # [0,1]
        transforms.Normalize([0.5]*3, [0.5]*3), # [-1,1]
    ])
    return tfm(img)  # (3, H, W)


def to_pil(x: torch.Tensor) -> Image.Image:
    x = (x.clamp(-1, 1) + 1) / 2.0
    arr = (x * 255).byte().permute(1, 2, 0).cpu().numpy()
    return Image.fromarray(arr)


def main(path: str) -> None:
    x0 = load_image(path)
    scheduler = DDPMScheduler(
        num_train_timesteps=1000,
        beta_schedule="scaled_linear",   # the SD-default
        beta_start=0.00085,
        beta_end=0.012,
    )

    frames = []
    for t in TIMESTEPS_TO_SHOW:
        # Sample one noise tensor per timestep so each step shows
        # a different realization, not a cumulative blur.
        eps = torch.randn_like(x0)
        timesteps = torch.tensor([t])
        xt = scheduler.add_noise(x0.unsqueeze(0), eps.unsqueeze(0), timesteps)[0]
        frames.append(to_pil(xt))

    strip = Image.new("RGB", (IMG_SIZE * len(frames), IMG_SIZE), "white")
    for i, f in enumerate(frames):
        strip.paste(f, (i * IMG_SIZE, 0))

    out = Path("forward_noise_strip.png")
    strip.save(out)
    print(f"Saved {out} — timesteps {TIMESTEPS_TO_SHOW}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python 02_forward_noise.py <image_path>")
        sys.exit(1)
    main(sys.argv[1])
03_generate_image.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter12/code/03_generate_image.py

Generate an image with Stable Diffusion 1.5 using a chosen scheduler
and a fixed seed for reproducibility. Useful for "before vs. after"
comparisons against a fine-tuned model.

Setup:
    pip install --upgrade \\
        "diffusers>=0.30" "transformers>=4.44" "accelerate>=0.30" \\
        "safetensors>=0.4" "huggingface_hub>=0.24" torch

Run:
    python 03_generate_image.py "a corgi astronaut on Mars, cinematic"
"""

import sys
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
SEED = 42
STEPS = 25
GUIDANCE = 7.5


def main(prompt: str, out_path: str = "out.png") -> None:
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=dtype)
    # Swap the slow default scheduler for a fast multistep solver.
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe = pipe.to(device)

    generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(SEED)

    image = pipe(
        prompt=prompt,
        num_inference_steps=STEPS,
        guidance_scale=GUIDANCE,
        generator=generator,
    ).images[0]

    image.save(out_path)
    print(f"Saved {out_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print('Usage: python 03_generate_image.py "your prompt"')
        sys.exit(1)
    main(sys.argv[1])
04_attach_lora.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter12/code/04_attach_lora.py

Attach a LoRA to Stable Diffusion's UNet using PEFT — the same library
you used in Chapters 7–8 for the language model. The target modules are
the attention projection layers (to_q, to_k, to_v, to_out.0), which is
where text conditioning enters the network.

This prints the parameter counts so you can see exactly how few weights
you'll actually be training compared to the full model.

Setup:
    pip install --upgrade \\
        "diffusers>=0.30" "transformers>=4.44" "accelerate>=0.30" \\
        "peft>=0.11" "safetensors>=0.4" "huggingface_hub>=0.24" torch

Run:
    python 04_attach_lora.py
"""

import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"


def count_trainable(module):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    torch_dtype=torch.float32,  # train in fp32 for stable gradients
)
unet = pipe.unet

total_before = sum(p.numel() for p in unet.parameters())
print(f"UNet total params:    {total_before/1e6:>10.2f} M")

# Freeze everything first; LoRA will toggle its own layers back on.
for p in unet.parameters():
    p.requires_grad_(False)

# LoRA on the attention projections — both self-attn and cross-attn
# layers share these names, so a single target_modules list covers both.
lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=8,
    lora_alpha=8,
    target_modules=["to_q", "to_k", "to_v", "to_out.0"],
    lora_dropout=0.0,
    bias="none",
)

unet_lora = get_peft_model(unet, lora_config)

trainable_after = count_trainable(unet_lora)
print(f"LoRA trainable params:{trainable_after/1e6:>10.2f} M "
      f"({100*trainable_after/total_before:.2f}% of UNet)")

# Sanity check: see one of the freshly attached LoRA layers
for name, module in unet_lora.named_modules():
    if "lora_A" in name:
        print("Example LoRA layer:", name)
        break
05_dreambooth_loop.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter12/code/05_dreambooth_loop.py

A minimal, readable DreamBooth-style training loop with LoRA. This is
the *core* of the training — not a production-grade script. It exists
so you can read every line and see exactly what's happening.

Inputs you supply:
- A folder of 3–8 photos of your subject (e.g. ./subject/*.jpg)
- An instance prompt that includes a rare token, e.g. "a photo of sks dog"
- An optional folder of class-prior images and a class prompt, e.g. "a photo of a dog"

Setup:
    pip install --upgrade \
        "diffusers>=0.30" "transformers>=4.44" "accelerate>=0.30" \
        "peft>=0.11" "safetensors>=0.4" "huggingface_hub>=0.24" torch torchvision

Run:
    python 05_dreambooth_loop.py \
        --subject_dir ./subject \
        --instance_prompt "a photo of sks dog" \
        --output_dir ./lora_out
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
from torchvision import transforms
from PIL import Image

from diffusers import (
    AutoencoderKL,
    DDPMScheduler,
    StableDiffusionPipeline,
    UNet2DConditionModel,
)
from transformers import CLIPTextModel, CLIPTokenizer
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
IMG_SIZE = 512


class SubjectDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, image_dir: Path, prompt: str, tokenizer):
        self.paths = sorted([p for p in image_dir.glob("*")
                             if p.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"}])
        if not self.paths:
            raise ValueError(f"No images in {image_dir}")
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.tfm = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.CenterCrop(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.5]*3, [0.5]*3),
        ])

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.paths) * 100  # epochs-via-repetition

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path = self.paths[idx % len(self.paths)]
        pixel = self.tfm(Image.open(path).convert("RGB"))
        tok = self.tokenizer(
            self.prompt,
            padding="max_length",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.tokenizer.model_max_length,
            return_tensors="pt",
        ).input_ids[0]
        return pixel, tok


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--subject_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--instance_prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output_dir", default="./lora_out")
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=800)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-4)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    # Load components individually so we can attach LoRA to the UNet only.
    tokenizer = CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="tokenizer")
    text_encoder = CLIPTextModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="text_encoder", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    vae = AutoencoderKL.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="vae", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="unet", torch_dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    noise_sched = DDPMScheduler.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="scheduler")

    # Freeze text encoder + VAE.
    for m in (text_encoder, vae):
        for p in m.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)

    # LoRA on the UNet's attention projections.
    for p in unet.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    lora_cfg = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=8,
                          target_modules=["to_q", "to_k", "to_v", "to_out.0"])
    unet = get_peft_model(unet, lora_cfg)
    unet.train()

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        [p for p in unet.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=args.lr)

    ds = SubjectDataset(Path(args.subject_dir), args.instance_prompt, tokenizer)
    loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=True, num_workers=2)

    step = 0
    for pixel, input_ids in loader:
        pixel = pixel.to(device, dtype=dtype)
        input_ids = input_ids.to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            # Encode pixels into the VAE latent and scale by SD's convention.
            latents = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.sample() * vae.config.scaling_factor
            encoder_hidden_states = text_encoder(input_ids.unsqueeze(0))[0]

        # Sample a random timestep and matching noise.
        bsz = latents.shape[0]
        t = torch.randint(0, noise_sched.config.num_train_timesteps,
                          (bsz,), device=device).long()
        noise = torch.randn_like(latents)
        noisy = noise_sched.add_noise(latents, noise, t)

        # Predict the noise. This is the entire learning signal.
        pred = unet(noisy.float(), t, encoder_hidden_states.float()).sample
        loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(pred.float(), noise.float())

        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()

        if step % 25 == 0:
            print(f"step {step:>4} | loss {loss.item():.4f}")
        step += 1
        if step >= args.steps:
            break

    out = Path(args.output_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    unet.save_pretrained(out)
    print(f"\nSaved LoRA adapter to {out.resolve()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
chapter12/code/06_load_adapter_and_generate.py

Apply a previously-trained LoRA adapter to a base Stable Diffusion
pipeline and generate samples with your rare-token prompt.

Setup:
    pip install --upgrade \\
        "diffusers>=0.30" "transformers>=4.44" "accelerate>=0.30" \\
        "peft>=0.11" "safetensors>=0.4" "huggingface_hub>=0.24" torch

Run:
    python 06_load_adapter_and_generate.py ./lora_out
"""

import sys
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
SEED = 7


def main(lora_path: str, prompt: str = "a photo of sks dog wearing a top hat") -> None:
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=dtype)
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe.load_lora_weights(lora_path)
    pipe = pipe.to(device)

    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(SEED)
    img = pipe(prompt, num_inference_steps=25, guidance_scale=7.5, generator=g).images[0]
    img.save("subject_generation.png")
    print("Saved subject_generation.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python 06_load_adapter_and_generate.py <lora_path> [prompt]")
        sys.exit(1)
    prompt = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "a photo of sks dog wearing a top hat"
    main(sys.argv[1], prompt)

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import io
import os

# Check if an image was uploaded in the previous cell
if 'uploaded' in globals() and uploaded:
    # Get the first (and likely only) uploaded filename
    filename = list(uploaded.keys())[0]
    img_data = uploaded[filename]

    # Open the image using PIL from the bytes data
    try:
        original_image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(img_data))
        # Convert to RGB to handle different image modes consistently
        if original_image.mode != 'RGB':
            original_image = original_image.convert('RGB')
        original_array = np.array(original_image)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error opening or converting image: {e}")
        print("Please ensure the uploaded file is a valid image.")
        exit()

    # Create a pure noise array of the same shape as the original image
    # This noise will be random values between 0-255
    pure_noise_array = np.random.randint(0, 256, original_array.shape, dtype=np.uint8)

    output_dir = "noisy_images"
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.makedirs(output_dir)
    print(f"Saving noisy images to: {output_dir}/")

    for step in range(1, 41): # 40 steps, from 1 to 40
        alpha = step / 40.0 # Blending factor, goes from 0.025 to 1.0

        # Blend the original image with the pure noise image
        # Convert to float for calculation to avoid overflow, then back to uint8
        blended_array = ( (1 - alpha) * original_array.astype(np.float32) +
                          alpha * pure_noise_array.astype(np.float32) )

        # Clip values to ensure they are within the valid 0-255 range for image pixels
        blended_array = np.clip(blended_array, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

        # Convert back to PIL Image
        noisy_image = Image.fromarray(blended_array)

        # Save the image
        output_filename = os.path.join(output_dir, f"noisy_image_step_{step:02d}.png")
        noisy_image.save(output_filename)
        # print(f"Saved {output_filename}") # Uncomment to see each save message

    print(f"\nImage noise addition complete. {step} images saved in the '{output_dir}' directory.")
else:
    print("No image was uploaded. Please run the previous cell to upload an image first.")

← Previous11.3 · Inference, Evaluation, Domains, and Troubleshooting→ Next12.1 · UNet, Latent Space, Text Encoder, and Schedulers
12.1Chapter 12 · Diffusion Models

UNet, Latent Space, Text Encoder, and Schedulers

Noise predict karne ka kaam UNet karta hai — U-shaped network jo input ko baar-baar downsample karke coarse representation banata hai, phir wapas original resolution tak upsample karta hai. Neeche jane se global context milta hai, upar aane se pixel-precise output — aur skip connections dono ko jodte hain, taaki fine detail (edges, textures) dobara invent na karni pade aur gradients bhi achhe se flow karen.

Stable Diffusion 1.5 — numbers ke saath

64×64×4 latent par chaar down blocks resolutions 64² → 32² → 16² → 8² banate hain, channels 320 / 640 / 1,280 / 1,280. Beech me mid-block (8×8) hai jahan sabse deep reasoning hota hai aur prompt ka global influence sabse strong hota hai. Phir up blocks wapas 64 tak le jate hain, har level par skip connection se corresponding down block ke features milte hain. Aakhir me output projection 64×64×320 ko wapas 64×64×4 predicted noise me badal deta hai. Tensor trace: 64 → 32 → 16 → 8 → 16 → 32 → 64 — wahi U-shape jisse naam aaya. Component sizes: text encoder 123.1M, VAE 83.7M, UNet 859.5M — UNet hi sabse bada hai, aur fine-tune me wahi touch hota hai. SD 1.5 ka UNet ~860M parameters, SDXL ka 2.6B.

Prompt aur timestep UNet me kaise ghuste hain?

Timestep sinusoidal embedding se aata hai (transformer ki position encoding jaisa) aur FiLM modulation se UNet ki har layer ko pata chalta hai ki kis timestep ko denoise kar rahe ho. Prompt cross-attention se aata hai: image features queries (Q) bante hain, text keys aur values (K, V) — har spatial location text se poochhta hai ki kaun sa word us par lagta hai. "Sunglasses" wali patch "sunglasses" token par max score karegi aur uska weighted blend apne features me kheench legi. Yeh wahi cross-attention hai jo VLM me thi, bas ulta direction me chal rahi hai.

Text encoder — CLIP, frozen rehta hai

SD 1.5 ka text encoder CLIP ViT-L/14 hai, 400M image-text pairs par train hua — prompt ko 77 tokens tak pad/cut karke 77 vectors (768 dimensions each) deta hai. SDXL do text encoders parallel use karta hai; naye models T5 use karte hain (behtar prompt adherence, zyada VRAM). Fine-tune me text encoder lagbhag hamesha frozen rehta hai — sirf do exceptions: rare-token training (DreamBooth, Textual Inversion) aur style-specific prompt tokens. 95% LoRA use cases me sirf UNet seekhta hai, aur prompt-image interaction cross-attention weights se hota hai — bilkul sahi jagah.

Schedulers — speed ka sawaal

Scheduler ke paas koi trainable parameters nahi hain — yeh pure math hai. Training time par woh batata hai ki timestep t par kitna noise add hua tha; inference par woh batata hai ki predicted noise se thoda kam noisy image kaise banani hai. DDPM ko 1,000 steps chahiye — bahut slow. DDIM ~50 steps, DPM++ / DPM-Solver 20–30, Euler 20–30 (Ancestral 30–40), UniPC 10–15. Training me DPM ya DDIM use karo (noise-prediction objective ke liye cleanest fit), inference me DPM++ ya UniPC par switch karo. Code me scheduler swap karne se 50-step generation (12–15 seconds) 25-step (6–8 seconds) me badal jata hai, quality me barely farak.

Yaad rakho: UNet me do cheezein ghusti hain — timestep (sinusoidal embedding + FiLM) aur prompt (cross-attention, 77×768 vectors). Scheduler sirf trajectory control karta hai, seekhta kuch nahi — phir bhi wahi inference ko 1,000 steps se 25 steps par le aata hai.

← Previous12 · Diffusion Models→ Next12.2 · The Full Pipeline, Guidance, and LoRA
12.2Chapter 12 · Diffusion Models

The Full Pipeline, Guidance, and LoRA

Ab saare pieces ko jod kar full pipeline dekhte hain. Stable Diffusion me ek generation me teen forward passes hote hain: text encoder prompt ko vectors me badalta hai, UNet 20 ya usse zyada passes me random latent ko clean latent me denoise karta hai, aur VAE decoder clean latent ko 512×512×3 RGB image me badal deta hai.

Full pipeline — chhe steps

  1. Tokenization: CLIP prompt ko 77 tokens me todta hai.
  2. Encoding: 77 tokens text encoder se guzar kar [77, 768] tensor (conditioning "c") banate hain.
  3. Noise sample: Gaussian noise se ek random latent zT banta hai.
  4. Denoise loop: 20–25 iterations (DPM++ par) — UNet noise predict karta hai, scheduler latent update karta hai.
  5. Decode: final latent z₀ VAE decoder se [3, 512, 512] pixel tensor banta hai.
  6. Save: pixels [0, 1] me clip karke [0, 255] par scale karo, image file save karo.

Code example: prompt "a corgi wearing sunglasses", seed 42, 20–25 inference steps, guidance scale 7.5 — seed pin karo to reproducibility milegi, badlo to wahi prompt par alag image. num_inference_steps zyada ho to quality thodi behtar, time linear zyada — DPM++ ke liye 20–25 sweet spot hai.

Classifier-free guidance — formula

εfinal = εuncond + scale × (εcond − εuncond). Training me 5–10% baar model ko empty prompt diya jata hai, taaki woh bina conditioning ke bhi generate kar sake. Inference par UNet har step do baar chalta hai: ek baar real prompt se (εcond), ek baar empty prompt se (εuncond). Scale = 1 ho to sirf conditional prediction milti hai; scale 7.5 ya zyada ho to "prompt ke saath" aur "prompt ke bina" ka farak exaggerate ho jata hai — image prompt ki taraf aggressively steer hoti hai. Cost 2× compute per step hai, lekin prompt adherence dramatically behtar hoti hai. Guidance scale 10+ par prompt se chipakna badhta hai lekin diversity aur naturalness kam hoti hai; 3–5 par creative latitude zyada; 7.5 broadly accepted default hai.

Negative prompts — underused tool

Unconditional path ka ek neat side effect: empty string ki jagah negative prompt pass karo — jo nahi chahiye woh likho ("blurry, low quality, extra limbs, watermark, text"). Wahi math ab generation ko negative prompt se door aur positive prompt ki taraf dhakel deta hai. "Extra fingers, malformed hands" human generations ko saaf karta hai, "text, watermark, signature" fake captions rokta hai. Fine-tuned LoRA ko base model se compare karte waqt negative prompt ko control karna zaroori hai, warna comparison fair nahi hoga.

Fine-tuning — LoRA UNet ki attention par

Har attention block me chaar projection matrices hain: to_q, to_k, to_v, to_out.0 — self-attention aur cross-attention dono me wahi chaar naam, isliye ek LoRA config dono ko cover karti hai. Rank 8–32 typical hai, 0.8M trainable parameters — UNet ke 859.52M ka sirf 0.09% — aur adapters 50–150 MB ke hote hain. Ek farak dhyaan do: language-model LoRA ke mukable yahan koi task_type nahi hota — UNet language model nahi hai, PEFT ke predefined tasks me se kisi se match nahi karta, isliye use chhod do aur PEFT generic wrapper use karega. 1% se kam weights, bilkul wahi jagah jahan image aur text interact karte hain — wahi naye subjects aur styles encode hote hain.

Yaad rakho: diffusion fine-tune ka mantra — LoRA UNet ki attention projections par, loss MSE predicted noise par, data image-caption pairs. Guidance scale 7.5 default, negative prompt hamesha use karo, aur LoRA compare karte waqt seed aur negative prompt dono pin karo.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 12 — Diffusion Models
← Previous12.1 · UNet, Latent Space, Text Encoder, and Schedulers→ Next13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
13Chapter 13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models

Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models

Chapter 12 me tumne diffusion model ko andar se dekha — frozen VAE, frozen text encoder, noise predict karta UNet, aur pixels banata scheduler. Ab us knowledge ko use karke asli me train karenge, ek hi consumer GPU par, end to end. Do bilkul alag outcomes: ek specific subject sikhana (tumhara dog, product, chehra) aur ek specific style sikhana (brand photography, illustrator ka haath, anime line art).

Do recipes, ek mechanism

Dono recipes me wahi LoRA UNet ki attention projections (to_q, to_k, to_v, to_out.0) par lagta hai, VAE aur text encoder frozen rehte hain, scheduler ke paas seekhne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi. Badalta hai sirf dataset ka shape aur captions:

  • Subject training — kya draw karna hai: ek hi cheez ki kai photos, sab ek rare token wale caption ke saath (jaise "sks dog") — model rare token ko us specific cheez se bind kar leta hai.
  • Style training — kaise draw karna hai: alag-alag subjects ki kai photos, sab ek hi visual idiom me — model alag token ko brushwork, palette, lighting aur composition se bind karta hai.

Subject training me data narrow hota hai aur class-prior set chahiye (warna model bhool jata hai ki aam dog kaisa dikhta hai). Style training me data broad hota hai aur koi class prior nahi — style ki "class" to poori visual duniya hai jo us lens se render hoti hai. Aksar dono ek saath chahiye hote hain — specific product, specific brand style me — aur practice me do alag adapters train karke inference par compose karna cleaner hota hai.

Chapter ka arc: pehle DreamBooth se subject, phir style LoRA se look, phir adapters ko compose karna aur deploy karna — aur ek quantitative evaluation harness jo bataye ki adapter ne sach me woh seekha jo tum chahte the.

Yaad rakho: diffusion fine-tune me sabse important cheez dataset ka shape hai — subject ke liye ek cheez ki kai photos, style ke liye kai cheezein, ek look. Architecture aur training loop dono recipes me same hain.
00_download_dog_example.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/00_download_dog_example.py

Download the canonical DreamBooth reference dataset, `diffusers/dog-example`,
from the Hugging Face Hub and stage it into a folder this chapter's training
scripts can read.

The dataset is 5 JPEG photos of one specific corgi (the same dog used in
the original DreamBooth paper). It's the standard "hello world" subject
for diffusion fine-tuning tutorials, which means you can compare your
training results against every other recipe on the internet that uses it.

After running this script, you'll have a `./dog_subject/` folder containing
the 5 reference photos and a ready-to-use `metadata.jsonl`. You can then
hand that folder to 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py via --subject_dir.

Run:
    python 00_download_dog_example.py --out_dir ./dog_subject
"""

import argparse
import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

# The dataset repo. This is a public, MIT-style licensed tutorial dataset.
REPO_ID = "diffusers/dog-example"
INSTANCE_PROMPT = "a photo of sks dog"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", default="./dog_subject",
                    help="where to stage the dataset")
    ap.add_argument("--instance_prompt", default=INSTANCE_PROMPT,
                    help="caption to attach to every subject photo")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Download the whole repo into the HF cache, then copy just the images out.
    print(f"downloading {REPO_ID} from the Hugging Face Hub...")
    cached = snapshot_download(repo_id=REPO_ID, repo_type="dataset")
    cached_path = Path(cached)

    # The dataset ships JPEGs at the root (and possibly under data/).
    images = sorted(cached_path.glob("*.jpeg")) + sorted(cached_path.glob("*.jpg"))
    if not images:
        images = sorted(cached_path.rglob("*.jpeg")) + sorted(cached_path.rglob("*.jpg"))
    if not images:
        raise SystemExit(f"no images found inside {cached_path}")

    rows = []
    for i, src in enumerate(images):
        dst = out / f"{i:02d}.jpg"
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
        rows.append({"file_name": dst.name, "text": args.instance_prompt})

    with (out / "metadata.jsonl").open("w") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    print(f"\nstaged {len(rows)} images in {out.resolve()}")
    print(f"instance prompt: {args.instance_prompt!r}")
    print("\nnext step:")
    print(f"  python 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py \\")
    print(f"      --subject_dir {out} \\")
    print(f"      --class_dir   ./class_dog \\")
    print(f"      --instance_prompt {args.instance_prompt!r} \\")
    print(f"      --class_prompt  'a photo of a dog' \\")
    print(f"      --out_dir     ./dog_lora")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
00b_generate_class_prior.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/00b_generate_class_prior.py

Generate a class-prior dataset for DreamBooth training.

Prior preservation needs ~200 images of the broader class your subject
belongs to ("dog" if you're training one specific dog, "lamp" if you're
training one specific lamp, etc.), generated by the BASE Stable Diffusion
model. Training on these alongside your subject images stops the model
from collapsing the whole concept of "dog" onto your specific dog.

This script does just that one thing. It's split out from the training
loop so you can:
- generate the class set once and reuse it across many training runs
- inspect the generated images and drop bad ones before training
- resume an interrupted generation (existing files are skipped)
- swap models or settings independently of training

Run:
    python 00b_generate_class_prior.py \
        --class_prompt "a photo of a dog" \
        --out_dir ./class_dog \
        --count 200

Tips:
- 200 images is the canonical number. You can get away with 100, but
  not with 50.
- 20 inference steps is enough for class-prior images. They don't need
  to be masterpieces; they just need to look like "a dog."
- This takes 10-15 minutes on a consumer GPU for 200 images at 512px.
  You only do it once per class.
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--class_prompt", required=True,
                    help='caption for class-prior images, e.g. "a photo of a dog"')
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", required=True,
                    help="where to write the generated class images")
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=200,
                    help="how many class-prior images to generate")
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=20,
                    help="inference steps per image (20 is plenty)")
    ap.add_argument("--guidance", type=float, default=7.0,
                    help="classifier-free guidance scale")
    ap.add_argument("--negative_prompt", default="",
                    help="optional negative prompt (e.g. 'blurry, watermark')")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0,
                    help="base seed; each image uses seed + index for variety")
    ap.add_argument("--model_id", default=MODEL_ID,
                    help="base SD model to generate FROM (must match the one"
                         " you'll fine-tune)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Find what's already on disk so we can resume.
    existing = sorted(p for p in out.glob("class_*.png"))
    start_idx = len(existing)
    if start_idx >= args.count:
        print(f"already have {start_idx} images in {out}; nothing to do")
        return
    if start_idx > 0:
        print(f"resuming: found {start_idx} existing images, "
              f"generating {args.count - start_idx} more")

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    if device != "cuda":
        print("WARNING: running on CPU. This will be very slow.")

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        args.model_id,
        torch_dtype=torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32,
        safety_checker=None,
    )
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe = pipe.to(device)
    pipe.set_progress_bar_config(disable=True)

    print(f"generating {args.count - start_idx} images "
          f"with prompt: {args.class_prompt!r}")

    for i in range(start_idx, args.count):
        # Each image gets a different seed so we get variety, not 200 copies.
        gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(args.seed + i)
        image = pipe(
            prompt=args.class_prompt,
            negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt or None,
            num_inference_steps=args.steps,
            guidance_scale=args.guidance,
            generator=gen,
        ).images[0]
        image.save(out / f"class_{i:04d}.png")
        if (i + 1) % 10 == 0 or i == args.count - 1:
            print(f"  {i + 1}/{args.count} generated")

    print(f"\ndone. {args.count} class-prior images in {out.resolve()}")
    print("\nnext step:")
    print(f"  python 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py \\")
    print(f"      --subject_dir ./dog_subject \\")
    print(f"      --class_dir   {out} \\")
    print(f"      --instance_prompt 'a photo of sks dog' \\")
    print(f"      --class_prompt   {args.class_prompt!r} \\")
    print(f"      --out_dir     ./dog_lora")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
01_curate_dataset.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/01_curate_dataset.py

Take a folder of raw images (either a style set with many subjects, or a
DreamBooth subject set with one subject) and produce a clean training set:
- resize to a target edge length (preserving aspect ratio, then center-crop
  to a square if you want a fixed shape)
- convert everything to RGB
- strip EXIF/metadata
- drop near-duplicates using a perceptual hash
- write a metadata.jsonl file with empty captions (caption step is separate)

For a DreamBooth subject set, pass --square because subjects benefit from
fixed-aspect crops centered on the subject.

Run:
    python 01_curate_dataset.py \
        --in_dir ./raw_images \
        --out_dir ./training_set \
        --size 512
"""

import argparse
import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageOps

EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp", ".bmp"}


def phash(img: Image.Image, hash_size: int = 16) -> int:
    """Tiny perceptual hash. Resize to NxN greyscale, threshold by mean,
    pack into an int. Good enough to catch obvious dupes."""
    g = img.convert("L").resize((hash_size, hash_size), Image.LANCZOS)
    pixels = list(g.getdata())
    avg = sum(pixels) / len(pixels)
    bits = 0
    for i, p in enumerate(pixels):
        if p > avg:
            bits |= 1 << i
    return bits


def hamming(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return bin(a ^ b).count("1")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--in_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=512)
    ap.add_argument("--square", action="store_true",
                    help="center-crop to a square; otherwise keep aspect ratio")
    ap.add_argument("--dup_threshold", type=int, default=6,
                    help="hamming distance below which two images are dupes")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    in_dir = Path(args.in_dir)
    out_dir = Path(args.out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    seen_hashes: list[int] = []
    rows: list[dict] = []
    dropped_dupes = 0

    paths = sorted([p for p in in_dir.glob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in EXTS])
    if not paths:
        raise SystemExit(f"No images in {in_dir}")

    for i, p in enumerate(paths):
        try:
            img = Image.open(p)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"skip {p.name}: cannot open ({e})")
            continue

        img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(img).convert("RGB")

        # dedupe
        h = phash(img)
        if any(hamming(h, s) < args.dup_threshold for s in seen_hashes):
            dropped_dupes += 1
            continue
        seen_hashes.append(h)

        # resize
        if args.square:
            img = ImageOps.fit(img, (args.size, args.size), Image.LANCZOS)
        else:
            img.thumbnail((args.size, args.size), Image.LANCZOS)

        # strip metadata by writing a fresh file
        out_name = f"{i:04d}.png"
        out_path = out_dir / out_name
        img.save(out_path, "PNG", optimize=True)

        rows.append({"file_name": out_name, "text": ""})

    # metadata.jsonl is the schema Hugging Face's ImageFolder loader expects.
    with (out_dir / "metadata.jsonl").open("w") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    print(f"kept   {len(rows)} images")
    print(f"dropped {dropped_dupes} duplicates")
    print(f"wrote  {out_dir / 'metadata.jsonl'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
chapter13/code/01b_generate_style_dataset.py

Generate a synthetic style training set using SDXL.

We use SDXL (not SD 1.5) deliberately. The style training script in
this chapter fine-tunes an SD 1.5 LoRA. If we generated this dataset
with SD 1.5 itself, we'd be training the model on its own outputs, and
the fine-tuned LoRA would be enforcing a look the base model already
makes. By generating with a stronger, architecturally different model
(SDXL has a larger UNet, two text encoders, and was trained on a
different dataset), the resulting LoRA actually transfers a new style
into SD 1.5's output distribution.

The flow this script implements:
1. SDXL renders each subject in a defined visual style at 1024x1024.
2. We resize each image to 512x512 (the resolution our SD 1.5 LoRA
   will train at).
3. We caption each image with a SHORT trigger phrase, not the long
   style description. The long description goes into generation;
   the short trigger is what the LoRA learns to bind to the look.
4. We write metadata.jsonl, ready for 04_train_style_lora.py.

VRAM: SDXL at fp16 with attention slicing fits in roughly 9 to 10 GB.
Comfortable on a Colab T4 (16 GB).

Time: about 12 to 15 seconds per image on a T4 at 30 inference steps,
so the default 80 subjects takes roughly 16 to 20 minutes end to end.

Run:
    python 01b_generate_style_dataset.py --out_dir ./style_set
"""

import argparse

from pathlib import Path

import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionXLPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0"

SUBJECTS = [

    "an ice cream cart on a sunny boardwalk",
]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", default="./style_set")
    ap.add_argument("--style_suffix", default=DEFAULT_STYLE_SUFFIX,
                    help="long descriptive style prompt sent to SDXL")
    ap.add_argument("--trigger", default=DEFAULT_TRIGGER,
                    help="short trigger phrase written into metadata.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--gen_size", type=int, default=1024,
                    help="SDXL generation resolution")
    ap.add_argument("--out_size", type=int, default=512,
                    help="downscaled resolution for SD 1.5 training")
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=30)
    ap.add_argument("--guidance", type=float, default=7.0)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0,
                    help="base seed; each image uses seed + index")
    ap.add_argument("--max_subjects", type=int, default=80,
                    help="generate only the first N subjects from the built-in list")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    if device != "cuda":
        print("WARNING: SDXL is impractical on CPU; this would take many hours.")

    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32
    print(f"loading {MODEL_ID} ({dtype})...")
    pipe = StableDiffusionXLPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID,
        torch_dtype=dtype,
        variant="fp16" if device == "cuda" else None,
        use_safetensors=True,
    )
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe = pipe.to(device)
    # Keep peak VRAM low enough for a T4.
    pipe.enable_attention_slicing()
    pipe.enable_vae_tiling()
    pipe.set_progress_bar_config(disable=True)

    subjects = SUBJECTS[:args.max_subjects]
    print(f"generating {len(subjects)} images at {args.gen_size}x{args.gen_size}, "
          f"saving at {args.out_size}x{args.out_size}")
    print(f"style suffix used for generation: {args.style_suffix!r}")
    print(f"trigger written into captions:   {args.trigger!r}\n")

    rows = []
    for i, subj in enumerate(subjects):
        prompt = f"{subj}, {args.style_suffix}"
        gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(args.seed + i)
        img = pipe(
            prompt=prompt,
            negative_prompt="blurry, low quality, watermark, text, signature, "
                            "deformed, extra limbs",
            num_inference_steps=args.steps,
            guidance_scale=args.guidance,
            width=args.gen_size,
            height=args.gen_size,
            generator=gen,
        ).images[0]
        # Downscale to SD 1.5's training resolution.
        if args.out_size != args.gen_size:
            img = img.resize((args.out_size, args.out_size), Image.LANCZOS)
        out_path = out / f"{i:03d}.png"
        img.save(out_path)
        # Caption uses the short trigger, not the long style suffix.
        rows.append({
            "file_name": out_path.name,
            "text": f"{subj}, {args.trigger}",
        })
        if (i + 1) % 5 == 0 or i == len(subjects) - 1:
            print(f"  {i+1}/{len(subjects)} generated")

    with (out / "metadata.jsonl").open("w") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    print(f"\nWrote {len(rows)} style training images to {out.resolve()}")
    print(f"  Generated with SDXL at {args.gen_size}x{args.gen_size}")
    print(f"  Downscaled to {args.out_size}x{args.out_size}")
    print(f"  Style trigger in captions: {args.trigger!r}")
    print("\nBefore training, hold out ~10% of these for evaluation:")
    print(f"  mkdir -p {out}_holdout && "
          f"mv {out}/00[0-7].png {out}_holdout/")
    print("\nThen train:")
    print(f"  python 04_train_style_lora.py \\")
    print(f"      --data_dir {out} \\")
    print(f"      --out_dir  ./mybrand_lora \\")
    print(f"      --steps 1500 --rank 16 --lr 1e-4")


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""
chapter13/code/02_caption_with_blip.py

Auto-caption every image in a curated style dataset using BLIP-2, then
append a style trigger phrase. The trigger is what the LoRA will bind
the style vocabulary to. Pick something the base model doesn't already
recognize: 'in mybrand style', 'awxstyle illustration', etc.

Notes:
- Describe the SUBJECT, not the style. The model already has a strong
  prior for words like 'watercolor' or 'oil painting'. If your captions
  contain those phrases the LoRA learns 'subject + watercolor' instead
  of 'subject + your trigger'.
- The trigger goes at the end so the rest of the caption stays general.

Run:
    python 02_caption_with_blip.py \
        --dir ./style_set \
        --trigger "in mybrand style"
"""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import Blip2Processor, Blip2ForConditionalGeneration

MODEL_ID = "Salesforce/blip2-opt-2.7b"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dir", required=True, help="curated dataset folder")
    ap.add_argument("--trigger", required=True, help="style trigger phrase")
    ap.add_argument("--prompt_template",
                    default="Question: describe the subject of this photo in one short phrase. Answer:",
                    help="BLIP-2 prompt; we only want the subject, not the style")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    proc = Blip2Processor.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
    model = Blip2ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=dtype).to(device)
    model.eval()

    folder = Path(args.dir)
    meta_path = folder / "metadata.jsonl"
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing {meta_path}; run the curation script first")

    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in meta_path.open()]

    for row in rows:
        img = Image.open(folder / row["file_name"]).convert("RGB")
        inputs = proc(images=img, text=args.prompt_template,
                      return_tensors="pt").to(device, dtype=dtype)
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=30)
        subject = proc.tokenizer.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)
        subject = subject.replace(args.prompt_template, "").strip().rstrip(".").lower()

        # Compose the final caption.
        row["text"] = f"{subject}, {args.trigger}"

    with meta_path.open("w") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    # Print a few samples so you can sanity-check the captions.
    print("Sample captions:")
    for row in rows[:5]:
        print(f"  {row['file_name']}: {row['text']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
03_train_dreambooth_lora.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/03_train_dreambooth_lora.py

Train a DreamBooth LoRA on Stable Diffusion 1.5. This script teaches the
model a SINGLE subject (your dog, your product, your face). It is the
sibling of 04_train_style_lora.py, which teaches a visual style.

Two ideas drive DreamBooth:
1. Rare-token binding. Use a token the model has almost never seen
   (e.g. "sks") so that fine-tuning can bind your subject's visual
   features to that token without fighting an existing prior.
2. Prior preservation. Generate ~200 images of the broader class
   (e.g. "a photo of a dog") with the base model and train on them
   alongside your subject images. This prevents the model from
   collapsing the general concept onto your specific subject.

Inputs:
    --subject_dir       folder of 3-8 subject photos (any size). The easiest
                        way to populate this is to run 00_download_dog_example.py,
                        which stages the canonical diffusers/dog-example
                        dataset (5 photos of one corgi) for you.
    --class_dir         folder of ~200 auto-generated class images. If empty,
                        this script will populate it on first run.
    --instance_prompt   caption for the subject images,
                        e.g. "a photo of sks dog"
    --class_prompt      caption for the class-prior images,
                        e.g. "a photo of a dog"

Outputs:
    --out_dir           the trained LoRA adapter, saved as safetensors.

Run (with the dog-example dataset):
    python 00_download_dog_example.py --out_dir ./dog_subject
    python 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py \
        --subject_dir ./dog_subject \
        --class_dir   ./class_dog \
        --instance_prompt "a photo of sks dog" \
        --class_prompt "a photo of a dog" \
        --out_dir     ./dog_lora \
        --steps 1200
"""

import argparse
import math
from collections import deque
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
from torchvision import transforms
from PIL import Image

from diffusers import (
    AutoencoderKL,
    DDPMScheduler,
    StableDiffusionPipeline,
    UNet2DConditionModel,
)
from transformers import CLIPTextModel, CLIPTokenizer
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from peft.utils import get_peft_model_state_dict
from safetensors.torch import save_file

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
IMG_SIZE = 512


class CaptionedFolderDataset(Dataset):
    """Read every image in a folder and pair each with a fixed caption."""

    def __init__(self, folder: Path, prompt: str, tokenizer, repeat: int = 1):
        self.paths = sorted([p for p in folder.glob("*")
                             if p.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"}])
        if not self.paths:
            raise ValueError(f"no images in {folder}")
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.repeat = repeat
        self.tfm = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.CenterCrop(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.5] * 3, [0.5] * 3),
        ])

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.paths) * self.repeat

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path = self.paths[idx % len(self.paths)]
        pixel = self.tfm(Image.open(path).convert("RGB"))
        ids = self.tokenizer(
            self.prompt,
            padding="max_length",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.tokenizer.model_max_length,
            return_tensors="pt",
        ).input_ids[0]
        return pixel, ids


def maybe_generate_class_images(class_dir: Path, class_prompt: str,
                                target_count: int, device: str):
    """If the class folder is empty, generate prior images using the base model.
    Skip if the folder already has enough images."""
    class_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    existing = sorted(p for p in class_dir.glob("*.png"))
    if len(existing) >= target_count:
        print(f"class folder already has {len(existing)} images; skipping generation")
        return
    print(f"generating {target_count - len(existing)} class images for "
          f"prior preservation ({class_prompt!r})")
    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None).to(device)
    pipe.set_progress_bar_config(disable=True)
    for i in range(len(existing), target_count):
        img = pipe(class_prompt, num_inference_steps=20).images[0]
        img.save(class_dir / f"class_{i:04d}.png")
    del pipe
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()


def build_validation_set(loader, n, vae, text_encoder, scheduler,
                          device, dtype, seed=12345):
    """Pre-cache N (latent, text-embedding, timestep, noise) tuples for clean
    periodic evaluation. The variance from random t and random noise sampling
    is the dominant noise floor in diffusion training loss; fixing those two
    things across evaluations turns the eval loss into a clean monotonic-ish
    signal that can actually be plotted."""
    g_cpu = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
    items = []
    it = iter(loader)
    for _ in range(n):
        try:
            pixel, ids = next(it)
        except StopIteration:
            it = iter(loader)
            pixel, ids = next(it)
        pixel = pixel.to(device, dtype=dtype)
        ids = ids.to(device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            # .mode() instead of .sample() removes the VAE's stochasticity.
            latent = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.mode() * vae.config.scaling_factor
            txt = text_encoder(ids)[0]
        t = torch.randint(0, scheduler.config.num_train_timesteps,
                          (1,), generator=g_cpu).long().to(device)
        noise = torch.randn(latent.shape, generator=g_cpu,
                            dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
        items.append({"latent": latent.detach(),
                      "txt": txt.detach(),
                      "t": t,
                      "noise": noise.detach()})
    return items


def save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, save_dir):
    """Save the PEFT-wrapped UNet's LoRA in diffusers-native format.

    This avoids two failure modes:

    1) `unet.save_pretrained()` writes PEFT-format adapters whose key names
       and adapter_config.json paths confuse `pipe.load_lora_weights()`.
    2) `diffusers.utils.convert_state_dict_to_diffusers` is supposed to strip
       PEFT's `base_model.model.` prefix and the `.default.` adapter-name
       segment, but its behavior varies across diffusers versions. On some
       installs it leaves the prefix in place, which makes inference fail
       with a "Target modules ... not found in the base model" error.

    To sidestep both, this helper rewrites the keys explicitly and writes the
    safetensors file directly. After saving, `save_dir` contains exactly one
    file (`pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors`) whose key naming convention is
    the one `pipe.load_lora_weights()` expects: each key starts with `unet.`,
    contains no `base_model.model.`, and has no `.default.` adapter-name
    segment.
    """
    save_dir = Path(save_dir)
    save_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Remove any pre-existing adapter files so there's only one canonical
    # source of weights left when we're done. This covers both the PEFT-native
    # format (`adapter_*`) and the diffusers-native format
    # (`pytorch_lora_weights.*`), in case the directory was used by a prior run.
    for stale in [
        "adapter_config.json",
        "adapter_model.safetensors",
        "adapter_model.bin",
        "pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors",
        "pytorch_lora_weights.bin",
    ]:
        (save_dir / stale).unlink(missing_ok=True)

    raw = get_peft_model_state_dict(unet)

    cleaned = {}
    for k, v in raw.items():
        new_k = k
        # 1) Strip PEFT's wrapper prefix.
        if new_k.startswith("base_model.model."):
            new_k = new_k[len("base_model.model."):]
        # 2) Strip the adapter-name segment if PEFT inserted it.
        new_k = new_k.replace(".lora_A.default.weight", ".lora_A.weight")
        new_k = new_k.replace(".lora_B.default.weight", ".lora_B.weight")
        # 3) Add the diffusers `unet.` prefix.
        cleaned[f"unet.{new_k}"] = v

    # Defensive sanity check: anything that still looks PEFT-shaped is a bug.
    bad = [k for k in cleaned if "base_model" in k or ".default." in k]
    if bad:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Key cleanup failed; {len(bad)} keys still PEFT-shaped. "
            f"Example: {bad[0]}")

    save_file(cleaned, str(save_dir / "pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors"))

    # Print a few sample keys so you can verify the format from the run log.
    samples = list(cleaned.keys())[:3]
    print(f"  wrote {len(cleaned)} tensors to "
          f"{save_dir / 'pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors'}")
    for s in samples:
        print(f"    key: {s}")


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate(val_items, unet, scheduler):
    """Mean MSE over the fixed validation set. Deterministic for a given UNet."""
    unet.eval()
    losses = []
    for item in val_items:
        noisy = scheduler.add_noise(item["latent"].float(),
                                    item["noise"], item["t"])
        pred = unet(noisy, item["t"], item["txt"].float()).sample
        losses.append(F.mse_loss(pred.float(), item["noise"]).item())
    unet.train()
    return sum(losses) / len(losses)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--subject_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--class_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--instance_prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--class_prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=1200)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--prior_weight", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--class_count", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--log_window", type=int, default=50,
                    help="length of the moving-average window for loss logs")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint_every", type=int, default=300,
                    help="save an intermediate adapter every N steps; 0 disables")
    ap.add_argument("--val_size", type=int, default=32,
                    help="number of fixed (image,t,noise) tuples for validation")
    ap.add_argument("--eval_every", type=int, default=100,
                    help="run validation every N steps; 0 disables")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    # Auto-generate class-prior images if needed.
    maybe_generate_class_images(
        Path(args.class_dir), args.class_prompt, args.class_count, device)

    tokenizer = CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="tokenizer")
    text_encoder = CLIPTextModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="text_encoder", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    vae = AutoencoderKL.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="vae", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="unet", torch_dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    noise_sched = DDPMScheduler.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="scheduler")

    for m in (text_encoder, vae):
        for p in m.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)
    for p in unet.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)

    # Subject training is a narrow concept; a small rank is enough.
    lora_cfg = LoraConfig(
        r=args.rank,
        lora_alpha=args.rank,
        target_modules=["to_q", "to_k", "to_v", "to_out.0"],
        lora_dropout=0.0,
        bias="none",
    )
    unet = get_peft_model(unet, lora_cfg)
    unet.train()

    trainable = [p for p in unet.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    print(f"trainable params: {sum(p.numel() for p in trainable)/1e6:.2f}M")

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(trainable, lr=args.lr)

    # repeat=1 here; the outer epoch loop below handles re-iteration.
    subj_ds = CaptionedFolderDataset(
        Path(args.subject_dir), args.instance_prompt, tokenizer, repeat=1)
    prior_ds = CaptionedFolderDataset(
        Path(args.class_dir), args.class_prompt, tokenizer)

    subj_loader = DataLoader(subj_ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=True, num_workers=2)
    prior_loader = DataLoader(prior_ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=True, num_workers=2)
    prior_iter = iter(prior_loader)

    # Build a fixed validation set so we can report a low-variance loss curve
    # that's actually plottable. The dominant noise in per-step loss comes
    # from t-sampling and noise-sampling; freezing both removes it.
    val_items = None
    if args.eval_every > 0 and args.val_size > 0:
        # Use a small sequential loader so we always get the same images first.
        val_loader = DataLoader(subj_ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=False, num_workers=0)
        val_items = build_validation_set(
            val_loader, args.val_size, vae, text_encoder, noise_sched,
            device, dtype, seed=args.seed + 1)
        print(f"built validation set of {len(val_items)} fixed (image,t,noise) tuples")

    # An "epoch" here is one full pass over the (already-repeated) subject set.
    # We wrap the loader in an outer loop so training can keep going past one
    # epoch worth of samples. Without this, the for-loop would exit silently
    # the moment subj_loader exhausts, regardless of --steps.
    samples_per_epoch = max(1, len(subj_loader))
    epochs = math.ceil(args.steps / samples_per_epoch)
    print(f"requested {args.steps} steps; subj samples/epoch={samples_per_epoch}; "
          f"running {epochs} epoch(s)")

    # Rolling windows so we can log meaningful loss averages instead of the
    # wildly noisy per-step values. Diffusion training samples a random
    # timestep per step; per-step loss bounces around accordingly.
    subj_win = deque(maxlen=args.log_window)
    prior_win = deque(maxlen=args.log_window)

    step = 0
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        for pixel_s, ids_s in subj_loader:
            try:
                pixel_p, ids_p = next(prior_iter)
            except StopIteration:
                prior_iter = iter(prior_loader)
                pixel_p, ids_p = next(prior_iter)

            pixel = torch.cat([pixel_s, pixel_p]).to(device, dtype=dtype)
            ids = torch.cat([ids_s, ids_p]).to(device)

            with torch.no_grad():
                latents = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.sample() * vae.config.scaling_factor
                txt = text_encoder(ids)[0]

            bsz = latents.shape[0]
            t = torch.randint(0, noise_sched.config.num_train_timesteps,
                              (bsz,), device=device).long()
            noise = torch.randn_like(latents)
            noisy = noise_sched.add_noise(latents, noise, t)

            pred = unet(noisy.float(), t, txt.float()).sample

            # First half of the batch is the subject; second half is the class prior.
            pred_subj, pred_prior = pred.chunk(2, dim=0)
            noise_subj, noise_prior = noise.chunk(2, dim=0)

            loss_subj = F.mse_loss(pred_subj.float(), noise_subj.float())
            loss_prior = F.mse_loss(pred_prior.float(), noise_prior.float())
            loss = loss_subj + args.prior_weight * loss_prior

            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()

            subj_win.append(loss_subj.item())
            prior_win.append(loss_prior.item())

            if step % 25 == 0:
                # Moving-average loss is much more informative than per-step.
                subj_avg = sum(subj_win) / len(subj_win)
                prior_avg = sum(prior_win) / len(prior_win)
                print(f"step {step:>4} | subj {loss_subj.item():.4f} "
                      f"(avg{len(subj_win):>3} {subj_avg:.4f}) | "
                      f"prior {loss_prior.item():.4f} "
                      f"(avg{len(prior_win):>3} {prior_avg:.4f})")

            step += 1

            # Periodic fixed-validation-set evaluation. This is the clean
            # signal you should actually plot; per-step training loss is
            # too noisy to be useful, even with a 50-step moving average.
            if (val_items is not None and args.eval_every > 0
                    and step > 0 and step % args.eval_every == 0):
                val_loss = evaluate(val_items, unet, noise_sched)
                print(f"  -> val_loss @ step {step}: {val_loss:.4f}")

            # Periodic checkpoints so you can recover an earlier adapter
            # if the run starts overfitting before --steps is reached.
            if (args.checkpoint_every > 0 and step > 0
                    and step % args.checkpoint_every == 0 and step < args.steps):
                ckpt = Path(args.out_dir) / f"checkpoint-{step}"
                save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, ckpt)
                print(f"  -> saved checkpoint to {ckpt}")

            if step >= args.steps:
                break
        if step >= args.steps:
            break

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, out)
    print(f"\nSaved final LoRA adapter to {out.resolve()} after {step} steps")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
