"""
chapter13/code/03b_train_textual_inversion.py

Textual Inversion is the lightest-weight diffusion fine-tuning recipe.
You don't change any model weights at all. You only learn the embedding
for a single new token that the text encoder can then use.

The result is a ~3 KB file containing one 768-dimensional vector (SD 1.5)
or two vectors (SDXL, which has two text encoders). It's perfectly
composable with everything else, never damages the base model, and can
be shared and stacked freely.

The trade-off is fidelity: because you only get a single embedding to
work with, complex subjects (faces, products with fine detail) won't
look as close to the originals as a DreamBooth LoRA would.

Run:
    python 03b_train_textual_inversion.py \
        --subject_dir ./subject \
        --placeholder "<my-dog>" \
        --initializer "dog" \
        --out_dir ./my_dog_ti \
        --steps 3000
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
from torchvision import transforms
from PIL import Image
from safetensors.torch import save_file

from diffusers import AutoencoderKL, DDPMScheduler, UNet2DConditionModel
from transformers import CLIPTextModel, CLIPTokenizer

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
IMG_SIZE = 512

TEMPLATES = [
    "a photo of {}",
    "a rendering of {}",
    "a cropped photo of {}",
    "a close-up photo of {}",
    "a bright photo of {}",
    "a photo of one {}",
    "a clean photo of {}",
]


class TextualInversionDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, folder, placeholder, tokenizer):
        self.paths = sorted([p for p in folder.glob("*")
                             if p.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"}])
        self.placeholder = placeholder
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.tfm = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.CenterCrop(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.5] * 3, [0.5] * 3),
        ])

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.paths) * 100  # epochs-via-repetition

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path = self.paths[idx % len(self.paths)]
        pixel = self.tfm(Image.open(path).convert("RGB"))
        template = TEMPLATES[idx % len(TEMPLATES)]
        caption = template.format(self.placeholder)
        ids = self.tokenizer(
            caption,
            padding="max_length",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.tokenizer.model_max_length,
            return_tensors="pt",
        ).input_ids[0]
        return pixel, ids


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--subject_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--placeholder", required=True,
                    help="new token to learn, e.g. '<my-dog>'")
    ap.add_argument("--initializer", required=True,
                    help="existing token to initialize from, e.g. 'dog'")
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=3000)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=5e-4)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    tokenizer = CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="tokenizer")
    text_encoder = CLIPTextModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="text_encoder", torch_dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    vae = AutoencoderKL.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="vae", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="unet", torch_dtype=dtype).to(device).eval()
    noise_sched = DDPMScheduler.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="scheduler")

    # Add the new placeholder token. This grows the tokenizer's vocabulary
    # by 1 and adds one new row to the text encoder's embedding matrix.
    num_added = tokenizer.add_tokens(args.placeholder)
    if num_added != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"placeholder {args.placeholder} already exists in vocab")

    placeholder_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(args.placeholder)
    init_id = tokenizer.encode(args.initializer, add_special_tokens=False)
    if len(init_id) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"initializer must be a single token; "
            f"'{args.initializer}' is {len(init_id)} tokens")
    init_id = init_id[0]

    text_encoder.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))
    embeds = text_encoder.get_input_embeddings()
    with torch.no_grad():
        embeds.weight[placeholder_id] = embeds.weight[init_id].clone()

    # Freeze everything except the input embedding matrix.
    for p in unet.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    for p in vae.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    for p in text_encoder.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    embeds.weight.requires_grad_(True)

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW([embeds.weight], lr=args.lr)

    ds = TextualInversionDataset(Path(args.subject_dir), args.placeholder, tokenizer)
    loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=True, num_workers=2)

    step = 0
    for pixel, input_ids in loader:
        pixel = pixel.to(device, dtype=dtype)
        input_ids = input_ids.to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            latents = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.sample() * vae.config.scaling_factor

        # The forward pass through the text encoder MUST include the embedding
        # layer in the computation graph, so we do NOT wrap text_encoder in no_grad.
        encoder_hidden_states = text_encoder(input_ids)[0]

        t = torch.randint(0, noise_sched.config.num_train_timesteps,
                          (1,), device=device).long()
        noise = torch.randn_like(latents)
        noisy = noise_sched.add_noise(latents, noise, t)

        pred = unet(noisy, t, encoder_hidden_states.to(dtype)).sample
        loss = F.mse_loss(pred.float(), noise.float())

        loss.backward()

        # CRUCIAL: zero out gradients for every OTHER token in the embedding
        # matrix. We only want to update the one row we added.
        with torch.no_grad():
            grad = embeds.weight.grad
            mask = torch.zeros_like(grad)
            mask[placeholder_id] = 1
            grad.mul_(mask)

        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()

        if step % 100 == 0:
            print(f"step {step:>5} | loss {loss.item():.4f}")
        step += 1
        if step >= args.steps:
            break

    # Save just the one learned vector.
    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    learned = {args.placeholder: embeds.weight[placeholder_id].detach().cpu()}
    save_file(learned, out / "learned_embeds.safetensors")
    print(f"\nSaved learned embedding to {out / 'learned_embeds.safetensors'}")
    print(f"File size: {(out / 'learned_embeds.safetensors').stat().st_size} bytes")
    print(f"Load at inference with pipe.load_textual_inversion(out_dir)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
04_train_style_lora.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/04_train_style_lora.py

Train a style LoRA on top of Stable Diffusion 1.5. This script is the
DreamBooth loop from Chapter 12 with the prior-preservation pieces
removed and the dataset broadened from a single subject to many subjects
sharing a single visual style.

Inputs:
    --data_dir : a folder containing PNG/JPG files plus a metadata.jsonl
                 where each row is {"file_name": "...", "text": "..."}.
                 (Produced by 01b_generate_style_dataset.py, or by
                 01_curate_dataset.py + 02_caption_with_blip.py for your
                 own real-world style set.)

Outputs:
    --out_dir : the trained LoRA adapter, saved as a single
                pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors file in diffusers-native
                key format.

Defaults are tuned for a ~100-image dataset on a single 16 GB GPU.

Logging:
    Diffusion training loss is intrinsically noisy because every step
    samples a random timestep t. We log three things every 25 steps:
      - the raw per-step loss (for completeness)
      - a 50-step moving-average loss (less noisy)
    And every --eval_every steps:
      - val_loss on a fixed set of (image, t, noise) tuples (the clean
        signal you should actually plot)

Run:
    python 04_train_style_lora.py \
        --data_dir ./style_set \
        --out_dir ./mybrand_lora \
        --steps 1500 \
        --lr 1e-4 \
        --rank 16
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
from collections import deque
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
from torchvision import transforms
from PIL import Image

from diffusers import (
    AutoencoderKL,
    DDPMScheduler,
    UNet2DConditionModel,
)
from transformers import CLIPTextModel, CLIPTokenizer
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from peft.utils import get_peft_model_state_dict
from safetensors.torch import save_file

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
IMG_SIZE = 512


class StyleDataset(Dataset):
    """One image, one caption per item. Caption already includes the trigger."""

    def __init__(self, folder: Path, tokenizer):
        meta = (folder / "metadata.jsonl")
        if not meta.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(meta)
        self.rows = [json.loads(line) for line in meta.open()]
        self.folder = folder
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.tfm = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.CenterCrop(IMG_SIZE),
            transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.5] * 3, [0.5] * 3),
        ])

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        row = self.rows[idx]
        img = Image.open(self.folder / row["file_name"]).convert("RGB")
        pixel = self.tfm(img)
        ids = self.tokenizer(
            row["text"],
            padding="max_length",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=self.tokenizer.model_max_length,
            return_tensors="pt",
        ).input_ids[0]
        return pixel, ids


def build_validation_set(loader, n, vae, text_encoder, scheduler,
                          device, dtype, seed=12345):
    """Pre-cache N (latent, text-embedding, timestep, noise) tuples for clean
    periodic evaluation. The variance from random t and random noise sampling
    is the dominant noise floor in diffusion training loss; fixing those two
    things across evaluations turns the eval loss into a clean signal that
    can actually be plotted."""
    g_cpu = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
    items = []
    it = iter(loader)
    for _ in range(n):
        try:
            pixel, ids = next(it)
        except StopIteration:
            it = iter(loader)
            pixel, ids = next(it)
        pixel = pixel.to(device, dtype=dtype)
        ids = ids.to(device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            # .mode() instead of .sample() removes the VAE's stochasticity.
            latent = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.mode() * vae.config.scaling_factor
            txt = text_encoder(ids)[0]
        t = torch.randint(0, scheduler.config.num_train_timesteps,
                          (1,), generator=g_cpu).long().to(device)
        noise = torch.randn(latent.shape, generator=g_cpu,
                            dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
        items.append({"latent": latent.detach(),
                      "txt": txt.detach(),
                      "t": t,
                      "noise": noise.detach()})
    return items


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate(val_items, unet, scheduler):
    """Mean MSE over the fixed validation set. Deterministic for a given UNet."""
    unet.eval()
    losses = []
    for item in val_items:
        noisy = scheduler.add_noise(item["latent"].float(),
                                    item["noise"], item["t"])
        pred = unet(noisy, item["t"], item["txt"].float()).sample
        losses.append(F.mse_loss(pred.float(), item["noise"]).item())
    unet.train()
    return sum(losses) / len(losses)


def save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, save_dir):
    """Save the PEFT-wrapped UNet's LoRA in diffusers-native format.

    Bypasses both `unet.save_pretrained()` (which writes PEFT-format files
    that confuse pipe.load_lora_weights) and the diffusers
    `convert_state_dict_to_diffusers` helper (which behaves differently
    across versions). Instead, we explicitly rewrite the keys ourselves:
    strip PEFT's `base_model.model.` prefix, strip the `.default.` adapter
    name segment, and add diffusers' `unet.` prefix.

    Also clears any stale adapter files in `save_dir` first, so the
    directory ends up with a single canonical adapter file. Otherwise an
    older training run's `adapter_config.json` can shadow the new save
    and confuse the loader.
    """
    save_dir = Path(save_dir)
    save_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    for stale in [
        "adapter_config.json",
        "adapter_model.safetensors",
        "adapter_model.bin",
        "pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors",
        "pytorch_lora_weights.bin",
    ]:
        (save_dir / stale).unlink(missing_ok=True)

    raw = get_peft_model_state_dict(unet)

    cleaned = {}
    for k, v in raw.items():
        new_k = k
        if new_k.startswith("base_model.model."):
            new_k = new_k[len("base_model.model."):]
        new_k = new_k.replace(".lora_A.default.weight", ".lora_A.weight")
        new_k = new_k.replace(".lora_B.default.weight", ".lora_B.weight")
        cleaned[f"unet.{new_k}"] = v

    bad = [k for k in cleaned if "base_model" in k or ".default." in k]
    if bad:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Key cleanup failed; {len(bad)} keys still PEFT-shaped. "
            f"Example: {bad[0]}")

    save_file(cleaned, str(save_dir / "pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors"))

    samples = list(cleaned.keys())[:3]
    print(f"  wrote {len(cleaned)} tensors to "
          f"{save_dir / 'pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors'}")
    for s in samples:
        print(f"    key: {s}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--data_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=1500)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--batch_size", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--grad_accum", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--alpha", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--log_window", type=int, default=50,
                    help="length of the moving-average window for loss logs")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint_every", type=int, default=300,
                    help="save an intermediate adapter every N steps; 0 disables")
    ap.add_argument("--val_size", type=int, default=32,
                    help="number of fixed (image,t,noise) tuples for validation")
    ap.add_argument("--eval_every", type=int, default=100,
                    help="run validation every N steps; 0 disables")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    weight_dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

    tokenizer = CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="tokenizer")
    text_encoder = CLIPTextModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="text_encoder", torch_dtype=weight_dtype).to(device).eval()
    vae = AutoencoderKL.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="vae", torch_dtype=weight_dtype).to(device).eval()
    unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, subfolder="unet", torch_dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    noise_sched = DDPMScheduler.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, subfolder="scheduler")

    for m in (text_encoder, vae):
        for p in m.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)
    for p in unet.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)

    lora_cfg = LoraConfig(
        r=args.rank,
        lora_alpha=args.alpha,
        target_modules=["to_q", "to_k", "to_v", "to_out.0"],
        lora_dropout=0.0,
        bias="none",
    )
    unet = get_peft_model(unet, lora_cfg)
    unet.train()

    trainable = [p for p in unet.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    n_train = sum(p.numel() for p in trainable)
    print(f"trainable params: {n_train/1e6:.2f}M "
          f"({100*n_train/sum(p.numel() for p in unet.parameters()):.2f}% of UNet)")

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(trainable, lr=args.lr)

    ds = StyleDataset(Path(args.data_dir), tokenizer)
    loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=True,
                        num_workers=2, drop_last=True)

    # Build a fixed validation set so we can report a low-variance loss curve.
    val_items = None
    if args.eval_every > 0 and args.val_size > 0:
        val_loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=1, shuffle=False, num_workers=0)
        val_items = build_validation_set(
            val_loader, args.val_size, vae, text_encoder, noise_sched,
            device, weight_dtype, seed=args.seed + 1)
        print(f"built validation set of {len(val_items)} fixed (image,t,noise) tuples")

    epochs = math.ceil(args.steps * args.grad_accum / max(1, len(loader)))
    print(f"requested {args.steps} optimizer steps; "
          f"samples/epoch={len(loader)}; running up to {epochs} epoch(s)")

    # Moving-average windows. We accumulate per-MICRO-step losses, not
    # per-optimizer-step, so the window covers a lot more random-t samples.
    micro_win = deque(maxlen=args.log_window * args.grad_accum)

    step = 0
    accum = 0
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        for pixel, input_ids in loader:
            pixel = pixel.to(device, dtype=weight_dtype)
            input_ids = input_ids.to(device)

            with torch.no_grad():
                latents = vae.encode(pixel).latent_dist.sample() * vae.config.scaling_factor
                encoder_hidden_states = text_encoder(input_ids)[0]

            bsz = latents.shape[0]
            t = torch.randint(0, noise_sched.config.num_train_timesteps,
                              (bsz,), device=device).long()
            noise = torch.randn_like(latents)
            noisy = noise_sched.add_noise(latents, noise, t)

            pred = unet(noisy.float(), t, encoder_hidden_states.float()).sample
            loss = F.mse_loss(pred.float(), noise.float())
            (loss / args.grad_accum).backward()
            micro_win.append(loss.item())
            accum += 1

            if accum % args.grad_accum == 0:
                optimizer.step()
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                step += 1

                if step % 25 == 0:
                    last_loss = micro_win[-1]
                    avg = sum(micro_win) / len(micro_win)
                    n_micro = len(micro_win)
                    # The moving average covers up to log_window optimizer
                    # steps worth of micro-steps. Report both numbers.
                    print(f"step {step:>5} | last {last_loss:.4f} "
                          f"(avg over {n_micro} micro-steps: {avg:.4f})")

                # Periodic fixed-validation-set evaluation.
                if (val_items is not None and args.eval_every > 0
                        and step % args.eval_every == 0):
                    val_loss = evaluate(val_items, unet, noise_sched)
                    print(f"  -> val_loss @ step {step}: {val_loss:.4f}")

                # Intermediate checkpoints.
                if (args.checkpoint_every > 0 and step > 0
                        and step % args.checkpoint_every == 0
                        and step < args.steps):
                    ckpt = Path(args.out_dir) / f"checkpoint-{step}"
                    save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, ckpt)
                    print(f"  -> saved checkpoint to {ckpt}")

                if step >= args.steps:
                    break
        if step >= args.steps:
            break

    out = Path(args.out_dir)
    save_lora_for_diffusers(unet, out)
    print(f"\nSaved final LoRA adapter to {out.resolve()} after {step} steps")
    print("Load it with pipe.load_lora_weights(out_dir)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
05_lora_strength_sweep.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/05_lora_strength_sweep.py

Generate a grid of images at multiple LoRA strengths so you can pick the
strength that looks best for production. Fix the seed, fix the prompt,
sweep the scale.

The pivotal argument is cross_attention_kwargs={"scale": s}. Set s=0 to
see the base model exactly; set s=1.0 to see what you trained; go higher
to push the style further (at the risk of artifacts).

Run:
    python 04_lora_strength_sweep.py \
        --lora ./mybrand_lora \
        --prompt "a steaming cup of tea on a wooden table, in mybrand style" \
        --out grid.png
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler
from PIL import Image

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"


def make_grid(images, cols=4):
    w, h = images[0].size
    rows = (len(images) + cols - 1) // cols
    grid = Image.new("RGB", (cols * w, rows * h), "white")
    for i, im in enumerate(images):
        r, c = divmod(i, cols)
        grid.paste(im, (c * w, r * h))
    return grid


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lora", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--negative_prompt",
                    default="blurry, low quality, watermark, text")
    ap.add_argument("--scales", nargs="+", type=float,
                    default=[0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5])
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=12345)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=25)
    ap.add_argument("--guidance", type=float, default=7.5)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="grid.png")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe.load_lora_weights(args.lora)
    pipe = pipe.to("cuda")
    pipe.set_progress_bar_config(disable=True)

    images = []
    for s in args.scales:
        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(args.seed)
        img = pipe(
            prompt=args.prompt,
            negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt,
            num_inference_steps=args.steps,
            guidance_scale=args.guidance,
            generator=gen,
            cross_attention_kwargs={"scale": s},
        ).images[0]
        # annotate so the grid is self-documenting
        img.load()
        images.append(img)
        print(f"scale={s:>4.2f}  -> done")

    grid = make_grid(images, cols=min(4, len(images)))
    grid.save(args.out)
    print(f"wrote {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
06_compose_multiple_loras.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/06_compose_multiple_loras.py

Load two or more LoRA adapters into a single pipeline, give each one a
weight, and generate with all of them active. This is how you ship a
single inference call that carries a brand style AND a specific subject
AND a particular lighting recipe.

The diffusers helper does the bookkeeping for you:
    pipe.load_lora_weights(path, adapter_name=...)
    pipe.set_adapters(names, adapter_weights=weights)

Internally, each LoRA layer accumulates its delta:
    y = W·x + Σ scaleᵢ · Bᵢ·Aᵢ·x

Run:
    python 05_compose_multiple_loras.py \
        --style ./mybrand_lora \
        --subject ./acme_mascot_lora \
        --light ./studio_lighting_lora \
        --prompt "a portrait of sks mascot, studio lighting, in mybrand style"
"""

import argparse
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--style", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--subject", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--light", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--style_w", type=float, default=0.8)
    ap.add_argument("--subject_w", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--light_w", type=float, default=0.4)
    ap.add_argument("--prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--negative_prompt",
                    default="blurry, low quality, watermark, text, extra limbs")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=12345)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="composed.png")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)

    # Each load_lora_weights call attaches that adapter under the given name.
    pipe.load_lora_weights(args.style, adapter_name="style")
    pipe.load_lora_weights(args.subject, adapter_name="subject")
    names = ["style", "subject"]
    weights = [args.style_w, args.subject_w]

    if args.light:
        pipe.load_lora_weights(args.light, adapter_name="light")
        names.append("light")
        weights.append(args.light_w)

    pipe.set_adapters(names, adapter_weights=weights)
    pipe = pipe.to("cuda")

    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(args.seed)
    image = pipe(
        prompt=args.prompt,
        negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt,
        num_inference_steps=30,
        guidance_scale=7.5,
        generator=gen,
    ).images[0]
    image.save(args.out)
    print(f"wrote {args.out}")
    print(f"active adapters: {names} with weights {weights}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
07_evaluate_lora.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/07_evaluate_lora.py

Three quantitative checks for a style LoRA:

1. Prompt fidelity. Does the generated image still match what the prompt
   describes? Measured as CLIP cosine similarity between the generated
   image embedding and the prompt's text embedding.

2. Style similarity. Does the generated image carry the trained style?
   Measured as CLIP image-image cosine similarity between the generated
   image and the *style reference set* (the held-out training images).
   We average over the reference set so noisy individual references
   don't dominate.

3. Subject preservation. Does the trained model still know how to draw
   ordinary subjects? Measured by running both the base and trained
   models with the SAME prompt + seed, then taking the CLIP cosine.
   Wildly different outputs (cosine < 0.5) suggest the LoRA collapsed
   the base model's general knowledge.

All three together give you a single CSV row per evaluation prompt that
you can graph over training checkpoints.

Run:
    python 06_evaluate_style_lora.py \
        --lora ./mybrand_lora \
        --style_refs ./style_set_holdout \
        --prompts prompts.txt \
        --out scores.csv
"""

import argparse
import csv
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from PIL import Image
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler
from transformers import CLIPProcessor, CLIPModel

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
CLIP_ID = "openai/clip-vit-base-patch32"


def cos(a, b):
    return F.cosine_similarity(a, b).item()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lora", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--style_refs", required=True,
                    help="folder of held-out images that exemplify the style")
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", required=True,
                    help="text file with one evaluation prompt per line")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=4242)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=25)
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="scores.csv")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = "cuda"

    # CLIP for all three measurements.
    clip = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(CLIP_ID).to(device).eval()
    cprc = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(CLIP_ID)

    # Reference style embedding = mean of all held-out reference images.
    refs = sorted(Path(args.style_refs).glob("*.png")) + \
           sorted(Path(args.style_refs).glob("*.jpg"))
    ref_imgs = [Image.open(p).convert("RGB") for p in refs]
    ref_inputs = cprc(images=ref_imgs, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        ref_feats = clip.get_image_features(**ref_inputs)
        ref_feats = F.normalize(ref_feats, dim=-1)
        style_anchor = ref_feats.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        style_anchor = F.normalize(style_anchor, dim=-1)

    # Base pipeline (no LoRA).
    base_pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    base_pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(base_pipe.scheduler.config)
    base_pipe = base_pipe.to(device)

    # Trained pipeline (load the LoRA into a separate pipe so we can compare).
    lora_pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    lora_pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(lora_pipe.scheduler.config)
    lora_pipe.load_lora_weights(args.lora)
    lora_pipe = lora_pipe.to(device)

    prompts = [line.strip() for line in open(args.prompts) if line.strip()]

    rows = []
    for p in prompts:
        gen_a = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(args.seed)
        base_img = base_pipe(p, num_inference_steps=args.steps,
                             generator=gen_a).images[0]
        gen_b = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(args.seed)
        lora_img = lora_pipe(
            p, num_inference_steps=args.steps, generator=gen_b,
            cross_attention_kwargs={"scale": args.scale}).images[0]

        with torch.no_grad():
            inputs = cprc(text=[p], images=[base_img, lora_img],
                          return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to(device)
            img_feats = F.normalize(clip.get_image_features(
                pixel_values=inputs["pixel_values"]), dim=-1)
            txt_feats = F.normalize(clip.get_text_features(
                input_ids=inputs["input_ids"],
                attention_mask=inputs["attention_mask"]), dim=-1)

        base_feat, lora_feat = img_feats[0:1], img_feats[1:2]
        fidelity = cos(lora_feat, txt_feats)
        style    = cos(lora_feat, style_anchor)
        preserve = cos(lora_feat, base_feat)

        rows.append({
            "prompt": p,
            "prompt_fidelity": round(fidelity, 4),
            "style_match":     round(style, 4),
            "subject_drift":   round(1 - preserve, 4),
        })

        print(f"{p[:60]:60s}  fid={fidelity:.3f}  style={style:.3f}  "
              f"drift={(1-preserve):.3f}")

    with open(args.out, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
08_merge_lora_into_base.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/08_merge_lora_into_base.py

Bake a LoRA back into the base UNet weights so you can ship a single
.safetensors file with no adapter dependency. After merging:
  - inference no longer needs PEFT installed
  - the cross_attention_kwargs scale knob is gone (frozen at 1.0)
  - the resulting model is the same size as the base

Use this at the END of iteration, once you've settled on a strength.

Run:
    python 07_merge_lora_into_base.py \
        --lora ./mybrand_lora \
        --out  ./mybrand_full
"""

import argparse
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lora", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0,
                    help="effective LoRA strength to bake in")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    pipe.load_lora_weights(args.lora)
    pipe.fuse_lora(lora_scale=args.scale)
    pipe.unload_lora_weights()       # drop the adapter; the weights are fused now
    pipe.save_pretrained(args.out)
    print(f"merged + saved to {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
09_ip_adapter_inference.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
chapter13/code/09_ip_adapter_inference.py

IP-Adapter is the zero-shot alternative to DreamBooth. Instead of
training per-subject, you load a small pre-trained adapter (about 50 MB)
that contains an image encoder plus a cross-attention pathway. At
inference you pass a REFERENCE image alongside your prompt, and the
adapter biases the cross-attention to pull from the reference.

There are three common flavors:
- IP-Adapter (general image conditioning)
- IP-Adapter FaceID (specialized on face identity)
- IP-Adapter Plus (higher fidelity, slower)

You don't train anything yourself. The trade-off is that you can't pick
up stylistic nuance the way a trained LoRA can; IP-Adapter is for
"render something that resembles THIS specific reference image."

This script shows the general-purpose flavor. The FaceID variant is
nearly identical; only the model name and the call signature change.

Run:
    python 09_ip_adapter_inference.py \
        --reference ./reference.png \
        --prompt "a portrait in soft afternoon light" \
        --out portrait.png
"""

import argparse
import torch
from PIL import Image
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, DPMSolverMultistepScheduler

MODEL_ID = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
IP_ADAPTER_REPO = "h94/IP-Adapter"
IP_ADAPTER_FILE = "ip-adapter_sd15.bin"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--reference", required=True,
                    help="path to the reference image you want to condition on")
    ap.add_argument("--prompt", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--negative_prompt",
                    default="blurry, low quality, watermark, text")
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=0.7,
                    help="how strongly the reference influences output (0..1)")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=12345)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=30)
    ap.add_argument("--guidance", type=float, default=7.5)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="ip_adapter_out.png")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_ID, torch_dtype=torch.float16, safety_checker=None)
    pipe.scheduler = DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
    pipe.load_ip_adapter(IP_ADAPTER_REPO, subfolder="models", weight_name=IP_ADAPTER_FILE)
    pipe.set_ip_adapter_scale(args.scale)
    pipe = pipe.to("cuda")

    ref = Image.open(args.reference).convert("RGB")

    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(args.seed)
    image = pipe(
        prompt=args.prompt,
        negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt,
        ip_adapter_image=ref,
        num_inference_steps=args.steps,
        guidance_scale=args.guidance,
        generator=gen,
    ).images[0]

    image.save(args.out)
    print(f"wrote {args.out}")
    print(f"reference: {args.reference}  scale: {args.scale}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
