← Previous12.2 · The Full Pipeline, Guidance, and LoRA→ Next13.1 · DreamBooth: Teaching a Subject
13.1Chapter 13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models

DreamBooth: Teaching a Subject

Diffusion model fine-tune karne ki sabse common wajah hai use ek specific subject sikhana — tumhara product, pet, company mascot ya apna chehra. Technique ka naam hai DreamBooth. Do core ideas hain, aur dono ko samajhna zaroori hai.

Do core ideas — rare token aur prior preservation

Pehla: subject ko refer karne ka tareeka. "My dog" nahi keh sakte — "dog" ki embedding pehle se strong general notion ki taraf point karti hai, aur fine-tuning gradient ko us ingrained knowledge se ladna padega. Isliye ek rare token chuno jo model ne lagbhag kabhi dekha hi na ho — jaise sks ya ohwx. Training me model us token ko tumhare specific dog ki visual concept se rapidly bind kar leta hai.

Dusra: prior preservation — model ko bhoolne mat do ki generic "dog" kaisa dikhta hai. Bina iske, tumhare dog ki kuch photos par train karne se model ka "dog" ka concept corrupt ho jayega aur har dog tumhare dog jaisa dikhne lagega. Isliye subject images ("a photo of sks dog") ke saath generic dogs ki images ("a photo of a dog") bhi train karo — dono losses add hote hain, class-prior term par ek chhota weight ke saath.

General recipe

  1. 3–8 high-quality photos — background, pose aur lighting vary karo. Zyada count nahi, variety chahiye; paanch achhi photos pachaas mediocre photos se behtar hain.
  2. 200 ya zyada class-prior images autogenerate karo — base model se "a photo of a dog" kam se kam 200 baar, phir best 200 hand-select karo.
  3. UNet ki attention layers par LoRA attach karo.
  4. 800–2,000 steps, learning rate ~1e-4, batch 1 per stream, gradient accumulation 4.
  5. Adapter save karo — 30–90 MB.
  6. Inference par rare token se prompt karo: "sks dog wearing a top hat in the Sistine Chapel".

Step 1 — subject photos

Reference dataset diffusers/dog-example hai — ek specific corgi ki paanch photos, alag angles se. Script 00_download_dog_example.py photos download karke metadata.jsonl likhta hai, har photo ko caption "a photo of sks dog" ke saath pair karke. Yeh dataset jaan-bujh kar chhota hai: 1,200 steps, LR 1e-4, rank 8 par train karo to model "sks dog" par reliably wahi corgi de, aur "a dog" par generic dog — isse alag result mile to setup me kuch gadbad hai. Yeh tumhara control variable hai.

Step 2 — class-prior set

Script 00b_generate_class_prior.py base model se class images generate karta hai — har image ke liye alag seed, taaki 200 alag dogs milen, ek hi dog ki 200 copies nahi. 20 inference steps kaafi hain — quality top ki zaroorat nahi, class clearly depict honi chahiye. Generate karne ke baad folder ko scan karo aur obvious failures delete karo (watermarked stock photos, missing dogs, multiple dogs). Yeh set ek baar per class banta hai, baad ke runs reuse karte hain.

Step 3 — training loop, do streams

Script 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py do dataloaders banata hai — subject ("a photo of sks dog") aur prior ("a photo of a dog"). Har step me har stream se ek sample le kar batch size 2 me concatenate karo, ek saath UNet se guzaro, phir split karke alag losses compute karo: loss = subject loss + prior_weight × prior loss, prior weight typically 1.0. Baaki flow wahi hai: VAE se latent, CLIP se caption, random timestep t aur noise, UNet noise predict kare, MSE loss. Log me trainable params 1.59M dikhte hain, aur 1,200 steps par final adapter save hota hai.

Yaad rakho: DreamBooth = rare token + prior preservation. Rare token bina ladai ke naya concept bind karta hai, class-prior images purana concept bachate hain. Dono me se ek bhi skip kiya to adapter ya to subject seekhega hi nahi, ya har dog ko tumhara dog bana dega.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 13 — Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
← Previous13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models→ Next13.2 · Evaluating DreamBooth and Tuning It
13.2Chapter 13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models

Evaluating DreamBooth and Tuning It

DreamBooth train karne ke baad sabse pehle ek unintuitive sach samajh lo: diffusion training loss intrinsically noisy hota hai. Har step ek fresh random timestep t sample karta hai — low t easy hota hai (halka sa noise), high t hard (bhaari noise). Isliye step 1075 par subject loss 0.0345 ho sakta hai aur step 1125 par 0.5768 — beech me kuch galat nahi hua, bas unlucky timestep aur unlucky image draw hui. Language-model training me per-step loss aisa nahi hota.

Moving average kaafi nahi — fixed validation set chahiye

50-step moving average spikes ko smooth karta hai, lekin woh bhi window me kitne high-t samples aaye us par depend karta hai — log me averages 0.05 se 0.14 ke beech bina clear trajectory ke ghoomte hain. Asli signal fixed validation set hai: shuruaat me 32 frozen (image, timestep, noise) tuples sample karo, har 100 steps par unhi par model chalao aur mean MSE ko val_loss ke roop me report karo. Timesteps aur noise kabhi badalte nahi, isliye val_loss ko sirf model badal sakta hai — curve clean aur plottable hoti hai. Book ke run me val_loss 0.083 se 0.074 tak gira — lagbhag 10% down — slow downward drift aur flattening tail, healthy DreamBooth curve ka sign. Cost minimal hai: har 100 training steps par 32 forward passes, lagbhag 1% overhead. Agar val_loss step 600 par bottom out karke upar chadhne lage, to overtraining hai — curve ke bottom wala checkpoint lo. Agar woh starting value se neeche hi na jaye, to learning rate bahut low hai ya captions galat hain.

Checkpoints — final sabse achha nahi hota

Script har 300 steps par intermediate adapters save karta hai (checkpoint-300, checkpoint-600, ...). Paach training images aur 1,200 steps par tum overtraining ki boundary par ho — step 600 ya 900 wala checkpoint step 1,200 wale se behtar dikh sakta hai. Run ke baad unhe visually compare karke winner chuno. End-to-end CLI path teen scripts ka hai — 00_download_dog_example.py, 00b_generate_class_prior.py, 03_train_dreambooth_lora.py — aur hardware par depend karke 15 minutes se kuch hours lagte hain.

Inference aur sanity check

load_lora_weights + set_adapters se adapter load karo aur trigger token ke saath prompt karo ("sks dog wearing a top hat in front of the Eiffel Tower"). Phir wahi scene trigger ke bina bhi try karo ("a dog wearing a top hat..."). Agar dusra prompt bhi tumhara dog de, to problem hai — zyada class-prior weight ya kam steps se retrain karo.

Hyperparameters jo matter karte hain

  • Rank: recognizable subject ke liye 16 se shuru karo (time/capacity kam ho to 8). Zyada rank adapter ko bada aur overfitting-prone banata hai.
  • Steps: SD 1.5 ke liye 800–1,500, SDXL ke liye 1,200–2,000. Subject loss ruk jaye to training roko.
  • Class-prior weight: 1.0 matlab subject aur class losses ko equal weight. Prior collapse dikhe (class loss upar chadh raha hai) to weight badhao; subject barely dikhe to kam karo — lekin 0.3 se neeche mat jao, warna prior kho jayega.
  • Class count: 200 se shuru karo, 100 se kaam chal sakta hai, lekin usse neeche mat jao; 400 se upar diminishing returns hain.

Ek gotcha: LoRA kabhi load hi nahi hota aur pipeline bina error ke base model jaisi image de deta hai. Book ki training script diffusers-native format (pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors) me save karti hai — PEFT format (adapter_config.json + adapter_model.safetensors) ki key names ko diffusers ka loader kabhi misread kar leta hai. Aur yaad rakho: val_loss monotonic hona healthy run ke liye necessary hai, sufficient nahi — aakhir me generated images ko aankhon se dekhna hi final judge hai.

Yaad rakho: per-step loss ko dekh kar ghabrao mat — woh noise hai, signal nahi. Fixed val_loss dekho, checkpoints har 300 steps par save karo, aur trigger ke bina wala sanity check kabhi mat bhoolna.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 13 — Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
← Previous13.1 · DreamBooth: Teaching a Subject→ Next13.3 · Style LoRA, Composing Adapters, and Deployment
13.3Chapter 13 · Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models

Style LoRA, Composing Adapters, and Deployment

Style training dusra flavor hai — architecture wahi, training loop wahi, lekin data design ulta. Counterintuitive sach: ek specific style sikhane ke liye tumhe kai alag subjects usi style me dikhane hote hain. Agar training set me sirf teacups hain, to model seekh lega ki style sirf teacups par lagta hai — "a bicycle in mybrand style" poochho to bicycle ya to aayegi hi nahi, ya usme teacup ke elements honge. Cross-attention me style embedding ko image features ki taraf pull karna seekhna hai; agar woh hamesha teacup features hi dekhe, to seekhi hui direction "teacup jaisa bano" hogi, "brand jaisa bano" nahi.

Style dataset — chaar pieces

Images, captions, metadata.jsonl, aur ek held-out evaluation set jise kabhi train nahi karte. 50–100 images target karo — 30 se kam par model overfit karke specific training images ke textures aur subjects seekh leta hai; 200 se zyada par compute waste hota hai, fayda nahi. Quality count se zyada matter karti hai: borderline examples, text/watermark wale, ya hesitate karne wale images hata do. Size sahi karo (SD 1.5 ke liye 512×512), metadata strip karo, duplicates hatao. Subjects deliberately vary karo — 80 images ka balanced set jaise 20 portraits, 20 products/still lifes, 20 interiors/environments, 20 outdoors/landscapes. 70% portraits wala dataset silently portrait composition par overfit kar dega.

Captions aur trigger — style ko describe mat karo

Caption ka kaam do-fold hai: subject specify karo aur style ko sirf trigger se jodo. Example: "a steaming cup of tea on a wooden table, in artdecostyle" — subject ka verbose description, lekin style ki koi definition nahi ("shot on film", "golden hour" jaise visual words se bacho, warna process confuse hoga). Captions haath se likho ya BLIP-2 se automate karke har caption padho — hallucinations, missed objects aur style descriptions ko saaf karne me kuch minutes lagte hain aur fayda bahut hai. Dataset generate karne ke liye SDXL use karo, SD 1.5 nahi — SD 1.5 se generate karke SD 1.5 ko train karna circular hai (base model apne hi output distribution ka corner enforce kar raha hai); SDXL ka bada UNet aur alag training data real cross-model style transfer banata hai. Art Deco worked example: trigger "in artdecostyle", 80 images, script 01b_generate_style_dataset.py.

Trigger gate nahi hai — soft pull hai

Yeh sabse important practical fact hai: single-style LoRA me trigger ek switch nahi hai. Training me har image ke caption me trigger tha, isliye LoRA ne kabhi unstyled image + nontrigger caption ka regime dekha hi nahi. Adapter load hote hi style har forward pass par apply hoti hai — trigger prompt me ho ya na ho, scale 1.0 par style aayegi hi. Trigger low scales (0.3–0.5) par thoda zyada pull karta hai aur multiple LoRAs compose karte waqt disambiguator ka kaam karta hai. True gated behavior chahiye to mixed dataset se train karo — lagbhag aadhi styled-and-triggered, aadhi unstyled-and-untriggered images. Style band karne ke liye set_adapters me weight 0.0 do ya unload_lora_weights() call karo.

Training — DreamBooth minus prior

Loop wahi hai, bas class-prior term nahi: VAE se latent, CLIP se caption, random timestep t, Gaussian noise, UNet predicted noise, MSE loss — aur gradient accumulation se microbatches jod lo. Book ke run me 1,500 steps, LR 1e-4, rank 16, val_loss lagbhag 0.097 par settle hui. Per-step loss phir bhi noisy hai — val_loss line se convergence padho, moving average sirf yeh confirm karne ke liye ki kuch blow up to nahi ho raha. Style training aksar overfit karne se pehle ek sweet spot se guzarti hai, isliye step-1,000 adapter step-1,500 wale se behtar dikh sakta hai, chahe val_loss abhi bhi descend kar rahi ho.

Strength sweep — scale 0.6–0.9

Har LoRA layer compute karta hai: y = W₀x + scale·(BA)x. Scale 0 par base model exactly, scale 1 par trained jaisa, zyada par artifacts. Production me scale 1.0 lagbhag kabhi best nahi hota — sweet spot 0.6–0.9 hota hai. Sweep script (05_lora_strength_sweep.py) wahi prompt, wahi seed, 12 scales (0.0 se 1.7) par grid banata hai. Seed pin karna zaroori hai, warna do cheezein ek saath compare ho rahi hongi. Grid se pata chalta hai: concept kis scale par recognizable hota hai, artifacts kab shuru hote hain, prompt fidelity kab tak solid hai. Yahi sweep DreamBooth adapters par bhi kaam karta hai — subject barely recognizable ho to retrain se pehle scale thoda badha kar dekho.

Composing adapters — zyada se zyada teen

Subject 1.0, style 0.7–0.8, light effect low (jaise 0.4) — deltas seedha add hote hain, kyunki teeno wahi to_q/to_k/to_v/to_out.0 projections target karte hain. Prompt me har trigger mention karo — adapter load hone se trigger automatically load nahi hota, woh cross-attention pathways se control hota hai. Teen LoRAs care ke saath doable hain; chaar ya zyada mushkil ho jata hai — usse zyada chahiye to combined dataset par ek adapter train karo.

SD 1.5 se aage aur deployment

SDXL: 2.6B UNet, do text encoders, 1,024 px — target modules wahi, lekin ~2× time aur VRAM (rank 16 par 20–24 GB). SD3 / Flux: UNet ki jagah Diffusion Transformer (DiT) blocks, target names qkv/proj jaise hote hain, target_modules="all-linear" se abstract ho jata hai. Video diffusion wahi noise-prediction objective frames par lagata hai; ControlNet composition pin karta hai (depth/edge/pose map se); IP-Adapter bina training ke reference image ka influence deta hai. Deployment ke liye fuse_lora adapter ko base UNet weights me bake kar deta hai (scale frozen ho jata hai) — single-file ship, PEFT ki zaroorat nahi, inference thoda fast bhi.

Failure modes

  • Loss bounce kar raha hai: false alarm hai — val_loss dekho, aankhon se images dekho.
  • Style/subject dikh hi nahi raha: LR 2e-4 par badhao, zyada steps train karo, phir zyada unusual trigger chuno.
  • Prior collapse: har dog tumhara dog lagta hai — 200 fresh class images banao, prior weight 1.5 karo, kam steps train karo.
  • Style overwhelming: har output same lagta hai — pehle wale checkpoint par wapas jao, rank ghatao, dataset ki subject diversity dekho.
  • Training images yaad aa rahi hain (memorization): zyada diverse images jodo, rank ghatao, kam steps, light random crops/flips.
  • Trigger inconsistent / style bina trigger ke bhi lag rahi hai: pehla metadata audit ka issue hai; dusra expected behavior hai (upar dekho).
  • Faces bhool gaya: training set objects ki taraf biased tha — 15–20 in-style portraits jod kar retrain karo.
  • 12 GB card par OOM: attention slicing aur VAE tiling on karo, gradient checkpointing on karo, batch 1 + accumulation 4–8.
  • Blurry/oversaturated: guidance issue hai, LoRA issue nahi — guidance_scale 7.5 se 5.0 karo; zyada noisy lage to steps 20 se 30 karo.
  • Fixed seed par bhi alag results: torch.Generator(device="cuda") use karo, CPU generator nahi. Slow first inference: normal hai — CUDA kernels compile hote hain; startup par ek warm-up generation chalao.
Yaad rakho: style sikhane ke liye subject vary karo, style narrow rakho. Trigger switch nahi, soft pull hai. Aur retrain karne se pehle hamesha strength sweep try karo — scale knob hi sabse pehla aur sabse sasta fix hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 13 — Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
← Previous13.2 · Evaluating DreamBooth and Tuning It→ Next14 · Optimization and Quantization
14Chapter 14 · Optimization and Quantization

Optimization and Quantization

Ab tak tumhare paas ek fine-tuned model hai jo kaam karta hai — lekin woh us GPU par chalta hai jis par tumne train kiya tha, ship karne wali machine par nahi. 16-bit me merged medical model 16–18 GB ka hai aur load hone ke liye utni hi VRAM mangta hai — developer ke laptop, $200/month inference budget, ya hospital ke air-gapped mini-PC par yeh nahi chalega. Is chapter ka kaam hai "train ho gaya" aur "deploy ho gaya" ke beech ka gap band karna.

Teen levers

  • Merging: adapter ko base me fold karke ek single standard artifact banao — model chhota nahi hota, lekin deployment target ko PEFT samajhne ki zaroorat khatm ho jati hai, aur har forward pass par do extra chhote matrix multiplies ka overhead bhi khatm hota hai.
  • Quantization: weights ko 16-bit se 4-bit par le jao — model lagbhag 4× chhota, aur inference fast bhi (kyunki LLM inference memory-bound hota hai: chhote weights move karne me kam time lagta hai). Lossy hai — art yeh hai ki precision wahan kho jaye jahan model ko farak na pade.
  • KV-cache optimization: conversation badhte hi keys/values ka cache weights se bhi bada ho sakta hai — use shrink aur manage karna hoga, warna long-context par model beech me out of memory ho jayega.

Teeno levers size–speed–accuracy triangle ke andar move karte hain — teeno ko ek saath max nahi kar sakte. Zyada tar fine-tuned models ke liye sweet spot 4-bit par nikalta hai, lekin yeh chapter tumhe woh faith par lene ke bajaye measure karke confirm karna sikhata hai. Optimization ek irreversible button nahi hai — reversible decisions ki pipeline hai, har step measured: merge karo, parity check karo; quantize karo, perplexity aur task accuracy measure karo; bit width chuno, quality knee ke sahi side par hone ki pushti karo.

Merging — formula aur 4-bit trap

Har adapted layer ke liye: Wmerged = Wbase + (α/r) · (B@A). merge_and_unload() yeh expression ek baar evaluate karke result ko weight tensor me likh deta hai aur A/B matrices discard kar deta hai — ab tumhare paas ek plain model hai, koi adapter attached nahi, serve time par PEFT dependency nahi. Script 01_merge_adapter.py hai.

4-bit merge trap: QLoRA training me base 4-bit (NF4) me load hua tha — usi par merge karna tempting hai, lekin 16-bit adapter delta ko pehle se compressed weights me add karne se sloppy double-quantization hoti hai aur quality loss dikhta hai. Sahi tareeka: base ko fresh bfloat16/fp16 me load karo, adapter attach karo, merge karo, phir alag controlled step me quantize karo. Tokenizer bhi merged model ke saath save karo (adapter directory se — custom tokens ya chat-template changes wahi se aate hain), warna tokenizer mismatch se model "load to hota hai, jawab ajeeb deta hai" wali debugging nightmare ban jati hai.

Parity verify karo — logits se, full text se nahi

Merge ke baad prove karo ki merged model adapter-attached model jaisa behave karta hai: wahi prompts dono se guzaro aur next-token logits compare karo — argmax match karta hai ya nahi, aur max |Δlogit| kitna hai. Full greedy generations ko token-for-token compare mat karo — chhoti rounding differences se lambi decode me transcripts drift kar sakte hain, chahe merge bilkul sahi ho, aur false alarm milega. Genuinely broken merge (galat dtype, tokenizer mismatch, corrupted weights) turant dikhega: alag predicted token aur bada logit gap.

Kab merge NA karo

Ek model, ek adapter — merge sahi hai. Lekin agar tum kai fine-tunes serve karte ho (per customer ya per specialty alag adapter), to merging storage aur memory ko adapters ki ginti se multiply kar deta hai — har merged model base ki full copy hai. Us case me ek base memory me rakh kar chhote adapters ko per request hot-swap karo — vLLM yahi multi-adapter pattern support karta hai, jo Chapter 15 me aayega.

Yaad rakho: merge full precision me karo, quantize baad me alag step me. Parity logits se verify karo, full text se nahi. Aur merge karne se pehle soch lo — ek expert serve kar rahe ho ya fleet, kyunki fleet ke liye adapter ko alag rakhna hi sahi hai.
00_finetune_gemma4.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
00_finetune_gemma4.py
----------------------
Fine-tune Gemma 4 (E4B) on the medical Q&A dataset with QLoRA, producing the
LoRA adapter that the rest of this chapter merges and quantizes.

Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/[Name]/synthdata
    Alpaca-style columns: instruction, input, output (+ metadata, format).
    One "train" split, ~5,321 examples pooled from three teacher models.

Why this script exists in Chapter 14: a LoRA trained on an OLD base (e.g.
google/gemma-3-4b-it) cannot be merged into a Gemma 4 model. If you're
migrating to Gemma 4, retrain the adapter here first, then run
01_merge_adapter.py.

The Gemma 4 gotcha, handled correctly below: Gemma 4 wraps its linear layers
in Gemma4ClippableLinear, which PEFT can't attach to directly. The fix is to
OMIT target_modules so peft>=0.19.0 applies its Gemma-4-aware defaults (the
language-model linears, skipping the clippable wrappers). Do NOT pass an
explicit target_modules list.

Requirements (CUDA GPU, ~16 GB VRAM is enough for E4B in 4-bit):
    pip install -U "peft>=0.19.0" "trl>=0.12" transformers datasets \
        accelerate bitsandbytes

Usage:
    python 00_finetune_gemma4.py                 # vanilla base
    python 00_finetune_gemma4.py --qat           # start from QAT checkpoint (§14.7)
    python 00_finetune_gemma4.py --out ./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora --epochs 1
"""
import os
# Gemma 4 is multimodal, so transformers reaches into its image/video utils,
# which try to `import tensorflow`. A broken TF/protobuf combo crashes the
# import; we don't use TF, so skip it. (Set BEFORE importing transformers.)
os.environ.setdefault("USE_TF", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("USE_FLAX", "0")

import argparse
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
from peft import LoraConfig
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer

VANILLA_BASE = "google/gemma-4-e4b-it"
# Starting from the unquantized QAT checkpoint makes the eventual 4-bit
# quant nearly lossless (see section 14.7).
QAT_BASE = "google/gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized"


def build_dataset(tokenizer, dataset_id, val_frac=0.05, seed=42):
    """Load the Alpaca-style medical set and render each row with the Gemma
    chat template into a single 'text' field for supervised fine-tuning."""
    ds = load_dataset(dataset_id, split="train")

    def to_chat(ex):
        # Fold the optional 'input' field into the user turn.
        user = ex["instruction"]
        if ex.get("input"):
            user = f"{user}\n\n{ex['input']}"
        messages = [
            {"role": "user", "content": user},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": ex["output"]},
        ]
        # Gemma 4 ships a "thinking" reasoner mode. Our targets are direct
        # answers with no thought block, so train (and later serve) with
        # thinking OFF so the template matches the data. Otherwise the model
        # is prompted to think but never shown a thought block, and at
        # inference it emits a reasoning preamble before answering.
        return {"text": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages, tokenize=False, enable_thinking=False)}

    ds = ds.map(to_chat, remove_columns=ds.column_names)
    # Small validation slice for loss monitoring. Keep your real evaluation
    # TEST set (Chapter 9 / section 14.8) separate and disjoint from this.
    return ds.train_test_split(test_size=val_frac, seed=seed)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", default=None, help="override the base model id")
    ap.add_argument("--qat", action="store_true",
                    help="start from the unquantized QAT checkpoint (§14.7)")
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default="[Name]/synthdata")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora")
    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--max-seq-len", type=int, default=1024)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base_id = args.base or (QAT_BASE if args.qat else VANILLA_BASE)
    print(f"Base model: {base_id}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(base_id)
    splits = build_dataset(tokenizer, args.dataset)
    print(f"train={len(splits['train'])}  val={len(splits['test'])}")

    # QLoRA: load the base in 4-bit NF4 to fit a single GPU. (Training in
    # 4-bit is fine; you'll RELOAD the base in bf16 for merging in script 01.)
    bnb = BitsAndBytesConfig(
        load_in_4bit=True,
        bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
        bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
    )
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        base_id, quantization_config=bnb, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map="auto",
    )

    # LoRA config — NOTE: no target_modules. peft>=0.19.0 fills in the
    # Gemma-4-aware defaults, which is what avoids the Gemma4ClippableLinear
    # "is not supported" error.
    lora = LoraConfig(
        r=16,
        lora_alpha=32,
        lora_dropout=0.05,
        bias="none",
        task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
    )

    # Training config. A couple of arg names drift across library versions:
    #   - transformers <4.41 used `evaluation_strategy` (now `eval_strategy`)
    #   - SFTConfig: newer TRL uses `max_length`; older TRL used `max_seq_length`
    # If you hit a TypeError on those, rename to match your installed version.
    cfg = SFTConfig(
        output_dir=args.out,
        num_train_epochs=args.epochs,
        per_device_train_batch_size=2,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=4,
        learning_rate=args.lr,
        lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
        warmup_ratio=0.03,
        bf16=True,
        gradient_checkpointing=True,
        gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False},
        optim="paged_adamw_8bit",
        logging_steps=10,
        eval_strategy="steps",
        eval_steps=100,
        save_strategy="epoch",
        max_length=args.max_seq_len,   # older TRL: max_seq_length=...
        dataset_text_field="text",
        report_to="none",
    )

    trainer = SFTTrainer(
        model=model,
        args=cfg,
        train_dataset=splits["train"],
        eval_dataset=splits["test"],
        peft_config=lora,            # SFTTrainer applies LoRA + k-bit prep
        processing_class=tokenizer,  # older TRL: use tokenizer=tokenizer
    )

    trainer.train()

    # Save ONLY the adapter (small). 01_merge_adapter.py folds it into a
    # fresh bf16 base.
    trainer.save_model(args.out)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(args.out)
    print(f"\nSaved LoRA adapter to {args.out}")
    print("Next: python 01_merge_adapter.py --base", base_id,
          "--adapter", args.out, "--out ./medical-gemma-merged")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
01_merge_adapter.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
01_merge_adapter.py
-------------------
Merge a trained LoRA adapter into its base model, IN FULL PRECISION,
then verify parity against the adapter-attached model before writing.

This is the foundation step for Chapter 14. The two things that matter:
  1. Load the base in bf16/fp16, NOT 4-bit. Merging into a 4-bit base
     double-quantizes and silently degrades quality. Quantize AFTERWARD.
  2. Verify parity: with greedy decoding the merged model must reproduce
     the adapter-attached model's output token-for-token.

Requirements / Gemma 4 gotchas:
  - Gemma 4 wraps its linear layers in Gemma4ClippableLinear, which PEFT
    cannot attach a LoRA to directly. peft>=0.19.0 handles this AT TRAINING
    TIME: omit target_modules and it targets the LM linears, skipping the
    clippable wrappers (incl. the vision/audio towers).
    => Train the adapter with peft>=0.19.0 and DEFAULT target modules.
    => Upgrading PEFT does NOT rescue an adapter whose saved target_modules
       already point at the wrappers; that adapter must be retrained.
  - The adapter must have been trained on the SAME Gemma 4 base. A Gemma 3
    adapter cannot be merged into a Gemma 4 model (wrong layer types and
    wrong weights); inspect adapter_config.json -> base_model_name_or_path.
  - Give the merge enough memory to hold the full bf16 model (~16 GB+ for
    E4B). If device_map="auto" offloads weights to the meta/disk device,
    merge_and_unload() will fail or corrupt weights (see the guard below).

Usage:
    python 01_merge_adapter.py \
        --base google/gemma-4-e4b-it \
        --adapter ./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora \
        --out ./medical-gemma-merged
"""
import os
# Gemma 4 is multimodal, so transformers reaches into its image/video utils,
# which try to `import tensorflow`. A broken TF/protobuf combo in the
# environment then crashes the whole import. We never use TF here, so tell
# transformers to skip it. (Must be set BEFORE importing transformers/peft.)
os.environ.setdefault("USE_TF", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("USE_FLAX", "0")

import argparse
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, AutoProcessor
from peft import PeftModel

PARITY_PROMPTS = [
    "What are the first-line treatments for type 2 diabetes?",
    "Explain the mechanism of action of beta blockers.",
    "When is a CT scan preferred over an MRI?",
    "List the common side effects of metformin.",
]


def generate(model, tok, text, max_new_tokens=120):
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": text}]
    # Gemma 4's tokenizer returns a BatchEncoding (dict), not a bare tensor,
    # so use return_dict=True and unpack with **inputs into generate().
    inputs = tok.apply_chat_template(
        msgs, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True
    ).to(model.device)
    prompt_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, do_sample=False)
    return tok.decode(out[0][prompt_len:], skip_special_tokens=True)


def sanitize_tokenizer_config(out_dir):
    """Gemma 4 tokenizers can round-trip `extra_special_tokens` as a list,
    which later crashes any AutoTokenizer load (e.g. llama.cpp's GGUF
    conversion) at `_set_model_specific_special_tokens`. Coerce it back to a
    dict so the merged folder is portable. The real special tokens live in
    tokenizer.json regardless, so this is safe."""
    import json
    import pathlib
    p = pathlib.Path(out_dir) / "tokenizer_config.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return
    cfg = json.loads(p.read_text())
    if isinstance(cfg.get("extra_special_tokens"), list):
        cfg["extra_special_tokens"] = {}
        p.write_text(json.dumps(cfg, indent=2))
        print("  (normalized tokenizer_config.json for GGUF compatibility)")


def next_token_logits(model, tok, text):
    """Next-token logits for a prompt. This is the robust parity signal:
    we compare what the model predicts next, not a long greedy decode."""
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": text}]
    inputs = tok.apply_chat_template(
        msgs, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True
    ).to(model.device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits[0, -1].float().cpu()
    return logits


def check_merged_integrity(model, out_dir):
    """Prove the save wrote every tensor the model actually holds.

    Compare the keys the in-memory merged model exposes against the keys written
    to disk. This catches a genuine save-time drop (a tensor the model has but
    the file lacks) WITHOUT assuming every layer is identical. That assumption is
    wrong for modern architectures: Gemma 4 E4B shares KV across a block of
    layers (config.num_kv_shared_layers), so the tail layers legitimately have no
    k_proj / v_proj / k_norm of their own. A uniform-layer check would raise a
    false alarm on exactly those correct checkpoints. The reference is what
    transformers instantiated, not a guess about layer shape.
    """
    import glob
    shards = glob.glob(os.path.join(out_dir, "*.safetensors"))
    if not shards:
        return  # non-safetensors save; skip
    from safetensors import safe_open
    written = set()
    for f in shards:
        with safe_open(f, "pt") as sf:
            written.update(sf.keys())

    expected = set(model.state_dict().keys())
    # transformers legitimately keeps tied weights out of the file (e.g. an
    # lm_head tied to the input embeddings), so don't count those as dropped.
    tied = set(getattr(model, "_tied_weights_keys", None) or [])
    missing = expected - written - tied
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"ABORT: the save dropped {len(missing)} tensors the model holds "
            f"(e.g. {sorted(missing)[:3]}). The merged checkpoint is incomplete; "
            "re-merge with the whole model resident (--device cpu on a high-RAM "
            "box) so nothing is offloaded during the merge."
        )
    print(f"Integrity OK: all {len(expected)} in-memory tensors were written "
          f"({len(written)} on disk).")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--adapter", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--max-drift", type=int, default=1,
                    help="max prompts allowed to drift before aborting")
    ap.add_argument("--device", choices=["auto", "cpu", "cuda"], default="auto",
                    help="where to load the bf16 base. Use 'cpu' on a runtime "
                         "whose GPU can't hold the full bf16 model (~16 GB for "
                         "E4B); merging is just math and runs fine on CPU.")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() else torch.float16

    # device_map="auto" can offload to meta/disk on a small GPU and corrupt the
    # merge. Forcing CPU avoids that when the GPU is too small for bf16.
    device_map = {"cpu": {"": "cpu"}, "cuda": {"": 0}, "auto": "auto"}[args.device]

    print(f"Loading base {args.base} in {dtype} on '{args.device}' (NOT 4-bit) ...")
    base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.base, torch_dtype=dtype, device_map=device_map
    )

    # Guard: if the box was too small, device_map="auto"/"cuda" offloads part
    # of the model to CPU or disk. Merging while offloaded silently DROPS the
    # non-LoRA weights (e.g. attention k_norm) in the offloaded layers when the
    # model is saved, producing a checkpoint that fails to load in a serving
    # stack with "weights were not initialized from checkpoint". Catch every
    # offload form: params left on the meta device AND an hf_device_map that
    # placed any module on cpu/disk when we did NOT ask for a CPU merge.
    meta = [n for n, p in base.named_parameters() if p.device.type == "meta"]
    dev_map = getattr(base, "hf_device_map", {}) or {}
    offloaded = [m for m, d in dev_map.items()
                 if str(d) in ("cpu", "disk") and args.device != "cpu"]
    if meta or offloaded:
        raise SystemExit(
            "ABORT: part of the model was offloaded to CPU/disk (not enough "
            "VRAM to hold the full bf16 model, ~16 GB+ for E4B). Merging while "
            "offloaded silently drops the non-LoRA weights in the offloaded "
            "layers. Re-run with --device cpu on a high-RAM runtime, or use a "
            "GPU that fits the whole model."
        )

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.adapter)

    print("Attaching adapter and capturing reference logits ...")
    peft_model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, args.adapter)
    ref_logits = [next_token_logits(peft_model, tok, p) for p in PARITY_PROMPTS]

    print("Merging adapter into base weights ...")
    merged = peft_model.merge_and_unload()

    # Parity check: the merged model and the adapter-attached model should
    # predict the SAME next token for each prompt. We compare next-token
    # logits, NOT long greedy generations: in bf16 the merged path
    # (W' = W + dW, then W'x) and the adapter path (Wx + dWx) round slightly
    # differently, so a 100-token greedy decode can diverge even on a perfectly
    # correct merge. Matching the argmax (with near-identical logits) is the
    # right, robust signal.
    print("Verifying parity (next-token prediction must match) ...")
    drift = 0
    for p, ref in zip(PARITY_PROMPTS, ref_logits):
        got = next_token_logits(merged, tok, p)
        same = int(ref.argmax()) == int(got.argmax())
        max_diff = (ref - got).abs().max().item()
        drift += 0 if same else 1
        print(f"  {'MATCH' if same else 'DRIFT'} | max|d logit|={max_diff:6.3f} "
              f"| {p[:40]}")

    if drift > args.max_drift:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"ABORT: {drift} prompts predicted a different next token (max "
            f"{args.max_drift}). That points to a real merge problem (dtype or "
            "tokenizer mismatch), not just rounding."
        )

    print(f"Parity OK ({drift} mismatch). Saving merged model to {args.out} ...")
    merged.save_pretrained(args.out, safe_serialization=True)

    # Prove the save wrote every tensor before trusting the checkpoint. Parity
    # confirms the math; this confirms nothing was dropped on the way to disk.
    check_merged_integrity(merged, args.out)

    tok.save_pretrained(args.out)

    # Save the FULL processor, not just the tokenizer. Gemma 4 is multimodal,
    # so its base ships an AutoProcessor (tokenizer + image/audio preprocessing
    # config). A serving stack like vLLM resolves the checkpoint as the
    # multimodal architecture and refuses to start without preprocessor_config
    # .json / processor_config.json, even when you only ever send text. Saving
    # the processor here writes those files so the merged model serves cleanly.
    # It's best-effort: a purely text-only base has no processor, so we fall
    # back silently to the tokenizer we already saved.
    try:
        AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.base).save_pretrained(args.out)
        print("Saved full processor (multimodal preprocessor configs included).")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"No AutoProcessor for this base ({e.__class__.__name__}); "
              "tokenizer-only save is fine for a text-only model.")

    sanitize_tokenizer_config(args.out)
    print("\nSample from the merged model:")
    print(" ", generate(merged, tok, PARITY_PROMPTS[0])[:240])
    print("Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
02_convert_to_gguf.sh — Shell script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 02_convert_to_gguf.sh
# ---------------------
# Convert a merged HF model to GGUF and quantize it to Q4_K_M, the
# portable path that runs on CPU, Apple Silicon, and GPU via llama.cpp.
#
# Steps:
#   1. (one-time) clone + set up llama.cpp tooling
#   2. HF model  -> 16-bit GGUF (translation only, no compression)
#   3. (optional) build an importance matrix on in-domain text
#   4. 16-bit GGUF -> 4-bit Q4_K_M (this is what actually shrinks it)
#   5. verify with a quick generation
#
# Usage:
#   ./02_convert_to_gguf.sh ./medical-gemma-merged medical_calibration.txt

set -euo pipefail

MERGED="${1:?path to merged HF model dir}"
CALIB="${2:-}"            # optional in-domain text file for imatrix
QUANT="${3:-Q4_K_M}"
LLAMA_DIR="${LLAMA_DIR:-./llama.cpp}"

# 1. One-time setup -----------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -d "$LLAMA_DIR" ]; then
  git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp "$LLAMA_DIR"
  cmake -B "$LLAMA_DIR/build" -S "$LLAMA_DIR"
  cmake --build "$LLAMA_DIR/build" --config Release -j
  pip install -r "$LLAMA_DIR/requirements.txt"
fi

F16="medical-gemma-f16.gguf"
OUT="medical-gemma-${QUANT}.gguf"

# 2. HF -> 16-bit GGUF (no compression) ---------------------------------
python "$LLAMA_DIR/convert_hf_to_gguf.py" "$MERGED" \
    --outfile "$F16" --outtype f16

# 3. Optional importance matrix (recommended for <=4-bit) ---------------
IMATRIX_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$CALIB" ] && [ -f "$CALIB" ]; then
  "$LLAMA_DIR/build/bin/llama-imatrix" \
      -m "$F16" -f "$CALIB" -o medical.imatrix
  IMATRIX_ARGS=(--imatrix medical.imatrix)
fi

# 4. Quantize -> Q4_K_M (the step that shrinks ~8GB -> ~2.5GB) ----------
"$LLAMA_DIR/build/bin/llama-quantize" \
    "${IMATRIX_ARGS[@]}" "$F16" "$OUT" "$QUANT"

# 5. Verify -------------------------------------------------------------
echo "=== sanity generation ==="
"$LLAMA_DIR/build/bin/llama-cli" -m "$OUT" -n 120 \
    -p "What are the first-line treatments for type 2 diabetes?"

ls -lh "$F16" "$OUT"
echo "Done: $OUT"
03_perplexity_sweep.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
03_perplexity_sweep.py
----------------------
Measure the damage. For each quantized GGUF variant, compute:
  - perplexity on a held-out text set  (tripwire: lower is better)
  - task accuracy on the medical test set (the number that matters)
and print a table so you can see the quality knee.

Requires:  pip install llama-cpp-python
The medical test set must be DISJOINT from training and calibration data.

Usage:
    python 03_perplexity_sweep.py --test-set test_set.jsonl
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
from llama_cpp import Llama

# Map a label -> GGUF path. Add/remove rows to match what you built.
VARIANTS = {
    "f16  (baseline)": "medical-gemma-f16.gguf",
    "Q6_K":            "medical-gemma-Q6_K.gguf",
    "Q5_K_M":          "medical-gemma-Q5_K_M.gguf",
    "Q4_K_M":          "medical-gemma-Q4_K_M.gguf",
    "Q3_K_M":          "medical-gemma-Q3_K_M.gguf",
}


def load(path, n_gpu_layers=-1, logits_all=False):
    # n_gpu_layers=-1 offloads ALL layers to the GPU, which is the difference
    # between minutes and an hour. It requires a CUDA build of llama-cpp-python:
    #   CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_CUDA=on" pip install --force-reinstall \
    #       --no-cache-dir llama-cpp-python
    # On a CPU-only build the flag is simply ignored (it stays on CPU).
    # logits_all=True is needed ONLY for perplexity and is expensive on a big
    # vocab, so we leave it off unless perplexity is actually requested.
    return Llama(model_path=path, n_ctx=2048, logits_all=logits_all,
                 n_gpu_layers=n_gpu_layers, verbose=False)


def perplexity(llm, texts):
    """Token-level perplexity over a list of held-out strings."""
    total_nll, total_tokens = 0.0, 0
    for text in texts:
        out = llm(text, max_tokens=0, echo=True, logprobs=0)
        lps = out["choices"][0]["logprobs"]["token_logprobs"]
        lps = [lp for lp in lps if lp is not None]
        total_nll += -sum(lps)
        total_tokens += len(lps)
    return math.exp(total_nll / max(total_tokens, 1))


def _token_f1(pred, ref):
    """Token-overlap F1 between a prediction and a reference string (the
    SQuAD-style metric). Returns a value in [0, 1]. This is a soft score that
    rewards saying the right things without demanding a verbatim match, so it
    actually moves as quantization degrades the answers, unlike exact match."""
    import re
    tok = lambda s: re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", s.lower())
    p, r = tok(pred), tok(ref)
    if not p or not r:
        return 0.0
    common = {}
    for w in p:
        if w in r:
            common[w] = min(p.count(w), r.count(w))
    overlap = sum(common.values())
    if overlap == 0:
        return 0.0
    precision = overlap / len(p)
    recall = overlap / len(r)
    return 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)


def medical_accuracy(llm, test_set):
    """Mean token-overlap F1 against the reference answers. For open-ended
    answers this is far more informative than exact/contains match (which is
    ~0 because the model paraphrases). For an authoritative score on answer
    quality, swap in an LLM-as-judge; F1 is the dependency-free stand-in that
    tracks relative quality across quantization levels."""
    total = 0.0
    for ex in test_set:
        prompt = f"<start_of_turn>user\n{ex['question']}<end_of_turn>\n<start_of_turn>model\n"
        out = llm(prompt, max_tokens=256, temperature=0.0)
        ans = out["choices"][0]["text"]
        total += _token_f1(ans, ex["answer"])
    return total / len(test_set)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--test-set", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--heldout-text", default=None,
                    help="text file for perplexity; defaults to test answers")
    ap.add_argument("--n-gpu-layers", type=int, default=-1,
                    help="layers to offload to GPU (-1 = all; 0 = CPU only). "
                         "Needs a CUDA build of llama-cpp-python.")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None,
                    help="cap the number of test rows graded, to keep it quick")
    ap.add_argument("--no-ppl", action="store_true",
                    help="skip the slow perplexity pass; grade with F1 only")
    ap.add_argument("--ppl-samples", type=int, default=15,
                    help="held-out texts to score for perplexity (when enabled)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    want_ppl = not args.no_ppl

    test_set = [json.loads(l) for l in open(args.test_set)]
    if args.limit:
        test_set = test_set[:args.limit]
    if args.heldout_text:
        heldout = [l for l in open(args.heldout_text) if l.strip()][:args.ppl_samples]
    else:
        # Cap count AND truncate length: perplexity cost scales with both.
        heldout = [ex["answer"][:600] for ex in test_set[:args.ppl_samples]]

    print(f"{'variant':18s} {'size':>8s}  {'ppl':>7s}  {'ansF1':>6s}")
    print("-" * 46)
    for name, path in VARIANTS.items():
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"{name:18s}  (missing: {path})")
            continue
        llm = load(path, args.n_gpu_layers, logits_all=want_ppl)
        ppl = perplexity(llm, heldout) if want_ppl else None
        acc = medical_accuracy(llm, test_set)
        size_gb = os.path.getsize(path) / 1e9
        ppl_s = f"{ppl:7.3f}" if ppl is not None else f"{'—':>7s}"
        print(f"{name:18s} {size_gb:6.2f}GB  {ppl_s}  {acc:5.1%}")
        del llm

    print("\nPick the smallest variant whose accuracy is still above the knee.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
04_kv_cache_quant.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
04_kv_cache_quant.py
--------------------
Two things:
  1. size_kv_cache(): compute the KV-cache footprint from first principles
     so you can budget memory for long context.
  2. A transformers generation that stores the cache in quantized form,
     letting you fit much longer context in the same memory.

See also the llama.cpp equivalent (runtime flags), shown at the bottom.
"""
import os
# Skip transformers' optional TensorFlow import (broken TF/protobuf in some
# environments crashes it); we don't use TF here.
os.environ.setdefault("USE_TF", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("USE_FLAX", "0")

import argparse
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer


def size_kv_cache(n_layers, n_kv_heads, head_dim, seq_len,
                  batch=1, bytes_per_value=2):
    """Bytes held by the KV cache. The leading 2 is keys + values.
    Note n_kv_heads (not n_attention_heads): GQA shrinks this directly."""
    return 2 * n_layers * n_kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * batch * bytes_per_value


def cache_budget_report():
    # Example: a 4B-class model with GQA.
    cfg = dict(n_layers=34, n_kv_heads=8, head_dim=256)
    print(f"{'ctx tokens':>12s} {'16-bit':>10s} {'8-bit':>10s}")
    for seq in (512, 4000, 8000, 16000):
        b16 = size_kv_cache(**cfg, seq_len=seq, bytes_per_value=2) / 1e9
        b8 = size_kv_cache(**cfg, seq_len=seq, bytes_per_value=1) / 1e9
        print(f"{seq:12d} {b16:8.2f}GB {b8:8.2f}GB")


def generate_quantized_cache(model_dir, prompt, nbits=4):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_dir, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto")
    # Gemma 4's tokenizer returns a BatchEncoding (dict); use return_dict=True
    # and unpack with **inputs into generate().
    inputs = tok.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True
    ).to(model.device)
    prompt_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]

    out = model.generate(
        **inputs,
        max_new_tokens=512,
        do_sample=False,
        cache_implementation="quantized",       # store KV in quantized form
        cache_config={"backend": "quanto", "nbits": nbits},
    )
    return tok.decode(out[0][prompt_len:], skip_special_tokens=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=None, help="HF model dir for a live demo")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    print("=== KV-cache budget (GQA, 4B-class model) ===")
    cache_budget_report()

    if args.model:
        print("\n=== generation with a 4-bit quantized cache ===")
        print(generate_quantized_cache(
            args.model, "Summarize the key risk factors for stroke."))

# llama.cpp equivalent (8-bit keys and values at serve time):
#   ./llama-cli -m medical-gemma-Q4_K_M.gguf \
#       --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 -c 8192 -p "..."
05_compression_pipeline.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
05_compression_pipeline.py
--------------------------
End-to-end, gated compression pipeline:

    adapter + base
        -> MERGE (fp16)          + parity check
        -> CONVERT to GGUF f16
        -> QUANTIZE to Q4_K_M
        -> EVALUATE vs fp16 baseline
        -> GATE on accuracy drop  (fail loudly if over budget)
        -> SHIP (artifact + eval report)

The point of the gate: compression isn't done when the file is smaller,
it's done when the file is smaller AND you've proven it's still good enough.

This script wires together the helpers shown elsewhere in the chapter:
  - 01_merge_adapter.py
  - 02_convert_to_gguf.sh
  - 03_perplexity_sweep.py
"""
import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


class QualityGateError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def run(cmd):
    print(f"$ {' '.join(cmd)}")
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)


def merge_adapter(base, adapter, out="medical-gemma-merged"):
    run([sys.executable, "01_merge_adapter.py",
         "--base", base, "--adapter", adapter, "--out", out])
    return out


def convert_and_quantize(merged, calib, quant="Q4_K_M"):
    run(["bash", "02_convert_to_gguf.sh", merged, calib, quant])
    return f"medical-gemma-{quant}.gguf"


def task_accuracy(gguf_path, test_set):
    """Thin wrapper around the grader in 03_perplexity_sweep.py."""
    from importlib import import_module
    sweep = import_module("03_perplexity_sweep")  # noqa: keep filename import
    llm = sweep.load(gguf_path)
    return sweep.medical_accuracy(llm, test_set)


def write_report(path, quant, base_acc, quant_acc, drop):
    report = Path("compression_report.md")
    report.write_text(
        f"# Compression Report\n\n"
        f"- Artifact: `{path}`\n"
        f"- Quant: **{quant}**\n"
        f"- fp16 baseline accuracy: **{base_acc:.1%}**\n"
        f"- quantized accuracy: **{quant_acc:.1%}**\n"
        f"- accuracy drop: **{drop:.1%}**\n"
    )
    print(f"Wrote {report}")


def compress(base, adapter, calib, test_set_path,
             quant="Q4_K_M", max_acc_drop=0.02):
    test_set = [json.loads(l) for l in open(test_set_path)]

    merged = merge_adapter(base, adapter)                 # §14.2 (parity inside)
    quantized = convert_and_quantize(merged, calib, quant)  # §14.6

    base_gguf = "medical-gemma-f16.gguf"                  # produced by convert
    base_acc = task_accuracy(base_gguf, test_set)         # fp16 reference
    quant_acc = task_accuracy(quantized, test_set)        # §14.7
    drop = base_acc - quant_acc

    if drop > max_acc_drop:
        raise QualityGateError(
            f"{quant} dropped accuracy by {drop:.1%} "
            f"(budget {max_acc_drop:.1%}). Try a higher bit width "
            f"(e.g. Q5_K_M).")

    write_report(quantized, quant, base_acc, quant_acc, drop)
    print(f"PASS: shipping {quantized} (drop {drop:.1%} within "
          f"{max_acc_drop:.1%} budget).")
    return quantized


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--adapter", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--calib", required=True, help="in-domain text for imatrix")
    ap.add_argument("--test-set", required=True, help="held-out jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--quant", default="Q4_K_M")
    ap.add_argument("--max-acc-drop", type=float, default=0.02)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    try:
        compress(args.base, args.adapter, args.calib, args.test_set,
                 args.quant, args.max_acc_drop)
    except QualityGateError as e:
        print(f"QUALITY GATE FAILED: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
06_use_qat_checkpoint.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
06_use_qat_checkpoint.py
------------------------
Claim most of the benefit of Quantization-Aware Training without running
the expensive QAT pass yourself: fine-tune on top of Google's UNQUANTIZED
QAT checkpoint, then quantize the merged model as usual.

The only change from the normal flow is the base model id. Everything
downstream (LoRA training in ch. 7-10, merge in 01_merge_adapter.py,
GGUF quantize in 02_convert_to_gguf.sh) is identical.

Why this works: the QAT-unquantized weights were trained to sit cleanly on
the 4-bit grid, so your fine-tune inherits that robustness and the final
q4_0 conversion costs far less accuracy than PTQ on a vanilla base.
"""
import os
# Skip transformers' optional TensorFlow import (broken TF/protobuf in some
# environments crashes it); we don't use TF here.
os.environ.setdefault("USE_TF", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("USE_FLAX", "0")

import argparse

# Vanilla base (PTQ path) vs. unquantized QAT checkpoint (QAT path).
VANILLA_BASE = "google/gemma-4-e4b-it"
QAT_BASE = "google/gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized"


def pick_base(use_qat: bool) -> str:
    """Return the base model id to fine-tune from."""
    return QAT_BASE if use_qat else VANILLA_BASE


def load_base_for_finetuning(use_qat: bool):
    """Load the chosen base in bf16, ready to attach a LoRA adapter.
    NOTE: load the *unquantized* QAT checkpoint, not a pre-quantized GGUF —
    you need full-precision weights to train and merge correctly."""
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    base_id = pick_base(use_qat)
    print(f"Fine-tuning base: {base_id}")
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        base_id, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto")
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(base_id)
    return model, tok

    # From here: attach your LoRA config and run SFTTrainer exactly as in
    # Chapter 8, then merge (01_merge_adapter.py) and quantize to q4_0
    # (02_convert_to_gguf.sh). No other step changes.


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--qat", action="store_true",
                    help="start from the unquantized QAT checkpoint")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    print("Recommended base ->", pick_base(args.qat))
    # load_base_for_finetuning(args.qat)   # uncomment to actually load
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 14 — Optimization and Quantization
← Previous13.3 · Style LoRA, Composing Adapters, and Deployment→ Next14.1 · How Quantization Works, the Format Zoo, and GGUF
14.1Chapter 14 · Optimization and Quantization

How Quantization Works, the Format Zoo, and GGUF

Quantization karne se pehle samajh lo woh weights ke saath karta kya hai — warna GGUF, GPTQ aur AWQ acronym soup lagega. Ek weight ek number hai (0.0237 ya -1.84). Float32 me 4 bytes, float16/bfloat16 me 2 bytes. Inference ke liye 16 bits per weight ki zaroorat lagbhag kabhi nahi hoti — weights seekhe ja chuke hain, gradients compute nahi ho rahe, bas forward pass me activations lagbhag wahi aane chahiye.

Mechanism — scale aur zero-point

Weights ka ek group lo, unka min aur max nikalo, aur us range ko 4-bit integers (0–15) par map karo. Recipe me do numbers hote hain: scale (har step ki value) aur zero-point (kaun sa integer asli zero ko correspond karta hai). Inference par dequantize karo: wapprox = (q − zero-point) × scale. Group size (32 / 64 / 128) matter karta hai: poori matrix ke liye ek scale lo (per-tensor) to ek bada outlier range ko itna stretch kar dega ki ordinary weights kuch integer values me crush ho jayenge; chhote groups me har block ko apni range milti hai, outliers sirf apne neighbourhood ko hurt karte hain. Chhote groups = behtar fidelity, thodi badi file. Symmetric quantization zero-point ko range ke beech me force karti hai (weights zero par centered hote hain to zero-point store karne ki zaroorat nahi); asymmetric lopsided distributions ko behtar handle karti hai. Aur weight-only vs weight-and-activation: weights static hain, isliye unhe quantize karna safe hai; activations har input par badalte hain aur unme nasty outliers hote hain — is chapter ke formats weight-only hain, math higher precision me chalta hai.

E4B me "E" ka matlab

Plain dense model me size = parameter count × bytes per weight hota — 4B-parameter model 2 bytes par lagbhag 8 GB hota. Lekin Gemma 4 E4B ~18 GB load hota hai, 8 GB nahi — kyunki "E" ka matlab "effective" hai. E4B per-layer embeddings use karta hai: har decoder layer ki apni chhoti embedding table hoti hai, jo lookup se cheap hai lekin disk par badi hai. Model compute time par 4B jaisa behave karta hai, lekin stored weights usse bahut zyada hain — aur quantization wahi stored weights shrink karta hai.

Format zoo — target se chuno

  • bitsandbytes NF4: QLoRA training ke liye fantastic (zero effort, Transformers se integrated), deployment ke liye bekaar — load time par quantize karta hai, ship karne layak compact file nahi deta, inference par sabse slow. Train karne ke liye rakho, serve karne ke liye nahi.
  • GGUF (llama.cpp): sabse portable — CPU, Apple Silicon (Metal), NVIDIA/AMD GPU, Ollama, LM Studio aur desktop apps. K-quants (Q4_K_M jaise) layers ke across bit widths intelligently mix karte hain. Laptop/Mac/CPU/desktop target ho to yahi default hai.
  • GPTQ: calibration-based, GPU-focused — chhote calibration set par model chalakar layer-wise error compensate karta hai. GPU inference par fast aur accurate.
  • AWQ: activation-aware — bade activations se interact karne wale salient weight channels ko protect karta hai. vLLM ke saath first-class support; llm-compressor se apply hota hai — lekin likhte waqt llm-compressor AWQ Gemma 4 architecture ko support nahi karta.
  • EXL2: enthusiasts ka format — mixed/fractional bit rates (jaise average 4.65 bits per weight), consumer GPU par excellent quality-per-byte, lekin GPU-only aur ExLlamaV2 runtime se tied.

Quantization speed kyun deta hai, jabki GPUs me 4-bit math units hote hi nahi? Kyunki LLM inference memory-bound hai, compute-bound nahi — har token ke liye poora model memory se compute units tak travel karta hai, aur wahi trip bottleneck hai. 4-bit model ek-chauthai bytes move karta hai — lekin sirf tab jab fused kernels weights ko on-chip memory me unpack karke seedha multiply me feed karen. Wahi format alag kernels ke saath 2–3× tokens-per-second me differ kar sakta hai.

GGUF in practice

Do steps: pehle convert (convert_hf_to_gguf.py, fp16, koi compression nahi), phir quantize (llama-quantize se Q4_K_M) — 15 GB se ~4.5 GB, script 02_convert_to_gguf.sh me wrapped hai. K-quant naam: Q4 = average 4 bits per weight, K = second-generation block structure (per-block scaling), trailing letter tier hai — S small, M medium, L large (important tensors ko thodi zyada precision). Sweet spots: Q8_0 lagbhag lossless (reference ke liye), Q6_K 16-bit se lagbhag indistinguishable, Q5_K_M strong middle ground, Q4_K_M workhorse (yahi se shuru karo), Q3_K_M se visible degradation, Q2_K extreme — medical model ke liye clear showstopper.

Importance matrix (imatrix)

4-bit ya neeche ke liye ek aur lever: calibration set par model chalakar measure karo ki kaun se weights sabse zyada matter karte hain, aur quantizer ko woh file do taaki woh un weights ko protect kare. Book ke run me 300 training-pool examples se calibration text banaya gaya (kabhi test set se nahi, hamesha in-domain — galat distribution par calibrate karoge to galat weights protect honge): 14,235.64 MiB se 5,041.55 MiB, 5.67 bits per weight. Train, calibration aur test pools ko disjoint rakho — quantizer ko test data dekhne doge to evaluation numbers fiction ban jayenge. Imatrix compute karna GPU par kuch minutes, CPU par lagbhag ek ghanta le sakta hai — GPU na ho to calibration set ko ~100 samples par shrink karo ya imatrix skip kar do; plain Q4_K_M pehle se solid deployable model hai.

Yaad rakho: format target se chuno — GGUF laptop/Mac/CPU ke liye, AWQ/GPTQ GPU serving ke liye, EXL2 consumer GPU packing ke liye, bitsandbytes sirf training ke liye. Aur quantized artifacts one-way doors hain — GGUF ya GPTQ file ko fine-tune nahi kar sakte, isliye bf16 merged model hi archive karo.

14.2Chapter 14 · Optimization and Quantization

QAT vs PTQ, and Measuring What Quantization Costs

Ab tak jo bhi dekha woh post-training quantization (PTQ) tha — finished model ko baad me compress karna. Uski built-in ceiling hai: weights full precision me train hue the, unse kabhi 4-bit rounding tolerate karne ko kaha hi nahi gaya, to compress karne par jo quality gayi woh gayi. Calibration aur imatrix loss kam kar sakte hain, khatm nahi.

QAT — training ke dauraan hi rounding simulate karo

Quantization-aware training (QAT) ulta approach hai: training ke dauraan hi low precision ki rounding errors simulate karo, taaki model aise weights seekhe jo quantization grid par comfortably baithe. Result: 4-bit model jo apne 16-bit parent ke bahut kareeb perform karta hai, PTQ wala gap zyada tar recover karke. Pehle QAT hard sell tha — 16-bit par train karo, phir 4-bit ke liye dobara train karo, mehenga kaam. Ab vendors yeh tumhare liye kar dete hain: Gemma 4 ke official QAT checkpoints available hain.

Official Gemma 4 QAT checkpoints — teen flavors

  • q4_0 GGUF build — llama.cpp ecosystem me drop-in use: LM Studio, Ollama, CPU/Apple Silicon/consumer GPU. Tumhare haath ke PTQ build ka QAT analog, lekin quality loss bahut kam.
  • w4a16 compressed-tensors build — vLLM ya SGLang se high-throughput GPU serving: 4-bit weights, 16-bit activations. GPU-serving artifact ka sabse reliable rasta.
  • Unquantized QAT checkpoint (google/gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized) — final compression se pehle ke half-precision weights. Fine-tuners ke liye yahi sabse important hai — aur matching draft models (speculative decoding ke liye) aur mobile-optimized variants bhi hain.

Subtlety samjho: QAT checkpoints base model par hain, tumhe tumhara medical model chahiye. Win yeh nahi hai ki QAT GGUF download karke ship kar do (isse tumhara fine-tune khatm ho jayega) — win yeh hai ki unquantized QAT checkpoint se fine-tune karo vanilla base ki jagah. Workflow wahi rehta hai — QLoRA fine-tune, merge, GGUF quantize — sirf pehle step me base model badal jata hai (BASE = "google/gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized"). Q4_0 par quantize karne par base weights pehle se quantization-robust hain, to tumhara fine-tuned version woh robustness inherit karta hai. Caveats: yeh Google ke end-to-end QAT jaisa mathematically identical nahi hai — tum quantization-friendly weights inherit kar rahe ho, apne data par QAT pass rerun nahi kar rahe — isliye measure karna zaroori hai. Aur har model QAT checkpoints ship nahi karta; model creator ne diye hon to use karo, nahi to PTQ + measurement se kaam chalao.

Measure karo — do metrics

Perplexity held-out set par — model text se kitna surprised hai, lower behtar. Cheap hai, judge ki zaroorat nahi, aur quantization wali broad degradation ke liye exquisitely sensitive hai. Yeh tripwire hai: perplexity jump red flag hai, flat perplexity necessary hai lekin sufficient nahi — model perplexity flat rakh kar bhi medical facts subtly galat kar sakta hai. Task accuracy domain test set par — wahi number jo asal me matter karta hai, kyunki woh model ke kaam ko measure karta hai. Sweep script 03_perplexity_sweep.py har variant ko load karke perplexity aur accuracy print karta hai.

Sweep 1 — accuracy table (alag run)

Ek run me accuracy sweep ke results: fp16 baseline 14.90 GB, perplexity 6.41, accuracy 84.2% → Q6_K 6.28 GB, 6.43, 84.1% → Q5_K_M 5.42 GB, 6.47, 83.8% → Q4_K_M 4.68 GB, 6.58, 83.1% → Q3_K_M 3.79 GB, 7.22, 78.6%. Baseline se Q4_K_M tak drop sirf lagbhag 1% hai, lekin model ek-tihai size ka ho gaya — aur Q3 par accuracy cliff se girti hai. "Knee" Q4 par hai.

Sweep 2 — F1 table (dusra, alag run — merge mat karo)

Book me ek dusri, task-based sweep bhi hai jo F1 score measure karti hai — yeh pehle wali accuracy table se alag run hai, alag numbers ke saath, isliye inhe ek table me merge mat karo: fp16 14.94 GB, perplexity 5.613, F1 44.0% → Q6_K 6.17 GB, 5.654, 43.4% → Q5_K_M 5.72 GB, 5.747, 43.3% → Q4_K_M 5.30 GB, 6.177, 42.1% → Q3_K_M 4.82 GB, 8.731, 40.0%. F1 low lag sakta hai, lekin open-ended questions ke liye healthy hai — token-overlap F1 model ke jawab ke words ko reference se compare karta hai, aur do perfectly good answers bhi paraphrasing ki wajah se fraction tokens hi share karte hain. Dono tables ki kahani ek hi hai: F1 44% se 42.1% tak dheere slide hota hai Q4 tak, phir Q3 par steep drop — wahi knee.

Yaad rakho: perplexity tripwire hai, task accuracy verdict hai — dono dekho. Aur do sweep tables alag runs hain (accuracy vs F1, alag perplexity aur sizes) — inhe kabhi ek table me merge mat karo. Q4_K_M default hai, lekin apne model par sweep karke confirm karo.

14.3Chapter 14 · Optimization and Quantization

The KV Cache, and the Full Compression Pipeline

Weights quantize karne se static size ka problem solve hua. Lekin memory ka dusra, dynamic consumer hai jo har token ke saath badhta hai — KV cache. Lambi inputs par yeh weights se bhi bada ho sakta hai, aur use manage karna hi model ko fast aur memory-bounded rakhta hai.

KV cache — formula

Har naya token pehle wale har token par attend karta hai. Pehle tokens ki keys (K) aur values (V) badalti nahi, isliye model unhe ek baar compute karke cache me store karta hai aur har agle token ke liye reuse karta hai — yahi optimization autoregressive generation ko practical banati hai. Size ka formula: kv_bytes = 2 × n_layers × n_kv_heads × head_dim × seq_len × batch × bytes-per-value (2 keys aur values ke liye). 4B-class model, 34 layers, 8,000-token context, 16-bit par — ek sequence ke liye 1 GB se zyada cache, weights ke upar. Kai conversations serve karo to cache hi decide karta hai kitna hardware chahiye.

Levers — GQA, cache quantization, PagedAttention, prefix caching, offloading

  • Grouped Query Attention (GQA): free win — kai query heads ek key/value head share karte hain, to n_kv_heads 4× ya 8× shrink ho jata hai. Modern architecture chunne se yeh muft me milta hai, configure karne ko kuch nahi.
  • KV-cache quantization: keys aur values ko 8-bit ya 4-bit me store karo — cache aadha ya ek-chauthai. llama.cpp me runtime flags (--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0), Transformers me cache_implementation="quantized" (quanto backend, 4 bits). 8-bit aam taur par quality me invisible hota hai; 4-bit kabhi long-range recall wale tasks par thoda cost karta hai — apne workload par test karo.
  • PagedAttention (vLLM): har sequence ke liye maximum length ka contiguous block reserve karne ki jagah cache ko chhote fixed-size pages me manage karo, demand par allocate karo — jaise operating system ki virtual memory. Common system prompt jaise identical pages requests ke beech share hote hain. Tum implement nahi karte, vLLM serve karke paate ho.
  • Prefix caching: har request wahi 800-token system prompt se shuru hoti ho to uske KV entries dobara compute kyun karo? Resident rakho aur reuse karo — time-to-first-token dramatically kam hota hai.
  • Offloading: cache GPU memory se bahar jaye to purane portions CPU RAM (ya disk) me spill karo aur demand par wapas lao. Latency ke badle capacity — overflow safety valve hai, per-request plan nahi.

Do aur optimizations — speculative decoding aur prefill/decode disaggregation

Speculative decoding: generation memory-bound hai — har token ke liye poora model memory se guzarna padta hai, jabki zyada tar tokens easy hote hain. Ek chhota draft model aage daud kar kai tokens propose karta hai, bada model ek forward pass me poori batch verify karta hai — accepted tokens free speedup hain, rejected par bade model ka prediction aata hai, to output lagbhag identical rehta hai. Typical speedup 2–3× predictable text par. Gemma 4 QAT collection ke draft models isi ke liye hain. Prefill/decode disaggregation: request ke do phases alag hardware chahte hain — prefill (poora prompt ek highly parallel, compute-bound pass) aur decode (ek-ek token, memory-bound loop). Scale par inhe alag GPU pools par split karo, prefill workers finished KV cache decode workers ko handover karte hain — data-center pattern hai, laptop wala nahi.

Full compression pipeline — quality gate ke saath

Script 05_compression_pipeline.py sab kuch ek repeatable pipeline me wire karta hai: merge → parity check → GGUF convert → quantize → measure. Core logic: base aur quantized dono ki task accuracy nikalo, drop = base_acc − quant_acc, aur agar drop max_acc_drop = 0.02 se zyada ho to pipeline loudly fail kare aur Q5_K_M try karne ko kahe — silently degraded model ship karne ki jagah. Compression tab done hota hai jab file chhoti ho aur prove ho ki woh abhi bhi kaafi achhi hai.

Before / after

Artifact: base + adapter (2 files) → medical-gemma-Q4_K_M.gguf (1 file). On-disk size: ~15 GB → ~4.5 GB. Loads on: 24 GB+ GPU → 8 GB laptop / CPU. Runtime dependency: transformers+PEFT → llama.cpp / Ollama. Task accuracy: 84.2% → 83.1% — sirf lagbhag ek point ki cost par data-center GPU se laptop tak ka safar.

Common pitfalls

  • 4-bit base me merge karna: double-quantization error bake ho jata hai — hamesha bf16/fp16 me merge karo.
  • Ghalat data par calibrate karna: medical model ko generic web text par calibrate karoge to medical questions par worse quantize hoga; test set par calibrate karoge to evaluation numbers fiction honge. Train, calibration aur test pools alag rakho.
  • Bina measure kiye ship karna: quantization degradation casual inspection se chhupti hai — teen cherry-picked prompts theek lagenge, user woh case hit karega jo tootta hai. Sweep chalao, table se decide karo.
  • Tokenizer ya chat-template mismatch: fine-tune ne special tokens ya template badla ho to woh har artifact ke saath travel karna chahiye — merged model aur GGUF dono me. Save tokenizer har step par.
  • Memory budget me KV cache bhoolna: weights ke liye hardware size karke deploy karoge, phir user lamba document paste karega aur cache weights se aage nikal jayega. Maximum supported context ke liye cache size up front compute karo.
Yaad rakho: compression pipeline ka gate hi asli product hai — max_acc_drop 0.02. File chhoti hona achievement nahi hai; file chhoti aur proven-good hona achievement hai. Aur KV cache ko budget me gino, warna woh production me surprise dega.
