← Previous14.2 · QAT vs PTQ, and Measuring What Quantization Costs→ Next15 · Serving the Expert
15Chapter 15 · Serving the Expert

Serving the Expert

Tumhare paas ab ek private expert model hai jo chal sakta hai — lekin disk par padi file product nahi hai. Jab tak koi process use memory me load karke requests sunne na lage, use koi call nahi kar sakta, koi user us tak pahunch nahi sakta. Yahi baat Chapters 12–13 ke diffusion models par bhi lagti hai — wahan sirf request ka shape alag hota hai (prompt aur image parameters andar, image bytes bahar), serving principles wahi hain.

Do ends of the spectrum

Edge case: ek user, ek machine, aksar offline — jaise clinic ki air-gapped machine jo patient data legally cloud ko bhej hi nahi sakti. Privacy aur simplicity dominate karte hain; model CPU, consumer GPU ya Apple Silicon par chalna chahiye; throughput matter nahi karta, kyunki ek waqt me ek hi conversation hai. Yahan Ollama strong hai. Throughput case: kai users, shared infrastructure, real product — traffic spike ke dauraan slowest user ki latency aur GPU saturation matter karte hain; continuous batching aur PagedAttention se GPU idle nahi baithta. Yahan vLLM ka territory hai. Achhi khabar: dono stacks wahi OpenAI-compatible API bolte hain, isliye tum edge par Ollama se prototype karo aur production me vLLM par deploy karo — client code badle bina.

Ollama — Modelfile

Ollama GGUF file se model tak ka fastest path hai: models manage karta hai, demand par load karta hai, sahi hardware assign karta hai, local HTTP API expose karta hai. Modelfile Dockerfile jaisa concept hai — model file, parameters aur config ek jagah: FROM ./medical-gemma-Q4_K_M.gguf; TEMPLATE me Gemma 4 ka <|turn> chat format bake hota hai (har turn <|turn> + role se khulta hai, isliye stop token turn-close par set hai); PARAMETER lines — temperature 0.3, top_p 0.9, top_k 40, num_ctx 8192; SYSTEM prompt. Template ko Modelfile me daalne se callers ko special tokens haath se assemble nahi karne padte.

Template mismatches — silent failure

Template mismatch error nahi deta — model load hota hai aur jawab bhi deta hai, lekin control tokens literal text ki tarah leak hote hain, generation stop token ke aage chalti hai ya beech me rukti hai, system prompt silently ignore hota hai, ya model base jaisa behave karta hai (kyunki fine-tune ka behavior exact token arrangement par keyed hai). Diagnose karne ke teen fast checks: ollama show --template ka output training ke apply_chat_template output se exactly match karna chahiye; system-prompt canary bhejo ("only reply like a pirate") taaki confirm ho instructions pahunch rahi hain; aur multi-turn exchange test karo, jo one-shot prompts kabhi touch nahi karte. Template verify hone ke baad bhi quality off lage to held-out test set ka ek slice served model par dobara chalao — Chapter 14 numbers se systematic drop dikhe to serving layer suspect hai, model nahi.

Create aur run karo

ollama create medical-gemma -f Chapter15/00_Modelfile se model register hota hai, phir ollama run medical-gemma "What are first-line treatments for type 2 diabetes?" se sawal poochho — ya sirf ollama run medical-gemma se chat session kholo. Ollama http://localhost:11434 par /v1 endpoint expose karta hai — OpenAI endpoints jaisa hi shape, jo client code ki zindagi aasan bana deta hai.

Yaad rakho: file product nahi hai, service product hai. Aur template mismatch sabse dhokhebaaz bug hai — model load hoga, jawab dega, lekin galat hoga. Canary test aur held-out retest hi use pakadte hain.
00_Modelfile — Ollama Modelfile — serve the quantized GGUF from Chapter 14  ·  GitHub ↗ 
# 00_Modelfile
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Turn your quantized GGUF artifact from Chapter 14 into a first-class Ollama
# model. Build it with:
#
#     ollama create medical-gemma -f 00_Modelfile
#     ollama run medical-gemma "What are the first-line treatments for T2DM?"
#
# The three things that make this a REAL deployment rather than a raw file:
#   1. FROM points at the exact GGUF you shipped, so the model you serve is
#      byte-for-byte the one you evaluated.
#   2. TEMPLATE bakes in the Gemma 4 chat format, so callers send plain
#      messages and never have to hand-assemble <|turn> / <turn|> tokens.
#   3. PARAMETER pins the decode settings you validated, so behaviour is the
#      same on every machine that pulls this model.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

FROM ./medical-gemma-Q4_K_M.gguf

# Gemma 4 chat template. The model was fine-tuned against this exact format;
# a mismatched template is the classic cause of a model that "loads fine but
# answers weirdly" (see Chapter 14's pitfalls).
#
# What changed from Gemma 2/3:
#   - Turns are wrapped in <|turn>ROLE ... <turn|> instead of
#     <start_of_turn>ROLE ... <end_of_turn>.
#   - There is a real "system" role, so the SYSTEM prompt below gets its own
#     turn instead of being folded into the first user message.
#   - Gemma 4 has a thinking mode, switched on by putting <|think|> in the
#     system turn. Chapter 14 trained with enable_thinking=False, so this
#     template never emits <|think|>. That keeps serving identical to training.
#
# The BOS token is not written here; Ollama adds it from the GGUF metadata.
# This template covers plain chat only (no tool calling or images), which is
# all the medical QA model was trained on.
TEMPLATE """{{- if .System }}<|turn>system
{{ .System }}<turn|>
{{ end }}
{{- range .Messages }}
{{- if eq .Role "user" }}<|turn>user
{{ .Content }}<turn|>
{{ else if eq .Role "assistant" }}<|turn>model
{{ .Content }}<turn|>
{{ end }}
{{- end }}<|turn>model
"""

# Pin decode settings you validated during evaluation. Low temperature for a
# domain where you want consistent, defensible answers. (Google's general
# defaults for Gemma 4 are temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64; we override
# them on purpose.)
PARAMETER temperature 0.3
PARAMETER top_p 0.9
PARAMETER top_k 40
PARAMETER num_ctx 8192
PARAMETER stop "<turn|>"

# Bake the guardrail persona into the served model so every caller inherits it,
# not just the ones who remember to send a system prompt. A system message
# sent by the caller replaces this default.
SYSTEM """You are a medical question-answering assistant for clinicians.
Answer concisely and cite the class of evidence when relevant.
You are not a substitute for professional judgement; flag when a question
needs a specialist or more patient context."""
01_openai_client.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
01_openai_client.py
-------------------
Talk to your private expert model using the official OpenAI Python SDK.

The point of this file: you do not write a custom client for your model.
Both Ollama and vLLM expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, so the same
code that talked to gpt-4 talks to your 4.5 GB medical Gemma running on a
laptop. You change two lines, base_url and model, and nothing else.

Run against Ollama (default):
    ollama serve                       # in another terminal
    python 01_openai_client.py

Run against vLLM instead:
    python 01_openai_client.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 \
        --model ./medical-gemma-merged

Streaming and non-streaming are both shown; streaming is what you want in a
UI so the user sees tokens as they are produced instead of waiting for the
whole answer.
"""
import argparse
from openai import OpenAI


def ask(client, model, question, stream=True):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]

    if not stream:
        resp = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=model, messages=messages, temperature=0.3, max_tokens=512,
        )
        return resp.choices[0].message.content

    # Streaming: print tokens as they arrive.
    out = []
    with client.chat.completions.stream(
        model=model, messages=messages, temperature=0.3, max_tokens=512,
    ) as s:
        for event in s:
            if event.type == "content.delta":
                print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
                out.append(event.delta)
        print()
    return "".join(out)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    # Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. For vLLM use http://localhost:8000/v1
    ap.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:11434/v1")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="medical-gemma")
    ap.add_argument("--no-stream", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # api_key is required by the SDK but ignored by a local server. Send anything.
    client = OpenAI(base_url=args.base, api_key="not-needed-for-local")

    question = "What are the first-line treatments for type 2 diabetes?"
    print(f"# {args.model} @ {args.base}\n")
    ask(client, args.model, question, stream=not args.no_stream)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
02_vllm_serve.sh — Shell script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 02_vllm_serve.sh
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serve your merged expert model with vLLM as an OpenAI-compatible API.
#
# vLLM is the throughput play: continuous batching + PagedAttention (Chapter 14)
# let one GPU serve many concurrent users far more efficiently than a naive
# loop. Use this when you are serving a product, not a single developer.
#
#   pip install vllm
#   bash 02_vllm_serve.sh
#
# Serve the MERGED bf16 model for maximum quality on a GPU with room, or point
# MODEL at a GPTQ / compressed-tensors build to fit a smaller card (see §15.4).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -euo pipefail

MODEL="${MODEL:-./medical-gemma-merged}"     # merged fp16 dir from Chapter 14
PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
MAX_LEN="${MAX_LEN:-8192}"                    # max context; sizes the KV cache

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
    --served-model-name medical-gemma \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port "$PORT" \
    --max-model-len "$MAX_LEN" \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --dtype bfloat16

# The server now speaks the same /v1 contract as Ollama and OpenAI:
#   curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
#     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#     -d '{"model":"medical-gemma",
#          "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain beta blockers."}]}'
#
# Point 01_openai_client.py at it with:
#   python 01_openai_client.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 --model medical-gemma

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 03_vllm_multi_lora.sh
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serve MANY experts from ONE base model. This is the callback to Chapter 14:
# when you have several fine-tunes of the same base (one adapter per specialty
# or per customer), do NOT merge and ship N full copies. Keep one base in GPU
# memory and hot-swap small LoRA adapters per request.
#
#   bash 03_vllm_multi_lora.sh
#
# Each request names which adapter it wants in the "model" field. vLLM applies
# the right adapter on the fly. Storage and memory cost scales with the base
# once, plus a few tens of MB per adapter, instead of a full model per expert.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -euo pipefail

BASE="${BASE:-google/gemma-4-e4b-it}"
PORT="${PORT:-8000}"

# Register each adapter as name=path. These are the LoRA dirs from earlier
# chapters; they must have been trained on the SAME base you serve here.
vllm serve "$BASE" \
    --enable-lora \
    --max-loras 4 \
    --max-lora-rank 16 \
    --lora-modules \
        cardiology=./adapters/cardiology-lora \
        oncology=./adapters/oncology-lora \
        general-med=./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --max-model-len 8192

# Route a request to a specific expert by naming the adapter as the model:
#
#   curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
#     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#     -d '{"model":"oncology",
#          "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Stage a T2N1M0 tumor."}]}'
#
# Switch "oncology" to "cardiology" and the next request uses a different
# adapter over the exact same base weights, with no reload.
04_structured_output.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
04_structured_output.py
-----------------------
Force your model to return valid JSON that matches a schema, every time.

An expert model is only useful in a pipeline if the software downstream can
parse its output. "Please respond in JSON" prompting fails often enough to
break production. Guided decoding solves it at the sampling level: the server
constrains the model so the ONLY tokens it can emit are ones that keep the
output valid against your schema. The result parses 100% of the time.

vLLM supports this through the OpenAI `response_format` / `guided_json` field.
Ollama supports it through its `format` field. This example uses vLLM.

    bash 02_vllm_serve.sh              # in another terminal
    python 04_structured_output.py
"""
import json
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="not-needed")

# The contract the rest of your system depends on.
TRIAGE_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "condition": {"type": "string"},
        "urgency": {"type": "string", "enum": ["routine", "urgent", "emergency"]},
        "refer_to_specialist": {"type": "boolean"},
        "reasoning": {"type": "string"},
    },
    "required": ["condition", "urgency", "refer_to_specialist", "reasoning"],
}

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="medical-gemma",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "58yo male, crushing chest pain radiating to left arm, "
                   "diaphoretic, 20 minutes. Triage this.",
    }],
    temperature=0.2,
    # vLLM extension: constrain generation to this JSON schema.
    extra_body={"guided_json": TRIAGE_SCHEMA},
)

raw = resp.choices[0].message.content
data = json.loads(raw)        # guaranteed to parse; that is the whole point
print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))

assert data["urgency"] in {"routine", "urgent", "emergency"}
print("\nParsed and schema-valid. Safe to hand to the next stage.")
05_load_test.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
05_load_test.py
---------------
Measure what your serving stack actually delivers under concurrency.

Two numbers decide whether a deployment is viable: per-request latency (how
long one user waits) and aggregate throughput (how many tokens/sec the server
sustains across all users). A single-user test tells you the first and hides
the second. This script fires N concurrent requests and reports both, so you
can compare Ollama vs vLLM on YOUR hardware instead of trusting a blog post.

    python 05_load_test.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 \
        --model medical-gemma --concurrency 16 --requests 64
"""
import argparse
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from openai import OpenAI

PROMPTS = [
    "What are the first-line treatments for type 2 diabetes?",
    "Explain the mechanism of action of beta blockers.",
    "When is a CT scan preferred over an MRI?",
    "List the common side effects of metformin.",
]


def one_request(client, model, prompt):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        temperature=0.3, max_tokens=256,
    )
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    toks = resp.usage.completion_tokens if resp.usage else 0
    return dt, toks


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:8000/v1")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="medical-gemma")
    ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    client = OpenAI(base_url=args.base, api_key="not-needed")

    latencies, total_tokens = [], 0
    wall_start = time.perf_counter()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.concurrency) as pool:
        futs = [
            pool.submit(one_request, client, args.model, PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)])
            for i in range(args.requests)
        ]
        for f in as_completed(futs):
            dt, toks = f.result()
            latencies.append(dt)
            total_tokens += toks
    wall = time.perf_counter() - wall_start

    latencies.sort()
    p50 = latencies[len(latencies) // 2]
    p95 = latencies[int(len(latencies) * 0.95) - 1]
    print(f"requests={args.requests} concurrency={args.concurrency}")
    print(f"wall time         {wall:6.2f} s")
    print(f"latency p50/p95   {p50:6.2f} / {p95:6.2f} s")
    print(f"throughput        {total_tokens / wall:7.1f} output tok/s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
06_fastapi_gateway.py — Python script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
"""
06_fastapi_gateway.py
---------------------
A thin production gateway in front of your model server.

Ollama and vLLM already speak OpenAI. So why put anything in front? Because
the last mile of serving is not inference, it is the boring operational glue:
an auth check so not everyone on the network can hit your model, a health
endpoint your load balancer can poll, a request timeout so one slow call can't
pin a worker forever, and a single place to add logging and rate limits.

This gateway forwards chat requests to your backend (Ollama or vLLM) and adds
those concerns without re-implementing inference. Crucially, it moves BYTES,
not parsed JSON: the response is piped through as the backend produces it, so
token-by-token streaming survives the trip. A gateway that called resp.json()
would buffer the whole answer, turning time-to-first-token into
time-to-last-token and breaking "stream": true requests entirely.

    pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx
    BACKEND=http://localhost:8000/v1 API_KEY=secret uvicorn 06_fastapi_gateway:app --port 9000
"""
import os
import time
import httpx
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException, Header
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask

BACKEND = os.environ.get("BACKEND", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
API_KEY = os.environ.get("API_KEY", "")           # empty disables auth

# Timeouts need care with streaming: CONNECT_TIMEOUT guards a dead backend,
# but the read timeout must be long enough that a healthy long generation
# doesn't get killed mid-stream. Tune READ_TIMEOUT to your slowest expected
# generation, not your fastest.
CONNECT_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("CONNECT_TIMEOUT", "5"))
READ_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("READ_TIMEOUT", "120"))

app = FastAPI(title="expert-gateway")
_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    base_url=BACKEND,
    timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=CONNECT_TIMEOUT, read=READ_TIMEOUT,
                          write=10.0, pool=5.0),
)


@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    # Cheap liveness check for a load balancer. Confirms the backend answers.
    try:
        r = await _client.get("/models")
        return {"status": "ok" if r.status_code == 200 else "degraded"}
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="backend unreachable")


@app.post("/v1/chat/completions")
async def chat(request: Request, authorization: str = Header(default="")):
    if API_KEY and authorization != f"Bearer {API_KEY}":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="invalid api key")

    body = await request.body()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        # Open the backend request in streaming mode. We get the response
        # headers here, but the body is NOT read yet -- it flows through the
        # StreamingResponse below as the model produces it.
        upstream_req = _client.build_request(
            "POST", "/chat/completions", content=body,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        upstream = await _client.send(upstream_req, stream=True)
    except httpx.TimeoutException:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=504, detail="model timed out")
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail="backend unreachable")

    ttfb_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
    # One structured log line per request is the foundation of observability.
    # With streaming we log time-to-first-byte; total duration would require
    # waiting for the stream to finish, which is exactly what we're avoiding.
    print(f'{{"path":"/v1/chat/completions","status":{upstream.status_code},'
          f'"ttfb_ms":{ttfb_ms:.0f}}}')

    # Pipe the response through untouched -- works identically for a single
    # JSON body and for an SSE token stream, because both are just bytes.
    # BackgroundTask closes the upstream connection after the last byte.
    return StreamingResponse(
        upstream.aiter_raw(),
        status_code=upstream.status_code,
        media_type=upstream.headers.get("content-type"),
        background=BackgroundTask(upstream.aclose),
    )
07_vllm_runtime_lora.sh — Shell script  ·  GitHub ↗ 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 07_vllm_runtime_lora.sh
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serve the UNMODIFIED base + apply the medical-qa LoRA at runtime on vLLM.
#
# Why this exists: a *merged* Gemma 4 E4B currently fails to load on vLLM,
# because a faithful merge drops the KV-shared tail layers' K/V weights and this
# vLLM version doesn't yet implement KV sharing (see the version note in 15.4.1).
# But the STOCK base loads fine, because its checkpoint physically ships those
# weights. So instead of merging, load the base and attach the small adapter at
# request time. You never write a stripped checkpoint, so you never hit the gap.
#
#   pip install vllm
#   bash 07_vllm_runtime_lora.sh
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -euo pipefail

BASE="${BASE:-google/gemma-4-e4b-it}"
ADAPTER_PATH="${ADAPTER_PATH:-./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora}"   # the trained LoRA dir
PORT="${PORT:-8000}"

# --max-lora-rank must be >= the adapter's r (see adapter_config.json). 16 is a
# safe ceiling for the r=4/8/16 adapters in this book; raising it only costs a
# little memory.
vllm serve "$BASE" \
    --enable-lora \
    --lora-modules medical-qa="$ADAPTER_PATH" \
    --max-lora-rank 16 \
    --served-model-name gemma-base \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port "$PORT" \
    --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

# Route a request to the fine-tune by naming the ADAPTER as the model:
#   curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
#     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#     -d '{"model":"medical-qa",
#          "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"First-line treatments for T2DM?"}]}'
#
# Name "gemma-base" instead to hit the un-adapted base, so you can A/B the two
# and confirm the adapter is actually changing the answers.
#
# Or reuse the chapter's client:
#   python 01_openai_client.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 --model medical-qa
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 15 — Serving the Expert
← Previous14.3 · The KV Cache, and the Full Compression Pipeline→ Next15.1 · The OpenAI Endpoint, Streaming, and vLLM at Scale
15.1Chapter 15 · Serving the Expert

The OpenAI Endpoint, Streaming, and vLLM at Scale

OpenAI endpoint format hosted API se baat karne ka de facto standard ban gaya hai: POST /v1/chat/completions, body me model name, messages ki list, aur temperature/stream jaise parameters. Ollama bhi yahi bolta hai, isliye tumhara client code backend se decoupled rehta hai — dono taraf contract samajhte hon to koi bhi side badal sakti hai bina application tode.

Client — do lines

OpenAI SDK ko base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1" par point karo — local server api_key ko ignore karta hai, SDK ko phir bhi chahiye hota hai. Baad me vLLM par jao to sirf wahi ek line badalti hai, baaki code wahi rehta hai. Yeh decoupling hi poori chapter ki jaan hai.

Streaming — fast nahi, fast feel hota hai

client.chat.completions.stream() se content.delta events token by token aate hain. Yeh response ko speed up nahi karta — shayad thoda slow bhi kare — lekin fast feel hota hai, kyunki user token by token padhta rehta hai, blank screen par spinning wheel dekhne ki jagah. Purana mechanism abhi bhi har SDK version par kaam karta hai: create() me stream=True pass karo aur chunk.choices[0].delta.content se text nikalo. Naya stream() helper usi ke upar convenience wrapper hai — typed events, with block se cleanup, aur ant me assembled final message. Purane SDK releases me woh client.beta.chat.completions.stream() par rehta tha — attribute error aaye to package update karo ya stream=True par fallback karo.

vLLM — throughput ke liye

Ollama ek conversation ke liye bana hai; concurrent users aate hi problem ka shape badal jata hai. vLLM ground-up throughput ke liye bana inference server hai — standard Hugging Face model directory padhta hai, to Chapter 14 ka merged bf16 model seedha kaam karta hai. Install venv me karo (pip install vllm), NVIDIA GPU chahiye — na ho to Colab ya Chapter 3 ke rental GPUs. Serve command: vllm serve ./medical-gemma-merged --served-model-name medical-gemma --port 8000 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --dtype bfloat16 (script Chapter15/02_vllm_serve.sh) — port 8000 par OpenAI-compatible server shuru hota hai, wahi client unchanged baat karta hai.

Do techniques — continuous batching aur PagedAttention

Continuous batching: naive server static batching karta hai — group collect karo, sab saath chalao, sabse slow request ka wait karo. vLLM token level par schedule karta hai: jis sequence ka kaam khatm hua, uski slot turant waiting request se refill ho jati hai — GPU kabhi idle nahi, naya kaam turant shuru. PagedAttention: har sequence ke liye maximum length ka contiguous block reserve karne ki jagah cache ko chhote fixed-size pages me manage karo, demand par allocate karo — virtual memory jaisa. Common system prompt jaise identical pages requests ke beech share hote hain, to wahi GPU memory me zyada concurrent conversations fit hote hain.

Measure karo, assume mat karo

Load-test script code/05_load_test.py configurable concurrency par requests fire karke per-request latency aur aggregate throughput report karta hai. Ollama ko concurrency 1 par aur vLLM ko concurrency 16 par chalao — shape saaf dikhega: Ollama single-user latency jeetta hai, vLLM concurrency badhte hi total throughput jeetta hai. Precision note: GPU par jagah ho to merged bf16 serve karo; na ho to GPU-friendly quantized build lo — GPTQ ya official QAT w4a16 checkpoints, Ollama wala GGUF nahi. Chapter 14 ka bit-width "knee" yahan bhi accuracy trade govern karta hai.

Gemma 4 considerations — teen quirks

  • CUDA version mismatch: vLLM prebuilt CUDA binaries ship karta hai; wheel ka CUDA driver ke CUDA se match na ho to import fail hota hai (libcudart.so.13 missing). Fix: nvidia-smi se driver CUDA dekho, vLLM reinstall karo taaki build match kare, runtime restart karo.
  • Processor files: Gemma 4 multimodal hai, isliye vLLM checkpoint ko Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration resolve karke preprocessor_config.json aur processor_config.json expect karta hai — text-only model ke liye bhi. Chapter 14 ka merge script full processor save karta hai, isliye yeh files pehle se present hongi.
  • Cross-layer KV sharing (num_kv_shared_layers): baad ki layers pehli layers ke keys/values reuse karti hain — memory win, lekin serving stack ko pattern explicitly implement karna padta hai. vLLM ka support Gemma 4 ship hone ke baad kai releases me mature hua; early versions merged checkpoint load nahi kar pate the (shared tail layers ke missing k_proj/v_proj tensors par fail — jo absent hone hi chahiye), ya runtime LoRA refuse karte the, ya usse bura — adapter load hua dikhata tha lekin silently base-model answers deta tha. Deploy se pehle latest vLLM install karo, apna path try karo, aur held-out test set ka slice served model par dobara chalao. Cleanly start hone wala server is baat ka proof nahi hai ki tumhara fine-tune serve ho raha hai.

Unmerged adapter serve karna

vllm serve google/gemma-4-e4b-it --enable-lora --lora-modules medical-qa=./medical-qa-v1-gemma4-lora --max-lora-rank 16 --served-model-name gemma-base --port 8000 --max-model-len 8192 — phir curl se medical-qa (fine-tune) aur gemma-base (base) ko side by side poochho. Dono ke jawab identical aaye to adapter apply hi nahi ho raha — production me pakadne ki jagah ek curl me pakad liya. Merged ek steady expert ke liye cleaner ship hai (ek file, koi configure karne ko nahi); unmerged iteration me jeetta hai — adapter retrain karo, server restart karo, merge-and-requantize cycle ke bina naya version test karo.

Kai experts, ek base — golden rule

Ek base GPU memory me, adapters per request hot-swap: --max-loras 4 ke saath --lora-modules cardiology=... oncology=... general-med=... (script Chapter15/03_vllm_multi_lora.sh). Request model field me adapter ka naam likh kar expert choose karti hai — cardiology ek sawal, oncology agla, dono wahi base weights par, beech me koi reload nahi. Economics saaf hai: das merged models = base ki das copies (storage aur GPU memory dono me 10×); das adapters = ek base + das chhote deltas. Golden rule: ek expert serve karo to merge karke ship karo; fleet serve karo to adapters alag rakho.

Yaad rakho: server ka cleanly start hona proof nahi hai — held-out test set ka slice dobara chalana proof hai. Aur unmerged vs merged ka faisla simple hai: ek steady expert ho to merge karo, iteration ya fleet ho to adapter alag rakho.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 15 — Serving the Expert
← Previous15 · Serving the Expert→ Next15.2 · Production Concerns, and the Future Is Specialized
15.2Chapter 15 · Serving the Expert

Production Concerns, and the Future Is Specialized

Demo aur service ka farak operational glue hai — output reliably parse ho, boundaries hon ki kaun model ko call kar sakta hai aur kab, aur observability ho ki kuch gadbad ho to pata chale. Yeh section wahi glue lagata hai, aur phir book ko band karta hai.

Structured output — guided decoding

Model se politely "JSON me jawab do" kehna production me aksar fail hota hai — brace se pehle ek stray sentence, trailing comma, hallucinated field — aur downstream code toot jata hai. JSON ek format descriptor hai, format khud nahi — JSON me output express karne ke countless tareeke hain. Fix guided decoding hai, jo prompt level par nahi, sampling level par kaam karta hai: server generation ko constrain karta hai taaki sirf wahi tokens emit ho sakien jo output ko tumhare schema ke against valid rakhte hain — invalid output unrepresentable ban jata hai. vLLM me guided_json: triage schema (condition string, urgency enum — routine / urgent / emergency, refer_to_specialist boolean) extra_body se pass karo, to json.loads(...) parse hone ki guarantee hai. Ollama me wahi capability format field se milti hai. Jab model chatbot nahi, bade system ka component ho, to yeh essential hai.

Gateway — thin layer, badi discipline

Ollama aur vLLM pehle se OpenAI bolte hain, to saamne kuch aur kyun? Kyunki model server ka kaam inference hai — baaki concerns alag hain: authentication (network par jo bhi ho woh tumhara GPU spend na kar sake), health-check endpoint (load balancer poll karke traffic route kare), request timeout (ek slow generation worker ko hamesha ke liye pin na kare), aur logs aur rate limits ke liye ek jagah. FastAPI gateway (script Chapter15/06_fastapi_gateway.py): /health backend ke /models endpoint ko poll karta hai; /v1/chat/completions Bearer API key check karta hai (galat ho to 401) aur backend timeouts ko 504 me translate karta hai — OpenAI contract preserve karte hue, taaki clients ko pata hi na chale peeche kya hai. Note: printed version poora response buffer karke return karta hai, isliye stream nahi kar sakta; full script StreamingResponse se bytes pipe karta hai, taaki streaming aur non-streaming dono untouched pass hon.

Observability aur capacity

Do numbers day one se log karo: per-request latency aur real concurrency par throughput. Gateway ki per-request structured log line hi iski seed hai. Averages par mat jao — sabse slow 5% users par nazar rakho, kyunki averages woh spikes chhupa dete hain jinse users chhod kar chale jate hain. Capacity planning me Chapter 14 ka KV-cache math wapas aata hai: static weights sirf memory budget ka ek hissa hain — user ne lamba document paste kiya to cache weights se aage nikal sakta hai. Maximum supported context up front compute karo, aur cache quantization ya PagedAttention se manage karo.

Conclusion — future specialized hai

Book ki shuruaat API wall se hui thi — per token rent par generalist, jo sab kuch thoda-thoda janta tha aur tumhare domain ke baare me lagbhag kuch nahi. Phir tum transformer ke andar gaye, LoRA aur QLoRA se kuch million parameters train kiye, loss curves padhna aur held-out test sets se evaluate karna seekha, aur DPO se model ko sirf sahi jawab nahi, sahi tareeke se jawab dena sikhaya. Phir language se bahar nikle — Gemma 4 ki vision side ko domain images par fine-tune kiya, aur diffusion me wahi playbook ek bilkul alag architecture par lagayi: DreamBooth se subject, style LoRA se look. Aakhir me adapter merge kiya, measure karke quantize kiya, aur do tareekon se serve kiya — laptop par privately Ollama se, production throughput par vLLM se.

LLM AI ka pehla era mutthi bhar multibillion-dollar generalists ka tha. Agla leap specialization hai — ek model jo sab kuch janta ho uski jagah specialists ka swarm, har ek ek narrow area me deep (hospital ke protocols, company ka codebase, illustrator ki style) — har ek itna chhota ki privately chal sake, itna sasta ki duniya badle to retrain ho sake. Book ki closing call: ek domain lo jise tum kisi bhi web crawl se behtar samajhte ho. Data jama karo. Train karo. Evaluate karo. Compress karo. Serve karo. Aur apne customers ko apni AI own karne me madad karo.

Yaad rakho: guided decoding se output parseable banao, gateway se service safe banao, slowest 5% users se health napo — aur phir apna expert banao. Future generalists ka nahi, specialists ka hai.
SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 15 — Serving the Expert

L1Interactive Lab

VRAM Math Lab — Kitni Memory Chahiye?

Model size, precision aur method badlo — dekho training ke liye kitni VRAM chahiye. Training memory inference memory se bahut alag hoti hai: optimizer states, gradients aur activations sab add hote hain.

TRY ITSliders ghumao — VRAM budget dekho
VRAM budget — kya fit hoga?

  
Usool (Chapter 3, Tables 3-1 to 3-5): 7B model ka full fine-tuning ~86 GB, LoRA ~17 GB, QLoRA ~7 GB leta hai. Full FT me weights + gradients (2 bytes/param) + optimizer states (8 bytes/param) + activations (~2 GB) add hote hain. QLoRA me base hamesha NF4 4-bit me store hota hai — precision selector us par lagu nahi hota.




SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — The Fine-Tuner's Workshop

Tokenizer Lab — Ek Line, Kitne Tokens?
Apna text type karo ya sample chuno — dekho alag vocabulary wale tokenizers usko kitne tokens me todte hain. Token count seedha cost se judta hai: har token ka paisa lagta hai.



  
TRY ITText badlo — token count dekho

  

    
    

      
      
      
      
    

    
  

  

  
Token count aur cost

  
Usool (Chapter 2): bada vocabulary matlab har word ke liye kam tokens, par bada embedding matrix. Book ka example: wahi 4 Chinese characters ek tokenizer me 4 tokens aur doosre me 2 tokens hote hain — isliye token count (aur cost) tokenizer par depend karta hai. Cost rates Chapter 1, Table 1-1 se hain.

L3Interactive Lab
LoRA Config Lab — Rank, Alpha aur Trainable Parameters
Rank aur alpha badlo — dekho kitne parameters train honge aur adapter kitna bada banega. LoRA poora weight matrix update karne ke bajay ek chhota low-rank update seekhta hai.



  
TRY ITRank badlo — trainable params dekho

  

    
    
    
  

  

  
Trainable parameters

  
Usool (Chapter 7): update ΔW = BA hota hai, aur forward pass h = W₀x + (α/r)·BAx. Book ka worked config: rank 16, all-linear par 38,879,232 trainable parameters — kul 7,979,980,064 ka 0.4872%, lagbhag 150 MB adapter. Rank 4 par wahi config 9.7M parameters (0.17%, ~39 MB) deta hai. Rank guide: 8 simple task, 16–32 sweet spot, 64–128 complex task, 256+ full fine-tuning ke kareeb — aur performance plateau karta hai, bada hamesha behtar nahi.




SOURCESource: Fine-Tuning AI, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — The Mechanics of Adaptation

F1End Matter · FAQs
FAQs
Fine-tuning interviews (current era) ke liye — LoRA se lekar DPO aur serving tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 LoRA kya hai aur ye full fine-tuning se kaise alag hai?
LoRA me base model ke weights freeze rehte hain aur sirf ek chhota low-rank update seekha jata hai — ΔW = BA, jahan B aur A chhoti matrices hain. Full fine-tuning me har weight update hota hai, isliye usme zyada VRAM, zyada storage aur catastrophic forgetting ka risk hota hai. LoRA adapter sirf kuch MB ka hota hai, merge karne par inference cost zero hoti hai, aur ek base par kai adapters rakh sakte ho.
Q02 QLoRA kya hai aur ye LoRA se kab behtar hai?
QLoRA me base model 4-bit NF4 me store hota hai (double quantization ke saath) aur us par LoRA lagta hai. Isse 7B model ki training ~7 GB VRAM me ho jati hai, jabki LoRA ~17 GB aur full FT ~86 GB leta hai. Jab GPU chhota ho ya Colab free tier par kaam karna ho, QLoRA se shuru karo — book ki bhi yahi salah hai. Dhyaan do: embeddings quantize nahi hote, isliye saving clean 4x nahi hoti.
Q03 LoRA me rank (r) kaise chunein? Bada rank hamesha behtar hai?
Nahi — performance plateau karta hai. Simple task ke liye rank 8, aam taur par 16–32 sweet spot hai, complex task ke liye 64–128, aur 256+ full fine-tuning ke kareeb pahunch jata hai. Book ka worked config rank 16 par 38,879,232 trainable parameters (0.4872%) deta hai. Pehle 16 se shuru karo, phir zaroorat pade to badhao — rank badhane se pehle data quality aur epochs check karo.
Q04 LoRA me alpha kya karta hai? Alpha = 2r ka rule kyun hai?
Forward pass me update ko (α/r) se scale kiya jata hai: h = W₀x + (α/r)·BAx. Alpha = 2r rakhne se scaling factor 2 hota hai, jo book ka default hai. Alpha badhane se adapter ka asar badhta hai — ye learning rate jaisa kaam karta hai. Alpha ko rank se alag tune karna ek aasan tareeka hai adapter ki strength badalne ka, bina dobara train kiye.
Q05 LoRA adapter ko merge kaise karte hain, aur kab merge NAHI karna chahiye?
Merge karne par W_merged = W₀ + (α/r)·BA hota hai — adapter base weights me fold ho jata hai aur inference overhead zero ho jata hai. Par merge tab mat karo jab multi-adapter hot-swapping chahiye ho ya vLLM ka runtime LoRA use karna ho. Aur kabhi 4-bit base me merge mat karo — pehle bf16/fp16 me merge karo, phir quantize karo, warna accuracy kharab hogi.
Q06 Full fine-tuning vs PEFT — interview me kaunsa kab choose karoge?
Jab data bahut zyada ho, domain base se bahut alag ho, aur GPU budget bada ho — tab full FT socho. Aam taur par PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA) behtar hai: kam VRAM, kam storage, kam forgetting, aur fast iteration. Book ka frame: 8B model ka full FT 68–72 GB VRAM mangta hai, jabki QLoRA 10–12 GB me ho jata hai. Zyada tar production fine-tune aaj LoRA se hi hote hain.
Q07 Catastrophic forgetting kya hai aur isse kaise bachte hain?
Jab saare weights update hote hain to model nayi task seekhte-seekhte apni general abilities bhool sakta hai — yahi catastrophic forgetting hai. Bachne ke tareeke: LoRA use karo (base freeze rehta hai), learning rate chhota rakho, general data ka thoda hissa training me milao, aur general-knowledge checks se forgetting measure karo. DPO me reference model aur beta isi drift ko control karte hain.
Q08 Full fine-tuning me VRAM kahan kharch hoti hai?
Sirf weights nahi — gradients aur optimizer states sabse bada hissa hote hain. Book ke hisab se 8B model par Adam states akele 48 GB (16-bit) lete hain, gradients 16 GB aur activations 4–8 GB. Isliye 7B ka full FT ~86 GB tak pahunch jata hai. 8-bit optimizer (paged_adamw_8bit) states ko 80 MB se 20 MB tak gira deta hai — ye ek aasan jeet hai.
Q09 VRAM math yaad rakhne ka shortcut kya hai?
Bytes per parameter yaad rakho: FP32 4 bytes, FP16/BF16 2 bytes, INT8 1 byte, INT4 0.5 bytes. 7B model FP32 me ~28 GB sirf weights ke liye leta hai — optimizer se pehle. Phir method ka multiplier lagao: full FT ~86 GB, LoRA ~17 GB, QLoRA ~7 GB (7B ke liye). Interview me pehle weights nikalo, phir gradients + optimizer + activations add karo — stepwise jawab do.
Q10 Training ke liye GPU kaise chunein — RTX 4090, A100 ya Colab?
Colab free T4 (~15 GB) shuruaat ke liye kaafi hai — book ki recommendation bhi yahi hai. RTX 4090 (24 GB) 7B tak LoRA/QLoRA ke liye solid hai. A100 40/80 GB full FT aur bade runs ke liye hai. Hamesha pehle VRAM budget nikalo, phir GPU chuno — ulta mat karo. Apple Silicon unified memory me bade model RAM me rakh sakta hai, par bitsandbytes support nahi milta.
Q11 Fine-tuning ke liye dataset me sabse zyada kya matter karta hai?
Teen pillars: relevance (domain ka data), correctness (sahi jawab) aur diversity (asli variation ki coverage). Quantity nahi, quality goal hai — LoRA ke saath kuch sau achhe examples bhi asar dikhate hain. Galat data model ko galat cheez faithfully sikha dega, isliye cleaning optional nahi hai.
Q12 Dataset cleaning me kya-kya karna zaroori hai?
Normalization (Unicode NFC/NFKC, HTML tags hatana), filtering (length cut-off, language detection, quality filter), aur deduplication (exact duplicates MD5 se, near-duplicates MinHash + LSH se). Dedup do baar matter karta hai: duplicate compute waste karta hai aur test examples training me leak karke evaluation ko inflate kar deta hai.
Q13 Synthetic data kab use karna chahiye aur kab nahi?
Jab asli data kam ho, private ho ya mehenga ho — tab teacher model se synthetic data banao. Jab asli data mil sakta hai, wahi jeetta hai. Teacher-student paradigm me bada teacher data generate karta hai aur chhota student us par fine-tune hota hai. Terms of service ka dhyaan rakho: kai proprietary APIs apne outputs se competing model train karne par rok lagate hain, isliye open-weights teacher use karo.
Q14 Synthetic data diverse kaise banayein? Naive generation kyun fail hoti hai?
Ek hi baar me 1,000 sawal mangne par repetitive, lagbhag identical output milta hai. Seed-based generation karo: categories × conditions × question types ko combine karke 320 seed combinations banao, phir sample karo — diversity design ki jati hai, ummeed nahi ki jati. Book me temperature 0.9 variety ke liye use hota hai aur 5 examples per call se sirf 200 calls me 1,000 examples bante hain.
Q15 Synthetic data ki quality control kaise karte hain?
Doosra model verifier ki tarah kaam kare — temperature 0.1 par lagbhag 10% examples review ke liye flag hote hain. Filtering rules: jawab 200–2,000 characters ke beech, condition jawab me aani chahiye, aur lagbhag 20% examples khona normal hai. 30% se zyada kho rahe ho to prompts sudharo; 5% se kam kho rahe ho to quality check bahut dheela hai. N-gram overlap ratio 0.7 se neeche repetition ka red flag hai.
Q16 Fine-tuned model ko evaluate kaise karte hain — sirf loss dekhna kaafi hai?
Nahi. Chaar tareeke, saste se mehenga: 100+ prompts par side-by-side comparison, perplexity, LLM-as-a-judge, aur domain benchmarks. Book me perplexity exp(eval_loss) base 27.412 se adapted 8.446 tak gira (~69% behtar), aur LLM-as-a-judge me adapted model ki win rate 73% thi. Har method ka apna bias hota hai — ek par bharosa mat karo.
Q17 Perplexity kya batati hai aur healthy range kya hai?
Perplexity = exp(eval_loss) — model text ko kitna achha predict karta hai. Book ka rule of thumb: 1–2 matlab leakage (test data training me aa gaya), 2–4 healthy, 6 se zyada matlab overfitting ya kharab fit. Perplexity tripwire hai, verdict nahi — final faisla task accuracy aur side-by-side comparison se karo.
Q18 LLM-as-a-judge ke biases kya hain aur unse kaise bachte hain?
Position bias (pehle wala jawab jeet jata hai) aur verbosity bias (lamba jawab behtar lagta hai) sabse common hain. Bachne ke liye A/B order randomize karo, strong judge model use karo, runs repeat karo, aur golden answers ke against score karo. Judge ko human evaluation ka replacement mat banao — wo ek signal hai, faisla nahi.
Q19 RLHF kya hai aur DPO usse kaise alag hai?
RLHF teen stages me hota hai: SFT, phir reward model, phir PPO optimisation — isme teen models aur do datasets chahiye, PPO finicky hai, aur reward hacking ka risk hai. DPO reward model ko hata deta hai aur chosen vs rejected pairs par seedha optimise karta hai: loss = −log σ(β · margin). Simple, stable, aur aam taur par pehli pasand.
Q20 DPO loss kaise kaam karta hai? Beta kya control karta hai?
DPO chosen aur rejected jawabon ki log-probabilities nikalta hai, frozen reference model ke against unka ratio leta hai, phir margin par loss lagata hai: −log σ(β · margin). Beta KL control hai — bada beta model ko reference ke kareeb rakhta hai. Default 0.1 hai, aaj-kal 0.01–0.05 bhi common hai. Beta bahut chhota ho to model drift kar jata hai, bahut bada ho to alignment ka asar kam ho jata hai.
Q21 DPO kab use karna chahiye aur kab bilkul nahi?
Jab failure style, tone ya safety ka ho — tab DPO behtareen hai. Jab failure knowledge ka ho — model ko facts hi nahi pata — tab DPO kuch nahi kar sakta; pehle SFT se knowledge sikhao. Book ka decision framework yahi hai: style/safety = DPO, knowledge = SFT + data. DPO run karne se pehle SFT adapter merge karo aur naya LoRA train karo.
Q22 DPO training ke practical numbers kya hain?
Book ki run: naya LoRA rank 8, alpha 8, dropout 0.1; beta 0.1; 3 epochs; batch 2×4 = 8; LR 2e-5 (5e-5 par overfit hota hai); cosine schedule; 266 train / 30 eval; ~33 steps per epoch; ~19M parameters (0.25% se kam). Training loss 0.68 se 0.14 tak gaya. Yaad rakho: har example do sequences hota hai, isliye memory SFT se lagbhag double hoti hai.
Q23 Quantization kya hai aur Q4_K_M 'knee' kyun hai?
Quantization weights ko kam bits me store karta hai — scale aur zero-point se floats ko chhote integers par map kiya jata hai. Book ke sweep me FP16 (14.90 GB, accuracy 84.2%) se Q4_K_M (4.68 GB, accuracy 83.1%) tak nuksan bahut kam hai, par Q3_K_M (3.79 GB) par accuracy 78.6% tak gir jati hai — wahi cliff hai. Isliye Q4_K_M workhorse hai: size me 3x chhota, accuracy lagbhag wahi.
Q24 Accuracy sweep aur F1 sweep ko alag kyun rakhna chahiye?
Kyunki ye do alag runs hain, alag metrics ke saath. Accuracy run me FP16 84.2%, Q4 83.1%, Q3 78.6% hai; F1 run me FP16 44.0%, Q4 42.1%, Q3 40.0% hai — aur unki perplexity values bhi alag hain (6.41 vs 5.613 FP16 par). Dono ko mix karke ek table banaoge to galat conclusion niklega. Interview me hamesha batao ki kaunsa number kis run ka hai.
Q25 QAT vs PTQ me kya fark hai?
PTQ training ke baad weights ko round kar deta hai — fast aur simple, par low bits par accuracy girti hai. QAT training ke dauraan hi rounding simulate karta hai, taaki model uske hisab se adapt ho jaye — behtar accuracy, par zyada mehnat. Book me official QAT checkpoints ka zikr hai jinse fine-tune kiya ja sakta hai. Aam deployment me PTQ se shuru karo; QAT tab jab Q4 se neeche jana ho.
Q26 KV cache kya hai aur ye memory budget me kyun matter karta hai?
Har generated token ke keys aur values cache hote hain taaki dobara compute na karna pade — formula: 2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × seq len × batch × bytes per value. 8k context par ye 1 GB se zyada ho jata hai aur har token ke saath badhta hai. GQA (kam KV heads) isko free me chhota karta hai. Lambi documents serve karte waqt KV cache hi aksar memory khatam karta hai, weights nahi.
Q27 vLLM vs Ollama — kaunsa kab use karein?
Ollama local/edge ke liye hai: single user, offline, privacy-first — single-user latency me jeetta hai. vLLM throughput ke liye hai: continuous batching aur PagedAttention se concurrent users par GPU kabhi idle nahi rehta. Dono OpenAI-compatible API bolte hain, isliye client code badle bina prototype se production ja sakte ho. Book ka load test yahi dikhata hai: concurrency badhne par vLLM aage nikal jata hai.
Q28 vLLM me runtime LoRA kaise serve karte hain?
vLLM ko --enable-lora ke saath chalao aur --lora-modules se adapters map karo, jaise medical-qa=./adapter-path. Phir model name se hi adapter choose hota hai — ek base model memory me, kai adapters hot-swappable. --max-loras 4 jaise flags se ek saath kitne adapters serve honge, ye control hota hai. Merged model ek expert ke liye cleaner hai; adapters ki fleet ke liye unmerged behtar hai.
Q29 Serving cost kaise estimate karte hain?
Pehle tokens/day nikalo (requests × tokens per request), phir GPU-hours (tokens / throughput), phir cost (GPU-hours × $/hour). Book ka token tax yaad rakho: API par $30 se $180 per million tokens tak rate hai, jabki khud ka chhota fine-tuned model usse bahut sasta pad sakta hai. Hamesha load test se measure karo — throughput assume karna sabse common galti hai.
Q30 Diffusion model ko LoRA se fine-tune kaise karte hain?
UNet ki attention projections (to_q / to_k / to_v / to_out.0) par LoRA lagta hai — VAE aur text encoder frozen rehte hain. Rank 8–32, lagbhag 0.8M trainable parameters (UNet ka 0.09%), aur adapter 50–150 MB ka banta hai. Subject ke liye DreamBooth (rare token + class-prior images) aur style ke liye style LoRA — mechanism ek hi hai, dataset alag hai.
Q31 DreamBooth me prior preservation kyun zaroori hai?
Rare token (jaise 'sks') ko subject se bind karte waqt model class ka matlab bhool sakta hai — jaise 'dog' ka matlab hi badal jaye. Isliye 200+ class-prior images ke saath train karte hain aur loss = subject loss + prior weight × prior loss rakhte hain (prior weight aam taur par 1.0). Recipe: 3–8 photos, 800–2,000 steps, LR 1e-4. Validation ke liye fixed 32 tuples use karo, kyunki per-step loss random timestep ki wajah se noisy hota hai.
Q32 Vision-language model (VLM) ko fine-tune karne ki strategies kya hain?
Teen strategies: (1) sirf language model par LoRA — sabse sasta aur aksar kaafi; (2) language model + projector — book ki choice, taaki vision features language space me behtar land karein; (3) vision tower bhi unfreeze — mehenga, sirf tab jab images encoder ki training distribution se bahut bahar hon. Book me QLoRA vision ke liye FAIL hota hai — quantized encoder confidently hallucinate karta hai — isliye bf16 LoRA use hota hai.
Q33 VLM fine-tuning me sabse common galti kya hai?
remove_unused_columns=False bhool jana — iske bina image data silently drop ho jata hai aur loss flat rehta hai. Doosri galti: resolution vs token budget ka dhyaan na rakhna — har image 70 se 1,120 soft tokens tak le sakti hai. Teesri: base model ko pehle test kiye bina seedha fine-tune karna — agar base tumhari images ko describe kar leta hai, to sasti strategy hi kaafi hai.
Q34 Learning rate schedule kya hota hai aur cosine kyun behtar hai?
Schedule batata hai ki training ke dauraan LR kaise badlega: ~10% warmup (LR dheere badhao), phir cosine decay (LR dheere-dheere girao). Warmup shuru ke unstable steps se bachata hai, cosine end me fine adjustments deta hai. Book me cosine linear se behtar paya gaya. LoRA ke liye 1e-4 se 2e-4 aur full FT ke liye 1e-5 se 5e-5 range hai — aur LR ko pehle 50–100 steps se diagnose karo, poori run ke baad nahi.
Q35 Epochs kitne rakhne chahiye? Zyada epochs hamesha behtar hain?
Nahi — zyada epochs overfitting laate hain, khaas taur par chhote dataset par. Guide: bade dataset par 1–2, medium par 3–5, 600 se kam examples par 10–20 epochs. Book ki run me 20 epochs ke baad step ~75 se divergence dikha aur validation loss ~0.88 par ruka. Best checkpoint aakhri nahi hota — har kuch sau steps par save karo aur validation par best ko chuno.
Q36 Overfitting ko loss curve se kaise pehchanein?
Healthy curve me train aur val loss saath-saath girte hain. Overfitting me train loss girta rehta hai par val loss ruk jata hai ya badhne lagta hai — book ki DPO run me flat validation loss ~step 40 se overfitting dikha. Underfitting me dono unche rehte hain, diverging me dono upar chadhte hain. Fix ka order: pehle LR halve/double karo, phir epochs, phir rank — aur 'good enough' par rukna seekho.
